paper.title: Prediction of MOF Adsorption Isotherms and High-Throughput Screening Using a Physics-Informed Membranes Graph Neural Network
paper.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are prime CO 2 -capture candidates, but grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) screening is costly when full isotherms, not single uptakes, are required; machine learning surrogates rarely resolve the continuous pressure response. We report a physics-informed pressure-aware multi-task graph neural network (PI-MGNN) to predict CO 2 uptake at arbitrary pressure and reconstruct isotherms from structure. From ~130,000 candidates, PCA and K-means select 5,023 representative MOFs, each simulated by GCMC at five pressures spanning 0.1-5.0 MPa, enforcing a continuous pressure response. Crystal graphs are processed by decoupled geometric and electrostatic graph-attention branches with auxiliary supervision, while a Gaussian-expanded pressure query is fused by cross-attention. PI-MGNN attains R 2 = 0.977 and MAE = 0.291 mol kg -1 ; isotherm MAEs are 0.428/0.312/0.330 mol kg -1 for high/medium/low-uptake MOFs, and cross-attention improves accuracy by 6.3%. Attention weights recover the pressure-resolved physics, enabling accurate and interpretable high-throughput screening.

paper.title: Tailored ZnO/Cellulose Separator Reconfigures Solvation Chemistry for Durable Magnesium Metal Batteries
paper.abstract: Abstract Magnesium metal batteries represent highly promising candidates for sustainable energy storage owing to their extremely high volumetric capacity (3833 mAh cm–3), abundant raw materials, and intrinsic safety. However, their practical viability is severely impeded by uneven Mg deposition, catastrophic interfacial side reactions, and continuous gassing behavior driven by uncontrolled electrolyte decomposition. Herein, we first report an inorganic inter-reinforced organic composite separator, fabricated by pairing cellulose with a zinc oxide (ZnO)-enhanced layer and designed to regulate the electrolyte solvation architecture by effectively anchoring solvent molecules. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that the electron-deficient Zn sites on ZnO enhance the solvent-capture ability of the polar hydroxyl groups on cellulose via bidirectional charge transfer. This interaction reconfigures the Mg2+ solvation sheath into a unique single-cluster structure, steering the formation of a dense, ultrathin, inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that facilitates rapid Mg2+ desolvation while suppressing parasitic side reactions. Consequently, the as-assembled Mg||Mg symmetric cells deliver an exceptional cycling lifespan exceeding 2000 h with minimal overpotential and exhibit robust compatibility across diverse electrolyte systems. This inorganic inter-reinforced organic strategy for modulating solvation chemistry offers a generalizable avenue toward long-life and high-safety magnesium metal batteries.

paper.title: Less can be more for predicting properties with large language models
paper.abstract: Abstract Predicting properties from coordinate–category data—sets of vectors paired with categorical information—is fundamental to computational science, manifesting in materials science as predicting formation energies or elastic moduli from crystal structures. While large language models (LLMs) have increasingly been applied to such tasks, optimal strategies for achieving reliable predictions remain elusive. Here we report fundamental limitations in LLM’s ability to learn from coordinate information in coordinate–category data. Through systematic experiments using synthetic datasets with tunable coordinate and category contributions, and a comprehensive benchmarking framework (MatText), we find that LLMs consistently fail to capture coordinate information while excelling at category patterns. This geometric blindness persists regardless of model size (up to 70 billion parameters), dataset scale (up to 2 × 10 6 structures) or text representation strategy. For material property prediction tasks dominated by structural effects, specialized geometric architectures consistently outperform LLMs, as evidenced by a clear ‘Graph Neural Network Language Model (GNN-LM) wall’ in performance benchmarks. Our analysis provides concrete guidelines for architecture selection in scientific machine learning.

paper.title: Progress toward a Better BOCS: Systematic Coarse-Graining with Local Density Potentials
paper.abstract: Abstract We introduce version 5.0 of the bottom-up open-source coarse-graining software (BOCS) package. BOCS employs the force-matching variational principle to parametrize potentials for coarse-grained (CG) models directly from atomically detailed simulations. BOCS version 5.0 significantly extends previous versions by treating potentials that depend upon the local density (LD) around each particle as well as potentials that depend upon the square gradient (SG) of this local density. We also describe a new package, PKG-BOCS, for simulating these potentials with LAMMPS. This software treats complex molecular topologies and provides considerable flexibility for defining the local density as well as the LD and SG potentials. We present numerical calculations that provide physical insight into these potentials and their dependence on the definition of the local density. These calculations also demonstrate the accuracy and reliability of our implementation. Finally, we demonstrate that LD potentials can improve the structural fidelity, thermodynamic properties, and transferability of CG models for water.

paper.title: Interfacial microenvironments enable abiotic ribonucleoside formation in micro- and nanoscale compartments
paper.abstract: The abiotic emergence of ribonucleosides remains a central challenge in origin-of-life research because ribonucleosides form inefficiently and are often unstable under prebiotically plausible conditions. Here we show that interfacial microenvironments within aqueous micro- and nanoscale compartments containing D-ribose, phosphoric acid, and nucleobases promote ribonucleoside formation by creating reaction-permissive physicochemical conditions independent of the specific compartment type. Across a diverse range of compartmentalized systems, including gas–oil–water micro/nanobubbles, gas–water micro/nanobubbles, microscale lipid-bilayer vesicles, and oil–water emulsion systems, ribonucleosides form abiotically in the absence of enzymatic catalysis. Under selected interfacial conditions, multiple ribonucleosides, including cytidine, are generated without added catalysts. Comparison among these systems reveals that interfacial architecture and coupled physicochemical properties strongly influence both reaction efficiency and product stability. CO 2 -based micro/nanobubbles support sustained cytidine accumulation, highlighting the importance of coupled gas–liquid and liquid–liquid interfaces. Ribonucleoside synthesis also depends on compartment size, whereas variations in oil content within micro/nanobubbles selectively modulate inosine formation, underscoring the sensitivity of nucleoside chemistry to interfacial properties. These findings identify interfacial microenvironments within micro- and nanoscale compartments as a general physical framework for ribonucleoside emergence and suggest that ubiquitous compartmentalized interfaces on early Earth could have provided robust settings for prebiotic ribonucleoside chemistry.

paper.title: Nonclassical condensation pathways revealed by the multivariable theory of nucleation
paper.abstract: Classical nucleation theory (CNT) provides a simple conceptual framework for nucleation but often fails to quantitatively reproduce experimental and numerical observations. In this work, we extend the theory by explicitly incorporating the multidimensional nature of nucleation and the coupled roles of kinetics and thermodynamics. Specifically, we treat the cluster density as an independent variable, within both sharp-interface and diffuse-interface descriptions. The kinetics are governed by dynamical density functional theory. Applied to liquid condensation in the Lennard-Jones system, our self-consistent, parameter-free two-variable (size–density) and three-variable (size–interface width–density) models reveal nonclassical nucleation mechanisms. At low supersaturation, both models recover the classical picture, in which clusters nucleate and grow at the equilibrium liquid density. As supersaturation increases, nonclassical behavior emerges: the critical cluster density decreases, and the nucleation pathway involves concomitant evolution in cluster size, density, and within the diffuse-interface description, interfacial width. Our diffuse-interface model reveals a rapid increase in interfacial diffuseness at high supersaturation. Near the spinodal limit, both models predict the critical cluster with diverging sizes, densities approaching that of the metastable initial phase, and vanishing work of formation, which provides a smooth connection between nucleation and spinodal decomposition. Comparison with molecular dynamics simulations demonstrates that both models substantially outperform CNT. However, the weak nonmonotonic dependence of the critical cluster density observed at very low supersaturation is captured only by diffuse-interface models. Overall, our findings indicate that CNT should be applied only in the low-supersaturation regime, and our work provides a robust foundation for its refinement beyond this limit.

paper.title: UpKast: Method, Model, and Database for Large-Scale Cross-Solvent Determination of pKa Values
paper.abstract: The acid dissociation constant, commonly written as p K a , plays a key role in chemistry. However, most p K a measurements have been conducted in only a handful of solvents, resulting in data scarcity for many relevant solvent systems. Herein, we introduce the UpKast-DB, which comprises of p K a estimates for around 3,000 acids and bases in 29 solvents. We constructed UpKast-DB using a quantum-chemical method that integrates solvation free energy calculations with experimental data. Furthermore, we trained a surrogate machine learning model UpKast-ML on the computed values, allowing for rapid and accurate prediction of p K a values beyond the acids and bases presented in UpKast-DB. The quantum-chemical and machine learning methods result in RMSEs of approximately 1 p K a unit relative to experimental values, slightly higher than the typical aleatoric uncertainty of underlying experimental data, but more accurate than many existing experimental measurements (which can have uncertainties up to, and sometimes beyond, 3 p K a units). The data and modeling approaches provide a means of productively augmenting existing p K a data sources, and represent a significant step toward general determination of p K a in any solvent. The dataset and models can be found on Zenodo: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23239570

paper.title: Tuning the Anchoring and ORR Activity of Sub-Nano Pt Clusters on HOPG via Ion Implantation and Oxygen Functionalization
paper.abstract: Sub-nanometer supported clusters are of interest in catalysis due to nearly complete precious metal atom utilization, generally high catalytic activity, and attractive tunability via size and clustersupport interactions. The stability of such clusters remains a challenge, however. We demonstrate anchoring and stabilization of size-selected Ptn, n = 2 - 10 clusters soft-landed on HOPG, achieved 2 by modifying the HOPG with 100 eV kinetic energy N(𝑛 1, 2) and Ar+ ions, with and without O2 oxidation of the ion-modified surfaces, prior to Ptn soft-landing. Ion modification is found to significantly improve the sticking probability for soft-landed Ptn, implying increased adsorption energies, and O2 exposure prior to cluster deposition increases the sticking probability to ~unity. DFT finds that Ptn bind preferentially to under-coordinated carbon sites created by the ion impacts, rather than to implanted N atoms, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and scanning tunneling microscopy both show that the defect-anchored clusters are stable against sintering. There is net electron transfer from the defect-bound clusters to the support, and the local defect structure may undergo significant restructuring due to Pt-C bond formation. To probe the effects of ion-modified HOPG on the chemical properties of the adsorbed Ptn clusters, we tested electrodes prepared by Ptn deposition on ion-modified HOPG for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The ion-modified electrodes showed ORR activity consistent with cluster size being maintained, and O2 modification enhanced both cluster anchoring and ORR activity. Thus, ion modification provides means to stabilize sub-nano cluster electrodes, while oxygen functionalization of the anchoring sites tunes the electrocatalytic activity.

paper.title: Detection and Characterization of the Cosmological Neutrino Background by EPR Spectroscopy on Molecular Hydrino with Implications for Telecommunications
paper.abstract: A hydrino atom, H(1/p) solved using a Maxwellian electrodynamics and relativistic mechanics, is atomic hydrogen with state energy En = -13.598/n2 eV, in which n = 1/p, and p is limited by the energy in the electric field of the proton to 126 whereafter the proton and electron decay. Electron transitions to hydrino states involve an initial non-radiative energy transfer to a catalyst that serves as an energy hole or sink of a quantized amount of energy, 2mE1 (m is integer) to be transferred to a catalyst such as HOH, a free or nascent water molecule. Furthermore, hydrino atoms can react to form the corresponding diatomic molecule referred to as molecular hydrino H2(1/p). In contrast to molecular hydrogen (H2), the molecular hydrino (H2(1/p)) is paramagnetic with S = ½ comprising a paired and unpaired electron in the same MO wherein the lower energy state central field is provided by photons akin to gluons in nucleons in addition to the field of the protons. Due to its unique structure, H2(1/p)) interacts with the neutrinos in the energy range of the cosmological neutrino background (𝐶𝜈𝐵) as confirmed by the neutrino mediated observations of predicted fine structure, predicted high magnetic field Paschen Beck effect, large downfield shifts, temporal changes of EPR spectra due to accumulated changes in fine structure state populations, extraordinary broadened signals, zero order absorption occurring in the perpendicular and parallel modes, and the observation of magnetic dipole-dipole interactions of H2(1/4)-H2 dimer requiring intramolecular angular momentum transfer from a neutrino excited fine structure state in H2(1/4) as well as unique temperature and matrix dependences of the EPR signals. EPR was used to detect and characterize the 𝐶𝜈𝐵 for the first time. The isotropic and parallel propagation nature of 𝐶𝜈𝐵 can be exploited for line of site telecommunications requiring no transmission power to transmit signals in any direction unattenuated and undispersed through any physical barrier, including the Earth.

paper.title: Electronic spectroscopy of (N2O) n + ( n = 2–6): Competition between the charge resonance and charge transfer bands
paper.abstract: A hemibond (two-center three-electron bond), formed by a charge resonance interaction, is a characteristic structural motif in radical cation clusters. Hemibonded clusters exhibit strong absorption in the UV–visible region, which is attributed to the charge resonance (CR) transition and serves as a marker band for hemibond formation. Despite its significance, how microsolvation affects the CR transition of the hemibonded ion core remains unclear. In this study, we performed electronic spectroscopy for (N2O)n+ (n = 2–6) clusters containing the hemibonded (N2O)2+ ion core to elucidate the microsolvation effect via clustering of N2O molecules. In the observed spectra, a charge transfer (CT) transition was detected in addition to the CR transition for n = 3. Our results reveal that the CR and CT transitions predominantly lead to the formation of N2O+ and (N2O)2+ fragments, respectively. As microsolvation proceeds, the CR band appears to exhibit a significant red shift. This is attributed to the contribution of the CT excitation to the N2O+ fragment channel via the thermal dissociation pathway.

paper.title: High-Throughput Computational Screening of Quinones for Electrochemical CO2 Capture
paper.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical carbon capture (ECC) with quinones is a promising, energy-efficient alternative to thermal systems, but oxygen sensitivity remains a significant challenge. The persistent trade-off between CO2 affinity (KCO2) and reduction potentials (Ered) requires identifying “borderline” species amenable to system-level optimization. Using density functional theory (DFT), we screened 31,000 quinones and identified 681 candidates with parameters suitable for oxygen-tolerant ECC. Our screening revealed unexplored structural motifs, including heterocyclic and extended aromatic systems, alongside intramolecular H-bonding effects. We also identified functional groups prone to structural fragmentation upon CO2 binding, which are unsuitable for durable operation despite favorable potentials. Finally, synthetic feasibility was assessed via a dual-metric approach, narrowing the selection to 20 high-priority quinones for experimental validation. This study provides a rational design roadmap for high-performance organic ECC sorbents.

paper.title: COSMO-RS-Based Theoretical Investigation of Equilibria in Protic Ionic Liquids
paper.abstract: Ionic liquids have become an increasingly important field of research. A subgroup, protic ionic liquids, have been shown to be excellent solvents even for poorly soluble materials such as cellulose or polyamides. Still, the composition of such liquids, e.g., their ionicity and the nature of formed aggregates, is mostly unknown and experimental attempts to shed light on this have been mostly unsuccessful. Herein, we report the development of the Python-based COSMOPIL program (COnductor-like Screening MOdel for Protic Ionic Liquids) to analyze the composition of protic ionic liquids via theoretical methods based on density functional theory (DFT) and the COSMO-RS (COnductor-like Screening MOdel for Real Solvents) implicit solvation model. The inputs of experimental data such as dielectric constants is not necessary. The COSMO-PIL program demonstrates the influence of acid/base ratios and residual water on the ionic liquid composition and allows the understanding of the reported poor ionicity of those liquids. Most notably, we explain this “ionicity gap” in protic ionic liquids, as even superbases fail to achieve full acid deprotonation, with a polarity mismatch between anion and cation, requiring residual acid as mediator.

paper.title: Solvent Dynamics and Multiconfigurational Treatment Drive the Anomalous Stokes Shift of HINA
paper.abstract: The 3-hydroxyisonicotinaldehyde (HINA) anion is one of the smallest known green-emissive fluorophores, yet the origin of its anomalously large Stokes shift (0.87 eV) remains unexplained. Given the well-established influence of the surrounding environment on the photophysical properties of fluorescent dyes, we examine its role in this shift by simulating the anion's absorption and emission spectra with four computational protocols that differ in configurational sampling, solvent treatment, and electronic-structure method. Wigner sampling protocols capture less than half of the experimental Stokes shift, whether the solvent is treated implicitly or explicitly, whereas QM/MM molecular dynamics sampling improves it significantly. Structural analysis associates this improvement with coupling between the first solvation shell and the intramolecular interaction between the aldehyde hydrogen and the hydroxyl oxygen, which is captured by molecular-dynamics sampling but not by the corresponding frozen-solute Wigner-sampling protocol. When combined with RMS-CASPT2, this sampling quantitatively reproduces the experimental spectra and Stokes shift (0.85 versus 0.87 eV), showing that quantitative description of the Stokes shift of HINA requires both solvent-induced conformational dynamics and a multiconfigurational electronic-structure treatment.

paper.title: Dry pebble rain could have delivered water to Earth through hydrogen reduction of iron oxide
paper.abstract: Much of the water on Earth could have been produced from dry silicate pebbles falling through the hot, hydrogen-rich primordial atmosphere as the planet formed. High-temperature experiments in streams of pure hydrogen demonstrate that the reduction of iron oxide in the silicates can produce water vapour in minutes or hours, and suggest that water production on Earth-sized exoplanets should be widespread.

paper.title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation
paper.abstract: Abstract ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

paper.title: Thermodynamic origin of atmospheric new particle formation: Theory for stable nucleating pairs
paper.abstract: Atmospheric new particle formation (NPF) has been observed across virtually all tropospheric environments, yet the meteorological conditions that favor or suppress it have resisted clear theoretical resolution. Here we show that, for neutral chemistries in which a strongly bound molecular pair constitutes the critical cluster, the thermodynamic precondition for NPF is set by a single quantity: the effective binding free energy of that pair, Δ G AB ° ( T , RH ) , which captures the competing influences of temperature and relative humidity in a closed-form analytical framework. Applied to the sulfuric acid–dimethylamine system in the boundary layer, the theory reproduces observed clustering across laboratory experiments and field campaigns spanning a polluted megacity, a remote high-altitude site, and an ultra-pristine boreal peatland, all without kinetic fitting parameters; precursor concentrations and the condensation sink enter as separable factors that govern the subsequent production rate. The framework reveals an optimal Δ G AB ° that maximizes cluster production, providing a thermodynamic basis for why NPF peaks at midday, favors spring over other seasons, occurs under heat wave conditions despite temperatures approaching + 40 ° C, and can even arise on rare evenings in near-pristine conditions. More broadly, the theory exposes the inherent relationship between atmospheric conditions and the earliest steps of particle formation, offering a general interpretive tool that complements and extends what observations and simulations alone cannot provide.

paper.title: Inductive bias and out-of-distribution generalization in deep learning surrogates for 2D PDE dynamics
paper.abstract: Abstract Partial differential equations (PDEs) are a foundational tool for modeling physical systems. However, high-fidelity numerical simulations are often computationally intensive, which has prompted the development of surrogate models in the field of scientific machine learning. While recent approaches have achieved high predictive accuracy by employing complex architectures and extensive datasets, many scientific applications offer only a limited number of simulation trajectories. In this study, we examine the impact of architectural inductive biases on the learning of two-dimensional PDE in data-limited settings. Instead of proposing a highly expressive model, we deliberately adopt a simple multi-channel U-Net modified to enforce periodic boundary conditions. In this study, we compare this architecture with transformer-based and UNet variants such as vision transformer (ViT), adaptive fourier neural operator (AFNO), PDE-Transformer (PDE-T), and UNet with Kolmogorov-Arnold Layers (KAN-UNet) under a common training setup across five PDE families. To keep comparisons uniform and to mimic partial observability in real measurements, we train all models on rollouts of a single representative scalar field per system. Despite its simplicity, the adapted U-Net consistently matches or outperforms these more complex models in forecasting accuracy, spectral similarity, and physics-based metrics while requiring substantially less training time. The findings of this study demonstrate that, in scenarios where data is limited, the judicious selection of inductive biases can often prove to be more advantageous than increasing the model complexity for the purpose of learning the dynamics of PDEs.

paper.title: Building the Data Foundations for the Design and Discovery of Transition Metal Complexes
paper.abstract: The unique chemistry of transition metal complexes (TMCs) enables several advanced technologies in diverse fields including renewable energies, medicine, and catalysis. Machine learning methods can accelerate their rational design but are bounded by limited dataset sizes, restricted chemical scopes, and insufficient quality. This Perspective surveys the current landscape of TMC datasets and investigates how they seek to address these challenges. The analysis focuses on the data curation processes as well as the scope of the properties provided, and their level of theory. Furthermore, the applications and methodological advancements enabled by TMC datasets are reviewed, including the generative design of metal ligands and the evolutionary optimization of TMCs. The Perspective concludes by outlining future directions, with particular emphasis on extending data to broader chemical scopes including non-equilibrium geometries, establishing community-wide data formats and benchmarks, and developing strategies to effectively integrate heterogeneous data sources.

paper.title: A hydrochromic porous aromatic framework for self-reporting, high-capacity atmospheric water harvesting
paper.abstract: Atmospheric water harvesting materials are typically optimised for sorption performance alone, despite the practical importance of monitoring sorbent loading. Here, we report a hydrochromic porous aromatic framework that integrates water capture and self-reporting within a single adaptive material. Sulfonation of PAF-1 affords the hydrophilic framework PAF-1-S that adsorbs 0.18 g·g-1 of water at only 10% RH and reaches 1.87 g·g-1 at 90% RH, combining exceptional low-humidity capture with the highest total capacity among the porous sorbents surveyed here. Water adsorption simultaneously induces a reversible, graded colour change, enabling direct visualisation of sorbent loading without external sensing hardware. Spectroscopic analysis indicates that this response arises from hydration-driven acid–base equilibria within the modified framework. Combined with rapid sorption kinetics, low-temperature regeneration and robust cycling stability, these findings establish responsive porous adsorbents as a strategy for intelligent sorption materials.

paper.title: Complementary Roles of Iodide-Mediated Pathways and Anion Dynamics in Lithium-Ion Transport in Li3PS4-LiI Glasses
paper.abstract: LiI addition enhances lithium-ion transport in sulfide glasses, yet the microscopic mechanisms linking halide incorporation to faster conduction remain unclear. Here, we investigate how LiI promotes Li+ migration in (100−x)Li3PS4–xLiI glasses by resolving changes in local structure, migration energetics, and anion dynamics. A machinelearning potential trained on newly generated ab initio molecular dynamics data and an existing sulfide-electrolyte dataset enables 10 ns simulations of approximately 5000atom glass models at 300 K over a LiI content range of 0–50 mol%. The potential is validated against density functional theory calculations, experimental densities, and X-ray total scattering profiles. Although the PS4 3–units remain intact and their time-averaged inter-unit correlations change little, Li+ diffusivity more than doubles across this composition range, accompanied by increased migration beyond local cage-like regions. To characterize the energetics of these pathways in a disordered environment, we introduce an analysis that combines Voronoi partitioning into P-and I–-centered domains with atomic potentialenergy fluctuations along Li+ trajectories. The resulting statistical local energy-barrier indicators allow comparisons between domain transitions without assigning absolute activation energies. This analysis reveals two complementary effects of LiI addition. Transitions involving I–-centered domains exhibit lower barrier indicators than direct transitions between P-centered domains, identifying favorable I–-mediated migration pathways. LiI addition also lowers the barrier indicators for direct P-to-P transitions, extending its influence beyond pathways that pass through I–-centered domains. Enhanced local translational and rotational dynamics of PS4 3–units accompany this broader reduction, suggesting that anion motion helps facilitate Li+ migration. These findings explain how LiI can enhance transport while largely preserving the average glass structure and highlight the combined roles of local migration pathways and anion dynamics in designing sulfide glass electrolytes.

paper.title: Structural and energetic signatures of SO2 and CH4 incorporation in imidazolium-based ionic liquids
paper.abstract: A systematic molecular dynamics study of sulfur dioxide (SO2) and methane (CH4) incorporation in 24 imidazolium-based ionic liquids is presented, spanning different anion families and cation alkyl chain lengths. The two gases represent limiting cases of solvation behavior in ionic liquids: SO2 exhibits strong electrostatic interactions and Lewis amphoteric character, whereas CH4 is governed primarily by weak London dispersion forces. Radial distribution functions, coordination numbers, cluster-size distributions, and interaction energies were analyzed to elucidate the molecular organization of the mixtures. The results show that neither SO2 nor CH4 substantially disrupts the polar network of the ionic liquids. SO2 partitions between the polar and nonpolar regions of the ionic liquid, leading to reduced self-association and more gas distributions, whereas CH4 preferentially occupies alkyl-rich regions and exhibits only weak self-association with minimal dependence on cation chain length. Interaction energy decomposition highlights the dominant role of electrostatics in SO2 solvation and the free volume-driven, weakly interacting nature of CH4 incorporation. These findings provide a molecular-level framework for rationalizing incorporation trends and for guiding the design of ionic liquids for gas separation, highlighting how polarity, anion charge distribution, and cation alkyl chain length can be tuned to enhance specific SO2 stabilization while controlling nonspecific CH4 accommodation in alkyl-rich free-volume domains.

paper.title: Toward a Local Manipulation of DNA by Quantum Fields
paper.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen bonds are the fundamental backbone for deoxyribo-nucleic acid (DNA) stability. In this Letter we investigate a new strategy based on plasmonic cavities to perform manipulation of hydrogen bonds in DNA. The analysis is performed using state-of-the-art Quantum Electrodynamics Coupled Cluster (QED-CC) calculations. We investigate whether in the strong coupling regime modifications of the nucleotide bases’ interactions can be induced in a totally nonintrusive manner. Our strategy proposes an alternative approach to methodologies based on a collective coupling to perform optical DNA manipulation.

paper.title: Substituent Effects on Anion Bonding and Disassembly of Hypervalent Iodine Macrocycles
paper.abstract: A series of phenylalanine-derived hypervalent iodine-based macrocycles (HIMs) bearing electron donating and withdrawing substituents were prepared. The HIM associations with the anion of tetrabutylammonium chloride (TBA-Cl) were systematically investigated using binding isotherms generated via NMR spectroscopy. The association constants of the resulting I-Cl bond were found to linearly correlate with the electronic substituents via Hammett analysis. Electron-withdrawing substituents strengthened the I–Cl bond and disassembled the macrocycle more readily. In addition, the shifting of HIM carbonyl frequencies obtained by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy were found to correlate with the binding affinities and provide an alternative predictive methodology to determine HIM disassembly and anion binding affinities.

paper.title: Mixed physics-informed neural networks for anisotropic diffusion: Energy error and directional coupling
paper.abstract: Abstract Mixed physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer a natural way to approximate potential and flux together in anisotropic diffusion. Balancing individual residual components can be useful, but leaves open how their directional coupling should enter the loss. We examine how this coupling affects the relation between residual and mixed energy error, and use this connection to study analytical and operator-probe weights. A weighted orthogonal decomposition yields sharp equivalence constants for the ideal residual functional, independent of coefficient contrast in the diffusion-weighted norms. A simple but revealing constant-flux example shows how every fixed positive componentwise weight can select the same suboptimal approximation. The exact error ratio is determined by off-diagonal coupling. This result holds for continuous and discrete losses with positive quadrature weights, even with exact conservation and minimization. The classical weight K -1 recovers the best approximation in this trial family. An operator-probe alternative combines the flux and potential-gradient response moments through their matrix geometric mean. Its spectral bounds yield a continuous upper bound on the energy error. Numerical comparisons show a particularly clear benefit from retaining coupling for constant rotated coefficients. In an independent 84-run study on two manufactured problems, probe weighting reduces geometric-mean mixed-energy errors by approximately 37% and 56% relative to the conservation-matched and original Euclidean baselines, respectively. The observed geometric-mean error is also slightly lower than with analytical weighting. Darcy-flow and heat-conduction examples illustrate the resulting potential, flux and error fields.

paper.title: Density Functional Theory of Dion-Jacobson Double Perovskite Halides
paper.abstract: First-principles density functional theory was used to study six (four unreported) hybrid layered double perovskites of the Dion-Jacobson A2MM ′′′ X8 family. All 6 compounds consist of organic diamines that bridge rock-saltordered inorganic octahedra, with Ag+ as the M ′ site and Bi+3/Sb+3 as the M′′′ site. Both aliphatic (1,3-diaminopropane [PDA], 1,4-diaminobutane [BDA], 1,8-diaminooctane [ODA]) and aromatic (para-phenylenediamine [PPDA]) spac-ers are investigated, revealing how composition affects the band gap character and magnitude. Formation energy analysis using the DFT-D3 method reveals negative formation energies with respect to relevant precursors. Furthermore, calculations using the complex dielectric function reveal key optical properties, including absorption coefficients, refractive indices, and complex permittivity.

paper.title: Phosphorus(V) Umpolung Converts Electrophilic Phosphates into Nucleophilic H-Phosphonates
paper.abstract: Ubiquitous in chemistry, biology and medicine, phosphate groups form the backbone of DNA and RNA, and their analogues like phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotides provide frontier therapies for challenging genetic disorders. However, the inherent electrophilicity of phosphorus(V) and thermodynamic stability of native P–OH bonds preclude their direct, latestage conversion into phosphate analogues. Here, we introduce a polarity-reversal (umpolung) strategy for converting electrophilic phosphates into nucleophilic H-phosphonates. This approach proceeds through two stages: P–OH thiolation into a thiophosphate followed by radical P–S cleavage, which generates the P–H bond. This sequence converts diverse phosphate substrates, such as complex drug scaffolds and nucleotides, into H-phosphonates that can undergo further phosphorus functionalization. The thiolation step also enables direct, one-pot conversion of P–OH into P–SH in nucleotides, providing a chemical route to the phosphorothioation of native phosphate backbones associated with bacterial and archaeal DNA defense. Therefore, phosphorus(V) umpolung reverses the polarity of phosphate chemistry, transforming otherwise stable P–OH bonds into synthetically versatile phosphorus functionalities.
paper.tldr: 该研究提出磷（V）极性反转策略，通过硫代化和自由基裂解，将亲电磷酸盐转化为亲核H-膦酸酯，实现后期直接合成磷酸类似物。

paper.title: Cholesteric Liquid Crystals for Ultratrace PFAS Detection
paper.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent, mobile water contaminants associated with adverse effects on human health and ecosystems. Current analytical methods require specialized instrumentation, complicating their on-site detection at ultratrace concentrations across distributed water infrastructures. Here we integrate fluorophilic partitioning and proton-responsive recognition within a cholesteric liquid crystal (CLC). The fluorinated component promotes selectivity over non-fluorinated structural analogues, whereas the pyridine receptor transduces protonation into changes in helical organization and reflected color. The formulation was confined within monodisperse spherical droplets and processed as a photocurable photonic ink to produce sensing strips with a strong reflection signal readable by portable fiber-optic spectroscopy. The platform detected five PFAS through concentration-dependent blue-shifts, reaching detection limits of 5.9 parts per trillion (ppt) without sample preconcentration and maintaining comparable performance across three water matrices. Coupling molecular recognition to collective supramolecular reorganization establishes CLCs as promising sensing materials for on-site ultratrace PFAS detection.
paper.tldr: 该胆甾相液晶体系通过氟亲和作用与质子响应识别，能在超痕量水平选择性检测PFAS并产生可见的颜色变化，适用于现场快速检测。

paper.title: Late-Stage Ligand Prioritization by Combining Rapid-Dissociation Filtering with MM/GBSA
paper.abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of binding free energies remains a central challenge in computational chemistry, largely due to the complexity of solvent effects and the trade-off between accuracy and computational cost. Explicit solvent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide detailed thermodynamic and kinetic insight, now routinely reaching microsecond timescales, while end-point methods such as MM/GBSA offer high efficiency but are sensitive to model parameters. In particular, the accuracy of MM/GBSA strongly depends on the atomic radii used to define the dielectric boundary within the implicit solvent framework. Here, we introduce an explicit–implicit hybrid workflow for late-stage ligand prioritization that integrates the strengths of both approaches. In this framework, microsecond-scale explicit solvent MD simulations act as a rapid-dissociation filter, flagging weak or unstable binders through spontaneous dissociation within the simulation window. MM/GBSA is then used to rank the remaining candidates. To improve the accuracy of the implicit solvent stage, we employ optimized atomic radii sets (OPTBIND), specifically designed for binding free-energy calculations. On the protein–ligand complexes of Curated32-4 set , a new curated benchmark of 32 complexes including 4 congeneric series, the entropy-free MM/GBSA stage with OPT- BIND 6D achieved Pearson r = 0.82 and Spearman ρ = 0.84, with 100% recovery of the experimental rank ordering across all four congeneric series, while a single-replica consistency test of the rapid-dissociation filter yielded an AUC of 0.88 and retained all 15 sub-micromolar binders. Finally, as a real-world drug design application, we apply the workflow to halogen substitutions in SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitors, demonstrating its ability to identify favorable chemical modifications. Notably, the approach prospectively identifies F→Cl and F→I as affinity-enhancing substitutions; the predicted enhancement for the chlorine analog is subsequently confirmed experimentally, while the iodine analog remains a testable prediction, highlighting its predictive power in guiding chemical optimization. Together, these results establish a practical framework for detailed studies of receptor–ligand binding and for late-stage ligand prioritization in drug discovery.

paper.title: The role of membrane properties and environmental footprint in shaping the cost-climate optimal carbon capture processes
paper.abstract: Membrane development for carbon capture is typically guided by CO2 permeability and CO2/N2 selectivity, although these properties alone cannot determine whether a material will deliver economically and environmentally favourable performance at scale. Herein, we develop a multi-criteria optimization framework that integrates a machine-learning surrogate model of a multi-stage membrane process with techno-economic analysis and life cycle assessment. By applying this framework to mixed matrix membranes, we investigate the interplay of membrane properties and membrane-specific inventories in defining process-level costs and environmental indicators. For the capture from flue gases produced by a waste incinerator plant and a cement plant, electricity is mostly driven by CO2/O2 selectivity within the investigated range and is the dominant contributor to process costs and climate change impacts. This makes the climate benefits of membrane-based capture strongly dependent on the electricity supply: high-performance membranes supplied with carbon-intensive electricity can have climate change impacts comparable to or even higher than those of low-performing membranes supplied with low-carbon electricity. Therefore, we show for the first time how the system-level context shapes the properties that must be prioritized and their target values to unlock economic and environmental benefits: membrane synthesis and lifetime have a substantial impact in the presence of clean electricity, whereas increasingly high CO2/O2 and CO2/N2 selectivity are needed in the presence of moderate to high carbon intensity. Overall, with this work, we identify priorities for improvement in membrane production and performance that could only be revealed by jointly considering process-level costs and environmental impacts.

paper.title: Stoichiometric Control in H 2 S-Mediated Nitrite Reduction at a Zn-site: Intercepting SNO 1− , SSNO 1− and HONO Intermediates
paper.abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) and nitrite participate in intertwined signaling chemistry, yet the factors governing product selectivity between nitric oxide (NO) and nitroxyl (HNO) and the underlying reaction pathways remain poorly defined. Here, we establish that reduction of a zinc-nitrite complex by H 2 S follows stoichiometry-dependent product selectivity. With 2 equiv of H 2 S, the reaction generates NO and HNO-derived nitrous oxide (N 2 O) trapped in 46.3% ± 2.1% and 19.7% ± 1.5%, yields, respectively. UV-vis and 15 N NMR spectroscopy along with phosphine-based intermediate trapping and DFT studies support a nucleophilic attack pathway involving zinc-bound thionitrite (SNO − ) and perthionitrite (SSNO − ) intermediates. We independently synthesize and crystallographically characterize the zinc-perthionitrite complex, identifying isomers with cis-ĸ 2 -S,O and unprecedented Y-shaped ĸ 2 -S,S coordination modes in the solid-state. In contrast, 5 equiv of H 2 S favors an acidbase pathway involving spectroscopically intercepted nitrous acid (HONO) intermediate and affords NO in 94.6% ± 1.5% yield, with only trace N 2 O. Reaction with hydrosulfide (HS − ) instead, generate a zinc-hydrosulfide-nitrite adduct without nitrite reduction; subsequent protonation produces NO exclusively. Together, these findings establish H 2 S stoichiometry and proton availability as complementary determinants of competing nitrite reduction pathways that control NO versus N 2 O selectivity at a redox-inactive zinc center.

paper.title: Conformational Heterogeneity and Local Electronic Structure in Wild-Type and Arctic Amyloid-Β42
paper.abstract: Amyloid-𝛽 42 is a heterogeneous system, widely known as an intrinsically disordered protein, or IDP, sampling a variety of conformations. However, how ensemble redistribution affects the underlying local electronic structure remains less well understood. In this study, classical molecular dynamics simulations are combined with population-aware density functional theory and reduced active-space calculations to compare the LVFFA fragment of the wild-type and Arctic (E22G) variants. Common-space principal component analysis, clustering, and Ramachandran plot analysis depicted distinct trajectory distributions and greater conformational heterogeneity for the E22G trajectory. Population-ranked conformations representing 60.58% of WT and 54.98% of Arctic populations yielded conditional population-weighted B3LYP/def2-SVP HOMO-LUMO separations of 5.81 and 5.95 eV, respectively. The 0.14 eV Arctic–WT shift remained positive across moving-block bootstrap analyses. Fragment expansion altered frontier-orbital ordering, although the spatial character of LVFFA-associated states was preserved. CASCI tested active-space sensitivity, and matched UCCSD-VQE calculations reproduced CAS(4,4) CASCI reference energies for the reduced Hamiltonians. Together, these results demonstrate the importance of population-aware conformational sampling and model-definition sensitivity when relating heterogeneous biomolecular ensembles to quantum-chemical properties.

paper.title: Infrared spectroscopy of MO(CH4) n (M = Ce, Y; n = 1–3) reveals two distinct adsorption configurations
paper.abstract: Investigation of the interactions of methane with metal oxides is crucial for elucidating absorption configurations at active sites of catalysts, which has proven to be a challenging experimental target due to the difficulty in size selection of neutral systems. In this work, the interactions of methane with rare earth metal oxides are studied by using size-specific infrared-vacuum ultraviolet spectroscopy and quantum chemical calculations. Two distinct configurations of methane adsorption are found in the MO(CH4)n (M = Ce, Y; n = 1–3) complexes. In the first configuration, the C and H atoms of methane are positioned between a Lewis acid-base pair (M2+–O2−); in the second configuration, one H atom of methane is oriented toward a Lewis basic oxygen anion (O2−). Such adsorption features of methane on cerium and yttrium monoxides are dominantly governed by electrostatic interactions. These findings provide key microscopic information for methane adsorption on metal oxides that are helpful for understanding the crucial initial steps in the catalytic cycles.

paper.title: PI3Kδ is selectively inhibited by roginolisib by stabilizing the C-terminal helix kα12
paper.abstract: Abstract Phosphoinositide 3-kinases (PI3Ks) are major regulators of cell growth, proliferation and signalling, constituting key therapeutic targets in cancer, inflammation, and other diseases. Individual class I PI3K isoforms control key cellular functions, imposing the need to generate isoform-specific inhibition for therapeutic intervention. Roginolisib is a selective PI3Kδ inhibitor that shows promise for the treatment of cancer. Using a combination of X-ray crystallography, molecular dynamics simulations, and hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, we describe the mechanism driving roginolisib’s potent and isoform-selective inhibition of PI3Kδ. Roginolisib uniquely stabilises the catalytic C-terminal helix kα12, locking the enzyme in an inactive conformation. This binding mode also results in more sustained inhibition of phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate formation in tumour samples of CLL patients. Inhibition of PI3Ks by stabilization of helix kα12 into an inactive conformation has not, to the best of our knowledge, been described before and may provide the basis for novel, more selective and effective pharmacological strategies.

paper.title: DHHC12 serves as a critical nutrient-responsive switch that couples amino acid sensing to insulin secretion
paper.abstract: Protein palmitoylation covalently attaches the energy metabolite palmitate to target proteins, yet how it is regulated by nutrient status remains elusive. Here, we identify the palmitoyltransferase DHHC12 as a critical nutrient-responsive switch, coupling amino acid availability to insulin secretion. Amino acid deficiency activates the kinase GCN2, which phosphorylates COPA at Thr777, enabling its function as an adaptor for the CRL4 E3 ligase complex and leading to ubiquitination of DHHC12 on two critical cysteine residues (Cys127 and Cys133, with Cys127 within the catalytic DHHC motif) and its subsequent degradation. In male mice, loss of Dhhc12 impairs insulin secretion and causes glucose intolerance. DHHC12 palmitoylates SYT7 to promote glucose-stimulated insulin exocytosis. The physiological relevance of this pathway is underscored by two human DHHC12 variants: the hypoglycemia-associated L196P mutant evades degradation, whereas the hyperglycemia-linked N238I mutant is constitutively degraded. Together, our findings establish the GCN2-COPA-DHHC12 axis as a direct nutrient-sensing mechanism that couples amino acid availability to systemic glucose homeostasis.

paper.title: Mild Heterogeneous Thiophene Hydrogenation Enabled by a Modified Palladium Catalyst
paper.abstract: Abstract Thiophenes are readily available sulfur heteroarenes and prominent motifs in medicinal and synthetic chemistry, but their direct heterogeneous hydrogenation to thiolanes remains challenging due to sulfur-induced catalyst deactivation and competing hydrodesulfurization. Here, we report a chloroform-induced surface modification strategy that enables the heterogeneous Pd(OH)2/C-catalyzed hydrogenation of thiophenes to saturated sulfur heterocycles. The method proceeds under mild hydrogenation conditions and provides access to a range of alkyl-, silyl-, aryl-, and benzofused thiolane derivatives. A hydrogenation-focused robustness assessment revealed compatibility with several functional groups that are commonly sensitive under Pd/H2 conditions, while preparative scope studies showed that functional-group-containing thiophenes can be converted when potentially interfering motifs are separated from the thiophene core by suitable alkyl or aryl spacers. Mechanistic experiments indicate that CHCl3 is not merely a beneficial solvent: CHCl3/H2 pretreatment of Pd(OH)2/C generates a catalytically competent material whose activity is retained after replacing CHCl3 with 2-MeTHF. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) analyses support the formation of persistent chloroform-derived organochlorine/C–Cl-type surface environments and chlorocarbon fragments. These findings establish solvent-induced catalyst modification as a useful design principle for challenging heterogeneous hydrogenations of sulfur-containing heteroarenes.

paper.title: Inclusion of three-body corrections in the relativistic equation-of-motion coupled cluster method: Application to electron detachment
paper.abstract: We present the formulation and implementation of a triples-correction scheme for relativistic equation-of-motion coupled-cluster calculations of ionization potentials. Both full and partial triples-correction schemes are implemented using the exact two-component atomic mean-field (X2CAMF) Hamiltonian in combination with Cholesky decomposition (CD) of two-electron integrals and a frozen natural spinor (FNS) truncation scheme to reduce computational cost. Benchmark calculations on halide anions, noble-gas atoms, hydrogen halides, and dihalogen molecules demonstrate the importance of triple excitations for the quantitative prediction of ionization potentials. The CCSD(T)(a)* scheme achieves a mean absolute error of ∼0.01 eV relative to full CCSDT for halide anions and noble-gas atoms and ∼0.08 eV relative to the experiment for dihalogen molecules. The X2CAMF approximation reproduces four-component Dirac–Coulomb results with negligible deviations, while the CD-FNS strategy substantially reduces the computational cost. The resulting partial triples-correction scheme scales as O(n7) with storage comparable to CCSD, providing an accurate and practical approach for relativistic ionization-energy calculations in heavy-element systems.

paper.title: The Electrical Double Layer in Batteries-Perspective on Complex Electrolytes and Future Directions
paper.abstract: The electrical double layer (EDL) defines the few nanometer region between an electrified surface and its interfacing electrolyte. This non-Faradaic interfacial phenomenon has often been overlooked in the battery field in preference to the Faradaic charge-transfer and interphasial forming reactions. Here, a perspective is provided to focus on the EDL and how it dictates much of the later reactions’ behaviors. Two fields of understanding are discussed-one being computational and how to accurately model the EDL in more complex electrolytes, the other being experimental and how to accurately probe the EDL. Both fields are of importance to designing electrolytes and electrodes for improved battery performance, all ofwhich is dictated through interfacial behavior. K E YWORD S

paper.title: Breaking the Additive Paradox in Aqueous Aluminum‐Ion Batteries via Weak‐Coordination Asymmetric Electrolyte Chemistry
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous aluminum‐ion batteries (AAIBs) are compelling for sustainable storage, yet the strong hydrolysis of Al 3+ acidifies the electrolyte, causing corrosion and passivation that necessitate modification. Additives designed to break the rigid Al 3+ solvation shell face a paradox: they often compromise reversibility via either dielectric collapse or kinetic deadlocks. Here, we break this paradox by establishing a weak‐coordination asymmetric electrolyte based on aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTF) 3 ), dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). DMSO coordinates to Al 3+ , displacing coordinated water to suppress water activity, but cannot preserve the dielectric environment. FEC compensates via three synergistic functions: high dielectric constant for electrostatic screening, weak hydrogen bonding for solvation asymmetry reinforcement, and reductive decomposition for solid electrolyte interphase(SEI) formation. The sequential coupling of DMSO‐mediated solvation disruption with FEC‐enables dielectric/interfacial compensation accelerates desolvation and stabilizes electrode: a fluorinated SEI enables 2000 h reversible Al plating/stripping, while a spinel‐to‐layer transformation creates a fluorinated interface on vanadium oxide with asymmetric channels, mitigating dissolution. The full cell retains 90.8% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g −1 . By showing that resolving one bottleneck can expose another, this work reframes additive optimization as sequential processes of identifying and compensating coupled failure mechanisms, generalizing a design principle for multivalent aqueous electrolytes.

paper.title: Noise-resilient training of machine learning interatomic potentials
paper.abstract: The accuracy of machine learning interatomic potentials suffers from reference data that contain numerical noise. Often originating from unconverged or inconsistent electronic-structure calculations, this noise is challenging to identify. Existing mitigation strategies, such as manual filtering or iterative refinement of outliers, require either substantial expert effort or multiple expensive retraining cycles, making them difficult to scale to large datasets. Here, we introduce a noise-resilient training method that automatically down-weighs noisy samples, without requiring additional reference calculations. By tracking the loss distribution via an exponential moving average, this unsupervised method identifies outliers throughout a single training run. We show that this approach prevents overfitting and matches the performance of iterative refinement baselines with significantly reduced overhead. The method’s effectiveness is demonstrated by recovering accurate physical observables for liquid water from unconverged reference data, including diffusion coefficients. Furthermore, we validate its scalability by training a foundation model for organic chemistry on the SPICE dataset, where it reduces both energy and force errors. This framework provides a simple, automated solution for training robust models on imperfect datasets across dataset sizes.

paper.title: Tracing the Physical Roots of Chemical Concepts through Artificial Intelligence
paper.abstract: The language of chemistry is universally based on simple concepts such as the atom and the bond. Yet, these concepts find no place in a physical description of the nanoscopic world, where–within a Born-Oppenheimer view–a molecule is ultimately represented by a three-dimensional mathematical function expressing the electron density surrounding a given set of nuclei. While several methods have been proposed over the past decades to define atoms and bonds through the analysis of the molecular electron density, consensus on a theory bridging chemical concepts to the underlying physics has not been reached, and this has corroborated the idea that chemical concepts have an intrinsic degree of vagueness. In this work, we harness the power of Artificial Intelligence to trace the physical roots of chemical concepts–from the simple idea of an atom or a bond, to more elaborate ones such as the particular ‘chemistry’ of an atom in a given molecular context–and assess to what extent these can be framed on a quantitative level. Using simple machinelearning models, we show that a computer can be successfully trained to discern the nuanced chemical character of atoms and bonds from compact representations of the electron density with an accuracy of 98 % and 99 %, respectively. These results indicate that elusive and articulated chemical concepts are actually hard-coded in the underlying physics and suggest that chemistry is less ‘fuzzy’ a science than is generally assumed.

paper.title: Ion Gradients Drive Flooding in Membrane-Electrode Assembly CO2 Electrolyzers
paper.abstract: Low-temperature carbon dioxide electrolysis (CO 2 E) provides a low-carbon-emission pathway to basic chemical products. While anion exchange membrane (AEM)-based CO 2 E can provide high selectivity towards carbon products, runtimes are far below industry requirements. Flooding is a major obstacle to long-term stability as it limits CO 2 access to the catalyst layer, but the reasons for continuous water fluxes to the cathode are poorly understood. Here we present a model-aided experimental analysis of the driving forces for flooding. By tracking high-frequency resistance, anolyte conductivity, and cathode water accumulation over 24-hour runtimes across a range of current densities, temperatures and anolyte concentrations, we reveal AEM ion gradients as the main driving force for both flooding and cation-crowding at the cathode catalyst. We then show how ion gradient management can maintain steady CO selectivity and increase maximum CO 2 E partial current densities, with temperatures acting as a primary factor in reducing ion gradients. Using these insights, we demonstrate stable CO production at 500 mA cm -2 on an ionomer-free Ag catalyst.

paper.title: Engineering a Proton-Regulating Interfacial Microenvironment for Durable RuO2 Electrocatalysis in PEM Water Electrolysis
paper.abstract: Abstract Proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis is a technology for hydrogen production, but its deployment is limited by the cost and durability of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. RuO2 exhibits intrinsic OER activity yet degrades rapidly under high-current-density operation and start–stop cycles. Sluggish interfacial proton dissipation may contribute to this instability by promoting proton accumulation and local acidification. Here, we report an atomic-level microenvironment engineering strategy via aliovalent strontium incorporation into rutile RuO2. Modified RuO2 features a structurally distorted and electronically polarized interface that, according to calculations, alters interfacial water organization and may favor oxygen-end-oriented water configurations near the Sr-modified regions. This modified interfacial environment is associated with alleviated local acidification, facilitated proton-transfer-related processes, suppressed lattice oxygen participation, and favored surface-confined oxygen coupling. Operando characterization in a PEM membrane–electrode assembly further supports dynamic interfacial water reorganization and enhanced proton-transfer kinetics under device-relevant conditions. Modified RuO2 delivers 10 mA cm–2 at 197 mV in acidic electrolyte and, in a PEM electrolyzer, achieves 1 A cm–2 at 1.686 V, operates for over 400 h with Ru dissolution suppressed to 5.79 ng h–1, and withstands 3102 start–stop cycles. These findings support interfacial microenvironment regulation as a strategy for improving the durability of Ru-based acidic OER catalysts.

paper.title: Enerzyme: An Efficient Reactive Neural Network Potential Training Framework for Enzyme Cluster Models with Application to Methyltransferases
paper.abstract: Abstract Quantum mechanical (QM) cluster models provide an effective framework for mechanistic studies of enzymatic reactions but QM calculations remain computationally demanding. Neural network potentials (NNPs) offer a promising route to reduce their cost, but enzymes introduce new challenges not faced by NNPs for small molecules, including large system sizes, the need for inclusion of solvent environments, substantial polarization, and charge transfer. Here, we demonstrate an integrated software framework for efficient training of NNPs for mechanistic study of enzymes, with demonstrations on QM-cluster models of S-adenosyl-l-methionine-dependent methyltransferases (MTases). Our Enerzyme code introduces modular, electrostatics-aware NNP architectures and combines automated QM-cluster construction with reactive dataset generation. The Enerzymette subpackage also automates reaction pathway exploration at both NNP and DFT levels of theory. We show that iterative flexible scans and nudged elastic band calculations impose stricter requirements on NNPs than conventionally employed dataset metrics. Nevertheless, we develop an approach to train NNPs on fewer than 1,000 system-specific data points to reproduce reaction energetics and transition-state structures on MTase clusters containing up to 545 atoms, approaching chemical accuracy with respect to the reference. We show that direct supervision of atomic charges and alignment of dielectric screening with QM-cluster calculations substantially improve simulation stability and accuracy and that multitask-learned atomic charges predict correct charge transfer and polarization trends and provide chemically meaningful descriptors of reactivity. Furthermore, we demonstrate transferability across chemically diverse catechol O-methyltransferase substrates, indicating NNPs learn generalizable reactivity patterns as training data is expanded across multiple enzymes. Together, these results establish a foundation for accelerating enzyme mechanistic studies and provide insights for future NNP development for biomolecular reactivity.

paper.title: A Redox-Switchable Framework Bridges Dilute-Stream CO2 Capture and Conversion
paper.abstract: Abstract Integrating CO2 capture from dilute sources with electrochemical conversion could bypass the energy-intensive separation and regeneration required in conventional carbon capture and utilization. Yet combining these functions, particularly for multicarbon electrosynthesis, remains challenging. Here, we report an ion-regulated conjugated pyridine-imine framework (Cr-PyN) that performs both electrochemical CO2 capture and selective conversion to acetate within a single metal-free molecular platform through potential-dependent molecular reactivity. Reduction activates the pyridine-imine unit for CO2 binding, while Na+ coordination within the crown cavity regulates the interfacial environment and suppresses hydrogen evolution. Cr-PyN captures CO2 directly from simulated flue gas (9.3% CO2, 3% O2) with an electron utilization efficiency of 0.98 and a minimum electrical energy requirement of 39 kJ mol–1 CO2. At more cathodic potentials in an aqueous flow electrolyzer, the same molecular framework selectively produces acetate with 71% Faradaic efficiency at –0.4 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode and remains stable over 120 h. Complementary in situ and ex situ spectroscopic studies, including operando FTIR and NMR, along with DFT calculations, support CO2 binding and subsequent reaction pathways toward multicarbon conversion.

paper.title: A hybrid quantum mechanics machine learning forcefield framework for accurate solute-dislocation interaction simulations
paper.abstract: Abstract Solute–dislocation interactions play a central role in controlling microstructural evolution and mechanical behaviour of structural materials, yet conventional atomistic modelling approaches struggle to combine the chemical accuracy with computational scalability. In the nuclear industry, these challenges become particularly acute, as experiments reveal strong correlations between solute segregation and irradiation-induced dislocation loops. However, theoretical insight remains limited because density functional theory (DFT) simulations are prohibitively expensive at relevant length scales, while traditional semi-empirical interatomic potentials lack the chemical fidelity required for predictive solute–defect calculations. Here, we introduce a hybrid quantum-mechanics/machine-learning (QM/ML) simulation framework that couples DFT with neural-network machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs), enabling DFT-informed atomistic dislocation simulations at reduced computational cost. We demonstrate the QM/ML framework’s capability by reproducing the experimentally observed Sn and Fe segregation to dislocation loops in Zr and investigating magnetically complex solute-dislocation interactions in steel. These results demonstrate the potential of the approach as a transferable framework for modelling irradiation-induced defect structures and benchmarking emerging MLIPs.

paper.title: Evaluation of birnessite-based electrocatalysts for ethylene glycol oxidation to formate: towards biocatalysis and electrocatalysis-based waste plastic upgrading
paper.abstract: Ethylene glycol (EG) electrooxidation provides an alternative anodic reaction to the 20 oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and enables the conversion of EG-containing plastic hydrolysates into value-added products, potentially facilitating downstream product recovery and purification. Its activity and selectivity depend on the surface redox chemistry of the catalyst and competition with OER. Here, Co-, Fe-, Ni-, and NiFe- 2 modified birnessite-derived manganese oxides were prepared by microwave-assisted 25 hydrothermal synthesis and evaluated for EG oxidation in alkaline media. The synthesis conditions affected both the MnOx phase and the metal content of the recovered solids, leading to hetero-structured electrocatalysts. The Ni-modified birnessite, prepared under neutral conditions with relatively high Ni content and a poorly crystalline birnessite-type structure, showed optimized EG oxidation activity for formate 30 production. The applied potential further affected the formate selectivity. At 1.6 V vs RHE, formate Faradaic efficiency reached 93%, while increasing the potential to 1.9 V increased the overall anodic current but reduced Faradaic efficiency. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) identified formate as the major soluble product, while glycolate was detected as an intermediate. 35 This study demonstrated proof-of-concept electro-oxidation of enzyme-catalysisderived EG from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyethylene furanoate (PEF) hydrolysates.

paper.title: The coefficient map, not the basis, limits how machine-learning surrogates of metal–organic framework water-adsorption beds transfer to unseen materials
paper.abstract: Machine-learning surrogates could let designers of metal–organic framework (MOF) water harvesters screen many candidate adsorbents without solving the transport equations for each. A surrogate fails on an unseen material for one of two reasons: its reduced basis cannot represent the true field, or its map from material parameters to basis coefficients predicts the wrong coefficients. Which one limits accuracy decides where method development should go, yet it is rarely measured. We measure it for a one-dimensional, non-isothermal convection–dispersion–adsorption model of a packed bed, verified against 4 closed-form solutions and compared, unfitted, with a published MOF-303 breakthrough curve. Seven explanations of the error were registered in advance, each with the evidence that would eliminate it, and tested on 240 held-out materials in five folds, with a cluster bootstrap that corrects for choosing the best configuration on the test materials. Beyond the first few modes the map, not the basis, limits accuracy: refining the basis 90× changes a per-mode map’s error by 0.9 % and a DeepONet’s by 12 %. More training materials still help (error ∝ N_mat^(-0.222)) and larger models are not ruled out, while Kolmogorov–Arnold networks lose to a same-size perceptron in every comparison by point estimate (exploratory, 12 materials). A physics-residual loss at a small weight improves transfer by 9 % (48 materials); larger weights hurt. Learning beats fitted closed forms 2.44-fold, yet a coarse finite-volume solve is more accurate than the perceptron surrogates (3.1 % normalised error) and cheaper below about 25,400 queries. Effort is better spent on the coefficient map and on training data than on richer bases.

paper.title: Electrostatic preactivation, a missing step in dioxygen activation
paper.abstract: Dioxygen is the oxidant of aerobic life, yet most closed-shell molecules are stable in its presence. 1–4 Conventional accounts of dioxygen activation begin with electron transfer to O 2 , typically from a redox-active metal centre or cofactor. 5–9 Here we show that preparing dioxygen to receive that electron is a separate function, discharged by the electrostatic environment alone, and that the two can be tuned independently. At the equilibrium geometry of neutral O 2 the anion that must receive the electron is unbound; 10,11 a Lewis-acidic field removes this obstacle before any charge moves, a stage we term preactivation . Point charges alone split the O 2 π* manifold and bind the anion at the neutral geometry. Reaction-path calculations show that inner-sphere electron transfer from the Zn–C bond, which generates a superoxide/alkyl-radical pair without metal-centred redox chemistry, is rate-determining. Calibrated on dialkylzincs alone, the in-plane anisotropy of the field gradient, with one term in the charge and distance of the metal resolved within the same series, predicts the π* splitting to within 7% in four enzyme active sites containing iron, copper, nickel or no metal. The electrostatic contribution of an enzyme active site to preactivation can thus be quantified on a scale calibrated with redox-silent organozinc compounds.

paper.title: Molecular Control of Thermal Transport across PEG-Coated Gold–Water Interfaces
paper.abstract: Understanding heat transport across polymer-coated surfaces is important for thermal management and for the design of functional nanomaterials used in technological and biomedical applications. Here, we use nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations to investigate thermal transport across Au(111) surfaces coated with thiolateanchored poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) self-assembled monolayers. By varying the terminal group among OH, NH2, NH + 3 , N(CH3) + 3 , and CH3, we determine how interfacial chemistry modifies the overall Kapitza resistance and the balance of the resistance among the Au–PEG interface, the PEG layer and the PEG–water interface. By resolving the unequal heat currents through the bare and coated sides of the simulation cell, we decompose the coated-side resistance into Au–PEG interfacial, PEG layer, and PEG–water interfacial contributions. The neutral polar and charged terminal groups exhibit similar total thermal resistances (4.2–4.7 K m2 GW−1), whereas the hydrophobic CH3 termination produces a marked increase to ∼ 7 K m2 GW−1, primarily because of the PEG–water interfacial resistance. The thermal transport trends are consistent with differences in interfacial hydration and polymer–water organization, whereas vibrational spectral overlap alone does not provide a sufficient descriptor across the complete terminal group series. Increasing the PEG chain length raises the resistance of the PEG layer, whereas the coverage dependence of the effective Au interfacial resistance is described by a parallel thermal circuit model that combines Au–water and Au–PEG heat transfer contributions. These results identify terminal group chemistry, PEG chain length, and surface coverage as molecular design variables for tuning the thermal resistance of polymer-coated solid–liquid interfaces.

paper.title: Certifying the Kinetics of Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials from Single-Point Energies
paper.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials are validated by force errors on equilibrium configurations, yet activated rates depend on transition regions that equilibrium sampling rarely visits. In a onedimensional metastable double well, the worst-case rate sensitivity to force error grows as eβB/2 with barrier height B; a path-space bound valid at any friction shows that force error certifies rare-event frequencies only to within a factor that grows at the same rate. The leverage density weights energy errors by their influence on reactive transport: it is the normalised dissipation density of the reactive current. For reversible overdamped dynamics, the Dirichlet and Thomson principles give two-sided capacity bounds, converted to metastable rate bounds by basin population corrections. A path representation evaluates their averages from reactive trajectories, committor values and single-point energies. Sampling uses reference paths to assess sampled transitions and model paths to expose additional or overpopulated pathways. In alanine dipeptide, closely matched force errors produce rate changes from 0.49 to 3.5, consistent with estimated intervals. In Li3OCl, mechanism-resolved upper endpoints track six models’ vacancy-hop rates with a systematic underestimation of about 7%. Labels selected from both ensembles improve kinetics even as force errors rise. We propose reporting the energy-error contrast M between the leverage density and the basins, and the spread σν under the leverage density, alongside force error; both are independent of the energy zero.

paper.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
paper.abstract: Abstract Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode–skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.
