paper.title: Gas-Conditioned Message Passing Graph Neural Network for Permeability Prediction in Polymeric Membranes
paper.abstract: Designing polymeric membranes for diverse gas-separation applications remains a critical challenge. Machine learning (ML) models can significantly accelerate this effort by capturing complex relationships between polymer-gas pairs and enabling permeability prediction over an extended chemical space of gases and polymers. In this work, we present a novel ML framework, the gas-conditioned message passing neural network (GC-MPNN), that jointly combines gas descriptors and polymer chemistry in a fused neural network model. Polymers are represented at the monomer level and encoded as molecular graphs, where node and edge information is propagated through message-passing layers. Six gas species (He, H2, N2, O2, CH4, and CO2) are represented using multiple descriptor sets spanning thermodynamic, kinetic, and electrostatic properties, along with one-hot encodings and combined feature sets that include kinetic plus thermodynamic descriptors and the full physicochemical descriptor set. For each descriptor combination, model hyperparameters are optimized using Bayesian optimization within a leave-one-gas-out (LOGO) validation framework. Test performance is then evaluated on the gas species excluded entirely from the corresponding training fold (out-of-training set) and compared across descriptor sets. For most gas species, the model achieves strong predictive performance (R2 ∼ 0.86–0.96), while CO2 remains more challenging in terms of absolute prediction accuracy (R2 ∼ 0.44). Active learning sampling further improves model performance by adding a few labeled samples from the test gas species into the training set. Among the three strategies tested, deep ensemble-based sampling and random sampling show strong improvement, with R2 reaching approximately ∼ 0.95 for all gas species, while evidential regression shows less consistent improvement. The model is further evaluated on a smaller polymer-gas dataset containing hydrocarbon species (C2H4, C2H6, C3H6, C3H8, and n-C4H10) using the GC-MPNN trained only on the six base gases, achieving moderate to strong Pearson correlations (r ∼ 0.77–0.89) for these out-of-training gases. Overall, this work presents a machine learning model that can learn transferable polymer-gas relationships from known gas species and extend them to previously unseen gases.

paper.title: Absorption and Emission Spectra in Aqueous Solution with Coupled-Cluster Accuracy
paper.abstract: Quantitative prediction of electronic spectra in water requires an accurate treatment of electronic excitation, nuclear structure, and state-specific solvation including effects from hydrogen bonding. Here, photoacids and photobases in aqueous solution are used as stringent test systems for statespecific embedded cluster reference interaction site model calculations combined with the iterative coupled cluster models CC2 and CC3. Wigner nuclear-ensemble and adiabatic Hessian Franck-Condon calculations reproduce absorption and emission band maxima on an absolute energy scale with typical errors of 0.1–0.2 eV without empirical shift or scaling corrections; the energies of resolved 0–0 transitions in photobases are even reproduced within a few hundredths of an eV. The simulations also resolve contributions from different excited states and changes in the emitting species. Derived excited-state acidity changes, ∆pK∗ a , show similar accuracy for photoacids and photobases, with residual errors governed by cancellation or accumulation between protonation states.

paper.title: Intermolecular Interactions, Proton Transfer, and Adatom Rearrangement during Cysteine Dimer Adsorption on Au(111)
paper.abstract: On nanostructured gold, the binding site of a cysteine dimer can move as it adsorbs. The consequences for intermolecular interactions, proton transfer, and the structure of the surface remain unclear. Here, we investigate cysteine dimers on Au(111) substrates with different adatom arrangements using density functional theory optimizations and Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics. The resulting trajectories show that adsorption can bring separated adatoms together into compact or extended structures, while other configurations split an existing adatom pair. These outcomes vary with the initial cysteine motif and intermolecular orientation. Deprotonated mercapto groups in thiolate and unconventional zwitterionic motifs bind directly to adatoms, whereas neutral thiols interact more with the underlying surface and can undergo proton transfer near the defects. paper.title: Tailoring Backbone Angles of Regioisomeric Covalent Organic Frameworks: Distinct O 2 Adsorption Modes Enabling Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) possess periodic skeletons and well‐defined catalytic sites, allowing precise molecular‐level regulation of interfacial properties in electrocatalytic oxygen reduction. However, conventional structural modifications fail to systematically tune oxygen adsorption geometry and interfacial electronic coupling. Here, we report a linkage‐angle engineering strategy that alters the bonding positions of reactive aldehyde groups to fabricate three regioisomeric COFs with predefined backbone dihedral angles of 180°, 120°, and 60°. The angle‑driven regioisomeric effect induces considerable differences in dipole moments together with uneven charge distribution. These collective structural features remodel oxygen‑surface interactions and modulate the intrinsic catalytic kinetics. Theoretical calculations confirm that the compact 60° framework of o ‐TPDA‐COF reconstructs confined pore interfacial microenvironments. Unlike the Griffiths‑type oxygen adsorption favored in its angular analogues, molecular oxygen preferentially adopts the Pauling configuration within o ‐TPDA‐COF to stabilize OOH* intermediates. Consequently, the optimal o ‐TPDA‐COF reaches an excellent H 2 O 2 productivity of 12.82 mol g cat −1 h −1 and a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 91.64%. This work realizes controllable modulation of oxygen‑adsorption behaviors in COF‑based 2e – oxygen reduction, delivering a novel geometry‑oriented design paradigm for porous electrocatalytic frameworks.

paper.title: Controlled Presodiation of Sodium‐Ion Cathode via Electron Cloud Engineering
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical presodiation offers a promising pathway to compensate sodium deficiency in cathode and anode materials, thereby enhancing the usable energy density of sodium‐ion batteries. This approach is particularly critical for P2‐ and tunnel‐type cathodes, such as Na 0.44 MnO 2 , where the as‐synthesized materials typically exhibit a 50%–60% sodium deficiency. However, conventional presodiation reagents possess excessively high reductive potential, often leading to oversodiation, structural degradation, and compromised electrode reversibility. Here, we report a rational electron‐cloud engineering strategy to precisely control the sodium chemical potential of presodiation agents. Guided by Hückel's rule, we demonstrate that tailoring π‐conjugation size and introducing electron‐withdrawing groups enables the adjustment of sodium chemical potential via a balance of conjugative and inductive effects. We identify 1‐indanone as an optimal presodiation reagent, capable of delivering sodium to Na 0.44 MnO 2 cathodes without any oversodiation. The resulting electrodes exhibit fully restored sodium inventories, an unprecedented first‐cycle Coulombic efficiency of ∼100%, and improved capacity retention over 350 cycles compared to untreated controls. Our findings establish a versatile framework for controlling sodium delivery in chemical presodiation, providing a new avenue for the design of next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries with enhanced stability and performance.

paper.title: Site-selective Halogenation of Aromatic C-H Bonds via Electrocatalytic Flavin Adenine Dinucleotide Cofactor Regeneration
paper.abstract: Flavin-dependent halogenases (FDHs) catalyze site-selective C–H halogenation of electron-rich aromatic compounds but rely on multienzyme cofactor-recycling systems to continuously supply reduced flavin (FADH 2 ). Here, we establish an overpotential-driven, mediator-assisted bioelectrocatalytic strategy for FADH 2 regeneration that eliminates auxiliary reductases, nicotinamide cofactors, and enzyme immobilization. Cyclic voltammetry confirmed the proton-dependent FAD/FADH 2 redox couple (-0.42 V vs Ag/AgCl, 3.5 M KCl) and the competing oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Bulk electrolysis involving the FDH RebH revealed that L-ascorbic acid suppresses ORR-derived species more effectively than conventional catalase/glutathione/superoxide-dismutase systems, increasing conversion of tryptophan to 7-bromotryptophan from 20% to 46% after 24 h at -0.7 V. Increasing the cathodic potential to -1.1 V improved yields to 64% without substantially improving the faradaic efficiency (FE~ 5%). Introducing redox mediators such as 2-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone (HNQ) and methyl viologen (MV 2+ ) enabled the HNQ/FAD pair to achieve quantitative halogenation within 10 h (FE ~ 14%) and the MV 2+ /FAD pair within 12 h (FE ~ 9%), enabling production of 8.8 mg of 7-bromotryptophan in a scale-up reactor. Moreover, the HNQ/FAD system exhibited a kinetic isotope effect (KIE) of ( k H / k D = 1.8) for product formation in H 2 O versus D 2 O, supporting proton involvement in productive FAD regeneration and potentially reflecting cooperation between mediator-assisted electron transfer and surface-adsorbed hydrogen (H ads ) produced during the hydrogen evolution reaction in accelerating FADH 2 formation. Extending this method to engineered RebH variant 4-V enabled halogenation of larger substrates, establishing a scalable electrochemical platform for FDH catalysis. These results establish how electron delivery, proton availability, and competing oxygen reduction govern productive electrochemical flavin regeneration and provide a scalable platform for FDH catalysis.

paper.title: AutoSolvate 2.0: Automated Preparation of Chemically Diverse Explicit-Solvent Systems for Multiscale Molecular Simulation
paper.abstract: Advanced quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM), machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), and hybrid methods provide powerful engines for modeling solution-phase chemistry. Yet before production begins, chemically diverse explicit-solvent systems must be parameterized, assembled at the desired composition, relaxed, equilibrated, and sampled. This preparatory “first mile” remains labor-intensive, requiring multiple software packages and manual customization, particularly for transition-metal complexes, solvent mixtures, and multicomponent electrolytes. Here, we present AutoSolvate 2.0, a modular, open-source framework that converts molecular structures and solution compositions into equilibrated, simulation-ready explicit-solvent ensembles. The new AutoMCPB module automates Metal Center Parameter Builder (MCPB.py)-based parameterization of transition-metal complexes (TMCs), while generalized system representations support multiple solutes and solvents at arbitrary molar, weight, or volume ratios. Standardized wrappers integrate force-field generation, box construction, minimization, heating, equilibration, classical sampling, and microsolvated-cluster extraction. Native classical molecular dynamics (MD) and TeraChem-based QM/MM workflows execute directly; equilibrated coordinates, velocities, trajectories, and clusters provide starting points for external quantum mechanical (QM), other QM/MM, MLIP training, and hybrid machine learning (ML)/classical workflows. JSON, guided command-line, and Model Context Protocol interfaces support high-throughput and agent-assisted use. We demonstrate these capabilities by reproducing the solvent-dependent absorption spectrum of an aqueous transition-metal photosensitizer, the composition-dependent microsolvation of water–acetonitrile mixtures, and characteristic ion-pairing features of a published multicomponent electrolyte simulation. Together, these applications establish AutoSolvate 2.0 as a preparation and initial-sampling layer connecting chemical system specification to classical, quantum, and machine-learning simulations. Rather than competing with higher-accuracy methods, AutoSolvate provides the on-ramp needed to apply them efficiently to complex explicit-solvent systems.

paper.title: Fully Automated System for Exploring Molecular Dynamics Trajectories
paper.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) studies often require separate tools for system preparation, simulation, enhanced sampling, analysis, and reporting, creating opportunities for inconsistent settings and undocumented decisions. We present FastMDXplora, an open-source Python framework built on OpenMM that integrates setup, simulation, analysis, and report phases through a single declarative configuration. A shared schema supports command-line and browser-based graphical interfaces. An optional artificial intelligence (AI) agent generates study configurations from natural-language descriptions, subject to the same validation as user-defined configurations. Each phase records its resolved settings, software versions, and execution environment. When a requested result lacks sufficient support, the software withholds it and reports the reason through a registry of 111 typed refusal codes. Fifteen estimator tests recover analytical benchmarks, including statistical inefficiencies within 2 % of reference values and WHAM reconstruction of analytical free-energy profiles from synthetic umbrella-sampling data with root-mean-square errors below 0.1 kJ mol−1. A labeled corpus of 25 defective and 26 clean studies produces the expected outcomes in all 51 cases. Calibration against ten replicas shows that singlerun standard errors at 20 ns can be up to tenfold smaller than replica-based estimates, even when the estimated correlation time is resolved. The software withholds standard errors when its correlation diagnostics fail, but passing these diagnostics does not establish calibrated uncertainty. In a trypsin–benzamidine case study, interaction analysis reveals differences in the engagement of Asp189 between two ligand charge states that are not distinguished by total contact counts. FastMDXplora provides an integrated framework for reproducible MD studies, combining workflow automation with explicit validation and provenance while preserving the need for independent assessment of sampling and uncertainty. The source code is available at https://github.com/aai-research-lab/FastMDXplora.

paper.title: Proximity‐Engineered Dual‐Atomic Cobalt Sites Enable Adaptive Spin Catalysis for Simultaneous Oxygen and Peroxide Reduction
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Breaking the intrinsic adsorption conflicts among oxygen intermediates remains a central challenge in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) electrocatalysis. Although spin‐state engineering offers an effective strategy for tuning catalytic activity, conventional approaches generally focus on a single‐spin configuration, which cannot simultaneously satisfy the distinct energetic requirements of different ORR intermediates. Here, we introduce an adaptive spin catalysis concept through proximity engineering of dual‐atomic Co sites confined within a one‐dimensional covalent organic framework. Precisely regulating the Co–Co separation while preserving the local coordination environment induces inter‐site electronic coupling, giving rise to coexisting high‐spin and low‐spin Co configurations. Combined spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations support a mechanistic framework in which these coexisting spin configurations provide complementary catalytic functions for distinct intermediates along the multistep ORR pathway, thereby alleviating adsorption conflicts. Consequently, the proximity‐engineered catalyst delivers outstanding ORR activity with a half‐wave potential of 0.96 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, outperforming both its spatially separated counterpart and commercial Pt/C. The catalyst also efficiently mediates both O 2 and H 2 O 2 reduction while suppressing peroxide decomposition, enabling enhanced performance in rechargeable zinc–air batteries and peroxide‐assisted aluminum–air batteries. This work establishes a molecular framework for exploiting spin‐state complementarity in atomic catalysts for advanced energy‐conversion reactions.

paper.title: Cerium Valence‐Gated Interfacial Exciton Reconstruction for Fluorescence Modulation
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial electronic coupling plays a decisive role in governing excited‐state evolution and signal transduction in optoelectronic systems, yet dynamically adaptive interfaces driven by valence‐state evolution remain largely unexplored in fluorescent sensing platforms. Herein, an Eu‐functionalized Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface is constructed to establish a valence‐responsive optoelectronic system for dual‐mode H 2 O 2 sensing. Upon oxidative stimulation, the Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface dynamically reconstructs the interfacial charge‐transfer network through Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ valence‐state evolution, enabling modulation of electron migration across the interface and synchronously regulating Eu‐centered luminescence, CTF‐derived fluorescence, and nanozyme‐mediated catalytic outputs. The results reveal that oxidative valence evolution induces adaptive interfacial electronic redistribution and excited‐state pathway reconstruction, thereby amplifying microscopic electronic perturbations into programmable fluorescence–catalytic responses. Beyond conventional sensing systems dominated by static emissive centers, this work demonstrates that adaptive interface states can function as dynamic optoelectronic units for intelligent signal transduction. Furthermore, the interfacial optical response can be integrated into flexible electrospun membranes and machine‐learning‐assisted visual recognition systems, enabling portable dual‐mode visual sensing. This work provides a new perspective for constructing adaptive optoelectronic interfaces through valence‐state engineering and establishes a general framework for next‐generation intelligent sensing platforms.

paper.title: Realising a Poschenrieder dual-sector electrostatic analyser for charge-detection mass spectrometry
paper.abstract: Megadalton biomolecular assemblies, including viral vectors, synthetic nanoparticles and protein aggregates, are increasingly important chemical and therapeutic entities, yet their heterogeneity often exceeds the resolving power and space charge tolerance of conventional mass spectrometry. To overcome these limitations, here we report the first realisation of a Poschenrieder dual-sector electrostatic analyser as a charge-detection mass spectrometer. The instrument traps individual ions in a continuous closed trajectory between two spherical electrostatic sectors, enabling induced-current detection over extended transients without end-cap deceleration. Coupled to a high-mass ion-transfer interface, the analyser supports both ensemble m/z measurements and single-particle charge detection of large biomolecular ions. We validate the platform using protein standards and demonstrate megadalton mass analysis of adeno-associated virus capsids, distinguishing empty and genome-containing populations in agreement with orthogonal mass photometry and Orbitrap-based measurements. Although charge-detection noise remains the principal performance constraint in this first-generation prototype, the dual-sector architecture offers a simple, high-capacity route to charge-detection mass spectrometry with substantial scope for improved resolution through miniaturisation and reduced detector capacitance.

paper.title: Two extrapolation axes for many-body systems: interaction without an interaction module, chemical mixtures as the main example
paper.abstract: We separate the extrapolation problem in many-body systems into two axes: toward combinations with more components, and toward components unseen. The prevailing pipeline—encode then interact—performs poorly when extrapolating in composition count. We propose a route that expresses interaction without an interaction module: a per-component encoder shaped by the task compresses interaction behaviour into each component’s encoding, and the encodings are combined and read out by a simple MLP. Where component identities are bounded while their combinations are not, this route performs better along the composition axis—a difference that follows from the underlying function form rather than from the data. Chemical mixtures are the main example, synthetic tasks isolate the two axes, and the same structure recurs in other fields.

paper.title: Charge‐Delocalizing sp‐Hybridized COFs for Selective H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is an important oxidant for chemical manufacturing, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications, yet its industrial production still relies mainly on the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Electrochemical H 2 O 2 synthesis via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) provides a sustainable alternative but is often hindered by sluggish charge transport and insufficient O 2 activation. Here, we develop a bond‐hybridization strategy by incorporating sp‐hybridized acetylene units into the vertex or linker of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). The resulting COFs feature extended π‐conjugation, enhanced charge delocalization, and electronically polarized pores, thereby strengthening O 2 adsorption and activation. Compared with sp 2 ‐dominated analogues, these sp‐hybridized COFs show faster charge‐transfer kinetics, higher H 2 O 2 selectivity, and improved 2e − ORR activity. In a flow cell, the optimized catalyst delivers an H 2 O 2 production rate of 27.8 mol g −1 h −1 and a peak Faradaic efficiency of 91.7% at 150 mA cm −2 . Mechanistic analyses combining electronic‐structure calculations and in situ vibrational spectroscopy reveal that sp hybridization reshapes frontier‐orbital distributions and local charge density, thereby coupling framework‐wide charge delocalization with favorable O 2 adsorption and *OOH stabilization. These results establish bond hybridization as a molecular‐level design parameter for catalytic selectivity in COFs, extending framework engineering beyond conventional functional‐group and building‐block modification.

paper.title: d -Electron Descriptors for Nitrate Reduction Reaction Activity in Co-Based Heusler Phase Electrocatalysts
paper.abstract: Abstract The tunability of electronic structure in intermetallics opens the door to systematic studies in catalysis. Here, we experimentally investigate various descriptors for the electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction using 9 Heusler phases as catalysts (Co2VSn, Co2MnAl, Co2MnGe, Co2MnSn, Co2FeGe, Co2MnSb, Ni2MnSn, Co2FeSi, and Co2FeAl). In contrast to previous studies with Co-based Heusler phases and oxide perovskites for OER, we find that generally, the total valence electron count, rather than eg filling, provides a better prediction of the activity. However, with period 5 Y elements, such as Sn and Sb, at high valence electron counts, Y-site d-band centers must also be considered. Reaction mechanism analysis by DFT also clarifies the role of X/Y sites. Hence, a single descriptor alone is not sufficient to rationalize catalytic activity across the full spectrum of Heusler phase compositions. So far, valence electron control has relied on single metal or binary alloy compositions for nitrate reduction; however, these Heusler phases help decouple the element identity and valence count while also serving as a guide for more catalysts based on ternary intermetallics. This work thus establishes multi-descriptor guidance for a wide group of catalyst compositions that were previously relatively unexplored.

paper.title: Imitation and Accuracy in Automated Electronic-Structure Method Selection
Intermediate Precision of Single-Molecule Break-Junction Conductance: Measurement, Uncertainty Budget, and Design Rules
paper.abstract: A break-junction experiment records thousands of single-molecule junctions in one session and reports a feature of their conductance histogram as the molecule’s conductance, with an uncertainty from resampling the traces. That is a withinsession sampling figure; how far the value moves between sessions is not measured or budgeted. We measure it in ISO 5725 and GUM form on archived STM-BJ recordings of DNA:RNA hybrid duplexes with repeat sessions at identical settings. On seven single-duplex groups, each two sessions from different recording rounds or dates, the intermediate-precision standard deviation of a session’s median is a factor of 1.46 (95% interval 1.28 to 2.15). Read in recording order, the median also wanders within a session with a correlation length near a hundred traces, so resampling understates the within-session uncertainty about threefold; counted consistently, the between-session term holds 74% of a single-session variance budget, and on records of this length it cannot be separated from slow drift. Five candidate remedies, tested under pre-registration, do not remove it. The expanded uncertainty of a single-session value, a lower bound that excludes calibration terms, is a factor of 2.4; spreading a fixed number of traces over more sessions reduces it, and a design rule gives the sessions a comparison needs. Public deposits from a second laboratory show a between-occasion component and the same within-session dependence. The figures are specific to the system; the method is not.

paper.title: How single-atom catalysis transformed from a nanoscience curiosity into a new paradigm for heterogeneous catalysis
paper.abstract: Single-atom catalysis has reshaped heterogeneous catalysis by shifting its central focus from surface and interface to isolated atom-centred active sites. This transition establishes a new paradigm for understanding reactivity, integrating experiments and theory, and advancing heterogeneous catalysis from empirical observations toward a more predictive and precise science.

paper.title: Mixed‐Valence Dimeric Olympicenyl Radical Cation With Improved Electrical Conductivity
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT p‐Type doping is an effective strategy for modulating molecular packing arrangement of organic compounds, thus improving their electrical conductivity. In this work, the first example of a mixed‐valence radical cation dimer based on an odd alternant hydrocarbon, [OR5] 2 +• [FeCl 4 ] − (OR5‐MV), was successfully prepared by the oxidation of olympicenyl radical (OR) derivative OR5 using FeCl 3 . X‐ray crystallographic analysis revealed that cation‐radical dimer [OR5] 2 +• , acting as a fundamental building block, forms [OR5] 4 2+ tetramer via a multi‐center–two‐electron bond, which further aggregates into a one‐dimensional chain in the solid state. SQUID measurement reveals that the magnetic susceptibility is dominated by the FeCl 4 – anions with no detectable OR5 moiety contribution. Theoretical calculations disclosed an open‐shell singlet ground state for [OR5] 4 2+ tetramer and demonstrated that the pancake‐bond formation between OR5 cation‐radical dimers confers significant energetic stabilization. Compared to the neutral compound, more uniform molecular packing and reduced intermolecular distance in the one‐dimensional columnar architecture of OR5‐MV facilitate effective intermolecular orbital overlap, leading to broader band dispersion along the molecular stacking direction. A substantially improved electrical conductivity of up to 10 − 3 S cm − 1 is achieved compared to neutral radical (10 − 9 S cm − 1 ), representing the highest value reported for monomeric odd alternant hydrocarbons.

paper.title: Resination-Assembled Soft Multiaxial Molecular Ferroelectrics Enable Exceptional Low-Electric Field Polarization Switching
paper.abstract: Abstract Resination of soft polymer ferroelectrics has recently emerged as a promising avenue to assemble high- performance electroactive materials, due to the coupling of ferroelectricity with enhanced mechanical and processable merits. However, it remains a huge challenge to stabilize ferroelectricity and dipolar activity at the resin–ferroelectric interface. For the first time, we adopt here the resination assembling strategy into the soft molecule-based ferroelectric (BZA)2(DMA)BiI6 (1, BZA = benzylammonium; DMA = dimethylammonium), which enables the unusual ferroelectric behavior of low-electric field switching of polarization. Compound 1 is a high-temperature multiaxial ferroelectric with six possible equivalent polarization directions and a low coercive electric field, arising from its stepwise phase transitions around 350 K (Tc). Strikingly, the precise resination of 1 with the epoxy-matrix composite yields a highly loaded composite with a microscopic cross-linked structure, whose polarization can be switched under a quite low coercive electric field (Ec ∼ 3.8 kV/cm). These shape-customized ferroelectric resin wafers of 1 have superior antielectric fatigue attributes after ∼104 cycles. Moreover, these wafers exhibit enhanced resistance to localized deformation, evidenced by a 30.9% decrease in maximum penetration depth relative to the bulk single crystals. As the first study on the resination of molecular ferroelectrics, our findings bridge the gap between molecular ferroelectrics and material engineering, which highlights the application potential of resinated molecular ferroelectrics.

paper.title: LLMs predict material properties based on atom types and not atom positions
paper.abstract: Accurately predicting properties of materials is one of the main challenges in computational materials science. Systematic experiments now show that large language models (LLMs) struggle to use positional information for the prediction of those properties. This limitation does not reverse as model or dataset sizes grow.

paper.title: Migratory Hydroamination of Alkenes via Iron-Hydride Catalysis
paper.abstract: Abstract The renaissance of catalytic metal hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT) offers advanced tools for hydroamination of alkenes. Despite these merits, state-of-the-art MHAT hydroamination protocols are largely limited to intermolecular coupling or intramolecular cyclization, thereby necessitating new catalytic platforms to explore MHAT reactivity and access unexplored hydroamination reaction pathways. Herein, we report an iron hydride-catalyzed migratory hydroamination of allylamines, enabled by a sequential MHAT process with finely tuned 1,2-amino migration. This strategy converts readily accessible allylamines into structurally diverse alkylamines and β-amino acids through a three-step radical cascade. This protocol features a broad tolerance toward a range of functional groups, encompassing complex drug and natural product derivatives. Beyond providing an efficient approach to medicinally relevant amine scaffolds, this work establishes a new paradigm for MHAT-enabled molecular editing through radical functional group migration, thereby expanding the synthetic repertoire of alkene hydroamination.

paper.title: Selective Formyl Deuteration of Aldehydes by Surface-Enriched Oxygen Vacancy Stabilized Pt on Ceria
paper.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) is a widely used methodology for deuteration; however, achieving both high isotope abundance and site-selectivity remains challenging for heterogeneous catalysts. Herein, we present a ceria supported platinum catalyst with surface-enriched oxygen vacancy (Ov) that shows impressive formyl deuteration performance with deuterium oxide (D2O) as the deuterium source under hydrogen-free conditions. Using p-methylbenzaldehyde as a model substrate, the typical catalyst achieves >95% deuterium incorporation (D-inc.) at the formyl position while effectively suppressing undesired reductive deuteration pathway. Experimental and theoretical results suggest that the surface-enriched Ov promotes the preferential adsorption of formyl groups on undercoordinated Ce sites, where the local charge redistribution renders the formyl-protons electron-deficient. Simultaneously, the anchored Pt centers effectively catalyze D2O dissociation, generating abundant D* and OD* species. These deuterium species readily interact with the electron-deficient formyl groups, driving hydrogen isotope exchange and forming deuterated aldehydes with high D-formyl selectivity. Substrate scope exploration and gram-scale continuous-flow deuteration experiments demonstrate broad compatibility, revealing its great potential for the selective synthesis of deuterated aldehydes.

paper.title: Algorithmic construction and exploitation of topology-constrained refinement models for semiexperimental equilibrium structures
paper.abstract: Semiexperimental equilibrium structures combine high-resolution rotational spectroscopy with computed vibrational and electronic corrections. Although the least-squares solution is well established, constructing the inverse model still requires expert choices of coordinates, symmetry, constraints, and parameter classes. We introduce MORPHEUS (Model Optimization and Refinement from Perceived Hierarchy, Equivalence, Uncertainty, and Symmetry), a reproducible framework that makes these choices explicit and tests them against topology, symmetry, rank, isotope coverage, and external reference information. Starting from Cartesian geometry, it builds non-redundant internal coordinates and a refinement model before fitting. Two alternative active spaces are supported: symmetry-adapted generalized internal coordinates and symmetry-adapted Cartesian displacements with translations and rotations removed. Across acyclic, cyclic, planar, fused, bridged, and flexible molecules, the workflow recovers effective dimensions, residuals, structural parameters, and uncertainties without manual construction of the active coordinate model. In camphor, the chemically validated model gives sub-milliangstrom bond corrections and remains stable under basis changes, robust losses, predicate-width scans, and multi-starts. A 49-atom testosterone demonstration shows how QC geometries, accelerated vibrational corrections, and class-constrained refinement models can be combined when isotope-rich data are unavailable.

paper.title: Selective, Catalytic Oxidation of Polyethylene Surfaces
paper.abstract: Polyethylene (PE) accounts for more than a quarter of all plastic produced, owing to its exceptional material properties and scalable production.1 However, pristine PE lacks critical properties, such as adhesion, that are needed for many additional commercial applications.2 Selective post-polymerization functionalization of PE can impart properties that are absent in the pristine polymer, but global functionalization in a uniform medium perturbs bulk properties.3–5 Here, we demonstrate catalytic functionalization of solid PE at a solid–liquid interface. The resulting materials possess enhanced surface properties while maintaining bulk properties, such as melting temperature or tensile strength. The method selectively converts methylene units to ketones with just 0.001 mol% iron catalyst below 80 °C with inexpensive oxidants. PE functionalized at the solid–liquid interface adheres to polar surfaces up to 90-fold more strongly than does pristine PE and up to 4-fold more strongly than does PE functionalized in a uniform medium at a comparable level. We demonstrate that the surface ketones can be modified to enhance adhesive strength further and that the augmented surface properties persist for longer than they do after other unselective functionalizations. Thus, selective C–H bond functionalization at the solid–liquid interface produces materials inaccessible by bulk functionalization methods or by traditional surface oxidations.

paper.title: Enhanced Aqueous-Phase Hydrodeoxygenation of Fatty Acids over CoP Anchored on P–N Co-Doped Carbon
paper.abstract: Abstract The aqueous-phase hydrodeoxygenation of biomass-derived fatty acids offers an alternative route for the production of diesel-range hydrocarbons, but remains a major challenge. Herein, we report a hydrophobic CoP catalyst anchored on P–N co-doped carbon spheres (CoP@PNC-900), which exhibits high performance for the aqueous-phase hydrodeoxygenation of palmitic acid at 270 °C and 2 MPa H2, delivering nearly complete conversion together with over 99% yield of C15+C16 alkanes. The enhanced performance arises from the synergy between CoP active sites and the hydrophobic interface, which promotes C–O bond cleavage while enhancing the contact between hydrophobic substrates and catalytic sites. Isotopic-labeling experiments demonstrate that water acts exclusively as the reaction medium rather than a hydrogen source. In situ FT-IR–MS analysis combined with DFT calculations confirms the hydrodeoxygenation- and decarbonylation-related pathways, with C–O bond cleavage of the alcohol intermediate identified as the rate-determining step in the hydrodeoxygenation pathway. Moreover, the catalyst exhibits a broad substrate scope for various fatty acids and esters as well as stable recyclability under hydrothermal conditions. Finally, a preliminary life cycle assessment (LCA) highlights the potential environmental benefits of the aqueous-phase catalytic process. This work establishes an effective strategy that integrates active-site engineering with interfacial hydrophobic microenvironment regulation for the aqueous-phase valorization of biomass-derived fatty acids.

paper.title: Local Structure and Dynamics of Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
paper.abstract: Abstract Resolving and controlling the local dynamical properties of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains a central challenge, particularly when assembled from large, flexible building units. Here, we combine synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function (PDF) analyses with machine learning-accelerated molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to resolve the local structure and dynamics of two three-dimensional imine-linked COFs, COF-682 [(DHP)(TAM)]imine, assembled from 6,13-dihydropentacene (DHP) and tetrakis(4-aminophenyl)methane (TAM), and COF-612 [(HBC-LA12)(HAPT)2]imine, assembled from nanographene dodecabenzaldehyde hexakis[3,5-bis(p-formylphenyl)-4,6-dimethoxyphenyl]hexabenzocoronene (HBC-LA12) and 2,3,6,7,14,15-hexa(4-aminophenyl)triptycene (HAPT). Validated against the experimental PDFs through ensemble-averaged calculations, the simulations show that the exposed π-surface and V-shaped geometry of the DHP linker endow COF-682 with enhanced local flexibility through face-to-face and offset π-stacking interactions differing in both their average interplanar separation and their ring-plane tilt angle. In contrast, the extended nanographene linker rigidifies COF-612 by maintaining the planarity of its fused cores, while the linker pendant aryl rings equip both COFs with enhanced librational ability. The simulations further provide quantitative measures of the translational and reorientational mobility of the linkers, revealing how local COF dynamics may be tuned by balancing noncovalent interactions and different degrees of aromatic rigidity. The PDF-MD experimental-computational approach holds promise as a general method beyond conventional crystallography to gain insights into the local properties of COFs with the aim of directing their dynamic function.

paper.title: Magnetic‐Field‐Assisted Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production From Ambient Air via Spin‐Matching‐Mediated Dual Charge Transfer
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis from ambient air is promising but constrained by spin‐forbidden O 2 activation, unidirectional charge injection, and inefficient O 2 mass transport. We introduce a spin‐matching‐enabled dual‐channel cooperative charge delocalization strategy based on a Fe ions and an N,N′‐di(4‐benzoic acid)‐3,4,9,10‐tetracarboxylic acid diimide ligand (Fe‐PDI). The polymer contains mixed‐valence Fe(II)/Fe(III) sites and adopts an intermediate‐spin configuration with a singly occupied axial d z 2 orbital. Experimental and computational results support a dual‐channel Fe–O 2 interaction involving O 2 ‐to‐Fe σ donation and Fe‐to‐O 2 π back‐donation with spin‐aligned electrons filling the O 2 antibonding orbitals, which converts conventional localized unidirectional injection into bidirectional cooperative delocalization. This interaction alleviates spin‐forbidden O 2 activation through a spin‐correlated •O 2 − intermediate while preserving the O─O bond, promotes selective protonation to *OOH, and enhances O 2 surface diffusion and H 2 O 2 desorption. Consequently, with benzylamine as a hole scavenger, Fe‐PDI achieves H 2 O 2 production rates of 19.17 and 23.26 mmol g −1 h −1 without and with an applied magnetic field, respectively, surpassing most reported photocatalytic systems. This work establishes a spin‐charge‐transport synergistic paradigm, offering a generalizable route for spin‐state engineering in single‐site catalysis.

paper.title: ACAT1/SOAT1 governs mitochondrial dynamics and thermogenesis via the mTOR-MFN2-USP2 axis in brown adipocytes
paper.abstract: Mitochondrial dynamics are crucial for brown adipose tissue (BAT) thermogenesis and systemic energy homeostasis; yet, the cholesterol-sensing pathways regulating these processes remain poorly defined. Here we report that ACAT1, an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident cholesterol esterase, acts as a critical rheostat of thermogenesis by governing mitochondrial dynamics in BAT. Mice with brown adipocyte-specific Acat1 deletion exhibit cold intolerance and exacerbated Western diet-induced obesity. Mechanistically, ACAT1 inhibition triggers intracellular cholesterol accu7mulation that activates mTOR-mediated phosphorylation of the mitochondrial fusion protein MFN2 at Serine 200. This modification recruits the deubiquitinase USP2, stabilizing MFN2 by inhibiting its proteasomal degradation and driving pathological mitochondrial fusion and ER-mitochondria contacts. Hence, our findings establish the ACAT1-mTOR-MFN2-USP2 axis as a fundamental mechanism coordinating cholesterol metabolism with mitochondrial dynamics, thermogenesis, and systemic energy balance, revealing its critical pathophysiological significance in obesity. Cholesterol levels must be precisely controlled in cells. Here, the authors identify the mTOR-MFN2-USP2 axis linking ACAT1-mediated cholesterol metabolism to mitochondrial homeostasis, critical for brown-fat thermogenesis and whole-body metabolism.

paper.title: Everyday adaptation in a gilded trap: Risk-taking and resilience in Maine’s lobster fishery
paper.abstract: Flexibility is widely regarded as an enabling factor of adaptive capacity among natural resource users. Yet, as ecological systems around the world become increasingly simplified and social environments reduce diversification options, flexibility is becoming limited. Despite this trend, efforts to study how people adapt within the confines of constrained social–ecological systems have been sparse. Here, we broaden the analysis of resilience through a study of the American lobster fishery in Maine, United States, one of the most valuable fisheries in the world. Drawing on 307,000 observations from 3,515 harvesters over a 13-y period (2010–2022), we used a generalized linear mixed-effects model to analyze how sociodemographic characteristics, economic conditions, and time shape the probability of fishing during poor weather conditions, which we define as high-risk. We find demographic and socioeconomic heterogeneity in risk-taking: Men, mid-career harvesters, and captains of larger businesses were more likely to fish in risky conditions, and both low landings and high catch prices increased risk-taking. Contrary to our prediction, however, we observed an overall decline in risk-taking through time. We argue that harvesters instead relied on everyday adaptation—individual-scale, short- and medium-term adjustments in business strategy that occur within the constraints of the existing social–ecological system—to maintain resilience without increasing risk. Observable shifts in fleet composition, including use of larger vessels and higher-capacity licenses, lend support to this understanding. These results suggest that even in highly constrained social–ecological systems, protected response spaces and comanagement structures can enable often overlooked forms of flexibility.

paper.title: Defect Engineering via Aggregation: Unlocking Hour‐Long Afterglow and UV Thermoluminescence in Self‐Embedded Carbon Nitride Quantum Dots
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon nitride quantum dots (CNQDs) exhibiting aggregation‐induced visible long persistent luminescence (LPL), ultraviolet (UV) high‐temperature afterglow (HTA), and thermoluminescence (TL) are reported for the first time. The CNQDs are synthesized via a facile solvent‐free thermolysis of biuret and display a blue LPL lasting over 1.5 h under ambient conditions. Upon heating to 150°C, intense UV HTA and TL emissions are generated. Mechanistic studies reveal that aggregation‐associated π–π stacking stabilizes triplet excitons, while aggregation‐stabilized defect‐related paramagnetic centers promote carrier capture and long‐term energy storage, with deeper traps serving as reservoirs for thermally activated release. Reverse intersystem crossing further transfers de‐trapped carriers from triplet to singlet excited states, resulting in a pronounced blue‐shift of the HTA and TL emissions into the UV region. Owing to the stability of the aggregates and their protective effect on excited states and trapped charges, the luminescence remains robust in aqueous dispersions, while the invisible UV TL signals remain clearly detectable after more than 15 days under ambient conditions. Leveraging these characteristics, we demonstrate applications in highly concealed information storage and high‐contrast bioimaging. This work establishes an aggregation‐induced defect‐engineering strategy for energy‐storage luminescent materials and opens a new pathway toward self‐embedded LPL/TL systems.

paper.title: Correlating Charge-Storage Kinetics, Quantum Capacitance, and Surface Charge Density in Bi2O2S: An Experimental-DFT Study
paper.abstract: Abstract Understanding charge storage in layered electrode materials requires distinguishing electrochemical kinetics from the intrinsic ability of the electrode to accumulate electronic charge. Here, phase-pure Bi 2 O 2 S was investigated using electrochemical measurements and density functional theory (DFT) calculations to establish this relationship. Cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic charge-discharge, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy revealed a strongly rate-dependent charge-storage response, with a specific capacitance of 866 F g⁻¹ at 1 A g⁻¹. The scan-rate dependence gave an average b-value of ~ 0.61, while Dunn analysis showed that diffusion-dependent processes dominate the charge-storage response. DFT calculations further demonstrated that surface modification alters the electronic charge-storage ability of Bi 2 O 2 S. The calculated quantum capacitance increased from 493.14 \(\:\mu\:F{cm}^{-2}\) for the pristine surface to 638.75 \(\:\mu\:F{cm}^{-2}\) following OH adsorption. Surface charge densities of 513.46 and 506.76 \(\:\mu\:C\:{cm}^{-2}\) were obtained for K-top and K-hollow configurations, respectively. Experimental surface charge densities approached the DFT-derived range at higher current densities, whereas larger deviations at lower current densities indicate additional contributions from electrolyte-mediated and Faradaic processes. These results establish an experimental-DFT framework for relating rate-dependent electrochemical charge storage to the intrinsic electronic charge-accumulation behaviour of Bi 2 O 2 S.

paper.title: Quantifying electronic insulation of solid-electrolyte interphases through electrolyte decomposition kinetics
paper.abstract: The pursuit of high operating voltage and energy density of battery packs imposes stringent requirements on the electronic insulation of solid-electrolyte interphases (SEI) in rechargeable lithium-ion batteries. Owing to complicated kinetic processes, direct experimental characterization of electronic insulation poses challenges, whereas first-principles computations provide valuable access to underlying microscopic parameters. However, existing methods often yield conflicting evaluations by focusing solely on electronic transmission at specific parts of SEI/electrolyte interfaces, ignoring electrolyte decomposition kinetics. Herein, we develop a computational framework combining the Marcus electron transfer model and constrained density functional theory to predict the resistance to electrolyte decomposition (RED), which quantifies how effectively the SEI suppresses decomposition. RED unifies two key physical factors: electronic transmission across interfaces and reorganization energy associated with electrolyte decomposition, thereby enabling component‑resolved, electrolyte‑dependent evaluation of SEI electronic insulation. Applying the framework to idealized crystalline graphitic C(0001)|SEI | electrolyte interfaces, we find that electrolyte-dependent reorganization can substantially alter, and in some cases reverse, the insulation ranking inferred from electronic coupling alone, identifying reorganization as a key contributor to the comparatively high electronic insulation of Li2CO3 in the systems examined. The present work establishes a proof-of-concept, component-resolved framework and a basis for future studies of structurally heterogeneous SEIs.

paper.title: Distinguishing electrostatic from ion-specific effects at charged oxide/water interfaces by sum-frequency spectroscopy
paper.abstract: Charged aqueous interfaces are ubiquitous, yet the ionic modulation of interfacial reactions is often empirically related to the bulk ion concentration without distinguishing pure electrostatic screening from ion-specific interactions. The Gouy–Chapman–Stern (GCS) model provides a mean-field description of the surface charge and ion distributions at such electrified interfaces, but direct experimental validation at the molecular level remains scarce. Here, we combine in situ sum-frequency spectroscopy of surface lattice vibrations with the modified Poisson–Boltzmann formalism to spectroscopically disentangle various ionic effects. Using the benchmark silica/water interface in NaCl solutions as a model system, we calibrated experimental deprotonation rates of surface silanol groups against the calculated surface proton concentrations. Below the Na+ concentration of ∼2 M, the apparent ion-induced acceleration of deprotonation is fully accounted for by electrostatic screening alone, with ion concentration dependence essentially reflecting the change in surface proton concentration. Above this threshold, the GCS model breaks down as ions specifically perturb the surface structure, causing the deprotonation rate to exceed the electrostatic prediction. This framework is further examined by calculations across different pKa values, ionic valences, and oxide species, providing a general basis for interpreting interfacial ionic effects beyond the mean-field limit.

paper.title: Scanning Electrochemical Microscopy Study of Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer Processes in Aqueous and Concentrated Hydrogen-Bonded Electrolytes: Reorganization Energies and Kinetic Correlations with Medium Acidity
paper.abstract: Electrochemical proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) reactions are ubiquitous, yet quantitative kinetic analysis of soluble redox species is often hindered by practical experimental limitations, such as mass transport, and mechanistic complexity. Here, we employed scanning electrochemical microscopy (SECM) in the feedback mode under stationary, time-independent conditions to investigate the electrochemical PCET kinetics of freely diffusing quinone molecules in aqueous and concentrated hydrogen-bonded electrolytes (CoHBEs) media by constructing rate constant (log k) vs. overpotential (η) plots (k-plots). This approach enabled the direct determination of the apparent electron transfer rate constant at each applied potential, bypassing the reliance on a specific kinetic model. It also captured potential-dependent changes in slope and curvature features that could be described by Butler-Volmer (BV) and Marcus-Hush-Chidsey (MHC) models to obtain standard rate constants (k0) and the reorganization energies (λ) under different reaction conditions. Using anthraquinone-2,7-disulfonic acid (AQDS) as a redox probe, we examined the proton-to-electron transfer ratios during PCET processes across acidic to basic pH conditions through Pourbaix analysis, in situ spectroelectrochemical methods including shifted excitation Raman difference spectroscopy (SERDS), and electronic absorption spectroscopy. We observed that, in both aqueous and CoHBE solvents with varying acidity, more basic environments exhibit larger k0 and smaller λ values as acidity decreases. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further revealed that multiple PCET pathways coexist, with their relative contributions depending on pH and applied potential. The greater contribution of sequential proton-electron transfer (SPET) pathways and lower activation barriers under more basic conditions provide a mechanistic understanding for the experimentally observed 2 / 41 faster kinetics because concerted PCET steps have larger reorganization energies. Furthermore, extending our approach to the benzoquinone (BQ)/hydroquinone (H2BQ) redox couple enabled the construction of two-tailed k-plots containing both anodic and cathodic branches, revealing redox asymmetry in PCET reactions. Theoretical modeling suggested that different operative reaction mechanisms between oxidation and reduction reactions as a potential origin of apparent redox asymmetry. This work lays the foundations for extracting electrochemical PCET kinetics for a variety of redox systems, electrode materials, and solution compositions and conditions of broad interest for energy storage and beyond.

paper.title: Cation‐Mediated Interface Engineering Directs Electrogenerated Reactive Oxygen Species Pathways
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Persistent organic contaminants are increasingly accumulating in saline waters, where high ionic strength and complex electrolytes hinder oxidative remediation. Electrogenerated reactive oxygen species (ROS) offer a promising route for pollutant degradation, yet the role of electrolyte cations in controlling ROS pathways remains poorly understood. Although singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) is more persistent and matrix‐tolerant than hydroxyl radicals (•OH), whether cation‐induced changes in interfacial water structure govern ROS selectivity remains unclear. Here, using atomically dispersed Cu on Fe 2 O 3 ‐carbon nanotubes (Cu 1 /Fe 2 O 3 ‐CNTs) as a dual‐ROS electrocatalyst, we show that alkali‐metal cations exert distinct effects on ROS generation. •OH production follows the expected cation‐size‐dependent trend, whereas 1 O 2 generation exhibits an anomalous maximum in Na + ‐containing electrolytes, leading to superior contaminant degradation. Quantitative ROS measurements, in situ electrochemical analysis, spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations show that this behavior is primarily governed by selective stabilization of the *OOH intermediate rather than enhanced O 2 adsorption. Na + promotes a highly interconnected interfacial hydrogen‐bond network that stabilizes *OOH and favors 1 O 2 formation. In natural seawater, this regulation enables >98.2% contaminant removal within 8 h at an estimated energy demand of 0.779 kWh m −3 . These findings identify electrolyte cations as important regulators of ROS selectivity and provide a basis for efficient saline‐water decontamination.

paper.title: Two-atom interaction potential database supporting physics-informed features for machine learning and material property prediction
paper.abstract: Accurately predicting the energy and relevant properties of molecules and complex crystalline systems remains a cornerstone of computational materials science. While density functional theory (DFT) offers high accuracy, its computational cost scales prohibitively for large-scale materials. In this work, we present a comprehensive, first-principles-derived database of two-atom interaction potentials and interatomic forces to accelerate the property prediction via physics-informed machine learning. Computed using spin-polarized DFT via the GPAW package, the database encompasses all 2346 possible atomic pairs generated from 68 unique elements as a function of interatomic distance. The practical utility of this database was demonstrated within the many-body expansion framework by engineering highly descriptive features to predict three distinct types of energy for benchmarking. First, the framework was applied to predict the total energy of molecules within the G2/97 database. Second, for defect energetics on 2D materials (the IMP2D database), localized concentric shell potentials and spatial gradients were introduced to capture the formation energy of adsorbate defects. Finally, for molecular energetics within the QM9 database, we developed advanced descriptors, including a potential-based matrix, a two-body Bag of Bonds, and a three-body Ray’s asymmetric parameter histogram to evaluate atomization energy. Evaluated using kernel ridge regression, the combined two-body and three-body feature set yielded an outstanding test result with the mean absolute error of 0.186 eV (R2 = 0.9994) on a 10 000-samples subset. This framework showcases the power of utilizing explicit, database-derived potentials as robust descriptors for high-fidelity predictions of energy and relevant properties.

paper.title: Architecting 3D Space‐Charge Heterointerfacial Networks for Electrode‐Scale Ion Transport
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing space‐charge effects to govern carrier dynamics is central to nanoionics, yet translating localized nanoscale transport into continuous electrode‐wide percolation remains challenging. Here, we report an architectural strategy that uses Na 2 O/Na 2 CO 3 heterointerfaces as local nanoionic transport units and organizes them into a bulk‐distributed, three‐dimensional network throughout a preformed electrode. This architecture is realized by coupling ultralow‐flux Na‐vapor metallization with mesopore‐regulated gas‐solid conversion in a preformed metal‐organic framework (MOF) host. The synergy of space‐charge carrier enrichment and MOF‐mediated lattice distortion simultaneously boosts carrier density and lowers migration barriers, yielding an estimated local interfacial conductivity on the order of 10 −7 S cm −1 at 25°C, from intrinsically insulating Na 2 O (10 −12 S cm −1 ) and Na 2 CO 3 (10 −23 S cm −1 ). Integrated with conducting carbon, this functionally percolating network enables stable solid‐state presodiation and ultrahigh‐rate sodium‐ion full cells. This work bridges the gap between nanoscopic interface physics and macroscopic device functionality, identifying the spatial connectivity of phase boundaries, rather than the localized space‐charge effect alone, as a programmable design variable for next‐generation solid‐state ionics.

paper.title: Transferable Atom-Pair Graph Neural Network for Few-Shot Reconstruction of Rigid Homobilayer Sliding Potential-Energy Surfaces
paper.abstract: Abstract Interlayer potential-energy surfaces (PESs) govern stacking stability, sliding barriers, and tribology in two-dimensional bilayers, but first-principles mapping is expensive. We introduce an atom-pair graph neural network (APGNN) whose nodes are interlayer atom pairs, placing the representation directly on the interface. Pretraining on 89 homobilayers from a 112-material 2DMatPedia benchmark reduces the 20-point mean absolute error on 23 unseen materials from 9.22 to 1.94 meV/Å2 and increases the mean R2 from 0.802 to 0.991. Leave-one-element-out tests further demonstrate transfer to compounds containing an element absent from pretraining, reducing the MAE by 50.5–58.6% relative to that for training from scratch at the same target-data budget. For MoS2, 10 single-point energies per stacking recover the equilibrium spacing, distance-dependent sliding barriers, and two-dimensional PES topology. Dense interlayer PESs thus become accessible at a fraction of the first-principles cost. The method is currently limited to rigid homobilayers; heterobilayers and relaxed moiré structures require further training data.

paper.title: Coordination-Controlled Stability of Pd Single-Atom Catalysts under Electrochemical Conditions
paper.abstract: Abstract Single-atom catalysts (SACs) maximize atom utilization and site-specificity for diverse chemical and electrochemical transformations. While activity and selectivity have been optimized through advanced synthetic methods, the electrochemical stability of SACs remains insufficiently understood and limits practical application. Here, we employ operando inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) to quantify the dissolution kinetics of palladium (Pd) SACs in acidic electrolyte across a wide potential window. Operando electrochemically coupled mass spectrometry (EC-MS) confirms concurrent carbon support corrosion. By systematically varying heteroatom dopants, applied potentials, electrolyte pH, and adsorbing anions, we decouple coordination-driven (intrinsic) and electrochemical (extrinsic) factors controlling metal leaching. Specifically, the external potential exhibits a more pronounced influence on the stability of Pd SACs, while the coordinating heteroatoms modulate stability through both direct interaction with the isolated Pd centers and influence on the carbon support. Complementary X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) reveal dynamic restructuring of the Pd coordination environment, linking local chemical structure to macroscopic stability. These results provide mechanistic insights into SAC degradation pathways and establish design principles for stable single-atom architectures in energy conversion applications.

paper.title: Redox Properties of the Copper Centers in Particulate Methane Monooxygenase
paper.abstract: Abstract Particulate methane monooxygenase (pMMO) and its homolog ammonia monooxygenase (AMO), central enzymes in the global carbon and nitrogen cycles, contain three highly conserved mononuclear copper centers, denoted CuB, CuC, and CuD. While these sites have been well characterized structurally and spectroscopically, with recent studies identifying CuD as the active site, their reduction potentials have not been measured. This knowledge gap has hindered efforts to determine how the two electrons and two protons required for substrate oxidation are sourced and delivered. Here, we have elucidated the redox properties of each copper center in pMMO/AMO by protein film voltammetry using samples with copper occupancies known from cryoelectron microscopy (cryoEM) structures. The reduction potential of the CuB site, −72 to −139 mV, is significantly lower than the ∼400 mV measured for the CuD site, with consistent values determined for pMMOs and AMO from different species. Mutation of a residue in the second sphere of CuB, Glu35, alters the redox potential and impairs cell growth and pMMO activity, indicating that redox chemistry at CuB might be functionally relevant. Finally, a Pourbaix diagram constructed for the CuBII/I and CuDII/I half-reactions suggests that a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process occurs at the CuD site but not at the CuB site. Thermochemical analysis of this proposed PCET process is compatible with electron delivery by a quinol reductant. These results provide new context for future investigations of the pMMO and AMO reaction mechanisms.

paper.title: Balancing composition and phase stability in High-Entropy Metal Phosphates for proton conduction
paper.abstract: The transition to sustainable energy technologies necessitates the development of proton-conducting electrolytes free from critical raw materials. Transition metal phosphate octahydrates (vivanite and pakhmoskyite analogues) offer a promising structural platform for proton transport via the vehicle mechanism, yet their performance is typically dominated by specific cation identity, with cobalt-based systems serving as the benchmark. This study investigates a high-entropy design strategy to decouple proton conductivity from cobalt reliance by stabilizing complex solid solutions containing up to several distinct metal cations (Ni, Co, Fe, Mn, Mg, Cu, Cd, Zn) within the phosphate octahydrate framework. Using a low-temperature aqueous precipitation method, we successfully synthesized single-phase high-entropy metal phosphates (HEMPs) and systematically evaluated their proton conductivity at 25 °C and 80 °C. While binary and ternary systems often require high cobalt concentrations to maintain performance, high-entropy compositions demonstrate a synergistic effect where increased configurational entropy correlates strongly with enhanced conductivity. Statistical analysis using Random Forest and ridge regression reveals that at 80 °C, configurational entropy surpasses cobalt content as the primary driver of transport performance. This entropy-driven enhancement allows for the significant reduction of cobalt to ~ca. 40 mol% without compromising conductivity, with optimised systems achieving values comparable to or exceeding the pure cobalt benchmark. These findings validate the high-entropy approach as a viable pathway for designing sustainable, high-performance proton conductors, demonstrating that structural disorder can effectively compensate for the reduction of chemically specific but critical elements in functional materials.

paper.title: Material and thermal properties of MgCl2 molten salt by ab initio and machine-learning molecular-dynamics simulations
paper.abstract: We study the structural, thermophysical, and dynamical properties of molten MgCl2 over a wide temperature range using Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics (AIMD) and molecular dynamics simulations based on machine-learning interaction potentials (MLIPs). MLIPs can achieve near-AIMD accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost, enabling simulations of larger systems and longer timescales. This opens up the possibility of studying the system under out-of-equilibrium conditions, which in turn allows for the calculation of physical properties, such as the thermal conductivity or viscosity, that cannot be obtained reliably for the typical time and length scales accessible to AIMD. We follow two complementary approaches to develop and evaluate the MLIPs. First, we develop a Deep Potential (DP) from scratch using AIMD trajectories at different temperatures. Second, we also evaluate two out-of-the-box foundation models and a fine-tuned version of one of them. The fine-tuning is performed using configurations from the AIMD trajectories originally used to train the DP. We compare the predictions of the trained DP, the foundation models, and AIMD simulations with the available experimental data and provide a comprehensive calculation of the most important physical quantities of molten MgCl2. We compute densities, radial and angular distribution functions, thermal conductivity, heat capacity, viscosity, and diffusion coefficients over the 1000–1600 K temperature range. This range is relevant to important technological applications such as thermal energy storage, generation IV nuclear reactors, and concentrated solar power systems. Finally, we briefly review the accuracy and performance of the different MLIP versions used throughout the work.

paper.title: Charge Donated by the Framework, Reactivity Expressed at the Metal: Tetrathiafulvalene-Programmed Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
paper.abstract: The decisive challenge in nitrate-to-ammonia electrosynthesis is not simply supplying electrons, but ensuring that successive nitrogen intermediates remain chemically convertible. Here, we establish a molecular strategy that differentiates framework-derived electronic character from metal-directed reaction selectivity through TU-420, a crystalline covalent organic framework integrating electron-donating tetrathiafulvalene and electron-accepting, metal-coordinating bipyridine units. Electronic-structure analysis identifies complementary donor-associated and acceptor-like states, while Xray absorption spectroscopy reveals distinct approximately six-coordinate Fe–O/N and four-coordinate Cu–O/N environments within the conserved architecture. Remarkably, TU-420-Fe achieves 98.1% ammonia Faradaic efficiency at −0.60 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode and an ammonia production rate of 4.33 mg h-1 cm-2 at −0.80 V, whereas TU-420-Cu exhibits substantially lower selectivity despite its stronger cathodic response. Isotope-labeling experiments establish nitrate as the nitrogen source, while in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and differential electrochemical mass spectrometry reveal signatures consistent with evolving nitrogen–oxygen and hydrogenated nitrogen species. Density functional theory identifies the mechanistic distinction: Fe supports a favorable *NHO-mediated reduction sequence with a maximum uphill free-energy increment of 0.30 eV, while substantially alleviating the energetic penalty associated with the competing *NOH-mediated route relative to Cu. These findings identify the energetic fate of partially reduced nitrogen, rather than electron consumption alone, as a determinant of ammonia selectivity and establish electronically differentiated covalent architectures as platforms for programming metal-dependent multielectron catalysis.

paper.title: The CO₂ Concentration Inversion Effect: *CO Generation Rate and *CO C–C Coupling Efficiency as Dual Kinetic Descriptors for Catalyst-Dependent C₂ Selectivity in Dilute CO₂ Electroreduction¹
paper.abstract: The electrochemical reduction of dilute CO₂ (5–33% v/v) to multicarbon (C₂₊) products offers a route to utilize industrial exhaust directly, bypassing energy-intensive CO₂ capture and purification. Our systematic investigations from 2023 to 2026 reveal a counter-intuitive paradigm: under dilute CO₂ feed, the C₂ selectivity of copper-based catalysts can surpass the pure-CO₂ baseline. Here we define the CO₂ concentration inversion effect as a kinetic regime where C₂ selectivity under dilute CO₂ exceeds the pure-CO₂ baseline—first in the FE(C₂)/FE(C₁) ratio and, for an increasing number of catalyst families, in the absolute C₂ Faradaic efficiency at matched potentials. This non-monotonic selectivity shows that C₂ formation is governed by a catalyst-tunable balance between *CO supply and coupling kinetics. We introduce two quantitative kinetic descriptors—the *CO production rate r (in mol cm⁻² s⁻¹) and the *CO C–C coupling efficiency η ∈ [0,1]—that jointly resolve the fate of *CO intermediates. In-situ FT–IR spectroscopy confirms that coupling efficiency is primarily governed by CO₂ concentration; we resolve a decoupling between microscopic η and the macroscopic FE(C₂₊)/FE(C₁) ratio. This framework, validated across B-doped Cu, Ag@Cu₂O and Cu₂(OH)₂CO 3 -derived Cu, challenges the implicit assumption that high-purity CO₂ is a prerequisite for efficient C₂₊ electrosynthesis.

paper.title: A Dual Vibrational Probe Framework for Studying Solvation in Highly Heterogeneous Molecular Environments
paper.abstract: Abstract Vibrational probes are essential for studying interactions and dynamics of complex environments, but they often rely on computer simulations to describe the system. Here, a dual-IR-probe approach based on the alkyne molecular framework is demonstrated for two probes: MOC (low polarity) and TFPB (nonpolar). In these dual-probes, the secondary IR-active group allows their precise localization, while the alkyne group is used to probe the dynamics. The approach is validated in two complex liquids: a deep eutectic solvent (DES) and a water micelle. In the DES, the dual-IR scheme experimentally locates MOC in one specific domain. In water micelles, MOC and TFPB localize selectively at the interface and within the hydrophobic core, respectively, providing an independent characterization of the two environments. The results demonstrate that the alkyne-based dual-probe is a versatile molecular framework for characterizing the structure, interactions, and dynamics of complex liquids using only experimental methods.

paper.title: Machine-learned, finite temperature Fermi-operator expansions suitable for GPUs and AI-hardware
paper.abstract: We present several finite-temperature recursive Fermi–operator expansion schemes based on the second-order spectral projection (SP2) method. Our approach builds on a previous observation that the electronic structure problem, as formulated through a recursive SP2 expansion, can be mapped onto the architecture of a deep neural network. Using this perspective, we generalize SP2 to finite electronic temperatures by constructing machine learning models that determine optimized recursive expansion coefficients. The same approach is also applied to the prediction of the electronic entropy for fractional occupation numbers. The coefficients are trained for a specified chemical potential and electronic temperature and are not available in closed analytical form. However, by employing an appropriate affine rescaling strategy to the Hamiltonian matrix, we eliminate the need to retrain the model for different temperatures and chemical potentials. Our approach avoids explicit diagonalization and relies solely on highly optimized matrix–matrix multiplication kernels. Compared to state-of-the-art diagonalization, we achieve an order-of-magnitude speedup in the single-particle finite-temperature density matrix calculation for small and moderately sized matrices on modern graphics processing units and dense matrix multiply units.

paper.title: AnDi-J: diffusion analysis of single-particle tracking data in Fiji
paper.abstract: Characterizing how particles diffuse is key to understanding biology across scales, yet extracting the underlying physical properties typically requires specialized tools rarely accessible to biology labs. Here we introduce AnDi-J, a Fiji plugin combining classical estimators with state-of-the-art machine learning for single-trajectory analysis and segmentation, requiring minimal knowledge of stochastic processes. It extracts diffusion coefficients and anomalous exponents, classifies trajectories into diffusion models, and segments heterogeneous trajectories into diffusive states, through powerful, easy-to-use visualization tools. See more at https://github.com/gorkamunoz/andi-j .

paper.title: Imaging of Electrochemically Programmed Single-Molecule Reactions
paper.abstract: Abstract Single-molecule reactions reveal intrinsic heterogeneity that is obscured in ensemble measurements. However, most existing approaches rely on extreme dilution, ultrasmall solution volumes, or physical confinement to keep individual events sufficiently sparse. Here, we introduce electrochemically programmed single-molecule reactions (PSMR), a pulse-regulated strategy that shifts single-molecule electrochemistry from passive observation to active control. It converts continuous interfacial reactions to a sequence of short, repeatable reaction trials. By tailoring the pulse waveform, PSMR controls the driving force and duration of each reaction trial, thereby regulating the probability of single-molecule reactions, while the relaxation interval between pulses allows the interface to recover before the next trial. This coordinated control enables single-molecule reactions to be actively regulated under conventional solution volumes and reaction concentrations. By coupling individual reaction events to single-photon emission through electrogenerated chemiluminescence (ECL), we can directly count and image the reactions. The ultrashort reaction windows and relaxation periods suppress diffusion-layer buildup, thereby preserving sensitivity to local reaction kinetics, even at high overpotentials. Using this approach, individual Au nanoparticles were imaged over a broad potential range, and particles as small as 5 nm were distinguished from the substrate background. Sparse photon events were accumulated over repeated trials and further analyzed using localization- and fluctuation-based algorithms, enabling super-resolution mapping of reaction activity beyond the optical diffraction limit. PSMR therefore provides a framework for actively regulating, quantitatively imaging, and spatially mapping single-molecule electrochemical reactions at nanointerfaces, opening new opportunities for mechanistic studies and rational design across molecular electrochemistry, electrocatalysis, and energy conversion.

paper.title: An Analytical Full-Dimensional Potential Energy Surface for the H + C3H8 Hydrogen Abstraction Reaction: Non-Equivalence of the Primary Hydrogens and Variational Transition State Theory Kinetics
paper.abstract: A new analytical full-dimensional potential energy surface, PES-2026, is reported for the gas-phase hydrogen abstraction reaction H + C3H8 → H2 + C3H7. It is built within the valence bond–molecular mechanics, VB-MM, framework and depends on 72 parameters, 65 of which were optimized against a focal-point CBS benchmark and against UMP2/cc-pVTZ geometries, harmonic frequencies and reaction paths. The surface describes the two chemically distinct abstraction channels, primary and secondary, and resolves them into three kinetically distinct channels: the six primary hydrogens are not equivalent, two of them being abstracted through an anti and four through a gauche saddle point whose adiabatic barriers differ by 0.26 kcalmol−1. Classical barrier heights of 12.05, 11.68 and 9.44 kcalmol−1 were obtained for the anti-primary, gauche-primary and secondary channels, reproducing the benchmark to within 0.04 kcalmol−1, and a relaxed two-dimensional torsional scan that did not enter the fit is reproduced with a root-mean-square deviation of 0.11 kcalmol−1. Thermal rate constants were computed between 200 and 1000 K with variational transition state theory and multidimensional tunnelling, CVT/µOMT, treating the three channels separately and summing them. At 300 K the total rate constant, 9.4×10−16 cm3 molecule−1 s−1, is 0.85 times the Tsang evaluation, and the calculated primary contribution, 5.6%, compares with the 4.3–4.7% derived from experiment and improves on the 9.5% of the most recent direct-dynamics study. Kinetic isotope effects are predicted for substrate and for attacking-atom substitution; the latter is inverse below ∼800 K, which is traced to the lowering of the adiabatic barrier upon deuteration of the incoming atom. The muonium analogue is also examined and is found to lie beyond the reach of a harmonic treatment.
