paper.title: Identifying intercalation electrodes for electrochemical ion recovery and desalination
paper.abstract: Water sources serve as a requirement for human consumption, industrial, and agricultural needs and a resource for valuable ions. Appropriate treatment of water that captures ions from the aqueous solution can give rise to suitable `products', such as critical ions (such as Li$^+$) in selective ion recovery and usable water in the case of desalination (i.e., removal of non-essential ions). Among myriad ion capture techniques, we focus on electrochemical methods using intercalation electrodes, an energy-efficient approach capable of both selectively extracting specific ions or non-selectively extracting multiple ions from diverse water sources. However, practical realization of electrochemical ion capture requires the use of robust cation intercalation electrodes, with the state-of-the-art olivine-FePO$_4$ and spinel-Mn$_2$O$_4$ exhibiting several shortcomings. Thus, we develop a high-throughput computational workflow to identify potential intercalation electrodes for both ion recovery and desalination from a pool of 20,414 Li, Mg, Ca, Na, and/or K-containing structures from the Materials Project database. Based on the construction of Pourbaix diagrams relevant for electrodes operating under seawater conditions, modifying criteria used for defining metastability in seawater, computing average intercalation voltages and the extent of metastability of electrode structures, and computational graphs to encode ionic selectivity, we identify a total of 11 promising electrodes for selective ion recovery and one possible desalination electrode. The promising materials identified in this work include Fe$_2$(MoO$_4$)$_3$, Li$_3$Fe$_2$(PO$_4$)$_3$, LiFeP$_2$O$_7$ for selective Li-recovery. Our study provides thermodynamic insights, qualitative trends, and a promising list of intercalation electrodes for experimental testing that should advance the field of electrochemical ion recovery.

paper.title: A "feature ODE" describing the learning behavior of shallow MLPs on simple functions
paper.abstract: We study the gradient flow training dynamics of two-layer multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) on anisotropic Gaussian data. Even in this simple setting, solving the dynamics in full is notoriously difficult, so we try something different. We propose a "feature ODE" that might be intuitively expected to describe the learning dynamics of a shallow MLP. We find that MLPs trained to learn simple target functions (low-order Hermite polynomials and staircase functions) actually roughly follow the loss trajectories from this feature ODE. This agreement is a surprise because of the size of the simplification and the fact that it does not come from a rigorous chain of approximations. We discuss this surprise and speculate on its reasons and uses.
paper.tldr: 该研究提出一种“特征ODE”简化模型，发现浅层MLP在简单目标函数上的损失轨迹与该模型大致吻合，这一意外结果值得进一步探索。

paper.title: Hierarchical universal open structure dataset for atomistic modeling
paper.abstract: Atomic-scale simulations have been transformed by machine-learning models that predict the properties of atomistic structures with the accuracy of quantum calculations, but at a small fraction of the cost. These models have increased dramatically in generality, thanks to the availability of synthetic datasets of ever-increasing size and scope. The proliferation of datasets, with properties often computed using different levels of electronic-structure approximation, is problematic, as there is often overlap between different datasets, and strong correlations between structures obtained with short molecular dynamics trajectories or geometry optimization. To address these problems, we introduce a protocol to stratify a dataset into a hierarchy of nested subsets, subsampling from the coarsest to the finest resolution based on an "ecumetric" built to reflect the latent space representation of several popular universal machine-learning interatomic potentials. We then use this approach to combine most of the open structural datasets currently available, consolidating them into MAD-COSMO, a well-organized collection of almost 1.7 billion structures, whose $2^{24}$ most diverse members form the MAD-CORE stratified coreset, which can be easily used for all sorts of tasks, from exploratory experiments to the training of foundation models at scale. We envision that this collection will guide and help coordinate future efforts, focusing them on the most relevant and/or undersampled regions of chemical and structural space, and that it will be further extended to incorporate the outcomes of the collective work of this community.
paper.tldr: 该数据集通过分层通用开放结构整合多样原子模拟数据，显著提升机器学习模型的泛化能力与训练效率，弥补现有合成数据集的冗余和关联性问题。

paper.title: Visualizing surface-reaction-driven chloride migration and cascading failure in sulfide solid electrolytes
paper.abstract: Moisture instability of sulfide solid electrolytes limits practical use in all-solid-state batteries. Spatially resolving gas--solid reactions during moisture exposure remains challenging. Here, cryogenic four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (cryo-4D-STEM) maps nanoscale degradation in low- and high-Cl argyrodite electrolytes, Li\(_6\)PS\(_5\)Cl and Li\(_{5.5}\)PS\(_{4.5}\)Cl\(_{1.5}\). Li\(_6\)PS\(_5\)Cl undergoes predominantly surface-localized degradation that progressively extends inward, whereas Li\(_{5.5}\)PS\(_{4.5}\)Cl\(_{1.5}\) exhibits rapid interior amorphization accompanied by outward chloride redistribution. Density functional theory calculations indicate a lower chloride-migration barrier along the modeled pathway in the higher-Cl composition, while chloride removal and vacancy formation distort the PS\(_4^{3-}\) framework and may destabilize the lattice. Surface treatment suppresses detectable large-scale chloride segregation and improves moisture tolerance, retaining 99.9% of the capacity measured at the start of 0.33 C cycling after 150 cycles. These results identify chloride redistribution as a key process in degradation propagation and suggest a route toward moisture-tolerant solid-state batteries.
paper.tldr: 该研究通过冷冻4D-STEM揭示了不同氯含量硫化物电解质在湿度下的降解路径差异：低氯体系表面降解逐步向内扩展，高氯体系则内部快速非晶化并伴随氯向外迁移。

paper.title: Bridging Ionic Field Strength Disparity in O3-Type Layered Oxides for High-Voltage Sodium-Ion Batteries
paper.abstract: Abstract O3-type layered oxides represent an attractive class of sodium-ion battery cathodes, combining high theoretical specific capacity and high pristine Na content. However, their deeply desodiated frameworks at high voltages (≥4.0 V) are prone to redox-coupled distortion of TMO6 octahedra within the transition metal (TM) slabs, leading to severe structural degradation. Here, we originally define an ionic field strength disparity coefficient (η), which enables quantitative evaluation of the local chemical-field heterogeneity. The η is derived from the ratio between the standard deviation and the average value of ionic field strength (Φ) of all TM ions, defined as Φ= Z/r2, where Z and r correspond to the ionic charge and ionic radius, respectively. Introducing compensatory cations with an intermediate Φ value between two cations featuring largely disparate Φ values effectively reconciles local chemical-field discrepancy and lowers the η parameter upon charge–discharge processes. Moreover, synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy, strain mapping analyses, and first-principles calculations reveal that the low-η sample demonstrates the reduced lattice strain and enhanced structural reversibility. Consistently, electrochemical evaluation shows that it retains more than 80% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 10C, markedly outperforming the unmodified counterpart with only 22% retention. This work establishes the η as a quantitative descriptor for inactive dopant selection and provides a general strategy for developing highly stable layered oxide cathodes.
paper.tldr: 该研究提出离子场强度差异系数，定量评估O3型层状氧化物正极在高电压下的结构稳定性，为钠离子电池设计提供新指标。

paper.title: Modeling electrodeposition of thin films with compact, dendritic, and random morphologies
paper.abstract: We summarize previously published computer simulation studies of a metal electrodeposition model that considers diffusive cation flux, a fast reaction in contact with the electrode or with the growing deposit, and adsorbed atom diffusion in finite time windows. Simulations with various parameters show compact, fractal, dendritic deposits, and dynamic transitions between different morphologies during the growth of individual samples. The dendritic shapes are characterized by hierarchical organizations in which branches of a given order reproduce the shape and crystalline orientation of the branches of the previous order, in contrast to the random branching of the fractal deposits formed by DLA and related models. The simulations show dendrites with maple leaf shape in SC lattices, pine tree shape in FCC lattices, and flower-like shape in HCP lattices, with surfaces predominantly oriented in the lowest-energy configurations of each lattice. Simulations with nucleation restricted to a nanoscale seed show the initial formation of faceted particles followed by dendrite formation, in agreement with silver electrodeposition on substrates patterned with gold nanoparticles. A quantitative application to faceted and dendritic silver obtained in the same experiment provides values of the model parameters which are consistent with the characteristic widths of these structures being of the same order of magnitude of the diffusion lengths of atoms on (111) and (001) surfaces. Using an extended model for iron electrodeposition on Si(100), the simulations qualitatively reproduce the initial formation of multilayer islands, small oscillations of the roughness of a polycrystalline compact film after island coalescence, and instability development. Possible directions for applying this modeling to the electrodeposition of other materials are suggested.
paper.tldr: 该模型模拟了电沉积中致密、树枝状及随机形貌的形成，并揭示了生长过程中不同形态间的动态转变。

paper.title: Physics-informed machine learning: a hybrid lens for fluid dynamics
paper.abstract: A neural network approach bridging Lagrangian and Eulerian perspectives transforms sparse observations into physically accurate, high-resolution maps of complex and chaotic fluid motions.
paper.tldr: 物理信息机器学习融合拉格朗日与欧拉视角，将稀疏观测转化为高分辨率流场，显著提升复杂湍流预测精度与效率。

paper.title: runner 2.0 : A software suite for high-dimensional neural network potentials
paper.abstract: We present runner 2.0, the “Ruhr University Neural Network energy representation,” a highly optimized software suite for training and evaluating high-dimensional neural network potentials (HDNNPs) of the second, third, and fourth generations. Long-range electrostatics and charge equilibration (QEq) for the description of non-local charge transfer in fourth-generation (4G) HDNNPs are accelerated by quasi-linear-scaling plane wave methods, reducing QEq computational complexity from O(N3) to O(N⁡log2⁡N) such that linear or quasi-linear scaling is achieved across all HDNNP generations. An optimized memory management strategy eliminates the training overhead traditionally associated with long-range interactions, allowing 4G-HDNNPs to be trained with the same efficiency as their local counterparts. Developed in modern Fortran (2003/2008 standards), combined with a hybrid Message Passing Interface (MPI)/Open Multi-Processing (OpenMP) parallelization scheme, runner 2.0 has been designed to run efficiently in any central processing unit (CPU) environment, from cost-effective local workstations to massive high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. Its modular library architecture facilitates straightforward binding to external simulation software; native interfaces to the Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator (LAMMPS) and the atomic simulation environment (ASE) provide full access to all its features, including built-in committee-based uncertainty quantification. The high efficiency and scalability of the runner 2.0 ecosystem are demonstrated through detailed benchmarks.

paper.title: Causality in liquid water as a hallmark of emergent glassy dynamics
paper.abstract: In molecular liquids such as water, time-delayed influences between microscopic or mesoscopic variables are typically probed using time-correlation functions, which are symmetric under detailed balance and therefore blind to dynamical asymmetries. Here, we characterize water’s dynamics using a causal inference metric that captures asymmetric couplings between collective variables. Analyzing equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations at ambient conditions and in the high-density liquid (HDL) regime of supercooled water, we uncover pronounced asymmetries in the couplings between orientational and translational degrees of freedom across multiple time and length scales. At room temperature, rotational modes exert a modest directional influence on translational dynamics. In contrast, in the supercooled HDL regime, translational motions emerge as the primary drivers of the dynamics, suggesting facilitation-like relaxation mechanisms characteristic of glassy systems. These results reveal a qualitative reorganization of dynamical couplings across thermodynamic conditions, implying that molecular liquids at thermal equilibrium can exhibit an emergent directionality in their fluctuation couplings. As a consequence, our analysis reveals that external perturbations acting on specific degrees of freedom can induce a stronger arrow of time in the causal relations between translational and orientational modes.
paper.tldr: 该研究发现液态水的定向与平移自由度之间存在显著的不对称因果耦合，表明其动力学具有类似玻璃态的内在不对称性。

paper.title: Understanding compression-extension error asymmetry in universal machine-learning interatomic potentials
paper.abstract: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials are increasingly used across diverse materials, yet their reliability under directional deformation remains unclear. We compare compression and extension along paired deformation paths from the same parent structures for eleven pretrained potentials. The benchmark comprises 1,963 Materials Project trajectory (MPtrj) parents and 1,286 experimental-source MinX-Eq parents at six strain magnitudes from 1% to 10%. Density-functional theory provides references for isotropic, uniaxial and biaxial loading in MPtrj and isotropic loading in MinX-Eq. At $\pm 10\%$, every model has a larger median force error under compression, with pooled isotropic compression-to-extension ratios of 2.12 and 3.30 for MPtrj and MinX-Eq. Decomposing error growth into DFT force-scale growth and relative-error evolution shows that relative errors decrease on both branches, faster under compression in MPtrj but slower under compression in MinX-Eq. Force-scale matching moves the error ratios toward unity, although MinX-Eq retains a compression-side excess across models. Radial and SOAP analyses place compressed structures at shorter separations and farther from public reference pools, while readout-associated model features show larger compression-side displacements. These results distinguish stronger physical responses from changes in relative predictive accuracy and provide a basis for assessing universal potentials in deformation simulations.
paper.tldr: 在拉伸和压缩对称变形下，多数通用机器学习原子间势的误差并不对称，压缩时中位误差更小，拉伸时更大，且随应变增大而明显。

paper.title: Modeling Transport and Mechanics in Anion Exchange Membranes to Optimize Continuous CO2 Separations
paper.abstract: Water transport in charged polymer membranes is strongly influenced by hydration-dependent transport properties and polymer-network deformation. Under water-activity gradients, spatial variations in water concentration induce swelling and mechanical stresses, while the resulting deformation can influence water transport. Capturing this bidirectional interaction is important for predicting membrane behavior under nonuniform hydration conditions. This study develops a transient finite element model of water transport and mechanical deformation in a Fumasep FAA-3-50 anion exchange membrane. The framework incorporates concentration-dependent water diffusivity, hygroscopic swelling, and nonlinear viscoelastic polymer response. Uncoupled, one-way coupled, and fully coupled formulations are compared to distinguish the effects of hydration-dependent diffusivity and mechanical coupling. In the fully coupled model, local water concentration governs swelling and mechanical response, while deformation, evolving membrane geometry, and mechanical pressure feed back into water transport. Simulations predict spatially and temporally nonuniform swelling and deformation that track the evolving water-concentration field. Relative to the uncoupled concentration-dependent diffusion model, mechanical feedback alters the predicted transport response, although transport remains primarily diffusion-driven. The fully coupled model is validated against steady-state water-transport measurements across water-activity gradients and reproduces the experimentally observed hydration dependence, with strongest agreement at intermediate hydration levels. These results highlight the importance of coupled hydration, swelling, deformation, and transport processes in models of hydrated anion exchange membranes and provide a framework for evaluating membrane behavior in moisture-facilitated transport applications.
paper.tldr: 该模型揭示膜内水浓度变化引起的溶胀与机械应力双向耦合，有助于优化连续CO₂分离的传输性能。

paper.title: Lewis–Brønsted Dual-Acid Sites Induced H-Down Interfacial Water Configuration and Accelerated Proton Transfer toward Enhanced Acidic Oxygen Evolution
paper.abstract: Abstract Efficient activation of interfacial water molecules and fast proton transfer are critical but challenging for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Herein, a Lewis–Brønsted dual-acid catalyst design strategy is proposed to achieve accelerated acidic OER by synergistically optimizing the configuration of interfacial water molecules and proton transfer kinetics on Mn-doped IrO2. In this catalyst, the Mn dopant serves as a Lewis acid site that readily captures hydroxyl groups, which perturbs the local hydrogen-bonding network and induces interfacial water molecules to form an H-down configuration toward surface active sites, thereby promoting the enrichment and dissociation of reactive interfacial water. On this basis, the formation of the Mn–Obri–Ir local structure enhances the Brønsted acidity of the bridge oxygen (Obri) site, accelerates the deprotonation of the Obri–H bond, promotes the formation of key OER intermediates and accelerates the reaction kinetics. Mn dopant also induces electron enrichment around Ir, suppresses excessive oxidation and dissolution of Ir species, and enhances catalyst stability performance. These synergistic effects enable Mn-IrO2 to achieve a 160 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm–2 and to operate stably for 1500 h at 10 mA cm–2 and 1200 h at 1.0 A cm–2 in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), demonstrating the promising potential of the Lewis–Brønsted dual-acid strategy in acidic OER catalyst design.

paper.title: Drying-Induced Size Segregation and Stratification in Colloidal Droplets across Binary, Ternary, and Polydisperse Systems
paper.abstract: We study evaporation-induced size segregation and stratification in binary, ternary, and polydisperse mixtures of colloidal particles within a drying droplet using Brownian dynamics (BD) simulations. We show that drying-induced stratification can occur in all three types of mixtures, with larger particles preferentially accumulating in the droplet interior and smaller particles near the droplet surface. In binary mixtures, size segregation becomes more pronounced as the Peclet number and the size difference between particles increase, and as the relative volume fraction of large particles and the initial particle concentration decrease. In ternary mixtures, three distinct layers form when the Peclet number is sufficiently high and the intermediate particle size is suitably selected. Under the conditions studied, increasing the fraction of intermediate-sized particles can also enhance separation between the small and large particles. These results are in qualitative agreement with previous studies of drying planar films. Extending the analysis to polydisperse systems, we find that the average particle size decreases with increasing radial distance under stratifying conditions. Furthermore, higher Peclet numbers and particle-size distributions with more particles at both size extremes lead to steeper radial gradients in particle size. Additionally, we use multi-particle collision dynamics (MPCD) simulations to assess the role of hydrodynamic interactions. BD simulations predict stronger stratification than MPCD simulations, although stratification persists in the MPCD simulations. Our results thus demonstrate that droplet-confined drying offers a simple and versatile strategy for engineering radial composition and size gradients in colloidal assemblies, thereby offering new opportunities for the controlled fabrication of hierarchically structured supraparticles.
paper.tldr: 模拟表明，干燥胶体液滴中大小颗粒发生分层，大颗粒富集内部、小颗粒靠表面，且随佩克莱数和粒径差增大而更显著。

paper.title: Microenvironment-Directed Galvanostatic Base Generation for Near-Neutral Hydrolysis of a Nerve-Agent Simulant
paper.abstract: Abstract Organophosphate hydrolysis under near-neutral conditions is intrinsically slow and generally requires strongly basic media or tailored catalysts. Here, we demonstrate that the electrolyte microenvironment can promote hydrolysis of dimethyl 4-nitrophenyl phosphate (DMNP) through an electrochemically generated base. Chemical controls show that DMNP hydrolysis depends on the combined effects of bulk pH, phosphate speciation, electrolyte concentration, and substrate accessibility. Under galvanostatic operation, cathodic water reduction generates OH– in situ, coupling hydrogen evolution to specific-base SN2(P) hydrolysis of DMNP. Time-resolved 31P NMR shows reciprocal DMNP consumption and dimethyl phosphate formation, while complementary UV–vis spectroscopy is consistent with formation of p-nitrophenolate. Although K2HPO4 and NaClO4 provide similar DMNP conversion at the same current, phosphate lowers the required overpotential and substantially improves energy-normalized conversion efficiency. Translation to a zero-gap membrane-electrode assembly enables stable full-cell operation and quantitative DMNP consumption within 1 h in a larger-volume, flow-compatible configuration. These findings establish galvanostatic in situ base generation as a controllable and modular strategy for organophosphate treatment in near-neutral aqueous media.

paper.abstract: Wan et al. introduce a physics-informed learning model that simultaneously predicts long-range particle paths and flow fields based on very limited trajectory measurements, validated in both simulations and blood-flow experiments.

paper.title: Secondary-Sphere Control of Electronic Structure and Ligand Basicity in Mo-Nitrogenase: A QM/MM Analysis Guided by Se K-Edge HERFD XAS
paper.abstract: Abstract Molybdenum nitrogenase catalyzes biological nitrogen fixation using a complex metallocofactor (FeMoco) containing three μ2-“belt”sulfides that exhibit distinct reactivity during catalysis. In particular, protonation at the S2B site imparts lability that facilitates substrate binding and may enable this sulfide to act as a proton donor. Although FeMoco is inactive outside its protein environment, how secondary-sphere residues tune its geometric and electronic structure to enable function remains unclear. We have previously shown that site-selective Se substitution of the μ2-sulfides provides a direct probe of the ligand environment using Se K-edge high-energy-resolution fluorescence-detected X-ray absorption spectroscopy (HERFD XAS). Despite the cofactor’s approximate C3 symmetry, Se-substituted sites display pronounced differences in Se HERFD XAS pre-edge intensities. Utilizing QM/MM calculations, we show that hydrogen-bonding (H-bonding) residues polarize the S3A and S5A sulfides, reducing metal–ligand covalency and attenuating pre-edge intensity, whereas hydrophobic residues surrounding S2B localize electron density and enhance its pre-edge intensity. These results demonstrate how hydrophobicity and H-bonding within the secondary coordination sphere modulate FeMoco electronic structure. More broadly, they show how the protein environment tunes ligand basicity to favor selective S2B protonation and provide design principles for controlling enzymatic function.

paper.title: Physics-Informed Site-Specific Molecular Interaction Learning Framework for Liquid–Liquid Phase Diagram Reconstruction and Extraction Process Design
paper.abstract: Abstract Liquid–liquid phase behavior is governed by the collective balance of intermolecular interactions and is central to predicting component partitioning and designing extraction-based separation processes. Existing thermodynamic and data-driven approaches can predict phase-equilibrium properties, but provide limited resolution of the molecular-interaction-to-phase-topology relationship underlying coupled binodal boundaries and tie-line families. Here, PSMI is proposed as a physics-informed site-specific molecular interaction learning framework that reconstructs ternary liquid–liquid phase diagrams directly from molecular structures. PSMI learns chemically meaningful intermolecular interaction sites through molecular representation learning and integrates chemical-potential consistency regularization to guide thermodynamically reliable phase reconstruction. The framework predicts coexisting extract and raffinate compositions along continuous phase paths and enables reconstruction of binodal boundaries and tie-line families. Across benchmark tests, PSMI accurately predicts coexisting extract and raffinate compositions and recovers phase-diagram topology, including both binodal shapes and tie-line directions. Interpretability analysis shows that PSMI identifies transferable molecular drivers underlying liquid–liquid phase separation, including chemically meaningful interaction patterns. Industrial case studies, together with a locally deployable web application, further demonstrate the practical utility and accessibility of PSMI for solvent screening and extraction process design. By resolving site-specific intermolecular interactions together with their macroscopic phase-partitioning consequences, PSMI provides a molecular-level perspective on how local chemical environments contribute to liquid–liquid phase behavior. This connection between localized molecular interactions and continuous phase-diagram topology provides a framework for understanding and designing complex liquid–liquid separation systems.

paper.title: Directional Charge Transport via Interlayer Electronic Coupling Enhances Photocatalysis in Covalent Organic Frameworks
paper.abstract: Abstract The design of efficient photocatalysts requires control over both exciton dissociation and the subsequent transport of charge carriers. Donor–acceptor two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are widely used to promote charge separation, but the role of directional charge transport in these layered materials is still not well understood. Here, we combine photophysical characterization and time-dependent density functional theory calculations to study three TAPD-based COFs for photocatalytic H2O2 production via oxygen reduction. All materials show efficient in-plane donor–acceptor charge transfer with similar exciton dissociation behavior. At the same time, clear differences appear in their charge transport properties. The calculations indicate that electrons move preferentially along the stacking direction, while holes remain more delocalized within the COF plane. This anisotropic transport is most pronounced in the COFs where stronger interlayer coupling favors the formation of interlayer charge-transfer states, as observed in transient absorption measurements. These states allow electrons and holes to separate over adjacent layers, which reduces recombination losses and corroborates the observed differences in photocatalytic activity. Our results indicate that directional interlayer charge transport, rather than local donor–acceptor charge separation alone, is an important factor in determining photocatalytic performance in COFs.

paper.title: Electrolytes that mind bridging the gap
paper.abstract: Silicon anodes enable high-energy-density Li-ion batteries but face reversibility challenges when operating under extreme temperature and charge-rate conditions. Now, a liquid electrolyte design results in interface protection and reduced electrode expansion during such operation, while also having lithium plating tolerance.
paper.tldr: 该研究设计了一种液态电解质，通过在极端温度和快充条件下保护硅负极界面并减少电极膨胀，同时耐受锂沉积，从而提升电池可逆性与能量密度。

paper.title: Directed assembly of cathode interlayers enables efficient binary organic solar cells
paper.abstract: Abstract Cathode interlayers create interfacial dipoles in organic solar cells to maximize device efficiency. However, the dipoles are highly dependent on the molecular orientation of the interlayers, which remain challenging to be controlled. Here, based on the amphiphilic nature of the interlayers, we show a stepwise film deposition approach using a polar solvent for active layer pretreatment and a bipolar solvent for subsequent interlayer self assembly. Sum-frequency generation vibrational spectroscopy reveals a preferred perpendicular orientation of the interlayer molecules, thereby enhancing the surface potential and reducing the charge transport resistance. As a result, we achieve a certified efficiency of 20.65% and fill factor of 82.7% in binary organic solar cells. This method is universally applicable to different cathode interlayers and active layers. Our work highlights the importance of controlling interlayer molecular orientation for unlocking significant performance gains, paving the way for further advancements in device optimization.
paper.tldr: 该研究表明，通过极性溶剂预处理和双极性溶剂自组装，可定向排列阴极中间层分子，提升有机太阳能电池效率并降低电荷传输电阻。

paper.title: Remote Control of Excited-State Chemistry in Positive Reversibly Switchable Fluorescent Proteins
paper.abstract: Abstract Positive reversibly switchable fluorescent proteins (+rsFPs) are genetically encoded fluorescent labels allowing super-resolution microscopy without the fading inherent in the better established negative (−) rsFPs. Typically, switching is initiated by an ultrafast excited-state isomerization reaction. Here, we investigate the ultrafast photophysics of four structurally similar variants of the archetypal +rsFP Padron, including Padron0.9, Padron2, Kohinoor, and a newly reported “reverse” Kohinoor mutant (Kohinoor S176F) using ultrafast optical and vibrational spectroscopy. Padron0.9 exhibits an efficient excited-state proton transfer (ESPT) reaction in parallel with photoisomerization, whereas Kohinoor and Padron2 do not. Remarkably, introducing the single reverse mutation S176F in Kohinoor restores Padron-like ESPT dynamics, even though the mutation is remote from the proton donor. This result demonstrates that a single amino acid residue near to, but not in direct H-bonded interaction with, the chromophore can govern the fate of excited states. TRIR measurements reveal distinct changes in the local hydrogen-bonding network and chromophore–protein interactions associated with ESPT-active variants and further reveal a key role for H-bonding between the chromophore and an arginine residue through a study of the R66K mutant of Padron0.9. Overall, these results show that subtle mutations shift the excited state between proton transfer and photoisomerization pathways, providing mechanistic insight into photoswitching in rsFPs, thus guiding the design of improved fluorescent proteins for superresolution bioimaging.

paper.title: Universal platform for rapid green surface functionalization of diverse porous membranes for sustainable water treatment
paper.abstract: Surface engineering is pivotal for tailoring membranes to complex water treatment processes, yet conventional strategies often involve multiple steps, toxic reagents, structural alteration, or specialized equipment. Here, we report a rapid, green, and universal surface modification strategy using Fenton-catalyzed hydrogel coating. Within minutes, an ultrathin cross-linked polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) network forms on porous membranes with diverse chemistries, pore sizes, and surface properties without altering their original pore architecture or porosity. The robust coating resists acid, alkali, heat, ultrasonication, and repeated folding. It enhances hydrophilicity, underwater superoleophobicity, and antifouling performance against oil-in-water emulsions, humic acid, and bovine serum albumin. The PVP network also enables uniform and stable deposition of carbon nanotubes, graphitic carbon nitride, MXene nanosheets, and titanium dioxide nanoparticles. The resulting composite membranes exhibit excellent long-term desalination performance. This simple, scalable, and eco-friendly platform provides a versatile route to advanced functional membranes for sustainable water treatment and resource recovery.

paper.title: Adsorbate Site Hopping—More Facts and Fiction: Driving Forces and Relevance for Heterogeneous Catalysis
paper.abstract: Abstract Adsorbate site hopping, defined here as surface-confined migration of adsorbed species or adsorbate equivalents between distinct sites, is a widespread phenomenon in heterogeneous catalysis and includes spillover between different surface phases. Because it enables communication between spatially separated functionalities, site hopping has often been viewed as a route to bifunctional catalytic synergy and, in some cases, to performance beyond constraints imposed by Brønsted–Evans–Polanyi relationships. However, its catalytic value is conditional rather than universal. Downhill migration to a stronger binding site may increase local barriers for subsequent transformation or introduce site-regeneration penalties, while kinetically accessible hopping may remain irrelevant if it does not reduce the energetic span of the catalytic cycle. In addition, apparent rate enhancements assigned to site hopping can arise from other modes of intersite communication, including desorption–readsorption, subsurface or bulk diffusion, ion–electron intersite coupling, catalyst restructuring, or changes in active-site identity. This Perspective develops a thermodynamic and kinetic framework for distinguishing these processes and assessing when site hopping becomes catalytically consequential. We discuss driving forces, hopping barriers, coverage and dynamic surface effects, kinetic signatures, and diagnostic pitfalls, with the aim of clarifying when site hopping can be used as a catalyst design principle.

paper.title: Nonsteady-State Oxidative Modulation of Pt Coordination on CeO2 to Balance the Activity–Selectivity Trade-Off in the Selective Hydrogenation of Nitroarenes
paper.abstract: Abstract Describing and disentangling the catalytic activity–selectivity trade-off remains a fundamental challenge in heterogeneous catalysis, particularly in reactions involving multifunctional groups. Herein, we report an effective strategy to balance this trade-off in the selective hydrogenation of nitroarenes by employing surface hydrogen–oxygen pulse titration under an oxidative atmosphere to initiate nonsteady-state oxidative modulation of Pt/CeO2 coordination. Thermochemical analysis and DFT calculations reveal that the pulsed treatment induces a transient exothermic process, driving the oxidation and structural fragmentation of Pt nanoparticles and gradually leading to the formation of isolated Pt1 single atoms. Atomic-resolution electron microscopy and quasi in situ X-ray spectroscopy further demonstrate that, unlike conventional thermodynamic treatments, this transiently induced evolution results in tunable coordination environments (from nanoparticles to single atoms) of central Pt atoms. In this structural transformation, the constructed Pt1–O2 single-atom sites on the CeO2 surface, with an average Pt oxidation state of ∼+0.9, not only enable preferential adsorption and activation of the nitro group while suppressing undesired hydrogenation of other reducible functionalities (e.g., C═C group) but also retain high H2 activation capability. As a result, the traditional activity–selectivity seesaw is shifted toward an optimized balance, affording outstanding performance in the selective hydrogenation of 4-nitrostyrene (2143 h–1 turnover frequency, 96% selectivity), as well as excellent substrate adaptability (10 types of substrates). This study offers new insights into coordination environment engineering via transient treatments and provides a general approach for the rational design of high-performance catalysts in complex hydrogenation reactions.

paper.title: Disentangling total-variance and signal-to-noise-ratio improves diffusion models
paper.abstract: Abstract Diffusion models have been widely adopted as a powerful generative framework across numerous scientific domains, yet their inherently iterative sampling process remains a significant computational bottleneck. While this is typically mitigated by reducing the number of reverse diffusion steps, sample quality becomes highly sensitive to the chosen noise schedule, i.e., the manner in which noise is introduced and the signal is reduced at each step. Although prior work has improved on the original variance-preserving and variance-exploding schedules, these approaches passively adjust the total variance, without direct independent control over it. In this work, we propose a novel total-variance/signal-to-noise-ratio disentangled (TV/SNR) framework, where TV and SNR can be controlled independently. Our approach reveals that schedules with exponentially exploding TV can be consistently improved by adopting a constant TV schedule while preserving the underlying SNR schedule. Furthermore, we demonstrate that generalizing the SNR schedule of optimal transport flow matching significantly enhances generation efficiency. Crucially, these gains remain consistent across various reverse diffusion solvers and reduce the search space to two independent and interpretable parameters, enabling fast and robust sampling for complex scientific applications, such as molecular structure generation.

paper.title: High-throughput study of electrical conductivity in ordered metals
paper.abstract: Abstract We present a computational framework that integrates machine learning with high-throughput ab initio calculations to screen over 2.8 million compounds for metallic transport. We identify several metallic candidates with predicted high conductivities comparable to that of aluminum (36.59 × 10 6 S/m). We perform full electron–phonon coupling calculations for the top-performing materials, yielding results in good agreement with available experimental data. Our analysis reveals that while the noble metals (Ag, Au, Cu) possess a conductivity that remains difficult to surpass due to their unique electronic structure and low scattering, compounds like LiBePt 2 can achieve good performance by utilizing valence electrons from light elements to shift high-scattering d -states beneath the Fermi level. This study not only identifies novel high-performance conductors but also demonstrates the predictive power of combining statistical learning with detailed ab initio calculations.

paper.title: Force Fields and Simulation Engines: Lessons Learned from Porting Amber ff14SB and ff19SB to GROMACS
paper.abstract: Abstract The GROMACS molecular dynamics simulation package has historically supported a number of molecular mechanics force fields, including Amber. Force fields have evolved over time and continue to do so through refinement of existing interactions and the definition of additional ones to more faithfully match real-world experiments and higher-level quantum chemistry calculations. Although users have provided a number of conversions of newer Amber force fields over the years, the two most recent Amber protein force fields, ff14SB and ff19SB, had not previously been officially ported to GROMACS. A technical challenge is that ff19SB introduces residue-specific backbone dihedral energy correction maps (CMAPs), which required new support in GROMACS for residue-aware force-field preprocessing and topology generation. Unlike older force fields such as CHARMM27, in which CMAPs are parameterized using only atom types, ff19SB extends this scheme with additional amino-acid typing. Here, we describe how we ported and validated the Amber ff14SB and ff19SB force fields for use with GROMACS as AMBER14SB and AMBER19SB, respectively. The ported force fields reproduce the Amber reference topologies exactly, with per-interaction energies matching to within the single-precision floating-point limit (<10–7 kJ/mol). To achieve this level of consistency between Amber and GROMACS, we resolved discrepancies in their handling of fundamental constants, parameter precision, and improper-dihedral atom ordering logic. In long unrestrained ubiquitin simulations, the converted ff19SB reproduces the conformational free-energy profile obtained with the native Amber implementation. This work provides the first official port of an Amber force field to GROMACS in more than a decade, improving feature parity between the two simulation packages. We provide a reproducible porting and validation procedure that can be used for modified variants and future versions of Amber force fields.

paper.title: Competing Effects of Strain and Curvature on Proton Transport through Corrugated Graphene
paper.abstract: Abstract Proton transport through graphene is strongly affected by nanoscale morphology, yet the atomic pathway responsible for enhanced permeation near corrugations remains unclear. Here, using first-principles calculations, we resolve proton permeation pathways through individual hexagonal carbon rings in mechanically distorted graphene. We find that a single corrugation creates a heterogeneous permeation landscape in which different carbon rings exhibit substantially different barriers depending on their local strain and curvature, and the most highly curved region is not necessarily the most permeable. Analysis of the permeation energies shows that corrugation partially relieves local in-plane compression relative to planar graphene under the same imposed compression, thereby lowering the transition-state energy, while the remaining barrier variation among rings within the corrugation arises predominantly from the curvature-dependent stabilization of the adsorbed initial state. In addition, concave curvature produces particularly strong initial-state stabilization because the local orbital orientation enhances the interaction with the adsorbed proton. Consequently, weakly curved carbon rings can exhibit permeation barriers that are lower than those of more highly curved regions. These results show that proton transport through corrugated graphene is governed by the local balance between the transition-state accessibility associated with lattice deformation and curvature-induced stabilization of the adsorbed state.

paper.title: When Reasoning Traces Conflict with Evidence: How Answer Configuration Shapes Evidence Following
paper.abstract: A reasoning trace retained at answer time plays two roles: it can raise accuracy, and it can compete with the current evidence when the two disagree. We disentangle these roles by crossing verified evidence versions with the traces generated from each and answering from the same traces and evidence under two configurations: continuation of the model's own thinking and a separate answer call. Across three model families (gpt-oss, Gemma4, Qwen3) on HotpotQA and MuSiQue, the separate call raises evidence-following over continuation by 29.9 to 60.6 points. On the same pairs, removing the trace lowers accuracy by similar amounts under both configurations. Yet continuation repeats the stale conclusion in most conflicts, and the separate call follows the current evidence far more often. Benefiting from a trace and deferring to it are therefore distinct properties. Further analyses show that the final line of a trace carries most of its value, gold evidence helps most before the trace is written, distractors weaken correction under a separate call, and renewed reasoning, unlike a verification instruction, follows the current evidence in most conflicts. Because trace deletion alone cannot reveal which source an answer follows, evaluations should report both properties together with the answer configuration.

paper.title: FlowMaker: From Tasks to Cost-Efficient Generative AI Workflow Deployments
paper.abstract: Generative AI workflows execute user tasks by composing sequences of LLM calls, where each call performs a sub-task (e.g., summarization or translation), forming a workflow. Executing such workflows requires decisions over workflow structure, model assignments, and deployment configurations, which jointly determine latency, cost, and accuracy under dynamic workloads and resource constraints. Existing systems optimize these decisions in isolation or fix them early, leading to suboptimal cost and goodput. We make two key observations. First, efficient serving requires jointly exploring all combinations of workflows, model choices, and deployment configurations under dynamic cluster state. Second, reuse of deployed LLMs is critical for reducing cost, but must be performed on-the-fly, as reuse depends on current load and resource availability. Together, these make selecting a workflow-variant-a combination of workflow, models, and deployment configuration-a time-critical problem. We present FlowMaker, which exposes a task-level interface and selects workflow-variants on behalf of users. To realize this, we design a constraint-guided load-aware pruning algorithm for fast, on-the-fly decisions. FlowMaker improves goodput by up to 10.14$\times$ and reduces cost by up to 2.77$\times$ compared to state-of-the-art baselines, including Murakkab.

paper.title: Understanding When Reflective Prompt and Skill Optimization Helps on Locally Served Reasoning Models: A Two-Model Study of GEPA and SkillOpt
paper.abstract: Reflective text-space optimizers such as GEPA and SkillOpt have reported large gains on frontier and mid-size models. We test replication across two reasoning-native target-serving configurations: DeepSeek V4 Flash through DwarfStar and Qwen3.8-27B through LM Studio. For each target, we evaluate the same held-out tasks and four conditions - minimal baseline, GEPA prompt, SkillOpt skill, and manually engineered prompt - on HotpotQA (n=500 per condition) and MATH-500 (n=250). In the primary Qwen v2 rerun under the same frozen protocol, GEPA selects the HotpotQA seed and exactly reproduces baseline behavior, whereas SkillOpt's validation gain reverses into held-out degradation. On MATH-500, GEPA raises exact match from 0.828 to 0.904 while reducing latency but increasing token consumption, so lower response time does not imply lower token cost. DeepSeek likewise shows its strongest GEPA effect on MATH-500 (0.852 to 0.908). Across both targets, GEPA's strongest gains occur on MATH-500, while neither optimizer improves the HotpotQA baseline. Optimization is therefore task- and method-dependent, and validation gains may reverse on held-out evaluation. An earlier Qwen run is retained as serving-sensitivity evidence. These results suggest that textual headroom for a model-task pair and the observed effect of a text-space optimizer are more informative when decomposed into content/reasoning, answer-realization/evaluator alignment, and serving-completion/reliability. The cross-benchmark pattern further suggests that optimization may benefit from low-ambiguity, actionable evaluation signals.

paper.title: Efficient deduction of encoded local response within a thermodynamically perturbed folded protein
paper.abstract: Externally imposed perturbations can subtly reshape protein structure and mechanics prior to the emergence of global unfolding signatures. Delineating locally sensitive zones, however, can pose immense challenges. Subjecting a small folded protein to isotropic pressure spanning 0.001–10 kbar, we develop a simplified and interpretable computational framework to characterize local responses embedded within its conformational ensemble. Pairwise mechanical stiffness descriptors are treated as high-dimensional mechanical fingerprints and projected using linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to identify the pressure ranges that maximally separate conformational populations. To attribute the discriminative mechanical changes to specific residues, we combine the LDA model with SHapley Additive exPlanations, yielding a ranked set of locally responsive sites. While the overall rigidity landscape of the protein shows only modest pressure dependence, the top-ranked residues exhibit pronounced, pressure-specific alterations in solvent association. Radial distribution functions and tetrahedral order metrics reveal significant reorganization of hydration structure around the leading hotspot across the LDA-inferred transition region, whereas low-ranked sites display weak or nonspecific hydration changes. Together, these results connect global thermodynamic perturbation to localized mechanical and hydration responses and suggest a practical route for prioritizing mutation sites and mechanistic hypotheses in perturbed biomolecular systems.

paper.title: Crossover from Asymmetric to Symmetric Electrowetting Linked to Double-Layer Restructuring
paper.abstract: Abstract Voltage-controlled wetting at solid–liquid interfaces is central to the performance of a range of electrochemical and microfluidic technologies, yet the molecular basis of polarity-dependent electrowetting remains unresolved. Classical electrocapillarity predicts a symmetric dependence of contact angle on applied potential, but experiments and simulations frequently exhibit pronounced asymmetry. Here, combining electrowetting measurements with atomistic simulations, we show that asymmetric wetting at aqueous carbon interfaces arises from the structure of the electrical double layer. By investigating aqueous KF and LiCl electrolytes at graphitic interfaces across lower concentration and water-in-salt regimes, we identify a crossover from strongly asymmetric electrowetting at lower concentration to a symmetric response at high concentration for KF, while LiCl retains a pronounced asymmetry. This transition is accompanied by corresponding changes in the solid–liquid interfacial tension, demonstrating that polarity-dependent wetting can arise from voltage-dependent molecular restructuring of the interfacial liquid, which modifies the interfacial thermodynamics, without invoking faradaic processes. We introduce interfacial connectivity, defined by the network of intermolecular interactions within the first adsorption layer, as a molecular descriptor linking double-layer structure to macroscopic wetting behavior. These results demonstrate that electrolyte-controlled electrowetting can recover the symmetric electrocapillary limit under appropriate conditions and establish a unified framework connecting double-layer structure, interfacial free energy, and voltage-dependent wetting.

paper.title: Mapping Collective Electron-Density Rearrangements at Oil–Water Interfaces Using Optimal Transport
paper.abstract: Abstract The electronic and spectroscopic properties of aqueous hydrophobic interfaces continue to be a topic of active research. One such open question is rooted in the origin of the apparent negative charge of oil droplets. Here, we deploy an information-theoretic optimal transport approach dubbed VIPER-CT (Voronoi-Informed Partitioning of Electron Redistribution for Charge Transfer), to construct the electronic T-matrix derived from the real-space electron density determined from first-principles simulations of an extended decane-water interface, sampled using neural-network-based Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics. This matrix operationally separates directional interphase charge transfer (CT) from intraphase density rearrangements. While decane-water molecular clusters of various sizes show small net CT from decane to water, the extended interface displays a systematic opposite electronic asymmetry, yielding a net CT from water to the hydrocarbon phase producing an average surface charge density of ∼0.003 e– nm–2 on the oil phase. This imbalance is accompanied by much larger intraphase self-polarization, particularly within the hydrocarbon phase, demonstrating that collective many-body polarization dominates the interfacial electronic response.

paper.title: Effect of interfacial water structure on the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions
paper.abstract: Weakly hydrated anions tend to partition to macromolecular surfaces, leading to salting-in at low salt concentrations. Recent studies have linked this partitioning to disruption of the interfacial water network. Here, we investigate the role of interfacial-water-network disruption as an indirect driving force for the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions and its interplay with direct solute-anion and anion-cation interactions using computer simulations. We study the adsorption of SCN$^{-}$ and I$^{-}$ ions on a model extended solute that interacts with water and ions only via van der Waals interactions. To probe the indirect contribution, we increase the effective solute size while simultaneously decreasing the attractive solute-water and solute-ion interactions, resulting in progressively greater disorder in the interfacial water network in pure aqueous solutions. Our results show that iodide adsorption increases despite weaker direct solute-iodide interactions and correlates with greater disruption of the interfacial water network, although iodide remains depleted overall. In contrast, preferential adsorption of SCN$^{-}$ decreases, but the rate of decrease becomes smaller at higher levels of interfacial-water-network disorder. This suggests that the indirect contribution associated with interfacial-water-network disruption partly compensates for the decrease in SCN$^{-}$ adsorption caused by weaker direct solute-SCN$^{-}$ interactions. Our results highlight that the indirect contribution associated with interfacial-water-network disruption promotes the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions on macromolecular surfaces, while the extent of adsorption also depends on direct solute-ion interactions and anion-cation pairing. This interplay may be particularly important in mixed-salt solutions, where the presence of strongly hydrated anions can also disrupt the interfacial water network.

paper.title: Quantum tunneling on water. III. An asymmetric Marcus-based electron-transfer model for microdroplet redox chemistry
paper.abstract: Water microdroplets support a broad range of spontaneous redox reactions at rates that often exceed expectations from bulk solution, yet a microscopic framework that is both mechanistic and quantitatively predictive across diverse acceptors remains lacking. In Parts I and II [C. Zhuang, N. Qian, and W. Min, J. Chem. Phys. 164(22), 224709 (2026) and J. Chem. Phys. 164(22), 224710 (2026)] of this series, we described microdroplet redox chemistry as concerted electron tunneling from partially solvated interfacial hydroxide to acceptors within a symmetric Marcus framework. Here, we extend this picture to an asymmetric, solvation-state-dependent framework in which reactant- and product-side reorganization energies are unequal and evolve along the interfacial dehydration coordinate. This generalization captures the partial breakdown of a single linear-response solvent coordinate at heterogeneous water interfaces and yields a corresponding asymmetric rate expression. Reanalysis of previously studied acceptors confirms consistency with the earlier symmetric model, while revealing that asymmetry becomes decisive in strongly imbalanced cases. Proton reduction by interfacial hydroxide provides a striking example: charge recombination generates highly unequal solvation responses and alters the predicted kinetics by orders of magnitude. Comparison with three independent experimental datasets yields rate estimates in encouraging agreement with experiment, supporting proton reduction as a baseline pathway of intrinsic microdroplet reactivity. A paired comparison of pyridine and benzene further defines a practical boundary for interfacial redox observability. Finally, parity analysis of all acceptors examined across this series shows broad quantitative agreement between predicted and experimentally inferred rate constants. Together, these results establish an asymmetric Marcus framework as a more faithful and predictive theory of electron transfer at heterogeneous water interfaces.

paper.title: Spectroscopic–Catalytic Onset Decoupling in Energy Electrocatalysis: Evidence, Mechanistic Hypotheses and Research Priorities from 250 Studies
paper.abstract: Spectroelectrochemical methods can be used to reveal the chemistry that governs energy conversion and storage at operating interfaces. The review represents 250 primary studies that employed in situ or operando spectroscopy across carbon dioxide reduction, oxygen evolution, hydrogen evolution, battery interfaces and organic electronics. Three findings stand out. First, only five studies in the entire corpus provide paired surface and bulk onset potentials and these reveal offsets from zero to nearly 300 mV. Second, the magnitude of this offset tracks the binding strength of the catalytic intermediate rather than the prominence of its spectroscopic signature. Third, dynamic surface reconstruction creates active phases that differ from the as-prepared material in 147 of 250 systems. The central construct that emerges is onset decoupling: spectroscopic detection of an intermediate does not guarantee catalytic turnover, because binding energetics and site density govern whether accumulated species convert to products. This construct predicts that catalysts with strong intermediate binding will show large offsets and poor activity, while weak binding will produce coupled onsets and high activity.

paper.title: Vibrational Excitation of Water Drives Proton Reactivity with Native Proteins During Mid-Infrared Laser Desorption Coupled to Mass Spectrometry.
paper.abstract: We discovered a vibrational-excitation-driven proton reactivity between proteins and their surrounding aqueous environment during mid-infrared laser Desorption by Impulsive Vibrational Excitation (DIVE). We show that this process, when coupled directly to high resolution mass spectrometry (MS) without secondary ionization sources, produces intact gas-phase ions of proteins retaining their compact conformations. The unexpected multiple protonation states of protein ions are generated through a series of concerted proton transfer processes to protein surface residues. We propose that laser-induced ionization via DIVE is facilitated by sub-nanosecond transient superheating and Grotthuss proton hopping processes. By coupling to high-resolution MS, protein ionization via DIVE opens up an avenue for chemical and structural characterization of proteins and their complexes directly from aqueous and physiological buffer environments.

paper.title: Sterically Shielded Cations Decouple Ion-Exchange Capacity from Water Uptake in Anion Exchange Membranes
paper.abstract: Anion exchange membranes (AEMs) for electrochemical devices must combine high ion-exchange capacity (IEC) with controlled hydration and dimensional stability. Water uptake is commonly rationalized in terms of IEC and intrinsic cation hydrophilicity, but this picture fails when the cationic site is locally shielded by the polymer architecture. Using the poly(bis-imidazolium) ionene Aemion+® as a model backbone-embedded AEM, we find that it absorbs only ~40% of the water taken up by pendant-cation analogues at matched IEC, reversing the trend expected from solution thermodynamics, which identifies its embedded dimethylimidazolium cation as the more hydrophilic one. All-atom molecular dynamics simulations reveal that adjacent aromatic rings create a three-dimensional steric envelope around the embedded cation, reducing first-shell water coordination by 69% and chloride coordination by 62% relative to the free cation in solution. Restricted access to the cation persists for the membrane in hydroxide form. To separate cation chemistry from architecture, we synthesize poly(phenylene oxide) (PPO) membranes bearing four pendant cations—tetramethylammonium (TMA), dimethylimidazolium (DMIm), piperidinium (Pip), and pyrrolidinium (Mpy)—at matched IEC and find that PPO–TMA and PPO–DMIm have indistinguishable hydration despite the substantially higher intrinsic hydrophilicity of DMIm⁺ in solution, with all four cations falling within a narrow hydration window. These results establish local steric accessibility — the ability of water and counterions to occupy the cation's first solvation shell — as a controlling descriptor for AEM hydration. Engineering cation accessibility therefore offers a molecular design strategy for high-IEC AEMs with controlled hydration and swelling.

paper.title: Dramatic pressure-induced slowdown and the soft glassy rheology of water at 2D material interface
paper.abstract: The flow of molecularly confined water has attracted considerable interest in recent years. Yet despite their exquisite character, current nanofluidic devices cannot probe molecular water flow beyond the linear-response regime, while nanomechanical force- based approaches have produced markedly inconsistent results. Here, using tuning- fork-based atomic force microscopy, we tackle these limitations by measuring the full linear-to-nonlinear, shear-dependent viscoelastic rheology of molecularly confined water at various two-dimensional material interfaces -- demonstrating pronounced rate effects in water flow response. The observed rheological behaviors are remarkably analogous to that of macroscopic soft glassy yielding materials and fully captured by a non-linear model accounting for the shear-induced acceleration of the dynamics -- a hallmark of disordered supercooled and metastable systems. We further unveil a pronounced pressure-induced slowdown in nanoconfined water dynamics, with relaxation times extending into the microsecond range and marked material dependence. These results reveal non-linear, glassy rheology as a general feature of interfacial water and offer a route to tunable, non-linear nanofluidic elements.

paper.title: Dynamic Anionic Speciation and Proton Transfer in Choline/Geranic Acid Mixtures Revealed by Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
paper.abstract: In carboxylate/carboxylic acid-containing ionic liquid systems, oligomeric complex anions have been shown to substantially alter transport properties; yet whether such persistent pairing survives in the presence of water remains an open question. The 1:2 choline/geranic acid mixture (CAGE12) provides an ideal case study: a promising therapeutic solvent unavoidably hydrated in biomedical use. Although hydrogen-bonded geranic acid (AGE)–geranate (GE) oligomeric motifs have been proposed and recently characterized spectroscopically, their prevalence and dynamical relevance in the liquid remain unclear, particularly in application conditions. Here, we employ DFT-trained NeuralIL machine-learned molecular dynamics to investigate hydrated CAGE12 containing 8 wt% water. The simulations reveal a highly dynamic hydrogen-bond network centered on GE, in which AGE, water, and choline continuously compete for coordinating the GE. AGE–GE associations are frequently observed but exhibit sub-picosecond lifetimes, indicating that they are transient structural motifs rather than persistent complex anions. Proton-transferred configurations are found to depend strongly on the local hydrogen-bond environment. Rare AGE-rich coordination environments are associated with proton-transferred configurations that remain stable, whereas the more abundant water-coordinated AGE–GE pairs are associated with reversible proton-transfer events and proton rattling. Overall, hydrated CAGE12 is best described as a dynamically evolving hydrogen-bond network in which transient local coordination, rather than persistent oligomeric anions, governs proton transfer and anionic speciation. These results highlight the critical role of water in disrupting complex anion formation in nonstoichiometric ionic liquids, with direct consequences for their transport and physicochemical properties.

paper.title: MARS: Machine-Learned Force Field Framework for Automated Conformational Sampling, Vibrational Spectroscopy, and Microsolvation
paper.abstract: Abstract We present MARS, an open-source Python package for automated conformational ensemble generation, infrared spectrum prediction, and explicit microsolvation of molecular systems. Built on JAX for GPU acceleration and automatic differentiation, MARS is carried out with machine-learned force fields (MLFFs), including SO3LR and MACE, with a four-phase conformational sampling workflow combining metadynamics, multitemperature molecular dynamics, and genetic algorithms. The package provides automated vibrational mode classification using Wilson B-matrix projections and functional group identification via graph-based pattern matching. We benchmark MARS on chemically diverse systems, including alkanes, halogenated aromatics, amino acids, peptides, drug-like molecules, phosphamides, host–guest complexes, and microsolvated biomolecular models. Semiempirical quantum-chemical methods have until now provided the practical state of the art for automated conformational sampling. Our benchmarks show that modern MLFFs can improve upon this paradigm by combining greater accuracy for high-level relative conformer energies with lower computational cost and more favorable scaling with molecular size. IR benchmarks against experimental gas-phase spectra additionally show performance comparable to quantum-chemical methods, with chemically interpretable mode assignments. Applications to alanine peptides, proline/β-cyclodextrin inclusion complexes, alanine dipeptide, and 2-methoxycyclohexanone further demonstrate that MARS captures conformational reorganization, noncovalent binding motifs, solvent-induced stability shifts, and spectroscopic signatures. These results establish MARS as a transferable and accessible platform for ensemble-based molecular modeling with machine-learned potentials. MARS is freely available at github.com/tcpunilu/mars.

paper.title: Poly(Ionic Liquid)-Engineered Interfacial Water Reorganization for Selective Acidic CO2-to-Formic Acid Electroreduction
paper.abstract: Abstract Acidic CO2 electroreduction offers a promising route to improve carbon utilization compared with alkaline or neutral systems. However, maintaining high product selectivity at industrially relevant current densities remains challenging because local CO2 depletion and excessive proton availability intensify the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we develop a bismuth sulfide (Bi2S3) catalyst modified with a long-chain imidazolium poly(ionic liquid) layer (PIL@BS) for electrocatalytic CO2-to-formic acid conversion at pH 2. In a flow cell containing 3 M KCl, PIL@BS catalyst delivers a high Faradaic efficiency for formic acid (FEFA = 98.4%) at a current density exceeding 300 mA cm–2 and maintains over 80% FEFA after 120 h of continuous operation. Even at low 15 vol % CO2 concentration typical of industrial flue gas, PIL@BS retains higher FA selectivity than unmodified BS, underscoring the effectiveness of PIL in suppressing HER under CO2-limited conditions. Structural characterizations and electrochemical analyses reveal that the PIL backbone creates a hydrophobic interface while preserving CO2 affinity and high ionic conductivity, effectively mitigating the flooding issues and enhancing the local availability of CO2. Operando spectroscopies further show that PIL-regulated interface facilitates access to weakly hydrogen-bonded water. Such interfacial water reorganization disrupts the extended hydrogen-bond network, attenuating the continuous proton-relay pathways that promote the competing HER while maintaining localized proton transfer for CO2 reduction. Combined with theoretical calculations, these findings indicate that the PIL-modified microenvironment enables a direct and energetically favorable hydrogenation pathway toward FA formation. This work highlights the PIL-engineered interfacial microenvironment as a key factor for overriding the intrinsic selectivity of a catalyst and enabling practical CO2 valorization.

paper.title: MOFFieldBench: A Machine Learning Benchmark for Continuous Electronic Fields in Metal-Organic Frameworks
paper.abstract: Machine-learning models for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) predominantly rely on atomic structures, whereas electron-density (ED) and electrostatic-potential (ESP) fields remain underexplored as scalable learning representations. These continuous fields encode complementary spatial and electronic information relevant to structure-property relationships, particularly pore geometry and guest-framework interactions, but costly first-principles calculations, storage requirements and the scarcity of systematically aligned datasets limit their broader use. Here we introduce MOFFieldBench, a multimodal benchmark comprising approximately 46,000 MOFs with one-to-one aligned crystallographic structures, ED fields and ESP fields. A unified workflow integrates field generation, error-controlled compression and sparse point-cloud representation, supporting field reconstruction, prediction of 13 material properties, multimodal property prediction and pairwise cross-modal retrieval. ED and ESP provide competitive representations for pore geometry, adsorption and separation properties. Multimodal fusion improves several prediction tasks relative to the best unimodal reference, supporting complementary predictive roles for atomic structures and electronic fields. Learned ED reconstruction closely approximates first-principles reference densities, while predicted-density initialization reduces self-consistent-field calculation time by 13.59\% on average in paired tests. These results support electronic fields as practical, informative learning modalities and establish MOFFieldBench as a resource for studying representation choice, multimodal learning and electronic-field-driven MOF modelling.

paper.title: Heterostructured p‐ and n‐ type Two‐Dimensional Polymer Electrochromic Films for Ambipolar Multistate Optical Modulation
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Redox‐active two‐dimensional polymers (2DPs) are promising as electrochromic layers due to their structural order and permanent porosity. However, most 2DP electrochromic layers can only be used in binary switching, which prevents multi‐state optical profiles from being accessed in a single device. This challenge is in part due to the difficulty of fabricating multi‐layer 2DP devices in which both redox‐active layers can participate in electrochemically driven color switching. In this report, we show how interfacial polymerization methods can provide multilayer, n ‐ and p ‐type 2DP layers that exhibit rapid reversible optical modulation, decent coloration efficiencies (up to 101 cm 2 C −1 ), and high stability over 100 cycles, with both layers actively participating in electrochromic switching. In stacked devices, the 2DP layer directly contacting the gel electrolyte exhibits electrochromic responses (rates, efficiencies, etc.) comparable to those of the corresponding single‐layer device, while the bottom‐buried layer shows a slight reduction in electrochromic performance. We attribute this slightly diminished performance to limitations in ion transport in the buried electrochromic layer, which are more pronounced in conventional non‐porous, multi‐layer electrochromic materials. These observations broadly suggest that multilayer semiconducting 2DPs may be useful in a range of mixed ionic‐electronic conductor applications, where multi‐state or ambipolar performance is desirable.

paper.title: Ion Pairing and Electrochemical Behavior of Al(OTf)3 in Propylene Carbonate Bilal Overton
paper.abstract: The development of practical aluminum-ion batteries requires electrolytes capable of stabilizing multivalent aluminum species while maintaining sufficient ionic conductivity and electrochemical activity. Here, we investigate aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTf)3) dissolved in propylene carbonate (PC) as a potential halide-free aluminum electrolyte using a combined computational and experimental approach. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to optimize coordination structures and predict speciation, redox potentials, and vibrational signatures of solvated aluminum complexes. Cyclic voltammetry reveals electrochemical activity with a reduction onset near 0 V versus Al/Al3+, consistent with computational predictions. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy indicates significant ionic association between aluminum and triflate anions, suggesting the coexistence of free and coordinated species in solution. Scanning electron microscopy of copper substrates after chronoamperometric deposition shows surface features consistent with metal deposition, while X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirms the presence of aluminum-containing species. The electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of approximately 5.4 mS cm-1 at ~0.6 M. These results demonstrate that Al(OTf)3/PC solutions support electrochemical activity of aluminum species but exhibit strong ion association, highlighting key challenges and opportunities for halide-free aluminum battery electrolytes.

paper.title: Boosting Ionomer Oxygen Transport via Pore Confinement in Carbon Supports for Low-Pt Fuel Cells
paper.abstract: Abstract Low-Pt proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are promising for hydrogen energy implementation, yet oxygen transport through ionomer-covered catalyst surfaces becomes increasingly limiting due to the resistance associated with dense ionomer films. Herein, we demonstrate a pore-confinement strategy to manipulate the spatial locality of Pt nanoparticles within porous carbon supports, enabling simultaneous regulation of ionomer distribution and molecular organization. Pt nanoparticles were selectively positioned on the external surfaces (Ptext/PC) or within the internal nanopores (Ptint/PC) of otherwise comparable supports, while maintaining similar Pt loading, particle size, and pore characteristics. Under H2-air condition, Ptint/PC delivered a peak power density ∼1.3 times higher than that of Ptext/PC, but a similar current density in the high-voltage region. Electrochemical analyses reveal that the performance enhancement originates from improved oxygen transport rather than catalytic activity. Wide-angle X-ray scattering and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the Pt nanoparticles confined within mesopores disrupt the dense packing of ionomer backbones, thereby boosting oxygen permeability at the catalyst–ionomer interface. By establishing a direct relationship between Pt locality, ionomer distribution, backbone organization, and oxygen transport, this work identifies catalyst locality as an effective parameter for engineering interfacial mass transport and provides a new design principle for low-Pt PEMFCs.

paper.title: Functional-Group Effects in Biopolymer Binders for Sodium-Ion Battery Electrodes: Interfaces, Rheology, and Electrochemical Performance
paper.abstract: Binders, though typically only a few weight percent of a battery electrode, play an outsized role in determining cell performance and sustainability. Water-soluble green binders have emerged as eco-friendly alternatives that enable aqueous slurry processing and easier recyclability. In this work, we leverage biopolymer-based binders (CMC/SBR, Guar Gum and ι-carrageenan) in sodium-ion battery electrodes (Prussian white cathodes and hard carbon anodes) to demonstrate a new paradigm of sustainable electrode design. Our findings highlight that biopolymer binders (Guar Gum and ι-carrageenan) can effectively “glue” sodium-ion battery electrodes together forming a robust structural network and refine the composition of the passivation layer on electrode interface through the functional groups (hydroxyl, carboxyl, and sulfate bonding). By replacing conventional binders with these green alternatives, high-capacity retention and rate capability were achieved when paired with hard carbon electrodes, all with the added benefits of aqueous processability and sustainability.

paper.title: Kinetic acceleration of phosphate remediation in dilute aquatic environments via photovoltaic-driven solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation
paper.abstract: The kinetic limitations of reclaiming low-level orthophosphate (PO43−) in low-conductivity natural water bodies impede the in-depth remediation of anthropogenic eutrophication. Conventional adsorption and electrocoagulation (EC) methods are hindered by excessive chemical reagent consumption, high electrical energy demand, and substantial metal electrode consumption. Here, we present a solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation (SEE) system that employs an interfacial coupling strategy to integrate dynamic ion enrichment with in situ anodic coagulation. By concentrating PO43− at the solid-state electrolyte interface, the system overcomes inherent mass-transport constraints and enhances ion conductivity in dilute media. This localized concentration gradient accelerates apparent reaction kinetics, achieving a removal rate of 0.197 mg/L·min, minimizing energy consumption to 0.0325 kWh/g P and iron consumption to 3.829 g/g P. Consequently, SEE enables efficient, one-step purification below strict regulatory thresholds ( ≤ 0.02 mg/L, China’s Class I Surface Water Environmental Quality Standard). Validated as a photovoltaic-integrated, boat-mounted unit, this approach offers a robust decentralized solution for natural waters, with techno-economic and life cycle assessments confirming its economic viability and low environmental footprint.
