paper.title: Interhalogen of Iodine Chloride Accelerates Charge Transfer for Efficient Li2O2 Oxidation in Lithium–Oxygen Batteries
paper.abstract: Abstract Li–O2 batteries suffer from sluggish Li2O2 oxidation kinetics at electrode/electrolyte interfaces, leading to large charge polarization and low energy efficiency. Soluble redox mediators (RMs) provide a solution-mediated pathway for Li2O2 decomposition and reduce the charge overpotential. However, the chemical oxidation of Li2O2 by oxidized RMs remains kinetically sluggish, resulting in persistent charge polarization. Herein, iodine monochloride (ICl), an interhalogen compound, is electrochemically generated in situ during the charge process to promote the oxidation of Li2O2. The large electronegativity difference between I and Cl promotes intramolecular charge transfer from I to Cl, creating an electrophilic iodine center (Iδ+) that increases the I–Cl bond polarity and strengthens the interaction with Li2O2. This lowers the decomposition barrier of Li2O2 from 2.39 to 0.77 eV, thereby facilitating its chemical oxidation. The Li–O2 battery delivers a low discharge/charge polarization of 0.52 V, effectively mitigating parasitic reactions at high voltages and enabling an extended cycling lifespan exceeding 800 h. This work provides a valuable design principle for developing redox mediators for efficient Li2O2 oxidation.

paper.title: Spontaneous Ether Hydrolysis on Cryogenic Water Ice Surfaces
paper.abstract: Abstract We report the hydrolytic cleavage of C–O bonds in aliphatic ethers at cryogenic water ice surfaces under ultrahigh vacuum conditions. Ethers are conventionally resistant to hydrolysis, requiring strong Brønsted acids and elevated temperatures for C–O bond activation; their reactivity toward neutral water ice at temperatures as low as 10–50 K is therefore unexpected. Using Cs+ reactive ion scattering and low-energy sputtering in combination with isotopic labeling (H2O vs D2O), we demonstrate that dimethyl ether (DME), tert-butyl methyl ether (tBuOMe), and diethyl ether (DEE) undergo hydrolysis to form the corresponding deuterated alcohols upon contact with amorphous and crystalline D2O ice between 10 and 150 K. Isotopic incorporation establishes D2O ice as the source of the incorporated hydrogen. CH3OD was formed even at 10 K in codeposited DME-D2O films and it persisted on crystalline ice, while tBuOMe exhibited distinct product selectivity through the appearance of a tert-butyl carbocationic fragment in low-energy sputtering. These observations reveal an unexpected chemical reactivity of cryogenic water ice toward aliphatic ethers and establish ether hydrolysis as a previously unexplored low-temperature surface reaction.

paper.title: Mode coupling theory analysis of water dynamics detected by dielectric spectroscopy
paper.abstract: Mode-coupling theory (MCT), one of the most prominent models of the glass transition, also makes various specific predictions for the molecular dynamics in the liquid state of matter. They can be best experimentally tested by evaluating susceptibility spectra covering a broad frequency range. In the present work, we clarify whether the most recent broadband dielectric-spectroscopy results on water, whose glass transition is highly disputed, are compatible with MCT. The so-called fast beta process, expected within this theory, should be detectable at low temperatures only, inaccessible in water due to its inevitable crystallization upon cooling. Therefore, we also investigate data on aqueous LiCl solutions, which can be easily supercooled. We find that all the available broadband dielectric data on these solutions and pure water are well consistent with MCT. Notably, this includes the expected interrelation of the critical temperature dependence of the alpha relaxation to its often-neglected non-Debye spectral shape. Moreover, the available data on the fast beta process, detected in a 14.8 mol% LiCl solution, are also well consistent with the theory. We find a smooth development of the derived MCT parameters with salt concentration which supports the validity of the critical temperature Tc = 222 K and system parameter lambda = 0.55 deduced here for pure water. We also compare the current dielectric relaxation-time results to those determined by other experimental methods and address the question whether information on the controversial fragile-to-strong transition of water can be obtained from such data. Finally, we discuss the significance of the dominant dielectric relaxation process of water for the glass transition as described by MCT, especially considering scenarios questioning its association with the alpha relaxation.

paper.title: SIFT-MS Enables Product-Specific Insight into Electrochemical Pulsed CO2 Reduction in Membrane Electrode Assemblies
paper.abstract: Abstract Pulsed electrolysis is a promising operating strategy for electrochemical CO2 reduction, but understanding how products form, accumulate, and are released during dynamic operation remains challenging, particularly in membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs). Conventional product analysis methods provide limited time resolution, making them poorly suited for resolving product-specific changes during pulses that are on the timescale of seconds. Here, selected-ion-flow-tube mass spectrometry (SIFT-MS) was used as a quasi-real-time analytical technique to measure the product concentrations during pulsed CO2 electrolysis in a MEA using a copper oxide nanoparticle-derived cathode catalyst. Methodology development for the SIFT-MS technique established the sampling and pulsing criteria required for reliable semi-quantitative analysis of the concentration of reaction products. Applying these methodology developments to pulsed electrolysis experiments unveiled how molecular structure influences product retention within the electrode and subsequent transport into the MEA outlet stream under pulsed CO2R conditions. A comparison of the measured concentrations of ethanol, ethylene, and acetaldehyde provided evidence that the formation of ethanol occurs through multiple contributing reaction pathways. The analysis of the measured concentrations of acetaldehyde, propionaldehyde, and 1-propanol provided evidence for the sequential formation of products through which the formation of aldehydes precedes the formation of 1-propanol. Overall, this work establishes SIFT-MS as a product-specific, quasi-real-time analytical technique for probing pulsed CO2R in membrane electrode assemblies that can unveil crucial information to aid in the development of future MEA electrolyzers and operational strategies.

paper.title: Machine Learning for Ionic Conductivity Prediction in Polymer Electrolytes: A Benchmark on Lithium Systems and a Feasibility Study on the Data-Scarce Multivalent (Mg, Zn, Na) Frontier
paper.abstract: Solid and gel polymer electrolytes are central to safer, more flexible batteries, and machine learning has been used to predict their ionic conductivity directly from composition and processing variables. Almost all of this work targets lithium-ion systems, for which large, curated datasets exist. Polymer electrolytes conducting multivalent or non-lithium cations (magnesium, zinc, sodium) are promising lower-cost alternatives but remain comparably underexplored, in part because no public, ML-ready dataset of their measured ionic conductivities exists. Here we validate a standard composition-to-conductivity pipeline (Random Forest and XGBoost regression) on OBELiX, a published dataset of 599 lithium solid-state electrolytes, reaching R2 = 0.79 against a mean-predicting baseline near zero. We then construct, to our knowledge, the first ML-ready dataset of Mg-, Zn-, and Na-conducting polymer electrolytes, systematically mined from the primary and review literature: 135 data points across 105 distinct host-polymer/salt systems. Applying the same pipeline to this new dataset, a tuned Random Forest reaches R2 = 0.47 under leave-one-out cross-validation, or 0.36 under a more conservative 5-fold estimate, well below the lithium benchmark. Through chemistry-informed feature engineering and a nested cross-validation check, we show this gap is driven primarily by data scarcity and literature measurement heterogeneity, not by model or feature choice. We argue the scarcity is itself the central finding: it puts a number, for the first time, on how far behind the multivalent and non-lithium polymer electrolyte literature sits relative to the lithium-ion mainstream. We release the curated dataset and pipeline to support future community data collection.

paper.title: Interfacial Engineering of 2D/2D BiVO4/V2CTx Heterostructures for Enhanced Symmetric Supercapacitor Performance Across Various Electrolytes
paper.abstract: Engineering well-defined heterostructured composites is an effective strategy for improving the electrochemical performance of energy storage systems. In this study, a 2D/2D BiVO 4 /V 2 CT x heterostructure was synthesized via a simple hydrothermal method and, for the first time, systematically tested as a symmetric supercapacitor electrode in neutral (1 M Na 2 SO 4 ), alkaline (1 M KOH), and acidic (1 M H 2 SO 4 ) electrolytes. The composite showed better electrochemical performance compared to pristine V 2 CT x , with specific capacitances of 191.5 F g -1 , 107 F g -1 , and 239 F g -1 in Na 2 SO 4 , KOH, and H 2 SO 4 , respectively, at 0.016 A g -1 . A high energy density of 83.3 Wh kg -1 at 147.5 W kg -1 was achieved in the neutral electrolyte, along with excellent rate capability and Coulombic efficiency. These improvements arise from the synergistic interaction between BiVO 4 and V 2 CT x , which increases active site accessibility and promotes efficient ion and electron transport. Overall, the results show that the BiVO 4 /V 2 CT x heterostructure is a promising and versatile electrode material for high-performance supercapacitors.

paper.title: Experimental umbrella sampling of a rotary nanomachine
paper.abstract: The free-energy landscape of a molecular system, which describes its free energy as a function of a few collective coordinates, governs its dynamics and function, but is challenging to determine experimentally. In molecular simulations, enhanced-sampling methods such as umbrella sampling use bias potentials to access regions of this landscape that are rarely visited by equilibrium fluctuations. Here, we transfer this concept to a single-molecule experiment: we combine electric-field biasing, in situ calibration of the bias potentials, and statistical reweighting to reconstruct the angular free-energy landscapes of rotary DNA nanomachines. The method resolves barriers exceeding 10 kBT and detects changes in local landscape shape caused by small modifications of the stator design. A systematic analysis of bias calibration, sampling, and finite-exposure averaging establishes the conditions required for accurate reconstruction. Experimental umbrella sampling thus relates nanoscale structure to the underlying free-energy landscape and supports the physics-informed design of artificial molecular machinery.

paper.title: Macromolecular association creates dispersity of components that determines liquid–liquid phase separation of oppositely charged polyions
paper.abstract: Developing insight into liquid–liquid phase separation in complex polyelectrolyte mixtures has acquired new urgency considering the role this process plays in the formation of biomolecular condensates, which are involved in diverse processes including, stress response, signal transduction, metabolism, gene regulation, and many human diseases. Condensates can be viewed as a biological membraneless structure situated, in scale and function, between macromolecules and cells. The physical properties of, and the physico-chemical environments within, condensates are very important determinants of their biological function. These properties and environments are determined by the phase separation process. Earlier experimental work in one of our laboratories characterized in detail a phase separation process in solutions of oppositely charged polypeptides. Considering new information being developed on macromolecular association in homogeneous solutions of oppositely charged polyions, we have revisited our earlier data looking into the influence of intermolecular association on the outcome of the phase transition. Such influence is clearly established in this Brief Report. We demonstrate that dispersity of species in homogeneous solution owing to macromolecular association affects phase separation by creating an open miscibility gap, leading to a dependence of the phase compositions on the initial polymer volume fraction. It is very likely that this plays a significant role in the formation of condensates in the biological context that may have been overlooked.

paper.title: Learning the Geometry of Materials Space with Trained Neural Tangent Kernels
paper.abstract: Neural networks trained to predict materials properties learn representations whose physical content can be difficult to extract. We use the neural tangent kernel (NTK), evaluated at trained parameters, to recover the geometry learned by a network that predicts superconducting transition temperatures from elemental composition alone. Kernel ridge regression with the trained NTK closely reproduces the network's predictive performance and substantially outperforms regression with the initial kernel. Spectral analysis and multidimensional scaling reveal a geometry dominated by a small number of directions. Clustering and local neighborhood analysis organize compounds into recognizable superconducting families and connect materials with related chemical and correlated-electron properties despite substantial differences in $T_c$. These results establish trained tangent kernels as practical probes of learned materials representations, connecting property prediction with the exploration of materials space.

paper.title: Grassmannian Density Learning for Physically Consistent Kohn–Sham Electronic Structure Prediction
paper.abstract: Deep-learning electronic-structure models show great potential to accelerate first-principles calculations, with broad implications for materials science, biology and drug discovery. Yet no consensus has emerged on which physical quantity should be modeled to represent electronic states. As two fundamental quantities that arise naturally in Kohn–Sham density functional theory, the Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian and electronic density have attracted the most attention. Hamiltonian prediction, however, devotes substantial modeling capacity to degrees of freedom that do not affect the occupied electronic subspace, whereas direct regression of density matrices or real-space densities removes this redundancy but cannot ensure that the prediction represents a physically admissible electronic state. Motivated by the fact that electronic states themselves reside on a constrained manifold, we observe that predicting coordinates directly on this manifold can simultaneously eliminate redundant degrees of freedom and preserve physical admissibility. Here we introduce GeoK, a framework that predicts compact occupied–virtual orbital-rotation generators as coordinates on the manifold of electronic states, thereby ensuring each prediction corresponds to a valid electronic state of the target molecular system. We further develop a neural-network architecture tailored to this geometric prediction task. Across in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks, as well as downstream applications, GeoK consistently improves electronic-state prediction over the evaluated Hamiltonian and unconstrained densityregression baselines, while supporting robust deployment in downstream first-principles workflows. These results establish orbital-rotation generator prediction as a principled and reliable paradigm for intrinsic electronic-state modeling, opening a route towards more accurate and transferable deep-learning electronic-structure models.

paper.title: Support Protection Mechanism Enables Efficient and Stable Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers
paper.abstract: Abstract Designing oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and long-term stability remains a critical challenge for the development of alkaline anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs). Here, we uncover a unique support protection mechanism in which lattice-confined ruthenium (Ru) single atoms offer robust protection for the spinel Co3O4 support, realizing outstanding stability in AEMWEs. Theoretical calculations and structural characterizations reveal that lattice confinement promotes the formation of robust Ru–O–Co bridges by simultaneously shortening the Co–O and Ru–O bond lengths, thereby suppressing Co dissolution and optimizing the electronic structure for efficient catalysis. Furthermore, in situ electrochemical analysis demonstrates that the lattice confinement of Ru atoms accelerates OER kinetics through facilitated proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) steps and partially activated lattice oxygen. As a result, the RuLCA-Co3O4 dominated by the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) exhibits a lower overpotential of 260 mV at 10 mA cm–2, which is lower than that of RuSCA-Co3O4 dominated by the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) pathway. Meanwhile, the lattice-confined RuLCA-Co3O4 exhibits nearly 9-fold lower Co dissolution compared to surface-coordinated RuSCA-Co3O4 after an accelerated durability test (ADT). Moreover, RuLCA-Co3O4 maintains an outstanding stability for over 1000 h in an AEMWE system with a low degradation rate of 88.1 μV h–1, outperforming RuSCA-Co3O4. This work establishes lattice confinement as an effective strategy to decouple activity-stability trade-offs in alkaline OER and provides a viable design principle for durable AEMWE anodes.

paper.title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Slaked Lime Utilizing a Diaphragm Flow Cell
paper.abstract: Abstract Slaked lime (Ca(OH)2) is one of the most widely utilized chemicals, with applications in diverse industries including construction, mining, water treatment, and chemical manufacturing. Currently, Ca(OH)2 is synthesized by coal-fired calcination of CaCO3 to make CaO, followed by exothermic hydration. Converting CaCO3 into Ca(OH)2 using electrochemically generated acid and base has attracted great interest because it could be powered by renewable electricity and would generate the CO2 byproduct in a pure form. Previous electrochemical Ca(OH)2 syntheses have incorporated the processing of calcium salts within the electrochemical cell to avoid acid–base recombination losses, but these cells have poor stability and high energy demand. Herein, we show that production of high-salinity acid and base solutions using a diaphragm flow cell (DFC) coupled with ex situ processing of CaCO3 substantially improves the efficiency of electrochemical Ca(OH)2 production. Using a closed loop with a simple KCl salt solution, we demonstrate the synthesis of >99% pure Ca(OH)2 for 0.088 to 0.10 kWh per mole at productive current densities of 158 to 334 mA cm–2.

paper.title: A Single-Li+ and Electron Mixed Conductor via Intrinsic Ion-Carrier Implantation in a Metal–Organic Framework
paper.abstract: We report a crystalline metal–organic framework (MOF) that enables efficient Li+ and electron conduction, where a triphenylene ligand functionalized with a propylsulfonate group is designed and utilized to introduce mobile Li+ ions while forming extended conjugation for electron transport. The resulting MOF exhibits a mixed conduction behavior in the solid state with a Li+ conductivity of up to 1.10 mS cm−1 and an electronic conductivity of 15.81 mS cm−1 at room temperature, together with a Li+ transference number close to 1.0. Mechanistic studies reveal that the conformationally dynamic propylsulfonate groups facilitate Li+ transport with low energy barriers in a manner resembling wobbling paddle wheels, and the rigid, conjugated scaffold promotes electronic conduction through in-plane π–d orbital coupling and interlayer interactions. This work establishes an effective bottom-up route for constructing crystalline, porous mixed Li+-electron conductors, offering a new platform for solid-state electrochemical devices requiring synchronized ion and electron transport.

paper.title: Challenging Atomistic Foundation Models on Disordered Carbons
paper.abstract: Foundation machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) promise broad transferability, yet their out-of-domain reliability is hard to establish. Here, we use pure and O/H-containing disordered carbon spanning multiple phases, competing hybridisations and porous frameworks to stress-test six popular foundation MLIPs. We first screen all six on density functional theory (DFT) energy and force errors and binding curves, then subject four to melt-quench-anneal molecular dynamics and evaluate the resulting structural observables. Binding curves and O/H-containing trajectories reveal unphysical extrapolation and dynamical failures that low DFT energy and force errors fail to reveal. Of the models tested, MACE-MH-1 is the most consistently robust, with low DFT errors and stable MD. Despite differing architectures, OMAT-based models share structural biases, highlighting the importance of training coverage. All four models generate structures of nanoporous carbon that reproduce the principal experimental and specialised carbon potential signatures. Incorporating O/H leaves short-range order largely unchanged but shifts pore-size distributions towards larger pores. These results emphasise the need for application-specific validation and extend molecular dynamics modelling of nanoporous carbon towards experimentally realistic structures.

paper.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Free Energy Calculations by Generalized Hierarchical Bayesian Inference
paper.abstract: Abstract Free energy calculations are routinely used to study molecular processes inaccessible to unbiased molecular dynamics, but their utility ultimately depends on knowing when and how much their predictions can be trusted. Uncertainty estimation is therefore essential for distinguishing genuine physical features of a free energy profile from artifacts arising from limited simulation data or inadequate sampling. Gaussian processes have emerged as a powerful framework for reconstructing free energy profiles together with predictive uncertainties. However, existing implementations typically condition on fixed hyperparameters and observation noise, preventing predictive uncertainties from adapting to the information content of the simulation data. Here, we develop a generalized hierarchical Gaussian process framework that accounts for these neglected sources of uncertainty. Applications to umbrella sampling and extended Lagrangian metadynamics of peptide-lipid membrane interactions demonstrate that the resulting uncertainty estimates track reconstruction errors across a wide range of sampling and data conditions.

paper.title: Load-Balanced Neural-Network-Aided Adaptive Tabulation of Phase Equilibria for Transcritical Multiphase Flows
paper.abstract: Simulating high-pressure transcritical flows with phase change is critical for advanced propulsion, yet traditional first-principles approaches, vapor-liquid equilibrium (VLE) calculations, consume most of the runtime and frequently fail to converge. Standalone machine learning models introduce heavy evaluation overhead across large grids, while dynamic tabulation still relies on fragile iterative solvers. To resolve these limitations, this study introduces a hybrid In-Situ Adaptive Tabulation and Artificial Neural Network (ISAT-ANN) framework. A pre-trained ANN replaces the iterative solver during table expansion to guarantee crash-free operation, while ISAT enables rapid data retrieval via local linear interpolation. To eliminate parallel load imbalances, an O(N) greedy load-balancing algorithm redistributes computational tasks across cores. Coupled with Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR), the framework was validated on a Mach 5 shock-droplet interaction benchmark. It accurately captured shock-interface dynamics without instability, achieving a 2.30 times speedup in thermodynamic calculations on a single core and 2.62 times in parallel over standalone ANNs, with AMR providing an additional 2.92 times overall efficiency boost. This plug-and-play framework offers a stable, scalable path for high-fidelity multiphase flow simulations.

paper.title: Electrochemically-driven dynamic surface chemistry breaks the selectivity-conversion tradeoff in the oxidative coupling of methane
paper.abstract: The partial oxidation of methane to C2 products such as ethylene (C2H4) and ethane (C2H6) is a notoriously challenging catalytic reaction since the key properties, namely the C2 selectivity and CH4 conversion, scale inversely with each other. Despite decades of research on catalyst design, this fundamental C2 selectivity-CH4 conversion tradeoff remains a preeminent challenge.1 While traditional thermochemical catalyst design approaches seem inadequate to surmount said challenge, the electrochemical oxidative coupling of methane (EOCM) presents an alternative approach to enhance catalytic performance by dynamically altering the working state of the catalyst. In this study, we use (La, Sr)1-xTiO3±δ as a model system to demonstrate how electrochemistry enables one to dynamically tune the surface chemistry for enhancing C2 selectivity. Depending on the bulk composition, we observe either step changes in C2 selectivity or even a continuously increasing C2 selectivity trend by using La0.24Sr0.60TiO3-δ: this composition, once electrochemically activated, can break the traditional OCM tradeoff. We demonstrate that any C2 selectivity enhancement effects are determined by the surface La/Ti and Sr/Ti ratios which dynamically evolve under electrocatalytic conditions. The enrichment of La at these surfaces is central to enhanced C2 selectivity values and is crucially modulated by both the initial surface and bulk composition. The results presented herein highlight the potential of electrochemical materials activation for overcoming traditional challenges in partial methane oxidation and provide guidance on materials design for maximizing the C2 selectivity of EOCM.

paper.title: Classical 1H NMR correlation rules as diagnostic tests: likelihood ratios from 168,211 experimental spectra
paper.abstract: How much does a signal between 3.3 and 4.5 ppm say about a proton on a carbon bearing oxygen? The correlation tables used to read 1H NMR spectra state where each proton type resonates, but not how much observing, or failing to observe, a signal in that range should change a chemist’s belief. We measured this for 42 single-signal correlation rules and coupling rules transcribed from two open teaching sources, treating each rule as a diagnostic test and computing positive and negative likelihood ratios (LR+ and LR−) on two independent collections of experimental spectra with known structures: 160,038 literature peak lists from NMRexp and 8,173 atom-assigned spectra from nmrshiftdb2. Rules and scoring were frozen before the confirmatory data were examined; the sources state positions and coupling ranges, and the integration and multiplicity clauses we scored are our formalisation of what those rules imply. The rules fall into two regimes. Windows in uncrowded regions carry real evidence (aldehyde C-H LR+ 34 and 20 on the two collections, carboxylic acid O-H 11), while no window between 1.0 and 4.5 ppm exceeds LR+ 3.5 by position alone (median 1.6 and 2.3 on the two collections), because the protons of other environments occupy it: the environment a window describes accounts for a median of 20% of the assigned signals inside it. A reported integration recovers part of the crowded region (alkyl methylene LR+ 2.5 to 38), and several of the strongest effects are negative observations that the tables do not quantify (no reported signal between 6.5 and 8.0 ppm, LR− 0.011 for an aromatic C-H). The published windows are narrower than the environments they describe, and LR+ agrees between the two collections (Spearman ρ = 0.92). A coupling constant considered without regard to which signal carries it holds little information; tied to the shift region of the protons the rule concerns, in an analysis added after the confirmatory run, it gains up to thirteen-fold. In a secondary analysis in the reciprocal direction, from structure to expected shift, the additive increment rules of the standard reference tables, audited on 73,049 assigned protons, predict benzene ring protons to 0.14 ppm and protons on sp3 carbon to 0.35 ppm, with heavy-tailed errors that call for a robust likelihood. Together the results give the qualitative tables a quantitative form, measured on the information that published peak lists actually carry, that can be encoded in automated interpretation.

paper.title: Anion‐Cation Targeted Regulation Enables Ultrafast and Stable Sodium Metal Batteries at Low Temperatures
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Anion‐dominated solvation and artificial interfacial engineering have been intensively pursued for low‐temperature sodium‐metal batteries (SMBs), yet they face constraints from temperature‐sensitive solvation dynamics and interfacial control. Here we propose anion‐cation‐targeted regulation via Sn(OTf) 2 that simultaneously constructs a solvent‐reinforced solvation structure and electrochemically induces an alloy‐based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) (Na 15 Sn 4 ), which goes beyond the prevailing anion‐centric strategy to address the critical challenges of SMBs at subzero temperatures. Competitive Sn 2+ ‐Na + coordination excludes PF 6 − from the primary solvation sheath, while OTf − and the ether groups of diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (DEGDME) coupling foster a solvent‐dominated configuration, substantially reducing the Na + desolvation energy barrier at low temperatures. This design enables Na||Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 cells to deliver a recorded 1050 cycles at −20°C and 20 C, and nearly 700 cycles at −50°C. Ah‐scale pouch cells sustain durable 450 cycles at −20°C, with a 6 Ah cell reaching 215 Wh kg −1 at 25°C (total cell mass). Our findings resolve the longstanding trade‐off between low‐temperature kinetics and stability in SMBs, offering a new design rationale beyond conventional interfacial engineering.

paper.title: Enhancing Propanol Production from CO2 Reduction with a Terbium-Doped Copper Nitride Electrocatalyst
authors: Jose Guillermo Rivera de la Cruz
paper.abstract: Abstract Propanol is one of the most complex products obtained from CO2 electroreduction (CO2R). Being an interesting precursor for synthetic fuels and a feedstock for the chemical industry, its electrochemical production has recently raised increasing interest. However, low selectivity for propanol has been achieved so far. Here, via exploring a variety of original lanthanide-doped copper nitride materials, we identified and characterized terbium-doped copper nitride as the most selective catalyst for propanol formation. It allowed CO2R to yield propanol with a Faradaic efficiency of 27% at a high current density of 300 mA cm–2 within a neutral (KHCO3 electrolyte) flow cell, surpassing the performance of previous CO2R catalysts. The high density of undercoordinated nitride-derived Cu sites, combined with the increased oxophilicity of the surface, likely promoted the selectivity toward alcohols. Thorough DFT calculations showed that Tb doping increased the affinity for oxygenate-associated C2* intermediates and lowered the free-energy barrier for reactions coupling the latter with CO* toward propanol.

paper.title: Contact Forces in Microgel Suspensions
paper.abstract: Within a model where micrometer-size soft colloidal particles are viewed as liquid drops, we theoretically study the contact interaction between them. We compute the exact deformation energy across a broad range of indentations and for various model parameters, and we show that it can be reproduced using either truncated superball or truncated spheropolyhedral variational shapes depending on the parameters. At large surface tensions representative of microgels, this energy is pairwise additive well beyond small indentations and can be approximated by a power-law dependence on indentation with an exponent around 2.

paper.title: Enhancing simulations of disordered protein ensembles with chemical shift restraints in coarse-grained models
paper.abstract: With more than one third of the human proteome being structurally disordered, intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) are key contributors to complex cellular functions, despite their highly dynamic conformational ensembles remaining elusive to conventional techniques in structural biology. Coarse-grained (CG) simulation methods thus serve as a gold standard to refine IDP ensembles. These methods, when relying on elastic network models or rigid body to sample secondary structure, are however inherently limited in their capability to model and sample transient secondary structure at a residue-level resolution as informed by experimental data. This fundamental limitation persists despite experimental evidence suggesting that transient structural propensities are a fundamental hallmark of IDP function. Through an artificial neural network capable of predicting backbone chemical shifts from C α -only protein conformations, we present a generalized framework which does not rely on dihedral parameterization to equip one bead-per-aminoacid CG force fields with the ability to sample functional elements of secondary structure. When applied on a large set of IDPs in isolation or condensates, our approach correctly recapitulates both local and global arrangements, yielding experimentally informed ensembles that can inform structure-mediated function and resolve force field limitations. This can yield a fruitful exploration of ensemble-to-function relationships in IDPs, allowing to explore phenomena such as secondary structure propensity and nucleation in condensates, conformationally selected binding motifs across disordered ensembles or conformational preferences of sequence-specific short-linear motifs.

paper.title: Modifier-Driven Proton Conductivity in Hybrid Glasses above 200 °C
paper.abstract: Abstract Compositional tuning is a cornerstone of inorganic glass science, yet analogous strategies remain underdeveloped for emerging metal–organic hybrid glasses. We introduce phosphate modification of zinc imidazolate glass as a route to hybrid glasses with tunable network connectivity and proton-conductive functionality. Melt-quenching of ZIF-zni with benzimidazolium dihydrogen phosphate (BP) affords a series of cm-scale, transparent bulk glasses across a wide compositional range. Systematic characterization reveals that modification proceeds through ligand exchange at zinc centers, increasing the average coordination number from 4 to above 5 and progressively depolymerizing the imidazolate network. Despite macroscopic homogeneity, X-ray total scattering identifies a quasi-periodic ordering at ∼11 Å, and 1H NMR spin relaxation establishes nanoscale phase segregation between ZIF-derived and BP-rich domains of 2–70 nm. This heterogeneity underpins proton transport under anhydrous conditions; conductivities of 10–5–10–3 S cm–1 at 240 °C follow Vogel–Tammann–Fulcher dynamics, confirming that segmental motion couples to ion mobility. Infiltrating the glass into a porous PTFE scaffold yields a composite membrane that achieves 8.4 × 10–5 S cm–1 at 170 °C under humidification and sustains steam electrolysis with near-unity Faradaic efficiency. These results establish network-modified hybrid glasses as a scalable and designable platform for intermediate-temperature solid electrolytes.

paper.title: Mass-independent oxygen isotope fractionation driven by energetic-particle irradiation of icy solids
paper.abstract: Mass-independent isotope fractionation (MIF) of oxygen provides key insights into atmospheric chemistry and the origin of isotopic anomalies in planetary materials. To date, MIF has been primarily associated with gas-phase processes involving symmetry-dependent reaction pathways, most notably ozone formation. Whether analogous effects can arise in condensed phases or at interfaces remains an open question. Here we report laboratory experiments demonstrating that energetic particle irradiation of icy oxide surfaces produces mass-independent oxygen isotope fractionation at temperatures as low as 10 K. Electron irradiation of SiO 2 and Al 2 O 3 substrates in the presence of H 2 O ice results in measurable shifts in Δ 17 O in the underlying solids. The resulting three-isotope relationships include slope-1-like behavior in SiO 2 and Al 2 O 3 and distinct, substrate-dependent trends in Al 2 O 3 , indicating that irradiation-induced defect formation and interfacial chemistry govern the isotope effects. The magnitude of the observed anomalies demonstrates that irradiation-driven processes can generate substantial oxygen isotope heterogeneity in condensed phases. These results identify a previously unrecognized class of MIF and provide a quantitative framework for interpreting oxygen isotope signatures in radiation-processed environments, including interstellar grains and early solar system materials.

paper.title: Unidirectional Hydrogen Migration Through Interfacial Engineering for Promoted Brønsted Acid Catalysis
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Though playing a critical role, the controllable and directional migration of reactive species in chemical reactions is still hard to achieve. Here, we propose an interfacial engineering strategy for constructing a hydrogen spillover nanodiode that channels hydrogen unidirectionally. Such a nanodiode design is materialized in a composite WO x /TiO 2 /Pt catalyst with spatially separated structure, where WO x and Pt particles are dispersed on the outer and inner surfaces of porous TiO 2 nanotubes, respectively. This nanodevice permits forward H migration (Pt→TiO 2 →WO x ) while suppresses the reverse path (WO x →TiO 2 ), as directly evidenced by in situ x‐ray absorption fine structure characterization under hydrogenation and H 2 generation reactions. This rectification behavior originates from the diode characteristics of the TiO 2 –WO x heterojunction, which hinders both proton and electron transfer from WO x to TiO 2 . Consequently, WO x /TiO 2 /Pt accumulates highly concentrated Brønsted acid sites in H 2 atmosphere and thus exhibits superior catalytic performance compared to the closely contacted WO x –Pt/TiO 2 catalyst. Up to 5.3 times higher liquid alkane yield has been achieved over WO x /TiO 2 /Pt relative to WO x –Pt/TiO 2 in the polyethylene hydrocracking reaction. This nanodiode design strategy is general and can be extended to other catalysts/species, offering mechanistic insight and boosting catalytic performance in diverse reactions.

paper.title: FlexUMM: Flexible Representation Learning for Unified Multimodal Models
paper.abstract: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) can integrate understanding and generation within a single backbone. However, it is commonly known that these two capabilities can cause conflicting representations, leading to a central question: how representation and computation should be shared across functionalities? Existing UMMs often rely on a largely fixed structure, where different inputs and functionalities follow the same depth and parameter-sharing pattern. We argue that this assumption is too restrictive: more effective unification requires sharing the computation that supports cross-functional communication while specializing the capacity that becomes task- or input-specific. We introduce FlexUMM, a flexible UMM framework that dynamically decides when to preserve shared computation, when to route specialized capacity, and when to stop further processing. Evidence shows that this flexible allocation improves UMMs along two complementary axes. It improves accuracy by reducing harmful competition between functionalities, and it improves efficiency by avoiding unnecessary computation once an input representation is sufficiently mature. Beyond simple architectural unification from the pre-trained models, FlexUMM works as a model-agnostic, functional plug-in to make existing UMMs more unified, stronger, and efficient. Code is available at: https://github.com/AIFrontierLab/TorchUMM/tree/main/src/umm/post_training/flexumm.

paper.title: CellDiffusion: Enhancing scRNA-seq data integration with accurate inference of cell-cell association
paper.abstract: Integrating single-cell transcriptomic datasets across laboratories, conditions, and technologies remains challenging because of cell type–specific batch effects and heterogeneous biological compositions. Current methods often fail to separate genuine biological variation from technical noise, misaligning distinct cell populations or leaving batch effects uncorrected. To address these challenges, we present CellDiffusion, an unsupervised graph-based model that propagates cellular features through a diffusion process to strengthen meaningful cell-cell associations in data integration. By learning a cell-cell attention network, CellDiffusion adaptively identifies corresponding populations across batches. Our approach applies cell-specific correction in data integration, generating cell embeddings that align cells across batches while preserving intrinsic cell types and developmental trajectories. We validate CellDiffusion across various datasets, including the human endometrium, one of the most dynamic and complex tissues featuring extensive cellular and molecular changes with the menstrual cycle. This framework also improves other essential analyses such as label transfer, clustering, and trajectory inference. CellDiffusion represents a powerful paradigm for accurate single-cell transcriptomic integrative analysis.

paper.title: Reversible zinc oxidation as a route to on-demand hydrogen delivery
paper.abstract: The transition to green hydrogen is limited by the absence of efficient synthetic pathways for on-demand, high-purity hydrogen at decentralized locations. Most solar and wind resources are located far from demand centres, and the infrastructure costs of hydrogen pipelines make them economically unfeasible for widespread deployment. Here we report a reversible energy vector-mediated synthetic pathway that uses metallic zinc for hydrogen distribution. Machine learning-guided screening identified lactate as a ligand that outcompetes hydroxide for Zn(II) coordination in alkaline media, doubling the soluble Zn(II) concentration to 1.12 M and enabling self-sustained, circuit-free hydrogen production. The system operates between 0 and 80 °C with approximately 99% Faradaic efficiency and achieves a volumetric hydrogen capacity of 137.9 to 218.4 kg H2 m−3, exceeding, to the best of our knowledge, many established and state-of-the-art carriers. This approach offers improved safety and practical deployment compared with existing carriers, providing on-demand green hydrogen for remote communities, mobile platforms and off-grid industrial sites.

paper.title: The landscape of gene loss and missense variation across the mammalian tree informs on gene essentiality
paper.abstract: Abstract Patterns of gene and sequence preservation across species provide insight into gene essentiality under natural selection. Here we developed two interspecies constraint metrics across 462 mammalian species: Gene Identity Score of Mammalian Orthologs (GISMO), which quantifies gene loss weighted by evolutionary distance to humans, and GISMO-mis, which measures missense constraint using the ratio of missense to synonymous variation across mammals. Both metrics are strongly correlated with human loss of function, missense and dosage constraint derived from large-scale sequencing studies, yet are largely independent of coding sequence length. GISMO and GISMO-mis identify essential genes missed by existing human-only metrics, particularly short genes. Genes in the most constrained deciles are enriched for rare variant associations in disorders linked to reduced fecundity, including schizophrenia, autism and neurodevelopmental disorders, and show strong enrichment for common variant heritability. These deciles also exhibit reduced copy number variation, consistent with dosage sensitivity. In addition, GISMO improves prioritization of recessive disease genes and captures signatures of homozygous selection across the mammalian tree. Taken together, GISMO and GISMO-mis leverage deep mammalian evolution to provide complementary, length-robust measures of gene essentiality that strengthen disease–gene prioritization and illuminate the selective forces shaping human biology.

paper.title: Layered Double Hydroxides with Interlayer Electrons Activate Strong Chemical Bonds
paper.abstract: Layered electrides are an unusual class of materials in which excess electrons occupy interlayer regions and serve as anionic, charge-balancing species. Many prototypical layered electrides are based on subnitrides and subcarbides, motivating the search for new types of host structures. Here, we use density functional theory (DFT) to characterize a class of layered electrides derived from layered double hydroxides (LDHs). Through an anion–electron exchange process, we predict that several LDH compositions can stabilize an electride state wherein significant charge is confined in the interlayer galleries. We evaluate the thermodynamic and finite-temperature stability of the LDH electrides, demonstrating that the balance between stability and interlayer charge can be controlled through partial anion exchange. DFT calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that the interlayer electrons impart unique chemical reactivity by facilitating the activation of strong chemical bonds, such as the spontaneous dissociation of Br 2 and the reduction of CO 2 to formate.

paper.title: Water regulates interface access and reactivity in CO2 electrolysis
paper.abstract: Understanding interfacial processes is important for achieving efficient CO2 electrolysis at high current densities. Now, two-dimensional correlated operando Raman spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics provide insight into the relationship between interfacial species, water structure and product selectivity under application-relevant conditions, revealing the role of water in regulating CO2 availability at the electrode–electrolyte interface.

paper.title: Electrolytes confined between polarizable surfaces in slit pores with anisotropic permittivity tensor
paper.abstract: We present a method that enables efficient simulations of coarse-grained electrolyte solutions inside a narrow slit pore with an anisotropic dielectric permittivity tensor. The electrostatic equations for polarizable surfaces are solved using a 2D periodic Green’s function method combined with a slab-corrected anisotropic 3D Ewald summation. We apply this approach in Monte Carlo simulations to study 1:1 electrolytes confined between both polarizable dielectric and metallic surfaces. Our results show that dielectric anisotropy strongly reshapes the double-layer structure. While the individual ion–image interactions depend strictly on the bulk-like parallel permittivity, the suppression of the perpendicular permittivity dramatically amplifies direct in-plane ion–ion correlations. Under strong anisotropy, these lateral correlations dominate the thermodynamics completely, rendering the structural profiles of mutually opposing dielectric and metallic boundaries practically identical by forcing the smaller cations directly into the contact plane of the larger anions.

paper.title: Construction of highly coarse-grained molecular models for aqueous electrolytes
paper.abstract: Molecular modelling of electrochemical systems at larger than atomic scales poses particular challenges, not least the ability to represent correct thermodynamic, hydrodynamic and dielectric properties while still being computationally viable for large scale applications. In the case of aqueous electrolytes such as those used in vanadium-based batteries with oxidation-reduction (redox) reactions, both a background medium that can respond to localised electric fields due to high-valence ions and control over ion transport properties are crucial to embed consistently in the model. To this end, we propose the use of Dissipative Particle Dynamics (DPD) combined with a newly-devised highly coarse-grained polarisable water model with pairwise interactions designed to produce realistic thermodynamic behaviour as the basis for the aqueous electrolytes found in vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFB). We consider how the core water model can be modified to incorporate the ionic species found in VRFB catholytes and anolytes, as well as how the DPD pairwise thermostat forces can be parameterised to attain realistic diffusivities for those species.

paper.title: Local Electric Fields at Organic-Inorganic Hybrid Interfaces Drive Electrocatalysis
paper.abstract: Abstract The local electric field generated at organic-inorganic hybrid interfaces can profoundly influence electrocatalytic reactions, yet how molecular interfaces regulate local field distributions and reaction pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we combine grand-canonical density functional theory with in situ surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy to investigate CO2 reduction at cobalt phthalocyanine-copper (CoPc-Cu) interfaces. Density functional theory calculations show that CoPc creates a confined interfacial microenvironment and modifies the charge distribution at the Cu surface, producing non-uniform local electric fields that are experimentally probed using the vibrational Stark effect of adsorbed CO. Theory and experiment reveal that this field heterogeneity modifies CO adsorption across neighboring Cu sites and increases the adsorption-energy difference between adjacent CO intermediates, thereby lowering the barrier for C–C coupling. Consistent with this mechanism, CoPc-Cu exhibits an enhanced C2+/C1 product ratio, particularly at modest cathodic potentials where the confined hybrid interface is preserved. This work provides direct in situ evidence that organic-inorganic hybrid interfaces can regulate electrocatalytic selectivity through local electric-field engineering, offering design principles for field-enhanced CO2 electroreduction.

paper.title: Decoupling Electric‐Field and Short‐Range Cation Effects in Acidic CO 2 Electroreduction
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Alkali cations play vital roles in suppressing hydrogen evolution and enabling CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) in acidic media, yet whether their identity‐dependent promotion originates from interfacial electric fields or short‐range interactions remains under debate. Here, we decouple these contributions by combining dielectric‐aware generalized modified Poisson–Nernst–Planck (GMPNP) modeling, in situ vibrational Stark analysis, and differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS). Low‐coverage 4‐mercaptobenzonitrile (MBN) on Au and Ag serves as an inert vibrational Stark probe of the local field. Both modeling and spectroscopy show that adding alkali cations strengthens the interfacial field under cathodic polarization, whereas replacing Li + with K + produces undetectable field change. Nevertheless, K + enhances CO formation by up to five‐fold relative to Li + , indicating the existence of cation‐specific short‐range effects. Increasing the cation concentration from 10 mM to 100 mM enhances both the field and CO formation without increasing the outer‐Helmholtz‐plane (OHP) cation concentration. Interfacial water spectra further reveal that K + disrupts hydrogen bonding and undergoes greater partial dehydration under CO 2 RR conditions. Thus, cation concentration governs a general field effect, whereas cation identity controls local water environment and short‐range interactions.

paper.title: DeepHartree: A Poisson-Coupled Neural Field for One-Shot Density Functional Theory
paper.abstract: Abstract Linear-combination-of-atomic-orbital (LCAO) density functional theory (DFT) incurs steep costs when it constructs Coulomb terms and iterates the self-consistent field (SCF) equations. Matrix-learning approaches can bypass parts of this workflow, but their outputs inherit the dimensions and conventions of a fixed orbital basis. We introduce DeepHartree, a Poisson-coupled neural field that connects continuous real-space prediction to LCAO electronic structure. An E(3)-equivariant network predicts the Hartree potential, and the Poisson equation converts this potential into electron density. Atom-centered Gaussian fields resolve the near-nuclear region, while a molecule-level correction enforces the electron count. Analytical Gaussian integrals and numerical quadrature connect the predicted fields to the Kohn–Sham matrix. One diagonalization provides estimates of frontier orbital energies and the occupied subspace, and yields the density matrix used to evaluate energy components and initialize SCF. Mean molecular weighted normalized mean absolute errors (wNMAEs) are 0.110% for QM9 and 0.199% for VQM24 on PySCF level-0 grids, increasing to 1.366% and 2.218%, respectively, on level-3 grids. Models trained on def2-SVP densities transfer without retraining to def2-TZVP and def2-QZVP, retaining total-energy accuracy and occupied-subspace agreement. The Hybrid method combines finite differences and first-order automatic differentiation with analytical Gaussian integrals and multilevel quadrature to accelerate field-to-matrix conversion. It achieves near-linear density-matrix construction in both alkanes and PEG chains. For the 1004-atom PEG chain, this construction is 8.75-fold faster than full AD and 7.34-fold faster than converged GPU4PySCF SCF. Without fine-tuning, the QM9 model attains a total-energy MAE of 9.437 meV atom–1 on 1000 larger OE62 molecules. Across the three basis sets, DeepHartree initialization reduces mean QM9 SCF iteration counts by 15.3–15.6%. For a 620-atom organic cage, it reduces total SCF wall-clock time by 12.9%, including initialization. These results establish continuous electrostatic fields as an accurate and scalable interface between machine learning and LCAO DFT.

paper.title: Halide Identity Shapes Ion Pairing and Solvent Dynamics in Aqueous Lithium Halide Electrolytes
paper.abstract: Abstract Predicting whether electrolytes associate or dissociate in water is challenging because direct ion attraction, hydration, solvent caging, and collective reorganization operate on comparable free-energy scales, and subtle changes in their balance can reverse the preferred ion-pairing state. Here, we develop machine-learned potentials trained on density-corrected r2SCAN to investigate how periodic trends across the halide series govern the thermodynamics, structure, and dynamics of aqueous lithium halide electrolytes. The resulting potentials of mean force reveal a systematic shift from the strongly stabilized contact ion pair in LiF toward solvent-shared and dissociated configurations for LiCl, LiBr, and LiI, with apparent dissociation constants spanning nearly 4 orders of magnitude. This thermodynamic progression emerges from the balance among direct ion attraction, hydration shell stability, solvent caging, and water-mediated screening. From F– to I–, the halide hydration shell becomes increasingly diffuse and labile, with faster water exchange and orientational relaxation. These changes provide a microscopic dynamical basis for the progression from structure-making to structure-breaking behavior, accompanied by a shift from strongly suppressed toward modestly enhanced water mobility. The same hydration contrast governs the coupling between ion separation and solvent reorganization during association and dissociation. Together, these results establish a unified molecular connection among association–dissociation equilibria, hydration shell dynamics, and solvent transport in aqueous electrolytes.

paper.title: Flexible force field-based screening and machine learning predictions for CO2 sorption and diffusion in MOFs
paper.abstract: Machine learning offers an efficient route for screening metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), but most existing models rely on rigid-framework simulations that neglect framework flexibility. In this work, DFT-derived flexible force fields were used to calculate CO2 sorption and self-diffusion for 5,418 MOFs, providing the training data for machine-learning models capable of rapidly predicting these properties. We investigated different ML algorithms, featurization methods, and the role of physical descriptors in predicting CO2 sorption and self-diffusion in MOFs. For CO2 sorption, a categorical boosting classifier coupled with Stoichiometric-45 featurization method used with scalar descriptors provided predictive accuracy of 76.1%. For CO2 self-diffusion, we tuned a categorical boosting regressor on revised autocorrelation functions coupled with scalar descriptors and achieved moderate predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.69). These results demonstrate that machine learning trained on properties generated from flexible force field simulations can substantially accelerate computational screening while incorporating key effects of framework flexibility, providing an efficient strategy for discovering MOFs for low-pressure CO2 capture. Summary Computational screening of 5,418 metal–organic frameworks using flexible DFT-based force fields captures framework motion effects on CO2 sorption and self-diffusion. Machine learning models were evaluated across descriptors and algorithms. A CatBoost classifier achieved 76.1% sorption accuracy, while an autocorrelation-based regressor predicted self-diffusion (R2 = 0.69), demonstrating the value of flexibility-aware modeling.

paper.title: Asymmetric Zn‐N 4 Single Atom Sites Facilitate Interfacial Desolvation for Ultrafast Zinc‐Ion Storage
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion hybrid capacitors (ZIHCs) offer a promising route to safe and low‐cost energy storage, yet their rate performance is constrained by sluggish interfacial desolvation of hydrated Zn 2+ ions and the limited electric double‐layer capacitance of carbon cathodes. Here, we introduce a dual interfacial regulation strategy that addresses both limitations through defect‐modulated Zn‐N 4 single atom sites embedded in carbon cathodes. Spectroscopic studies and theoretical calculations reveal that defect‐induced electronic asymmetry downshifts the Zn d ‐band center and generates nonbonding N/C 2 p states near the Fermi level, facilitating Zn 2+ ─H 2 O bond dissociation and accelerating interfacial desolvation. Simultaneously, enhanced electron delocalization increases surface charge density, favoring electric double‐layer formation and rapid charge accumulation. As a result, the optimized ZIHC delivers a high specific capacity of 201.5 mAh g −1 and an energy density of 146.5 Wh kg −1 , excellent rate capability (56% capacity retention at 100 A g −1 ) and long‐term durability (92.1% retention after 110,000 cycles). In situ and ex situ characterizations reveal a surface‐dominated storage mechanism involving facilitated Zn 2+ desolvation and reversible interfacial adsorption. This work establishes asymmetric single atom coordination as an effective design strategy for coupling interfacial desolvation with charge regulation in high‐rate aqueous energy storage.

paper.title: Performance of Neuroevolution Potentials for the Ionic Liquid [Emim][Ac]: A Systematic Benchmark of Four Density Functionals
paper.abstract: Abstract Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) based on Neuroevolution Potential (NEP) models were developed for the ionic liquid 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium acetate ([Emim][Ac]) using first-principles reference data generated with four density functionals: PBE-D3, RPBE-D3, optB88-vdW, and SCAN+rVV10. Using a unified training protocol, the resulting NEP models were systematically benchmarked against structural, thermophysical, transport, and hydrogen-bond-network properties, including radial distribution functions (RDFs), coordination numbers, neutron total scattering profiles, density, viscosity, ionic conductivity, and thermal conductivity. Spearman correlation analysis and weighted composite scoring were further used to establish a property-oriented evaluation framework for MLFF assessment and selection. The results reveal a pronounced dependence of NEP performance on the density functional used to generate the reference data. Although all four models reproduce the dominant local structural features of [Emim][Ac], appreciable differences emerge in medium-range structural ordering and transport properties. The PBE-D3-based NEP provides the most accurate overall description of structural properties, whereas the optB88-vdW-based NEP yields the closest agreement with experimental transport properties, particularly viscosity and ionic conductivity. Analysis of the hydrogen-bond network further reveals systematic relationships among hydrogen-bond populations, residence times, free-ion fractions, and ion transport. These results demonstrate that, for [Emim][Ac], the exchange–correlation functional used for reference-data generation influences the physical fidelity and property-specific performance of the resulting NEP models.

paper.title: The effect of electrocatalyst roughness and morphology on selectivity due to mass transport
paper.abstract: Mass transport can significantly affect electrocatalytic selectivity as surface-bound reaction intermediates are exchanged between the electrode and bulk electrolyte. The underlying desorption–re-adsorption–reaction mechanism allows an intermediate to escape the surface as a partially converted product or re-adsorb for continued conversion, but it is still not clear how the catalyst morphology affects this competition. Here, we focus on the role of the electrocatalyst surface morphology and its effective representation in transport-coupled kinetic models. Using CO selectivity during CO2 reduction on copper as a model system, we compare predictions from a 1D diffusion model, where surface roughness serves as a single morphological descriptor, against a more advanced 3D diffusion model that explicitly resolves the full catalyst geometry. We analyze the results in terms of overlapping diffusion spheres between neighboring catalyst particles and find that the two models largely agree across the experimentally relevant parameter space due to a simple disparity in length scales. As diffusion occurs on a ∼μm scale, spatially resolved features of typical nm-sized catalyst particles are inconsequential. Surface roughness thus emerges as a surprisingly robust descriptor of electrocatalytic selectivity within the desorption–re-adsorption–reaction mechanism.

paper.title: Information content is a general-purpose collective variable for enhanced sampling
paper.abstract: Enhanced sampling methods typically require predefined collective variables (CVs) that presuppose knowledge of reaction coordinates, restricting the discovery of unanticipated transition mechanisms or intermediates. Here, we show that a local measure of information content in atomistic systems is a general-purpose CV for rare event sampling across molecular and condensed-phase systems. The method biases simulations toward information-changing configurations following a well-tempered metadynamics approach, thus balancing novelty and thermodynamic accessibility. Blind exploration of potential energy surfaces enables unsupervised discovery of metastable basins and reaction pathways, including competing transition channels inaccessible to conventional order parameters. We demonstrate the generality of the method across five systems spanning conformational sampling, homogeneous nucleation, glass formation, and solid-state phase transformations. Our approach uncovers non-classical phase transformation mechanisms despite its focus on general information theoretical quantities rather than kinetic or thermodynamic factors.

paper.title: Universality of Lithium Metal and Solid Electrolyte Interphase Descriptors of Coulombic Efficiency Governed by Lithium Connectivity
paper.abstract: Coulombic efficiency (CE) is a key metric governing the cyclability of lithium metal anodes, motivating efforts to identify physicochemical descriptors that correlate with CE. Diverse descriptors spanning electrolyte thermodynamics and interphase properties have been proposed, but their interrelationships and underlying physical origins remain unclear. Here we show that, when evaluated across a consistent electrolyte set, these descriptors exhibit a common hockey-stick relationship with CE that can be unified through the mesoscale connectivity of lithium deposits. A percolation-like transition from isolated deposits to interconnected networks sharply suppresses inactive Li0 formation during stripping, which underlies the common CE transition across descriptors. Tuning plating current density reproduces this transition within individual electrolytes, demonstrating that connectivity is not uniquely determined by electrolyte chemistry. These findings establish lithium connectivity as a common mechanistic basis for diverse CE correlations and provide a framework for interpreting these correlations across distinct capacity-loss regimes.

paper.title: Effective Directionality in Electron-Transfer-Driven Reactions on Bifurcating Multidimensional Potential Energy Surfaces
paper.abstract: Electron transfer (ET) is microscopically reversible under a closed, finite, Hermitian Hamiltonian, yet ET-driven reactions are strongly directional: of several possible products, one is formed and kept. Standard theories explain this through thermodynamic driving forces, free-energy surfaces, or coupling to a continuum of environmental modes. We ask whether the geometry of a multidimensional Born-Oppenheimer surface, combined with relaxation into the molecule's own vibrational modes, can supply this directionality without an external bath. On model surfaces with a reaction coordinate and an orthogonal branching coordinate, the shape of the surface after the transition state decides which product forms within about one vibrational period, independently of barrier heights. Relaxation into a closed, energy-conserving set of internal harmonic modes, an idealized model of intramolecular energy redistribution, keeps that decision for hundreds of vibrational periods, even where the microcanonical equilibrium of the full system (reacting coordinates and modes together, at the same energy) favors the other product almost completely. When the branching follows an electron-transfer crossing between coupled diabatic surfaces, the decision can be quantum, and the same internal modes keep it. The decision is kept when the internal modes drain the exchange coordinate, the motion that carries one product into the other, faster than the products exchange. Across random surfaces, spectral densities and coupling patterns, an a priori estimate of this competition predicts most outcomes, and its failures trace to which coordinate holds the energy. Thermal and quantum modes remove the kept decision before they remove commitment. The irreversibility supplied by the internal modes is statistical, as for any finite bath; the geometry fixes the direction, both which product forms and which motion must be drained for it to be kept.

paper.title: An Always-Accepting Algorithm for Transition Path Sampling
paper.abstract: Abstract We present a one-way shooting algorithm for transition path sampling that accepts every proposed trajectory while sampling the correct transition path ensemble for systems with overdamped stochastic dynamics. The method combines an always reactive path generation scheme with a reweighting procedure that corrects the bias introduced by unit acceptance, improving efficiency by avoiding rejected trajectories. We show its performance on CO2 hydrate formation, where the enhanced efficiency enables the sampling of crystalline channels under conditions inaccessible to conventional algorithms.

paper.title: CRAFT-ε: A Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for the Static Relative Permittivity of Pure Organic Liquids
paper.abstract: The static relative permittivity is an important property in thermodynamic modeling, electrochemistry, and solvent design, but predicting it directly from molecular structure remains challenging because both electronic polarization and molecular dipole orientation contribute to the measured response. Here, we introduce CRAFT-ε (Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for ε), a conformer-resolved molecular descriptor model for predicting the static relative permittivity of neutral pure liquids. Conformer free energies, molecular dipoles, and atom-resolved polarizabilities are obtained from a GFN2-xTB/ALPB 10 workflow. The molecular dipole is decomposed into chemically defined polar-fragment vectors, allowing fitted corrections to retain both the magnitude and relative orientation of local dipolar contributions. Electronic and orientational polarization are combined with a group-contribution molar volume in the Onsager-Kirkwood-Fröhlich relation. A staged parameterization with 41 parameters is applied to nonpolar, polar, and hydrogen-bonding compounds. For 1393 liquids with permittivities between 1.5 and 183, CRAFT-ε reaches a five-fold cross-validated average absolute deviation of 2.40 ({R^2} = 0.93). Conformational averaging 15 is essential for liquids with several polar groups. Compared with an established fragment-based model with 139 parameters, it reaches a similar cross-validated RMSE (3.65 versus 3.41) with about a quarter of the parameters and applies to every liquid of the dataset. The resulting framework provides a computationally inexpensive route from molecular structure to liquid dielectric response and forms a basis for later application to solvent mixtures and electrolyte systems.

paper.title: Rigor & Reproducibility in Electrocatalysis: Best Practices for Kinetic Studies
paper.abstract: Kinetic measurements can support or falsify mechanistic hypotheses in electrocatalysis, but only when rates reflect intrinsic catalytic behavior and models separate kinetic information from experimental artifacts and interfacial complexity. This perspective presents best practices for acquiring and interpreting electrocatalytic kinetic data, including mitigating artifacts arising from transport, ohmic losses, catalyst restructuring, contamination, and incomplete product accounting. Similarly, we provide guidelines for constructing rate expressions that treat elementary charge transfer, adsorption, and surface coverage, which enable interpretation of kinetic observables like apparent transfer coefficients, rate orders, and apparent activation energies that reflect properties of an interconnected reaction network. Mechanistic conclusions are strongest when competing hypotheses are tested against multiple complementary observables, including spectroscopy, isotopic labeling, and theory, enabling meaningful and reproducible mechanistic comparisons across laboratories.

paper.title: Water–Organic Interfaces Drive Molecular Evolution from Squalene to Steroids
paper.abstract: Abstract In living cells, the conversion of squalene to lanosterol requires two dedicated enzymes and proceeds through 2,3-oxidosqualene as an essential intermediate. We show that water microdroplets contacting immiscible organic solvents accomplish this same multistep transformation without enzymatic catalysis. We propose that the oriented electric field across the water–organic interface generates reactive oxygen species that epoxidize squalene and then initiates acid-catalyzed ring-opening of the epoxide followed by a cationic polyene cyclization cascade to yield lanosterol. H218O labeling traced oxygen from water into TEMPO-derived and peroxyacetate ions observed by real-time mass spectrometry. LC–HRMS/MS further revealed C18–C30 reaction products with spectral matches to oxygenated terpenoid and steroid-like structures. We find that ethyl acetate is the most effective organic solvent because it generates peroxyacetic acid at the interface. Simulations show that a preformed protonated 2,3-oxidosqualene model remains hydrated and oriented after placement at the ethyl acetate–water interface, and calculations on microsolvation models indicate that an interfacial water configuration preferentially stabilizes the epoxidation transition state relative to the reactant by approximately 3 kcal mol–1. These results establish a plausible, abiotic pathway for steroid emergence and diversification at water–organic interfaces.

paper.title: Chemo‐Mechanically Robust Li‐Rich Oxide Cathode Interface Enabled By Ion‐Conductive and Antioxidant Binder
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxide (LRMO), characterized by distinctive anionic redox activity, has attracted considerable interest as a cathode candidate owing to the low cost and high energy density potential. However, their practical implementation is severely impeded by the intrinsically sluggish kinetics of the anionic redox reaction and the accompanying interfacial side reactions. Herein, a sodium phytate (SP) crosslinked PVDF binder is developed to enhance interfacial ion transport and suppress mechanochemical degradation from surface oxygen inactivation in LRMO. By tailoring the PVDF crystalline phase for Li + transport and introducing polar groups for enhanced binding, SP ensures a more uniform distribution of electrode components. More importantly, the SP suppresses irreversible surface lattice oxygen oxidation in LRMO, and thus quench the release of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and gaseous O 2 . Thereby, the LRMO@PVDF/SP electrode exhibits substantially enhanced chemo‐mechanical stability and an optimized cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI). It delivers exceptional initial Coulombic efficiency (95%) and discharge capacity (322 mAh/g at 0.1 C), as well as markedly improved cycling stability (maintaining ∼90% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 1 C). This work provides a facile yet scalable strategy for stabilizing the surface lattice oxygen of LRMO cathodes, paving the way for their commercial application.

paper.title: Accelerating Mechanistic Understanding and Prediction of Chemical Selectivity with Foundation Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
paper.abstract: Selectivity in chemical reactions is often dictated by small energetic differences between competing transition states of less than 2 kcal mol -1 . Computational predictions of selectivity for organic and organometallic reactions must reach these levels of quantitative accuracy, while simultaneously navigating the mechanistic and conformational complexity involved. Here, we assess the suitability of foundation machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for this task. We introduce the SELECT50 dataset, a chemically diverse collection of paired selectivity-determining transition state structures, evaluated at the ωB97M-V/def2-TZVPD//ωB97X-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVP level of theory, spanning representative cases of kinetically-controlled stereo-, chemo- and regioselectivities, along with competing mechanistic pathways. We compare the performance of four MLIPs, alongside semiempirical and low-cost quantum chemical approaches, in determining transition state geometries, energetic discrimination, and pathway ordering. The Universal Model for Atoms MLIPs UMA-M-1.1 and UMA-S-1.2 predict relative transition state energies with sub-kcal mol -1 accuracy and mean absolute errors of 0.36 and 0.44 kcal mol -1 , providing saddle points that closely reproduce triple-ζ DFT geometries. DFT single-point refinement further reduced the mean absolute error (MAE) to 0.25 kcal mol -1 , supporting DFT//MLIP as a practical strategy for selectivity prediction. The major reaction pathway was correctly assigned in up to 98% of cases. Beyond individual transition structures, MLIPs reproduce complete organic and organometallic reaction landscapes and enable full-system treatment of selectivity-determining assemblies containing up to 211 atoms. Finally, MLIP-derived transition state energetics strongly track experimental selectivity across Ni- and Pd catalyzed reaction families (R 2 = 0.87–0.90; ρ = 0.80), and with calibration, yield mean held-out MAEs of 0.12 and 0.63 kcal mol -1 . Our results position foundation MLIPs as practical surrogates for the exploration and screening stages of DFT-based mechanistic analyses, enabling the throughput required for large-scale catalyst, substrate, and reaction screening.

paper.title: Nonmetallic Anodes in Aqueous Batteries
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable aqueous batteries are considered as promising energy storage devices due to their low cost and high safety. In rechargeable aqueous batteries, nonmetallic anodes have attracted widespread attention since they generally possess the characteristics of abundant resources, high designability, and dendrite‐free. Although considerable research efforts have been made to design nonmetallic anodes, a comprehensive review about them is still absent. This review presents a systematic overview of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries, including conversion anodes and insertion anodes. Conversion‐type anode materials primarily involve hydrogen gas, chalcogen compounds, and organic compounds, whereas intercalation‐type anode materials focus on metal chalcogenides, Prussian blue analogues, and polyanionic compounds. In addition, their design principles are critically discussed with emphasis on energy storage mechanisms, merits and limitations, as well as compatibility with charge carriers and cathodes. In the final section, future developments and prospects in the design of high‐performance nonmetallic anodes for aqueous batteries are also discussed. It will shed light on the R&D of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries.
