paper.title: Cellulose Coating Altered the Electro-Chemo-Mechanical Evolution of Sodium Thioantimonate Electrolyte in Solid-state Sodium Batteries: An Operando Raman Study
paper.abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) attracted increasing attention due to their improved safety and energy densities; yet electrolyte decomposition and subsequent contact loss limited the interfacial stability of ASSBs. Herein, we report an operando Raman characterization that provides high voltage, time, and spatial resolutions, which enables simultaneous analysis of interfacial decomposition mechanism and morphological evolution. Using Na3SbS4 electrolyte (NSS) and its carboxymethyl-cellulose-encapsulated analogue (NSS-CMC) as exemplars, we precisely contrasted the subtle differences in the two-step reduction mechanism of the two electrolytes. In both systems, Na3SbS3 formed as an intermediate, and Na3Sb binary as one major final product; while the CMC coating altered the kinetics of Na3SbS3 formation and consumption, and extended the formation potential of Na3Sb from 1.35 V (seen in NSS) to 0.50 V (vs. Na/Na+). Oxidation of NSS and NSS-CMC both occur near 2.20 V, although CMC coating altered the crystallinity of the oxidative products. Simultaneously, we captured phenomena that are unique to solid-state electrochemical systems such as particle relocation, morphological change, and reversed reactions. We inferred CMC’s dual role as a voltage barrier and a mechanical buffer in suppressing the electro-chemo-mechanical decomposition of NSS electrolyte. The deep mechanistic insights unravel the exact modification needed for improved interfacial stability.

paper.abstract: Copper is uniquely capable of driving CO2 electroreduction toward multicarbon products, yet its performance deteriorates under industrially relevant conditions due to surface restructuring and increased hydrogen evolution. In this work, we systematically evaluate dilute CuPd alloy nanoparticles with controlled Pd content (2-6 at.%) and well-defined size distribution in a zerogap electrolyzer across current densities ranging from 100 to 300 mA cm-2. We demonstrate that dilute alloying improves the stability of the nanoparticles. At high current densities (200-300 mA cm-2), monometallic Cu undergoes significant degradation, while CuPd dilute alloys exhibit improved multicarbon selectivity and reduced hydrogen evolution. This behavior is attributed to stabilization of active sites against Cu oxidation and restructuring under high-rate while retaining the good selectivity of Cu, which is supported by in situ x-ray absorption spectroscopy and first principles calculations. paper.title: A machine learning closure for polymer integral equation theory
paper.abstract: Polymer reference interaction site model (PRISM) theory, a descendant of Ornstein–Zernike liquid state theory, is a powerful tool to predict the structure and thermodynamics of equilibrium polymer systems, but its accuracy and applicability can be limited in some important cases. Typically, these shortcomings are traced to the analytical closure relationships used to solve the integral equations. Here, we propose a machine learning (ML)-based closure relation trained on a dataset of coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations of homopolymer melts and solutions. PRISM theory with the ML closure outperforms traditional atomic closures (e.g., Percus–Yevick) in predicting the structure of typical coarse-grained model systems. We also use the ML closure to accurately model the results of small-angle neutron scattering experiments. This ML-enhanced PRISM theory can, therefore, enable rapid soft materials discovery and design efforts.

paper.title: Dynamic Reconstruction of Vanadium Oxide Species Modified Ruthenium‐Cerium Catalysts: Electron Bridge and Hydrogen‐Bond Network Disruption for Efficient Acidic Hydrogen Evolution
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing efficient electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media is critical for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Herein, we report a Ru–CeVO X catalyst with oxygen vacancies and surface vanadium oxide species. The optimized Ru–CeVO X exhibits excellent HER activity in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 , achieving overpotentials of 35.9 mV at 10 mA cm −2 and 193.6 mV at 1000 mA cm −2 , outperforming commercial Pt/C. In a PEMWE device, it delivers 1 A cm −2 at 1.80 V and maintains stability for over 400 h at 500 mA cm −2 . Time‐resolved ICP‐OES reveals in situ reconstruction, during which Ru 0 redeposits to form a dynamically stable, Ru‐rich active surface. Vanadium plays a dual critical role. The vanadium oxide species anchor onto the CeO 2 surface, constructing a Ru–O–Ce–O–V electron bridge that withdraws electrons from Ru, stabilizing Ru 0 and optimizing its d‐band center for near‐ideal H* adsorption. vanadium oxide species actively disrupt the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network, reducing strongly bound water and increasing free water molecules. This disruption facilitates H* recombination on adjacent Ru sites, accelerating the Tafel step which is the rate‐determining step of HER on Ru–CeVO X . Thus, vanadium‐induced reconstruction, combining electron bridging and hydrogen‐bond disruption, offers a powerful strategy for designing high‐performance acidic HER catalysts.

paper.title: Decoupling Water Dissociation and Hydrogen Adsorption via the Dual-Site Synergy of Spatially Coupled V Single Atoms and Ni5 Clusters for Efficient Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
paper.abstract: Abstract Efficient electrocatalysts for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) are critical to sustainable energy conversion, yet their performance is severely hampered by sluggish water dissociation kinetics. Herein, we design a synergistic catalyst in which V single atoms and Ni5 clusters are coanchored on N-doped graphene, enabling highly efficient alkaline HER. Density functional theory calculations uncover a distinctive dual-site mechanism: the Ni5 cluster acts as the active center for water dissociation, significantly reducing the energy barrier, while the adjacent V single atom introduces a unique bridge site for hydrogen adsorption at the V–Ni5 interface, thereby optimizing the hydrogen adsorption free energy (ΔGH*). This spatial coupling of V single atoms and Ni5 clusters cooperatively accelerates both water dissociation and hydrogen adsorption. The present findings establish a precise multiactive-site design principle, providing new theoretical insights to guide the development of high-performance alkaline HER electrocatalysts.

paper.title: What Information Is Required to Learn Molecular Pauli Potentials? A Nonlocal Descriptor Hierarchy for Orbital-Free Density Functional Theory
paper.abstract: Practical orbital-free density functional theory (OF-DFT) for molecules remains limited by the unknown Pauli contribution to the noninteracting kinetic energy. Here, we ask what information a density representation must contain for a machine-learned (ML) Pauli potential to drive an orbital-free Euler solution toward its Kohn–Sham (KS) reference. For C2H2, a frozen KS-derived Pauli-potential oracle yields an OF energy within 3.15 mHa of the KS reference, establishing the numerical accuracy attainable within the chosen finite representation. Coordinate-conditioned neural networks demonstrate that the Paulipotential field is learnable but do not provide a density-functional representation. Replacing coordinates with semilocal density descriptors leads to severe failure for both multilayer perceptron (MLP) and Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN) models. A descriptor-space identifiability analysis reveals the underlying cause: sparse representations leave approximately 14% of grid points ambiguous, whereas an atom-reaching 60-component nonlocal environment reduces this fraction to approximately 1.4%. Correspondingly, progressively adding nonlocal density information reduces the KAN energy deviation from −4594 to −16.0 mHa, while geometry-informed bond-centered descriptors further reduce it to −0.9 mHa. Applied independently to C2H4, the same descriptor strategy remains effective, yielding deviations of +24.0 and −13.5 mHa for KAN and MLP, respectively. Companion models also recover the principal spatial features of the Pauli energy density and strong covalent interaction profile. These results identify the resolution of descriptor ambiguity through extended and chemically structured nonlocal density information as a central representational requirement for molecular OF-DFT.

paper.title: Ice Deposition of Water Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry at Cryogenic Temperatures
paper.abstract: Water gas cluster ion beams (GCIBs) are increasingly used in cryogenic secondary ion mass spectrometry (cryo-SIMS) to improve the detection of biomolecules while preserving their molecular integrity. However, the effects of water cluster primary ion (PI) beams on cryogenically cooled surfaces are not yet fully understood. Here, we demonstrate that continuous bombardment with (H 2 O) n + GCIBs can induce ice deposition, which competes with sputtering and can ultimately obscure the underlying sample, thus compromising depth profiling and molecular analysis. Using deuterated (D 2 O) n + clusters and subsequent C60 + depth profiling, we confirmed that the deposited ice originates predominantly from water molecules introduced by the primary ion beam. Systematic investigation of cluster size and kinetic energy identified the energy per water molecule (E/n) as the key parameter governing the balance between net sputtering and ice deposition. Significant ice deposition occurred at E/n < 4 eV, whereas the substrate signal remained approximately constant at E/n > 5 eV. Measurements of the deposited ice cross-sections indicated that up to 40% of the incoming water molecules could remain on the surface under deposition-dominated conditions. Substrate temperature also influenced deposition, with ice accumulation observed below approximately 188 K for the investigated beam conditions. Experiments on copper, organic deposits, and mouse brain tissue further demonstrated that this phenomenon is not restricted to metallic substrates and that the deposition rate varies with surface composition. These findings establish beam energy per molecule, substrate temperature, and material-dependent sputtering behaviour as important factors controlling ice accumulation during cryo-SIMS using (H 2 O) n + GCIBs. Careful optimisation of GCIB parameters is therefore essential to minimise deposition artefacts and maintain reliable molecular depth profiling, particularly when cryogenic sample preservation is required. Lastly, the ability to deposit known amounts of ice in localised areas could prove useful for preparing samples with well-defined and controlled characteristics.

paper.title: Numerical Prediction of NaCl Solubility in Water Using the TIP4P/05 Water Model NaCl/Madrid
paper.abstract: The solid-liquid equilibrium and solubility of NaCl in water were investigated using molecular dynamics simulations with the NaCl/Madrid force field and the TIP4P/05 water model. Particular attention was given to the influence of the intermolecular cut-off radius, rcut, used to identify ions belonging to the crystalline phase. Simulations were initiated from a NaCl crystal immersed in an aqueous NaCl solution, following the configuration proposed by Manzanilla-Granados et al. After equilibration, the system was analysed over an extended simulation trajectory. The radial distribution function, g(r), was used to establish a physically motivated criterion for distinguishing the crystalline and aqueous phases. Specifically, the first minimum following the principal Na-Cl correlation peak was used to characterise the ionic coordination environment and constrain the range of meaningful cut-off radii. The number of ions remaining in the crystalline phase was then evaluated as a function of rcut, allowing the corresponding solubility to be estimated. The resulting curve exhibits a well-defined inflection point, providing a criterion for identifying the transition between predominantly crystalline and dissolved ionic populations. This approach offers a structural basis for determining NaCl solubility directly from the evolution of the solid-liquid system, avoiding the arbitrary selection of the cut-off distance. The results demonstrate that combining radial distribution functions with cut-off-dependent analysis provides a useful framework for characterising solid-liquid behaviour and estimating the solubility of ionic crystals through molecular dynamics simulations.

paper.title: Reliability of Short Molecular Dynamics Runs as Screening Labels: Noise Ceilings, Time Dependence and Adaptive Replicate Allocation
paper.abstract: High-throughput molecular dynamics (MD) produces the labels on which electrolyte screening and machine-learning models are built, but each label comes from one short, noisy run whose value still depends on the simulated time. We quantify their reliability, and how to spend a simulation budget given it, on HTP-MD, the largest public set of polymer electrolyte trajectories (6,137 runs of 5 ns and 133 of 50 ns). Lithium motion is diffusive in only 2 short and 5 long runs, the apparent diffusivity at a 5 ns lag is 1.95 times that at 25 ns, and the first 5 ns of a run are 1.63 times faster than its second half, biasing every short label upwards. From 94 systems simulated twice, a single 5 ns end-point label has reliability 0.47 (95% CI 0.31 to 0.63): no model can correlate with such labels much beyond about 0.69, a random forest on monomer fingerprints is indistinguishable from that ceiling (0.71), and roughly half of the run-to-run noise comes from the initial structure. A short run ranks widely different polymers well (Spearman 0.93) but not similar ones (0.68 within the screening set). In simulations with the measured noise, giving further runs only to candidates whose membership of the top set is uncertain matches four uniform replicates with 1.8 runs per candidate for the top 10% and 1.2 for the top 1%; a check on real runs is consistent but underpowered. A decision guide and all code are provided.

paper.title: Noncontact friction of a semiconductor with charge carriers of differing mobilities
paper.abstract: The coefficient of noncontact friction as measured in an electric force microscopy experiment is computed for a semiconductor with positive and negative charge carriers of distinct mobilities. The friction is determined for a sample represented by classical electrodynamics coupled to diffusing carriers in a dielectric continuum. The analysis generalizes previous work in which positive and negative carriers were taken to have identical mobilities, allowing application to a wider range of semiconductors. Dielectric and electrical properties of the material are shown to be revealed by the dependence of the friction on experimentally accessible parameters such as probe-sample separation and carrier density.

paper.title: Water-Model Dependence of Absolute Binding Free Energies across the Bromodomain Family
paper.abstract: The choice of explicit water model may affect absolute binding free energy (ABFE) predictions for bromodomains, whose conserved acetyl-lysine pockets contain structured waters. We assembled a benchmark of ten distinct bromodomain–ligand complexes with experimental isothermal titration calorimetry thermodynamics and compared four TIP-family water models, TIP3P, TIP4P, TIP5P, and TIP7P, using a common alchemical protocol. TIP3P gave the lowest point-estimate mean unsigned error (MUE), 1.56 kcal mol−1, against 1.89–2.11 kcal mol−1 for the other models, at the lowest cost. TIP7P correlated best with experiment (r = 0.73), but the experimental affinities span only 2.1 kcal mol−1, about the size of the errors of the models. The 0.55 kcal mol−1 MUE difference between TIP3P and TIP7P had a nominal 95% paired bootstrap interval that excluded zero when only the benchmark composition was resampled, but not when the calculated affinities were perturbed by their sampling-sensitivity measures or the four charged ligands were left out. No other paired difference was resolved, including after finite-size corrections for the charged ligands. The leg decomposition shows that solvent and complex contributions can compensate, so water-model effects must be judged over the complete binding cycle. With one calculation per complex and model, the higher-site TIP models gave no demonstrated accuracy benefit with this force field for 1.4–2.7 times the cost.

paper.title: Automated Materials Data and Knowledge Extraction using Machine Learning and Large Language Models
paper.abstract: Over the past decade, substantial efforts have been devoted to developing machine learning (ML) methods for extracting materials data and, where possible, materials knowledge directly from the scientific literature. This review traces the evolution of these methods from heuristic, rule-based pipelines through natural language processing (NLP) models and transformer-based encoders to, lastly, large language models (LLMs) and agentic systems capable of extracting materials information across multiple modalities, including text, tables, and figures. Beside construction of large, queryable materials databases and knowledge graphs that support downstream materials discovery, we discuss how these advances have enabled new capabilities, such as, generic question answering across materials science, AI co-scientists and chatbots for research assistance, and closed-loop optimization and discovery when integrated with autonomous laboratories. We critically assess the datasets generated using these approaches, their extraction accuracy and computational costs, and the respective strengths and limitations of different methodologies, and even provide practical guidelines for developing more reliable and scalable materials data extraction pipelines. Finally, we identify key open challenges, including the extraction of full materials structure-property-processing-performance tetrahedron at the sample level, the scarcity of reliable benchmark datasets for systematic evaluation, and the resolution of non-standard materials terminology across different document modalities.
paper.tldr: 该综述梳理了从规则方法到大型语言模型及智能体系统，用于从科学文献中自动提取材料数据与知识的技术演进。

paper.title: Tuning covalence for phosphorus-mediated C-C coupling in carbon monoxide electroreduction to multicarbon oxygenates
paper.abstract: Electrochemical carbon monoxide reduction (COR) is a promising route for sustainable production of multicarbon chemicals from CO2, as it bypasses the large carbon losses of direct CO2 electroreduction. In most electrocatalysts currently explored to tune COR selectivity towards highadded value multicarbon oxygenated molecules, like acetate and ethanol, copper is the catalytic site of C-C bond formation. Herein, we show that by designing nanoparticles of a strongly covalent copper compound, CuSi2P3, we retain isolated copper atoms during COR and trigger the intervention of phosphorus atoms as C-C coupling sites, without directly involving copper atoms. This profound change in COR mechanism results in a high selectivity towards C2 molecules (80 % Faradaic efficiency), especially oxygenates (73%), at a current density of -150 mA cm-2. This work reveals the importance of tailoring, via the crystal structure, the local environment of metal atoms, to achieve original selectivity in COR with new families of electrocatalysts.

paper.title: Inducing local heating fields in ferromagnetic high-entropy alloys to inhibit (bi)carbonate formation for durable CO2 electroreduction
paper.abstract: Carbonate precipitation at the cathode caused by local alkalinity during electrocatalytic CO2 reduction represents a major limitation to carbon efficiency and system durability. Now local heating induced in ferromagnetic high-entropy alloys by an alternating magnetic field reduces carbonate precipitation, extending durability in alkaline and neutral electrolytes.

paper.title: A porous solid electrolyte interface enables efficient electroreduction of captured carbon to CO
paper.abstract: Direct electrochemical conversion of captured carbon species offers a route to avoid the energy-intensive steps of thermal CO2 release, compression and transport in conventional carbon capture and utilization. In proton exchange membrane (PEM) reactors, however, the acidic cathode environment promotes hydrogen evolution and limits CO2 regeneration from (bi)carbonate capture media, resulting in low carbon utilization and high energy demand. Here we show a modular PEM–porous solid electrolyte (PSE) reactor for direct conversion of (bi)carbonate to CO. Using a transparent cell with in situ visualization, we reveal that the PSE regulates proton transport, reduces local proton reduction, limits bubble accumulation and facilitates CO2 transport to the cathode. The PEM–PSE reactor achieves a CO Faradaic efficiency of 90% at 200 mA cm−2, a carbon efficiency of 84%, and an energy consumption of ~26.0 GJ t−1 CO. It operates at current densities up to 800 mA cm−2, reaching a CO rate of ~8.0 mmol h−1 cm−2. These results highlight the regulation of proton and gas transport in the electrochemical conversion of captured carbon. Turning captured carbon dioxide into useful chemicals can save energy, but combining capture and conversion is difficult. Here, the authors report a membrane reactor converts bicarbonate solutions directly into carbon monoxide with high carbon efficiency and lower energy use.

paper.title: Crystal Structure Based Graph Neural Network And LLM Multi-Modal Approach for Material Magnetic Ordering Prediction
paper.abstract: AI/ML models are useful for the prediction of materials' properties. Recently, there has been great progress in developing Neural Network models to predict the properties of solids, molecules, and crystals, avoiding expensive and time-consuming laboratory testing. This study presents a novel AI/ML-based multi-modal approach to predict material magnetic ordering using material crystal structure information as input to a Graph Neural Network model (GNN) and semantic text descriptions of the material's properties and structure as input to a Large Language Model (LLM), before performing information fusion of the GNN and LLM outputs to predict material magnetic ordering in four classes (Non-magnetic, Ferromagnetic, Antiferromagnetic, Ferrimagnetic). The model is trained, validated, and tested on a dataset which is a combination of Materials Project dataset, Magndata dataset, and a set of uranium compounds with magnetic ordering determined in laboratory testing, with an 80/10/10 (training/validation/testing) data split. The proposed GNN and LLM multi-modal approach achieves better overall accuracy than both the standalone GNN and LLM approaches with three fusion strategies.

paper.title: Mapping Hierarchical Motifs in disorder-order transitions: learning structural motifs in supercooled liquids and crystals
paper.abstract: Disorder-order transitions pass through structurally rich intermediates that conventional order parameters cannot fully resolve. Here, we introduce a hierarchical motif framework to characterize structural motifs from nucleation of supercooled water. Inspired by language modeling, our framework learns a discrete vocabulary and a grammar of how motifs interact in space and time. By applying vector quantization (VQ) to the learned embeddings of a variational autoencoder (VAE) trained on the structural descriptors, we establish a vocabulary of motifs comprising discrete labels of liquid, transient, and ice motifs. Moreover, the VAE quantifies local disorder that decreases from liquid to ice motifs. Analysis of the motif grammar, including motif-motif transitions, spatial co-occurrences, and ring occupancies, unifies mechanistic descriptions of the spatiotemporal dynamics of ice nucleation. The transient motifs resolve two structural roles: locally-ordered low-density (LD) environments that constitute precursors during supercooling, and non-consolidating interfacial regions. These LD precursors organize into a continuum of ring networks, revealing two processes during nucleation: trimers/tetramers continuously re-organize into closed pentamers/hexamers in ring scaffolds, while atomwise motifs relabel in bursts along an energy ladder. Next, we extend the motif framework to characterize metastable motifs formed by hypothetical polymorphs in heterogeneous nucleation simulations, which elucidates how structural motifs at the ice/liquid interface control ice nucleation. Beyond disorder-order transitions in supercooled water, we further demonstrate the generality of our framework in characterizing transitions in the nucleation of silicon and liquid-liquid transition of water.

paper.title: Formate Electrosynthesis via Selective Ethylene Glycol Oxidation on Ni-Modified CeO2−x/NF
paper.abstract: Ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR) offers a route to replace the anodic oxygen evolution reaction while converting ethylene glycol into value-added products. Here, electrodeposited CeO2−x//NF and Ni-modified CeO2−x/NF were evaluated for EGOR in alkaline electrolyte. Ni modification markedly enhanced the polarization response, enabling a current density of 100 mA cm-2 at 1.61 V vs RHE without iR compensation, approximately 97 mV lower than that of the parent CeO2−x/NF electrode at the same current density. During potentiostatic EGOR at 1.8 V vs RHE in 1 M KOH containing 1 M ethylene glycol, the parent and Ni-modified electrodes sustained average current densities of 192 and 241 mA cm-2, respectively. 1H-NMR analysis identified formate as the dominant detected liquid product, with estimated formate Faradaic efficiencies of 83.2% and 92.9%, respectively. These results show that Ni modification enhances EGOR activity while maintaining efficient formate formation on CeO2−x-based electrodes.

paper.title: Molecular Triboelectric Fingerprinting of Brominated Aromatics and Time‐Resolved Monitoring of Suzuki–Miyaura Coupling
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Contact electrification at solid–liquid interfaces is highly sensitive to molecular electronic structure, yet its application to distinguish organic molecules and chemical transformations remains unexplored. Here, a systematic halogen substitution within brominated aromatic molecules is used to tune the interfacial electronic structure, enabling quantitative correlations among molecular structure, work function, surface potential, and triboelectric response. Molecularly modified polystyrene (PS) interfaces were fabricated by incorporating brominated aromatics (bromobenzene, 1‐bromo‐4‐chlorobenzene, and 1‐bromo‐4‐fluorobenzene) into a PS matrix coated on a copper wire. Systematic variation of the brominated aromatic substituents modulated the surface potential, work function, and triboelectric response of the PS interface. The molecular‐dependent triboelectric response was correlated with changes in work function measured by ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) and computational studies. Furthermore, owing to the high volatility of bromobenzene, which limits stable triboelectric sensing, its conversion into the significantly less volatile biphenyl through the Suzuki–Miyaura coupling reaction was monitored using a contact‐separation triboelectric system with copper oxide nanowires (CuO NWs). This work establishes a molecular framework linking interfacial electronic structure with triboelectric response, demonstrates self‐powered monitoring of chemical transformations, and introduces a strategy for detecting highly volatile VOCs through chemical conversion into more stable products.

paper.title: macroqc 2.0: An electronic structure theory software for large-scale applications
paper.abstract: macroqc is a quantum chemistry software package designed for high-accuracy electronic structure computations and large-scale molecular simulations. The macroqc framework provides efficient implementations of energies and analytic gradients for a wide range of many-body perturbation theory and coupled-cluster (CC) methods. In particular, the analytic gradient implementations of second-order Møller–Plesset perturbation theory (MP2), coupled-cluster singles and doubles (CCSD), and CCSD with perturbative triples [CCSD(T)] exhibit excellent computational performance, even in comparison with established commercial quantum chemistry programs. In addition to conventional correlated methods, macroqc incorporates several advanced capabilities, including molecular fragmentation techniques for ground and excited state molecular systems and density-fitted analytic gradients. The software also supports interoperability with selected external packages through a flexible plugin framework, allowing developers to construct customized interfaces and extensions. The notable features of macroqc are the linear-scaling systematic molecular fragmentation (LSSMF) and the cluster-in-molecule (CIM) approaches, which enable the application of high-level post-Hartree–Fock approaches to large molecular systems that would otherwise be computationally prohibitive. Furthermore, the new machine learning (ML) library enables the integration of data-driven approaches into quantum chemical workflows, providing efficient tools for developing and applying ML-based models for molecular property prediction and electronic structure computations. With its combination of efficient implementations, advanced theoretical methods, and extensible design, macroqc is expected to serve as a useful platform for a broad range of computational chemistry applications.

paper.title: A Bipolar Covalent Organic Framework Cathode Enabling a Six‐Electron Redox Process for Wide‐Temperature Sodium‐Ion Batteries
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) are promising for large‐scale energy storage because of the natural abundance and low cost of sodium. However, the development of cathodes that combine high redox‐site utilization with prolonged cycling across a wide temperature range remains challenging. Herein, we develop a heteroporous bipolar triphenylamine−benzoquinone covalent organic framework (TPBQ–COF)/carbon nanotube (CNT) composite cathode, TPBQ–COF@CNT, for wide‐temperature SIBs. The framework incorporates carbonyl groups and triphenylamine units as complementary n‐type and p‐type redox centers, while the CNT network improves electrical connectivity throughout the electrode. The ordered porous skeleton further provides accessible pathways for electrolyte penetration and ion migration. TPBQ–COF@CNT exhibits an average capacity decay of only 0.0012% per cycle over 15000 cycles at 5 A g −1 . Even in the full‐cell configuration, reversible capacities of 189 and 85 mAh g −1 are preserved after 200 cycles at 50°C and 500 cycles at −20°C, respectively. We identify carbonyl reduction and triphenylamine oxidation as the complementary reactions underlying the overall six‐electron redox process, with Na + and PF 6 − participating at distinct states of charge. These findings clarify how molecularly encoded cation and anion storage can remain electrochemically accessible during prolonged cycling over a wide temperature range.

paper.title: A Molecular Switch with Dual Responses to Electrochemical and Mechanical Stimuli
paper.abstract: Abstract Molecular switches capable of responding to two or more orthogonal stimuli are essential for advancing molecular-scale logic, sensing, and memory technologies. However, integrating distinct control mechanisms within a single-molecule architecture remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a single-molecule electrochemical-mechanical dual-control switch based on difluoroboron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) molecular junctions. We demonstrate that applying an electrochemical gate voltage threshold (−0.6 V) reduces the BODIPY core to a stable radical anion, effectively serving as a logic enable (EN) signal. Under this electrochemically activated regime, precision mechanical modulation (∼5.0 Å amplitude) via an STM tip cleanly dictates the molecular conformation. Compressive strain drives the formation of a highly conductive asymmetric Au–S/Au−π contact (the SET operation) with a two-order-of-magnitude conductance contrast, while tensile strain physically ruptures the Au−π interfacial coupling to recover the symmetric terminal Au–S anchoring (the RESET operation). This dual-input sliding molecular resistor operates stably at frequencies up to 200 Hz, with density functional theory calculations elucidating the underlying radical-enhanced resonant transport pathway. By seamlessly mapping these synergistic electro-mechanical inputs to digital logic, we successfully transform this molecular junction into a nonvolatile, nanoscale gated RS latch. Ultimately, our work establishes a highly robust and versatile design strategy for constructing complex, multistimuli-responsive molecular circuitry at the single-molecule limit.

paper.title: The AI debate is missing half the system
paper.abstract: Last month, leading executives of artificial intelligence (AI) companies warned the United Nations Security Council about the risks of losing human control over this rapidly advancing technology. Their recommendations focused heavily on safeguards, evaluation, and governance of AI models and systems, largely overlooking the risks that arise from the interactions of AI with people and institutions. AI safety needs to be addressed at the level of the human–AI system, not the AI model alone.

paper.title: A transposon inserted into HELD1 repressed maize husk leaf blade extension during maize domestication
paper.abstract: Husk leaves are the closest photosynthetic organs to the ear, which contribute directly to grain filling and have potential for yield improvement in maize. Teosinte has a long husk extended leaf blade, whereas maize exhibits a reduced or even no husk leaf blade. However, the genetic basis of this transition in the husk leaf during domestication remains unknown. In this study, we identified a major quantitative trait locus (QTL), Husk Extended Leaf Blade 1 ( HELD1 ), corresponding to the tassels replace upper ears1 ( tru1 ) gene. A 133-base pair (bp) Harbinger transposon inserted into the tru1 intron introduces two TEOSINTE BRANCHED 1 (TB1) binding motifs, thereby recruiting TB1 to directly enhance tru1 transcription. Further analyses revealed that TRU1 interacts with the transcription factor ALOG1, which in turn enhances the expression of liguleless2 ( lg2 ), a key regulator of ligule development. Together with brassinosteroid-deficient dwarf1 ( brd1 ) and GA2ox1 , these genes set up a regulatory network that defines the ligular-auricular position, controls the leaf blade-to-husk (sheath) ratio in husk and stem leaves, and regulates husk leaf blade length. Population genetic analyses indicate that HELD1 experienced significant human selection, resulting in the transposon insertion becoming the dominant allele in domesticated maize. Additionally, the teosinte HELD1 allele with extended husk leaf blades significantly enhances yield in maize. Our results demonstrate HELD1 is an important regulator of husk and stem leaf architectures, contributing to the ligular-auricular position to adjust the ratio of leaf blade to husk or sheath.

paper.title: Structure-coefficient theorem for evolutionary games on dynamic networks
paper.abstract: The authors establish a structure-coefficient theorem, showing that three universal coefficients capture evolutionary outcomes in changing networks, and identify dynamic core–periphery networks that promote cooperation, altruism, fairness and trust.

paper.title: Efficient and accurate steering of large language models through attention-guided feature learning
paper.abstract: Activation steering, or direct manipulation of internal activations to guide large language model (LLM) responses toward specific semantic concepts, is emerging as a promising avenue for both understanding how semantic concepts are stored within LLMs and advancing LLM capabilities. Yet, existing steering methods are remarkably brittle, with seemingly nonsteerable concepts becoming completely steerable based on subtle algorithmic choices in how concept-related features are extracted. In this work, we introduce an attention-guided framework for activation steering that overcomes three core challenges associated with steering: 1) automatic selection of relevant token embeddings for extracting concept-related features; 2) accounting for heterogeneity of concept-related features across LLM activations; and 3) identification of layers most relevant for steering. Across a steering benchmark of 512 semantic concepts, our framework substantially improved steering over previous state-of-the-art (nearly doubling the number of successfully steered concepts) across model architectures and sizes (up to 70 billion parameter models). Furthermore, we use our framework to shed light on the distribution of concept-specific features across LLM layers. Overall, our framework opens further avenues for developing efficient, highly scalable fine-tuning algorithms for industry-scale LLMs.

paper.title: Observation of Kondo Effect in Rhombohedral Graphene Superlattices
paper.abstract: Kondo effect in strongly correlated systems arises from the antiferromagnetic coupling between itinerant conduction electrons and localized magnetic moments, giving rise to a variety of exotic quantum phenomena. Two-dimensional moiré superlattice systems provide a highly tunable platform featuring topological flat bands, where Wannier orbitals are spatially confined by the periodic moiré potential and serve as localized magnetic moments, enabling the observable Kondo effect. Here we experimentally demonstrate Kondo interactions in hexalayer rhombohedral graphene moiré superlattices through magneto-transport and temperature-dependent measurements. With increasing magnetic field, the magnetoresistance exhibits an increase-decrease transition across a critical field B_c, while the Hall resistance R_xy undergoes a sign reversal near B_c. Moreover, as temperature decreases, the longitudinal resistance R_xx first increases logarithmically and then decreases following a T^2 behavior, indicating a transition to heavy fermion liquid. These behaviors can be consistently explained by the breakdown of Kondo singlets induced by either magnetic field or temperature, which liberates carriers previously bound to localized moments, thereby enhancing conductivity and altering the dominant carrier type. Furthermore, our results demonstrate that the Kondo interaction can be continuously tuned by both carrier density n and displacement electric field D, and suggest the emergence of a Kondo insulating state. Our findings provide deep insight into the Kondo effect in moiré engineered flat-band systems, paving the path for exploring exotic correlated quantum phases.

paper.title: Factorised Cartesian Atomic Cluster Expansion for Low-Cost Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
paper.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials can reach the accuracy of density functional theory at a fraction of its cost, but the most accurate equivariant models remain expensive, mainly because of the tensor operations they perform for every pair of neighbouring atoms. We present FACE, a factorised Cartesian atomic cluster expansion that removes this bottleneck. Each neighbour contributes only a small set of radial functions and messages, and all mixing of feature channels is done once per atom, so the cost per neighbour no longer grows with the size of the model. Custom GPU kernels evaluate the remaining steps, and long-range electrostatics, dispersion and short-range repulsion attach through a single interface. We show that the training divergences we encountered originate in how the network weights are scaled, and we introduce a distillation scheme in which an ensemble generates additional, uncertainty-checked training data. On five rMD17 molecules, with identical training budgets and hardware, FACE is about as accurate as a 64-channel MACE model (over three seeds: better on one molecule, within the seed spread on two, 7–14% higher force errors on two), while it is 5.7 times faster at inference (4.9 times at the same cutoff) and needs 3.5–3.9 times less GPU memory. Training costs about the same per step. Distillation lowers the energy and force errors of a single aspirin model by 20% at fixed width, to 2.26 meV and 6.74 meV/Å, close to the published MACE values (2.2 and 6.6), and the distilled model runs stably in molecular dynamics.

paper.title: Structural transition in one-dimensional water unveils the origin of multifurcated hydrogen bond weakening
paper.abstract: Water confined to low dimensions exhibits even more anomalous behavior than bulk water. Since these anomalies are primarily dictated by hydrogen bonds (hbs), we investigate hb behavior in quasi-one-dimensional water chains using density functional theory. We show that a water chain with two molecules per unit cell transforms from a single-file (low-linear-density) to a double-file (high-linear-density) structure under uniaxial compression. Furthermore, we show that repulsive interactions emerge when hbs become multifurcated. These additional repulsive forces weaken the hbs and play a crucial role in driving the structural transition. We demonstrate that the many-body interactions associated with hb cooperativity, as well as the repulsive forces from multifurcated hbs, are captured by classical dipole–dipole interactions. This indicates that both hb cooperativity and the weakening of multifurcated hbs are classical electrostatic phenomena, even though quantum effects dictate the strength of the effective dipoles involved. Finally, we discuss how these results provide insights for understanding the flow mechanism of water along pores of sub-nanometer diameter and aid in developing a simple, universal water model.

paper.title: Interfacial Charge Modulation of Covalent Metal–Organic Frameworks for Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical H 2 O 2 synthesis through the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction offers a sustainable alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Crystalline porous frameworks are attractive for this route because of their structural precision, yet poor electrolyte wetting and limited electrochemical accessibility often restrict their practical performance. Here, we report an interfacial charge‐modulation strategy that transforms covalent metal–organic frameworks into highly wetted and electrochemically accessible catalytic interfaces. By incorporating cationic ethidium bromide units into a trinuclear copper‐pyrazolate framework, we construct EB‐Cu 3 ‐COF featuring enlarged interlayer spacing, enhanced interfacial charge transfer, and optimized *OOH intermediate adsorption. Consequently, EB‐Cu 3 ‐COF achieves up to 99% H 2 O 2 selectivity and a flow‐cell production rate of 39 420 mmol·g cat −1 ·h −1 , ranking among the best‐performing non‐pyrolyzed porous organic electrocatalysts reported to date. This work establishes interfacial charge‐modulation as a design principle for translating crystalline structural precision into electrochemically active interfaces.

paper.title: Molecular/Ionic Coupling Enables a Cycling-Evolved Gradient Interphase for Durable Zinc Metal Anodes
paper.abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc batteries hold promise for energy storage, but viability is limited by the trade-off between interfacial thermodynamic stability and Zn2+ deposition kinetics. Existing strategies address solvation or electric-field regulation separately, overlooking the coupled interplay between molecular adsorption and ionic shielding and its influence on gradient interphase evolution. We establish a molecular/ionic coupling framework using NFSI as a desolvation promoter and Y3+ as an electrostatic modulator to quantitatively tune the near-interfacial environment by regulating the desolvation barrier and local electric field, thereby promoting the development of an organic/inorganic gradient SEI with an F/S-rich outer region and a ZnF2/ZnS-rich inner region. This interphase suppresses side reactions while maintaining fast Zn2+ transport. Bayesian optimization finds the optimal formulation, enabling Zn||Zn symmetric cells to cycle >2200 h, Zn||Cu half-cells to achieve 99.76% CE over 4000 cycles, and Zn||MnO2 full cells with enhanced rate and stability. This coupling strategy provides a data-guided and transferable design principle for molecular/ionic cooperative electrolyte engineering.

paper.title: Operando Time-Resolved Spectroelectrochemical Microscopy Reveals Distinct Electron Depletion Pathways in Electrocatalysis
paper.abstract: Abstract Understanding electrocatalysis requires direct knowledge of how charge carriers are distributed and consumed at active sites under the operating conditions. However, the spatiotemporal dynamics of injected electrons in working catalysts remain largely inaccessible, hindering a mechanistic understanding of catalytic heterogeneity. Here, we develop an operando time-resolved spectroelectrochemical microscopy that enables direct and quantitative mapping of electron density with microsecond temporal resolution and micrometer spatial resolution. Using monolayer MoS2 as a model system, we directly visualize the spatial redistribution and depletion of electrochemically injected electrons during the hydrogen evolution reaction. We observe pronounced site-specific electron depletion that correlates with catalytic activity and further identify two distinct mechanisms governing charge loss: reaction-limited depletion at highly active sites, including edges and Pt-functionalized sites, and injection-limited depletion in bilayer regions. These results establish a quantitative link between local charge carrier dynamics and catalytic activity and provide a general framework for probing nanoscale carrier dynamics in electrocatalysts.

paper.title: A Roaming-like Mechanism for Hydrogen Bond Network Rearrangements in Water Clusters
paper.abstract: Abstract Unraveling hydrogen bond network rearrangements governing water reactivity is central to the physical and life sciences. Water mediates roaming in other systems, but whether water itself can roam remains unresolved. By mapping the potential energy surfaces of the water dimer and trimer, which together exhaust the elementary rearrangements, we identify five candidate roaming pathways that share reactants and products with the known rearrangements but traverse a flat region near the O–H dissociation asymptote. Each roaming-like saddle point sustains a spin-polarized, broken-symmetry state with near-unity spin population on the migrating hydrogen, consistent with neutral radical character. Interpretable machine learning reaches 93.1% accuracy in buffered within-scan tests and quantifies descriptor contributions, complementing the electronic-structure characterization, although transfer to withheld scans is limited and a distance-and-cluster-size baseline performs comparably. These findings point to roaming-like H atom migration as a candidate elementary channel of hydrogen bond network rearrangement in water clusters, with implications for radical chemistry in extended networks.

paper.title: Helium Atom Scattering from Cold Salty Water: Impact of Microscopic and Mesoscopic Surface Structure
paper.abstract: Understanding the dynamics of gas–liquid surface scattering is of fundamental importance to interfacial phenomena ranging from atmospheric chemistry to heterogeneous catalysis. In this work, molecular beam scattering experiments and all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are carried out to study collisions of He atoms ( E i = 5.8 kJ mol −1 ; θ i = 45°, 60°, and 75°) from the surface of a cold salty water (8 m LiBr (aq) , 230 K) flat jet. The measured translational energy distributions are collected as a function of the scattering angle in the same plane of the incidence beam and indicate dominant impulsive scattering with little to no trapping–desorption signal. The fractional energy loss values are small and nearly invariant across a wide range of deflection angles. MD simulations with fine-tuned force field parameters reproduce the experimental energy transfer reasonably well, providing insight into the collision dynamics at the microscopic level. However, the highly diffuse experimental angular distributions with significant intensities in the direction parallel to the liquid surface ( θ f = 90°) are in sharp contrast to the narrower and near specular angular distributions in simulations. This theory–experiment discrepancy is attributed to capillary and mechanical waves of the liquid surface and much better agreement between theory and experiment for He scattering is achieved by invoking a mesoscopic washboard model. This model also successfully reproduces previously reported results for Ne at E i = 24.3 kJ mol −1 . Our combined experimental–computational approach establishes that microscopic collision dynamics and mesoscopic surface morphology jointly govern scattering from salty water surfaces, providing a framework for interpreting and predicting interfacial energy transfer in complex liquid environments.

paper.title: Disorder Beats Order: Carbon Microstructure Steers Radical Versus Cationic Pathways in Kolbe Electrolysis
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon electrodes are ubiquitous in organic electrochemistry, yet the structural origin of their selectivity in radical‐mediated reactions remains poorly understood. Here, we show that carbon microstructure is a primary determinant of product selectivity in Kolbe electrolysis, a prototypical electrochemical C─C coupling reaction central to fuel, fine chemical, and pharmaceutical production. We investigated eight carbon electrodes in two complementary libraries: five commercial carbons spanning diverse macroarchitectures, and carbon nanofibers with controlled graphitization. Both reveal a consistent structure–selectivity trend for various carboxylic acids and a mixed‐acid feed. Counterintuitively, the most disordered electrodes, despite the highest charge‐transfer resistance, give about an order of magnitude more Kolbe dimer than highly graphitized ones, which give little or none. Disordered, sp 3 ‐rich surfaces bearing oxygen functionalities strongly favor both Kolbe coupling (alkane) and Hofer–Moest products (alcohol/aldehyde), whereas graphitized, sp 2 ‐rich surfaces favor further oxidation to carbocations, yielding mainly alkenes and esters. Density functional theory calculations suggest that oxygen‐functionalized sites bind the alkyl radical about three times more strongly than pristine graphene, consistent with longer‐lived surface‐bound radicals that can couple. These findings help rationalize the widely used but poorly understood performance of reticulated vitreous carbon in organic electrosynthesis and offer guiding principles for rational carbon electrode design.

paper.title: Unraveling Water Balances behind Salt Formation in CO2 Reduction Electrolyzers
paper.abstract: Abstract Salt precipitation in CO2 electrolyzers remains a critical barrier to long-term stability, yet the underlying water-salt transport and balance are poorly understood. Here, we established a quantitative mass balance framework to account for water entering and leaving the cathode chamber from all possible sources and across different phases, thereby elucidating the origin of bicarbonate salt formation. We revealed that although the inlet CO2 stream typically flows through a water bubbler, it is often not fully saturated with water vapor and thus results in significant liquid water evaporation inside the cathode chamber. Although water crossover from the anolyte to the cathode is, in principle, sufficient to dissolve the cotransported K+ as carbonate species (or even bicarbonate in some cases), evaporation reduces the effective local liquid water-to-K+ ratio, leading to salt precipitation. Conversely, excessive humidification suppresses salt formation but induces electrode wetting and flooding, highlighting a fundamental trade-off between dehydration-induced crystallization and overhumidification-driven mass transport limitations. Together, these findings establish water management as a governing principle for stabilizing CO2 electrolyzers and provide engineering guidelines for controlling salt formation in electrochemical reactor systems.

paper.title: Characterizing the Hydrophobic Contribution to Adsorption on Ligand-functionalized Surfaces
paper.abstract: The hydrophobicity of functionalized surfaces is critical, as these surfaces are widely used to modulate adsorption, self-assembly, fouling, and molecular recognition by controlling interfacial interactions with surrounding molecules. Despite their importance, characterizing the hydrophobicity of functionalized surfaces and quantifying its contribution to these phenomena remain challenging. Here, we use molecular dynamics simulations and enhanced sampling methods to quantify the hydrophobicity of surfaces functionalized with multimodal ligands, which can interact with solutes through multiple interaction modes. Specifically, we study a series of multimodal ligands grafted to these surfaces, including Nuvia cPrime, a commercially available glycine-based chromatography ligand, and its amino acid-derived analogs, which differ from it by additional chemical groups with systematically varied hydrophobicity. We quantify surface hydrophobicity from the free energy of removing interfacial water molecules and compare our results with ligand logP values, the solvent accessible surface areas (SASA) of ligand chemical groups, and protein-induced water displacement observed in molecular simulations. We then validate the relevance of the resulting hydrophobicity ordering using experimental protein binding trends. We find that water removal from small, localized regions centered on ligand clusters better captures adsorption-relevant surface hydrophobicity than removing water from the entire surface because these regions more closely represent proteinbinding sites. Additionally, we show that variations in ligand clustering across the same surface alter chemical group exposure, as indicated by SASA, resulting in spatial heterogeneity in surface hydrophobicity. Overall, this work provides a molecular-level approach for characterizing functionalized surface hydrophobicity and guiding the design of interfaces that control molecular adsorption.

paper.title: Do Acid–Base Equilibria of Phenols in Pneumatic Sprays Follow the Bulk Expectations?
paper.abstract: Abstract Microdroplets have been reported to exhibit accelerated chemical reactivity relative to bulk solutions, yet the fundamental origins of this behavior remain poorly understood. Extremely unlikely protonation equilibria have been reported for some reactions in microdroplets. This necessitates systematic investigation of protonation equilibria in microdroplets using a series of molecules with well-defined acid–base chemistry. To address this problem, we investigate deprotonation of a family of substituted phenols spanning a wide range of pKa values (∼1–9.2 in water and ∼14–25 in acetonitrile). We generate microdroplets of solutions of phenols over a range of concentrations and measure the corresponding phenolate ion yield using mass spectrometry. In aqueous microdroplets, the observed ion yields are quantitatively consistent with the expected bulk equilibrium behavior. Therefore, phenol deprotonation in water is not affected by any previously reported unusual microdroplet acid–base chemistry. In contrast, phenols in acetonitrile microdroplets exhibit ion yields unexpectedly similar to those observed in water despite the dramatically different pKa scales in the two solvents. This suggests that deprotonation in nonaqueous microdroplets generated by nebulization may not follow the bulk equilibrium expectations and may require alternative explanations.

paper.title: Unconstrained learning of equivariant atomistic properties
paper.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have made first-principles accuracy routine for the potential energy surface (PES). Their backbones, often O(3)-equivariant by design, are increasingly used to learn other atomistic properties. Many of these are of high angular order or pseudotensorial character, defined per atom, or expanded on large atom-centered basis sets. Such targets strain equivariant GNNs, whose tensor products grow steeply in cost with angular order and can fail to represent the target if truncated, forcing difficult trade-offs between hyperparameters. Unconstrained models like the Point-Edge Transformer (PET) instead replace explicit O(3) algebra with edge-to-edge attention and learn equivariance from data, so that the same backbone can in principle learn any equivariant property. We demonstrate how to use PET to learn molecular dipoles and polarizabilities, NMR chemical shielding tensors, and auxiliary-basis expansions of the electron density. Increasing the backbone size systematically improves both accuracy and equivariance error, and targeted architectural and training choices reduce the symmetry breaking further. PET matches or improves on the released reference models at lower inference cost and, compared with equivariant models, a smaller memory footprint. The predictions give accurate IR and Raman spectra and isotropic shieldings; the predicted densities accelerate self-consistent field calculations and give one-shot ground-state properties, and pretrained density models transfer to higher levels of theory by fine-tuning on little data. The impact of approximate equivariance is small for most observables, further validating this approach to train fast, accurate, and useful surrogate models for properties beyond the PES.

paper.title: PYTHIA, a transferable machine learning framework for simultaneous defect and adsorption site optimization
paper.abstract: Machine learning has permeated material optimization, providing high value. Nevertheless, its re- liance on a high number of samples limits its applicability to relatively explored material families. In this paper we extend the applicability of machine learning to novel and understudied materials through the PYTHIA (Probabilistic Yet Transferable Hierarchical Interaction Architecture) framework. Pythia utilizes two of the most powerful machine learning concepts, foundational models and transfer learning. We employ a complex foundational model trained on a large dataset of chemically similar molecules, on a target that is physically close to our prediction target. Then, we freeze the weights and perform subspace alignment with the use of a transformer layer and add uncertainty quantification with gaussian processes. These two layers can be trained on a limited dataset yet allow us to leverage the gained knowl- edge and the studied materials and complex architectures. The resulting model is used as a surrogate for a Bayesian Optimization scheme. To showcase the robustness of the framework, we applied it to the investigation of adsorption and defect optimization of two distinct systems. paper.title: Oxidation-Induced Directional Iron Exsolution Awakens Interfacial Kinetics in Non-Stoichiometric Polyanion Cathodes
paper.abstract: Abstract Non-stoichiometric polyanion cathodes possess intrinsically favorable bulk-ion-diffusion potential, yet they often remain trapped in a kinetically dormant state. Using non-stoichiometric sodium iron phosphate (NFP) as a model system, we introduce mild thermal oxidation as a thermodynamic perturbation strategy. This treatment drives the directional exsolution of high-energy lattice Fe species toward the particle surface. Analysis of this reconstruction process reveals the underlying origin of the sluggish electrochemical response: the kinetic limitation does not arise primarily from the bulk framework, but rather from local Na/Fe antisite defects at the interface, which impose severe steric obstruction and kinetic barriers and thereby block trans-phase ion-transport pathways. Fe exsolution effectively removes these cationic blockages and simultaneously reconstructs a conductive interfacial network enriched in mixed-valence Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ species and vacancies. By eliminating the interfacial mass-transfer bottleneck, the intrinsic solid-solution Na-storage capability of the framework is released, delivering an initial discharge capacity of 130 mAh g⁻¹. This work elucidates a microscopic mechanism for actively reconstructing local defects through thermodynamic regulation and provides new interfacial-kinetic insight into activating the intrinsic electrochemical activity of metastable frameworks.

paper.title: Surfactant‐Mediated “ Oil‐in‐Water ” Electrolyte Design via Sonochemical Assembly: Low‐Dielectric Interfacial Regulation for Ultrastable Aqueous Zinc Batteries
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐metal batteries are plagued by severe performance degradation originating from the Zn anode's instability. Although electrolyte engineering has been widely established as a primary strategy to address this challenge, the utility of numerous promising species is intrinsically limited by their poor aqueous solubility. Herein, a surfactant‐mediated “ oil‐in‐water ” (denoted as SMOW) electrolyte design is proposed to unlock the potential of hydrophobic species. A long‐term stable micellar electrolyte is developed via sonochemically engineered self‐assembly, in which hydrophobic species are encapsulated within the surfactant micelles. Driven by interfacial electrostatic repulsion, these micelles release the hydrophobic species on the zinc anode surface. The enriched interfacial layer acts as an effective low‐dielectric shield, intrinsically accelerating Zn 2+ desolvation while physically isolating the Zn anode from reactive water molecules. Owing to the synergistic effect between the hydrophobic species and the surfactant, highly compact and dendrite‐free Zn deposition with suppressed parasitic side reactions is realized, enabling an ultralong cycling lifespan of over 3900 h for the Zn anode at 10 mA cm −2 . Furthermore, the assembled Zn||I 2 full cells deliver cycling for over 10000 cycles at 5 A g −1 with negligible capacity fading. This work provides a universal paradigm to break through the design constraints of aqueous electrolytes.

paper.title: Hybrid Solid Oxide Cell Enables Efficient and Robust High-Temperature CO2 Electrolysis
paper.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic conversion of CO2 into chemicals and fuels offers a promising route toward a circular carbon economy. High-temperature CO2 electroreduction in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) delivers high selectivity and energy efficiency, but balancing mechanical robustness and electrochemical performance remains challenging. Here, we address this challenge by introducing a hybrid ionic-conductor architecture that spatially decouples electrocatalysis, ionic transport, and mechanical support into function-specific layers. The resulting cell combines high mechanical robustness (fracture load > 7 N) with 1.5–3.0-fold higher CO2-to-CO activity than state-of-the-art SOECs over 600–800 °C. Stable operation is maintained for over 1000 h at 1.0 A cm–2. Furthermore, we demonstrate scalability with a single-cell area of 100 cm2, achieving total currents up to 120 A and powers up to 200 W. This work establishes an effective strategy for developing mechanically resilient, efficient, and scalable energy conversion devices.

paper.title: Dead-Potassium Activation Reconstructing Stabilized Interface Enables Stable Anode-Free Potassium Metal Batteries
paper.abstract: Abstract Anode-free high-energy-density potassium metal batteries (AFPMBs) are critically constrained by the irreversible accumulation of dead potassium (K) and severe dendrite growth. These issues stem from sluggish interfacial kinetics and the continuous fracture of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). A multifunctional electrolyte engineering strategy is proposed by incorporating bismuth iodide (BiI3) into a carbonate-based system to simultaneously regulate the bulk K+ solvation sheath, reconstruct the interfacial solvation structure, and reactivate dead K. Experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the iodide/triiodide (I–/I3–) species weaken the coordination of K+ with solvents and FSI– in the bulk electrolyte, generating a weakly coordinated solvation structure, which facilitates K+ desolvation. At the electrode interface, Bi-derived sites preferentially recruit and selectively adsorb free FSI– over carbonate solvents and promote their enrichment toward the inner Helmholtz layer, thereby reconstructing an anion-rich interfacial solvation structure that directs the formation of a robust inorganic-rich SEI. In parallel, the reversible I–/I3– redox couple can reactivate dead K. Benefiting from the synergistic suppression of dendrite growth, reduction of irreversible K loss, and enhancement of interfacial kinetics, the symmetric cells demonstrate stable cycling for over 1300 h at 0.5 mA cm–2 and 0.5 mAh cm–2. AFPMBs also demonstrate markedly improved cycling stability and capacity retention in the carbonate-based electrolyte. This work provides a foundation for designing advanced electrolyte additives to enhance electrochemical stability in AFPMBs.

paper.title: Image-Charge Barriers, Not Polaron Kinetics, Limit Charge Extraction at Ligand-Passivated CsPbI3 Interfaces
paper.abstract: Charge extraction across inorganic perovskite–organic ligand interfaces represents a critical materials bottleneck in perovskite optoelectronics, yet the defectindependent electrostatic origins of this process remain poorly understood. Here, we present a multiscale framework that combines first-principles density functional theory with macroscopic Scharfetter–Gummel drift-diffusion simulations to isolate and quantify this intrinsic transport barrier on CsPbI3 surfaces passivated by methylammonium (MA), butylammonium (BA), and phenethylammonium (PEA). We demonstrate that effective interfacial dielectric screening is governed by ligand orientational polarizability and adsorption geometry rather than isolated molecular polarizability, producing a counter-intuitive ordering εBA > εMA > εPEA that inverts the conventional molecular polarizability sequence. The resulting imagecharge barriers (Umax im = 202.6–229.8 meV) exceed kBT by nearly an order of magnitude, driving severe thermodynamic carrier depletion (CAF = 1.38 × 10−4–3.95 × 10−4), while all computed polaron reorganization energies (λ < 100 meV) confirm delocalized, large-polaron character—unambiguously establishing that the dominant bottleneck is electrostatic rather than kinetic. Despite its lowest electron reorganization energy (λe = 37.8 meV), PEA’s orientational locking generates the largest image-charge barrier (Umax im = 229.8 meV), whereas the conformationally flexible BA maximizes in-plane screening and reduces steady-state carrier accumulation by an order of magnitude under operational bias. Furthermore, ligand rigidity governs a structural electron–hole reorganization asymmetry (λh/λe = 0.98–1.85), establishing a defect-independent, purely structural mechanism for carrier selectivity. These findings deliver four quantitative design rules for charge-transparent passivation interlayers, replacing empirical ligand screening with a predictive framework anchored in orientational polarizability, adsorption geometry, and carrier-type symmetry. The identified image-charge barrier constitutes a Boltzmann activation energy Uim(T ) that is directly measurable via temperature-dependent photoconductance, providing an unambiguous experimental validation signature.

paper.title: Coordination Sphere Control Enables Hydride-Free Tandem Electrocatalytic E-Selective Semi-Hydrogenation
paper.abstract: Hydride-free electrocatalytic semi-hydrogenation offers an alternative to metal-hydride-based platforms, yet controlling alkene stereochemistry through such pathways remains challenging. Herein, we report an E-selective, redox-mediated Co-catalyzed platform enabled by cooperative control of the catalyst coordination sphere via ligand denticity and acid identity. Using a triphosphine ligand and ammonium chloride acid reverses the stereochemical preference of a previously developed Z-selective system, providing access to a range of E-alkenes in high yields and excellent stereoselectivity (up to 92% yield and >20:1 E:Z). Experimental and computational mechanistic studies support a mechanism involving a distinct proton transfer step with a chloride-mediated organization of the ammonium proton donor and Co catalyst. This allows for an initial inner-sphere protonation prior to cobaltocene-mediated reduction of the resultant Co(III)-alkenyl intermediate, followed by subsequent outer-sphere protonation to yield trans alkenes. These findings illustrate that coordination-sphere organization and precise control of proton transfer pathways may serve as complementary design principles in stereoselective electrocatalysis.

paper.title: Concentration-Dependent Speciation in ZnCl2 Electrolyte Solutions: Transferability of Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials and Speciation Sensitivity of EXAFS
paper.abstract: Predicting speciation in concentrated electrolytes requires accurate ion interactions and adequate sampling of slowly interconverting coordination environments. We combine Zn K-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) measurements with long-timescale molecular dynamics (MD) using machine-learning interatomic potentials to study aqueous ZnCl2 from dilute conditions to 30 m. We train revPBE-based DeepMD models with D3 corrections included or excluded for Zn-containing pairs and compare them with DPMD-SCAN, classical MD (CMD), and MACE-MATPES-r2SCAN. EXAFS calculations are benchmarked against hydrated and chloride-coordinated Zn reference complexes, then applied to MD ensembles alongside Zn-Cl coordination free-energy analysis. Increasing concentration reduces octahedral coordination, replaces water with chloride, and promotes chloride-bridged association. All three DeepMD models yield similar EXAFS at 3 m, but DPMD-SCAN shows greater transferability across concentrations, reproducing measured spectral trends, key features of mixed ZnCl2/LiCl spectra, and octahedral fractions consistent with other studies. DFT treatment strongly affects coordination free energies and aggregation; excluding Zn-related D3 corrections does not systematically improve EXAFS agreement. CMD shows larger spectral discrepancies and less consistent coordination trends. MACE-MATPES-r2SCAN improves upon CMD and yields spectra comparable to DPMD-SCAN, which provides more consistent agreement and greater computational efficiency. Neighbor-resolved analysis shows that distance disorder and scattering-path interference can produce similar EXAFS signatures for distinct coordination ensembles, highlighting the need for rigorous sampling and ensemble-averaged spectra to distinguish isolated from chloride-bridged Zn species.

paper.title: Directional Control of Droplet Motion via Geometric Gating
paper.abstract: We explore new methods for inducing the movement of water droplets on elastomeric substrates, such as polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Our approach builds upon the well-known phenomenon that water droplets move easily across these substrates when swelled with silicone oil. While designing shallow open channels and traps on a PDMS film offers a simple way to control a droplet's trajectory by tilting the substrate in two orthogonal directions, this method is poorly suited for manipulating multiple droplets simultaneously. To address this limitation, we introduce two new methods. The first method utilizes a piano-concave PDMS platform with a radius of curvature significantly larger than the size of the droplet and its translation distance. When the system's configuration is altered, this curved substrate consistently guides the droplet along a curved geodesic. The second method incorporates diode-like gates on the PDMS. These gates are created on either flat or piano-concave PDMS films by embedding thin, rigid plates into the elastomer prior to crosslinking, followed by swelling in silicone oil. This process generates sigmoidal steps that restrict droplet motion to a single direction. Finally, we demonstrate how combining these two strategies enables various forms of directed motion for both single and multiple droplets.
paper.tldr: 该研究表明，利用几何门控设计可实现液滴方向性操控，并支持同时处理多个液滴，优于传统倾斜基底方法。

paper.title: From Atoms to Reactors: A Critical Review of a Decade of Machine Learning in Heterogeneous Catalysis (2017–2026)
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT This critical review traces the evolution of machine learning (ML) across the full value chain of heterogeneous catalysis over 2017–2026, from catalyst discovery to reactor and process design, and across the principal reaction families (CO 2 reduction, water splitting, nitrogen chemistry, zeolite‐catalyzed transformations). Each stage is evaluated against four criteria — data foundation, method maturity, experimental validation and deployment readiness — through a structured capability scorecard. Digitalization has advanced from the top of the length scale downward: prediction of adsorption energies and atomistic potential‐energy surfaces is now mature, with errors of tens of meV relative to the reference DFT calculations and accelerations of three orders of magnitude over DFT, yet experimentally validated catalyst improvements remain rare. The most significant advance is the closed‐loop autonomous laboratory coupling Bayesian optimization, automated synthesis and high‐throughput testing. Large language models have begun to add a reasoning and orchestration layer, while kinetics, reactor and process design remain the least digitalized stages. We argue that the field's next decade of impact will be decided not by more accurate atomic‐scale prediction but by carrying ML into experimental validation and the reactor‐and‐process scale, where catalysis is hardest to industrialize and where data‐driven methods are weakest.

paper.title: Spontaneous defect formation as the origin of superionic transitions in antifluorite-type structures
paper.abstract: Solid-state electrolytes offer the possibility of safer and higher energy density batteries, yet only a limited number of materials achieve ionic conductivities suitable for practical applications. Type-II superionic conductors, which undergo continuous temperature-driven transitions between low and high ionic conductivity regimes are strong candidates for high-performance solid state electrolytes, but the transition mechanism is not sufficiently understood. In this study, we investigate the archetypical superionic conductors Li2O and Li2S with the antifluorite structure using long-time-scale molecular dynamics simulations with an Allegro machine-learning force field (MLFF) trained on density functional theory data selected using an on-the-fly active learning procedure. To this end, superionic transitions are identified around 1450 K for Li2O and around 1100 K for Li2S through continuous peaks in the heat capacity. Diffusion coefficients and concentration of Frenkel defects are found to exhibit strong non-Arrhenius behavior coinciding with the superionic transition where both diffusion activation energy and defect formation energy decrease significantly across the transition. This suggests a self-enhanced spontaneous defect formation mechanism, which drives the superionic transition and promotes increased ionic diffusion. These results identifies the microscopic origin of type-II superionic behavior as a result of correlated defect formation and support the design of improved solid-state electrolytes.

paper.title: Synthetic Stochastic Time Series from Generative Models
paper.abstract: Obtaining statistically converged time-series data represents a fundamental challenge in computational chemistry, where sampling is constrained by the prohibitive computational cost of high-fidelity simulations. The accuracy attainable from a finite simulation budget is governed by the standard-error scaling $1/\sqrt{n}$, rendering exhaustive sampling challenging for systems of realistic complexity. Here we show that generative models trained on high-quality stochastic trajectories can reproduce key statistical properties of the underlying process and generate additional synthetic trajectories at substantially lower computational cost, thereby enhancing the sampling accessible from a finite set of simulations. We present a systematic comparison of four generative architectures across two complementary data sources: an analytically tractable Ornstein-Uhlenbeck reference and donor-acceptor energy-gap trajectories from all-atom molecular dynamics simulations. Among the four architectures tested, the denoising diffusion probabilistic model reproduces the target statistics most consistently, across both data sources and across the range of correlation times examined, and generates far faster than the sequential Transformer. Specifically, for the energy-gap trajectories, augmentation from 0.1 ns of training data yields statistical estimates comparable in accuracy to those obtained from 0.25-0.50 ns of direct MD sampling. We further show that the benefit of synthetic augmentation is bounded by the information contained in the training data, producing a quality floor determined by both the training data and the generative model. Our findings establish diffusion-based generative models as an effective route to data-driven augmentation of stochastic time series in computational chemistry.

paper.title: Voltage versus concentration in ion channels: Physical signatures reveal rate-limiting steps
paper.abstract: Within the field of electrophysiology, I-V curves are a primary experimental means of characterizing ion channel behavior. By directly measuring ionic currents across membranes, electrophysiological techniques quantify key properties, including conductance, ion selectivity, and voltage dependence. We demonstrate a method of linking experimentally observed ion flux with microscopic mechanistic properties of channels. Although voltage and chemical potential can provide the same net electrochemical driving force, they perturb ion transport differently: voltage modifies transition rates throughout the permeation pathway, whereas chemical potential primarily alters ion uptake probabilities. Consequently, uptake, transfer, and release respond differently to the two driving forces, producing distinct flux signatures and causing chemical potential-driven flux to plateau while voltage-driven flux continues to increase. These differences encode the rate-limiting step (RLS) in open-channel flux. We propose a protocol based on three standard I-V measurements obtained under symmetric and asymmetric ion concentrations for elucidating the RLS. Application of this analysis to experimental data from the KcsA potassium channel identifies release as the RLS for outward permeation, consistent with available structural and computational evidence. Together, these results reveal how the physics of the electrochemical driving force shapes ion transport and provide an experimentally accessible strategy for connecting macroscopic electrophysiology measurements to microscopic transport mechanisms.
