paper.title: Mechanistic Insights of Jahn–Teller Effect Suppression in High-Entropy Prussian Blue Analogue Cathodes
paper.abstract: Abstract The Jahn–Teller (J-T) effect, as discovered by Hermann Jahn and Edward Teller in 1937, often causes lattice distortion and structural instability in Mn-based battery materials. Recent studies suggest that high-entropy design may help suppress J-T distortion, yet the underlying mechanism remains largely elusive due to their compositional complexity and structural disorder. Herein, using a Mn-based Prussian blue analogue as a case study, we employed a machine learning interatomic potential combined with synchrotron extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS) to elucidate the fundamental mechanism of the J-T suppression in high-entropy materials. Unexpectedly, EXAFS spectra reveal the absence of the typical J-T Mn–N bond-length splitting in our high-entropy Prussian blue analogue sample, but instead a broader Mn–N bond-length distribution. Machine learning-assisted calculations demonstrate the [MnN6] octahedra exhibit randomly oriented distortions along x-, y-, and z-axes in high-entropy lattices, resulting in the local distortion averaging out at the macroscopic scale. Further analysis of the local Mn coordination environment reveals that the high-entropy configuration enhances d-electron delocalization and reduces the energy splitting between Mn dx2–y2 and dz2 orbitals. This allows two structurally and electronically distinct distortion modes to coexist within the lattice, which disrupts long-range cooperative J-T order. Strikingly, the ultralong cycling stability of high-entropy K0.46[Mn0.21Co0.19Ni0.21Cu0.20Zn0.19][Fe(CN)6]0.98·1.69H2O is experimentally demonstrated, achieving 91.0% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles for aqueous ammonium-ion storage, which surpasses all of the Mn-based rechargeable batteries to date. Our study uncovers the microscopic mechanism of J-T suppression in high-entropy materials and provides an effective strategy for designing durable high-entropy battery electrodes.

paper.title: Glass-Box Deep Reinforcement Learning for High-Speed Flow Control
paper.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is challenging long-held assumptions in active flow control. By learning directly from interaction with a flow, DRL agents can find actuation strategies for nonlinear, unsteady flows without explicit models, often exploiting mechanisms that classical control would not anticipate. High-speed flows are a demanding test of this promise: shocks, shock/boundary-layer interactions, transition, aerothermal loading and microsecond-scale dynamics strain both algorithms and hardware. Yet most demonstrations remain idealized, low-speed simulations with limited evidence of robustness, interpretability, transferability or experimental deployment. In this perspective, we examine what constrains DRL-based high-speed flow control, including compressible simulation cost and fidelity, data efficiency, sensing in extreme environments, reward design, explainability, and generalization across Mach and Reynolds number. We argue that these limits reflect a tension between data-driven optimization and the structured physics, constraints and uncertainties of real flows. We then highlight where DRL may go beyond conventional approaches: adaptive control of shock-induced separation and turbulent boundary layers, coordination of distributed actuators, and discovery of unconventional flow-manipulation mechanisms.The central challenge, however, is translating these capabilities into reliable technology, which will require validated compressible simulation environments, physics- and constraint-aware learning, robustness to off-design conditions and sensor degradation, real-time operation, hardware-in-the-loop and wind-tunnel validation, and credible pathways to safety and certification.

paper.title: Nickel crossover builds single-atom catalysts
paper.abstract: An article in Advanced Materials demonstrates that nickel single-atom catalysts can be formed in situ within a CO2 electrolyser, achieving nearly 100% Faradaic efficiency towards CO.
paper.tldr: 该研究表明，在CO₂电解槽中原位形成的镍单原子催化剂，对一氧化碳的法拉第效率接近100%，为高效电催化提供了新途径。

paper.title: Decoding Perovskite Interfaces: Machine Learning Uncovers Geometry‐Matched Dual‐Site Hydrogen Bonding
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular passivation is central to efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics, yet interfacial molecules are still largely selected through chemical intuition and iterative experimentation. Here, an interpretable machine‐learning framework is developed that extracts chemically meaningful structure–performance relationships from literature data and uses them to guide molecular screening. Using approximately 100 data points, the model quantitatively relates six molecular and material features to photovoltaic performance, while SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis ranks their relative contributions and identifies hydrogen‐bonding capacity and adsorption strength as the two most influential factors. Guided by these data‐derived relationships, nine previously unexplored molecules were screened, with 2‐amino‐thiazole‐4‐carboxamide (ATC) and 1‐(2‐aminoethyl)‐1H‐pyrrole‐2,5‐dione (MPD) emerging as leading candidates. Theoretical and experimental investigations show that MPD exhibits stronger Pb 2 + coordination, whereas ATC forms stronger geometry‐matched multisite N─H···I interactions, increasing the calculated iodide‐migration barrier from 0.39 to 0.67 eV and suppressing interfacial iodide redistribution. ATC‐modified cells achieve a PCE of 27.13% and a certified stabilized efficiency of 26.59%, while retaining 90% of their initial efficiency after 1460 h of unencapsulated operation. The strategy further delivers efficiencies of 24.01% and 21.14% in 20.98 cm 2 rigid and 21.0 cm 2 flexible modules, respectively, providing a data‐to‐mechanism route for rational and scalable perovskite interface engineering.

paper.title: Reader--Writer Coupling in Transformer MLPs
paper.abstract: A transformer MLP gives each hidden channel two roles: a reader that decides when the channel responds, and a writer that decides what it adds back to the residual stream. Read as a key--value memory, the layer can be measured one factor set at a time: the pairing of readers to writers is carried only by their shared index, invisible to any quantity computed from one factor set alone. Yet training couples the two factors through their joint update, so we ask what reading them together shows. The block supplies the joint instrument: the MLP writes back into the very stream it reads, so the exact Jacobian of its update is square, and its agreement with its own transpose resolves into reader--writer terms whose inner products give each channel, read as a couple, a signed pairing coordinate. Ranked by this coordinate, each block we measure has a small core of strongly coupled channels; where initialization gives either sign equally, the core is nearly all opposed: each writer points against the direction its reader responds to. This opposed core recurs from the smallest models trained from scratch to released checkpoints; its sign is in place within a few percent of training and holds while the coupling grows. Read as couples, most channels return their contribution against the reader that fired it, and the readers of later blocks take it up; few show in the logits. Training holds the couples in place: flipping the opposed writers moves the output toward common tokens, and a writer permuted onto another reader regrows to fit that reader while the reader stays.
paper.tldr: 该研究表明，Transformer MLP中同一隐藏通道的读取器与写入器虽在功能上独立，但由于训练中的联合更新和雅可比矩阵的对称性，它们之间存在隐含耦合，并可通过方阵转置一致性来量化。

paper.title: RheOPT: Few-Shot Non-Newtonian Flow Prediction via Newtonian Pretraining of RheOFormer
paper.abstract: Despite advances in numerical methods, non-Newtonian flow simulations remain computationally expensive because velocity and stress must be advanced together through rate- and history-dependent constitutive dynamics. Neural-operator surrogates reduce inference cost after training, but their training data require the same expensive simulations they aim to replace, making data-efficient learning essential when only a few non-Newtonian simulations can be afforded. Here, we introduce the Rheological Operator Pretrained Transformer (RheOPT), which pretrains a transformer-based neural operator on inexpensive Newtonian simulations and fine-tunes it on a small number of non-Newtonian samples. Rather than transferring the Newtonian constitutive response itself, RheOPT reuses geometry-conditioned transport structure that remains useful after the stress model changes. We evaluate RheOPT in two geometry-matched settings: a $4{:}1$ contraction channel for Giesekus, Oldroyd-B, and Bingham fluids, and the oscillatory wake behind a triangular obstacle for Oldroyd-B flow. In the contraction, Newtonian pretraining substantially improves few-shot prediction, and a model fine-tuned on four target samples can match or exceed a from-scratch model trained on four times as many. This benefit is reliable under reversible instance normalization (RevIN) but dataset dependent under Global normalization, a difference we trace to the dynamic range of each fluid's velocity and stress fields. In the wake, where relative $L_2$ error alone cannot verify that vortex shedding is recovered, phase-insensitive diagnostics show that pretraining recovers the shedding frequency and wake fluctuation amplitude that are suppressed by the from-scratch model in the few-shot regime. Overall, RheOPT establishes Newtonian simulation as a physically grounded pretraining source for data-efficient non-Newtonian operator learning.
paper.tldr: 该研究表明，通过在廉价牛顿流体模拟上预训练，再少量微调非牛顿案例，可显著降低非牛顿流动预测成本并提升数据效率。

paper.title: Determining depth-resolved spatial distribution of solid–electrolyte interphase using non-destructive angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy for lithium-metal batteries
paper.abstract: The solid electrolyte interphase is a key performance regulator in Li-metal batteries, which are regarded as an important technology for future energy storage. Understanding this crucial interphase through non-destructive analysis is essential to advance the performance and lifespan of Li-metal batteries. We introduce angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy as a non-destructive technique for the depth-profile analysis of the solid electrolyte interphase in Li-metal batteries. Importantly, we show that this characterization technique displays a distinct advantage in preserving the solid electrolyte interphase's integrity compared to traditional sputtering-based depth-profiling. Our findings add to the understanding of compositional differences in the solid electrolyte interphase before the onset of Li electrodeposition and after Li plating. Moreover, we find significant variations in the thickness and distribution of solid electrolyte interphase species across different classes of electrolytes, which strongly influence the solid electrolyte interphase's protective properties and, by extension, Li-metal battery performance. This study benchmarks the application of angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy in revealing detailed, depth-resolved chemical composition of the solid electrolyte interphase in a non-destructive approach. Understanding the solid–electrolyte interphase formed on lithium is vital for improving the lifetime of lithium metal batteries. Here, authors show that angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy can reveal the depth-dependent composition of the interfacial layer without damaging it by ion sputtering.
paper.tldr: 该研究证明角分辨X射线光电子能谱可无损分析锂金属电池中固态电解质界面相的深度分布，优于传统方法且能保持其完整性。

paper.title: An efficient approach to electron-phonon coupling calculations of heterostructures within an all-electron framework
paper.abstract: A major challenge in calculating electron-phonon coupling at interfaces from first principles is the prohibitive computational cost due to the large supercells involved. Here, we present an efficient approach, which builds the electron-phonon matrix of weakly bound heterostructures from the properties of the isolated layers. The two key ingredients, the dynamical matrices and the potential response, are constructed in two steps. In the expansion step, these quantities are folded from the unit cells onto the supercell through an exact Fourier mapping. In the addition step, the interatomic force constants and the potential responses of the heterostructure are assembled blockwise from the corresponding quantities of the isolated layers, neglecting the weak interlayer contribution. The method is implemented in the electron-phonon module of the all-electron full-potential code exciting, enabling efficient calculations of the electron-phonon self-energy. We demonstrate the approach for the phonon dispersion and spectral functions of bilayer WSe$_2$ and pyridine/MoS$_2$, in comparison with exact reference calculations.
paper.tldr: 该方法通过傅里叶映射与叠加策略，显著降低了异质结构电子-声子耦合计算成本，并保持了全电子框架的准确性。

paper.title: Dynamic Extraction of Internal Active Species in Liquid Metal-Based Biphasic Catalyst
paper.abstract: Abstract Catalyst development is pivotal for industrial and energy advancements, yet it is fundamentally challenged by the static nature of the conventional solid catalysts. Their active sites, locked within rigid frameworks, are neither dynamically responsive nor regenerable, leading to an irreversible consumption during reaction cycles. Herein, we report an electrocapillary-enhanced dynamic extraction process to design a liquid metal-based biphasic catalyst (LMBC), enabling precise population control and in situ regeneration of active species. We establish two key thermodynamic criteria for the dynamic extraction mechanism to guide the LMBC development: alloying energy, which governs the tendency of active elements to form solid active alloys within the liquid metal matrix (gallium, Ga), and surface energy, which drives the dynamic extraction and surface exposure of internal active alloys. Through this mechanism, the quantity of exposed active species becomes adaptively adjustable, allowing fine-tuned control over the catalytic activity. Moreover, deactivated species can be replenished in situ from the liquid metal interior. This LMBC platform demonstrates universality and scalability in the alloy composition across diverse catalysis systems. Overall, this work provides a novel strategy for designing adaptive renewable catalytic systems.
paper.tldr: 该研究提出液态金属双相催化剂，通过电毛细作用实现活性物种的动态提取与原位再生，突破了传统固态催化剂活性位点静态受限的瓶颈。
affiliations: Tianjin University , , ,
paper.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

paper.title: How Far Can Foundation Models Be Distilled for Efficient Jet Tagging?
paper.abstract: Jet tagging is one of the most important applications of machine learning at the Large Hadron Collider. Recent models build in more physics knowledge or rely on large-scale pretraining, but the experiments place strict limits on their inference cost. Knowledge distillation can transfer their performance to small students that are cheap to run. We ask which properties of a teacher help the student, how small a student can get and how close it can come to the state of the art. On a jet tagging benchmark, we distil six teachers that differ in architecture, symmetry and pretraining, including two foundation models, into five small students. Every teacher improves every student, and the gain depends mainly on the strength of the teacher. We then shrink our two strongest distilled students, Transformer and L-GATr-slim, in width and in depth. With 20 thousand parameters, a distilled L-GATr-slim outperforms every published jet tagger trained from scratch at a fraction of the inference cost of every teacher. Even with two thousand parameters, it matches ParT, a model with a thousand times as many parameters. We also study what the students learn from their teachers. Our benchmark of inference cost shows that students of the same size can differ by almost an order of magnitude in speed. We release the code and the weights of all trained models.
paper.tldr: 该研究通过六种教师模型蒸馏至五种小型学生模型，证明所有教师均能提升学生性能，并评估了模型尺寸与性能的平衡极限。

paper.title: Atomic identification via the Prandtl-Tomlinson stick-slip mechanism
paper.abstract: Distinguishing atomic species is an ongoing challenge in the field of scanning probe microscopy. Typically, atomic force microscopy makes use of electrostatic interactions to perform atomic identification. Here we perform lateral force microscopy (LFM) measurements with a CO terminated tip of a partially oxidized Cu(110) surface and show clear differences between the metal and oxygen sites over a large z-range. This allows for atomic identification on a typical metal oxide. Density functional theory based calculations show that the tip-sample interaction is dominated by short-ranged orbital interactions and that the electrostatic contribution is negligible. At small tip-sample distances, LFM can probe the Prandtl-Tomlinson stick-slip mechanism on the single-atom scale. It is visible as a striking asymmetry in the forward and backward scan directions, experimentally revealing this fundamental model for nanotribology on the single-atom scale.
paper.tldr: 该研究通过横向力显微镜测量，并结合密度泛函理论计算，证明针尖与样品间的短程轨道相互作用主导了原子识别，静电力贡献可忽略。

paper.title: Capillary forces between two identical spherical particles
paper.abstract: The properties of colloidal suspensions and granular matter change drastically upon adding a small amount of liquid capable of forming capillary bridges between the solid particles. The attractive forces exerted by these liquid bridges induce the formation of particle aggregates and networks, which radically changes the macroscopic mechanical and rheological behaviour. Predicting these forces across bridge sizes, particle separations and wettability is therefore central to particle-scale modelling of capillary suspensions and wet granular matter. While the Young-Laplace equation governing the properties of the liquid bridges is well known, it lacks a convenient analytical solution. Current simulations therefore employ approximate analytic expressions, typically developed for contact angles below ~40° and bridge volumes below ~2.5% of the solid particle's volume. We compare several frequently used expressions from the literature with numerical solutions of the theoretical capillary forces. An overall good agreement is observed in the aforementioned parameter ranges, while the approximate expressions start to deviate outside their intended domains. We propose accurate and computationally efficient expressions for the capillary force that model this behaviour, for contact angles from 5° to 80° and bridge volumes from $10^{-6}$ to 0.15. We also explore mesoscopic 'fluid-scale' simulations of bridges by Multi-body Dissipative Particle Dynamics (MDPD), to ascertain whether this coarse-grained fluid model faithfully captures the continuum capillary forces. Remarkably, a good agreement is observed even for liquid bridges described by a mere few dozen fluid particles. Together, these results offer two approaches, at different resolution scales, for simulating bridges over a wide range of bridge volumes and contact angles.
paper.tldr: 该研究指出，预测毛细桥吸引力对湿颗粒材料建模至关重要，但Young-Laplace方程缺乏便捷解析解，需数值方法计算。

paper.title: Emergent Entropic Forces Drive Inverse and Reentrant Phase Transitions in Condensates of Intrinsically Disordered Proteins
paper.abstract: We present a phenomenological, mean-field model for condensates of intrinsically disordered proteins that describes inverse phase transitions and qualitatively predicts reentrant phase behavior as a function of salt concentration. The model is based on a matrix-based formulation of the Flory-Huggins free energy, in which the enthalpic interaction parameter and the protein valence, defined here as the number of effective "sticky patches", are treated as free parameters. Its central insight is that integrating out dynamics of fast-moving molecular species generates an effective entropic force that increases the free-energy barrier to mixing, even within a mean-field description. We account for this by linking Gaussian integration of co-solutes to the Schur complement of the matrix-based Flory-Huggins free energy. This provides a general thermodynamic framework illustrating how enthalpic interactions that increase the number of available microstates necessarily induce effective entropic forces. We demonstrate the expressiveness and predictive power of the model by qualitatively reproducing recent experimental observations on the rabies virus phosphoprotein.
paper.tldr: 该模型揭示盐浓度调控无序蛋白凝聚体转变源自熵驱动的有效力，并预测逆相变与重入行为的出现。

paper.title: Local and Sparse Kernel Operator Learning for Incompressible Flows: An Operator Lagrange Formulation
paper.abstract: We present a local and sparse kernel method for learning the solution operators of incompressible flows. It builds on our earlier property-preserving kernel method, whose global output reconstruction and dense operator regression scale poorly. Our method replaces the global output reconstruction by local divergence-free interpolants with divergence-free polynomials of any degree, solved in parallel on the GPU. These interpolants are divergence free, periodic on periodic domains, and, with a multiscale kernel, approach Kolmogorov statistics under refinement. A compactly supported kernel, positive semidefinite in any input dimension, makes the operator regression sparse. Its support radius, and hence the sparsity, is fitted to data, and optional affine polynomials in the input capture global trends. Operator Lagrange weights join the two. They cost one sparse solve per new input and act on the training fields before the output reconstruction, so their local coefficients are never formed. We show that, unlike direct evaluation, Lagrange evaluation does not amplify solve errors by the cancellation among spatial coefficients. On ten fluid benchmarks, validation selects sparse matrices nearly everywhere, with densities that mostly decrease as the training set grows, and affine augmentation lowers the error by more than an order of magnitude for forced isotropic turbulence. These sparse models are at least as accurate as our earlier dense method and more accurate than neural operators. Lagrange evaluation is as accurate as direct evaluation with local output reconstructions, and up to nearly three orders of magnitude more accurate with global ones. We also present GPU timings and storage.
paper.tldr: 该研究表明，所提出的局部稀疏核算子方法可高效求解不可压缩流，同时保持无散度等物理约束，并能在GPU上并行计算。

paper.title: Manifold-Informed Neural Networks for Low-Label ECG Electrolyte Inference
paper.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) supervise on the residual of a known differential operator. Many high-stakes inference problems admit no such operator: clinical signals, behavioral measurements, materials properties. We introduce the Manifold-Informed Neural Network (MINN), a PINN-parallel paradigm that replaces the physics operator residual with a manifold operator residual: a discrete Poisson equation $\mathbf{L}_G \mathbf{H} = s_φ(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{m})$ on a $k$-nearest-neighbor graph in the learned latent space, with a learned, task-aware source. The construction is a structural parallel to PINNs (squared operator residual plus label data, in place of operator residual plus boundary data); the $s{=}0$ limit recovers the homogeneous Laplace equation $\mathbf{L}_G\mathbf{H}=\mathbf{0}$ (classical manifold regularization solves the same equation but minimizes the Dirichlet energy $\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{H}^\top\mathbf{L}_G\mathbf{H})$, a different penalty form). The source $s_φ$ takes input features and auxiliary metadata directly, breaking the homogeneous smoothness prior that limits classical Laplacian penalties; gated Feature-wise Linear Modulation separately fuses metadata into the prediction branch. We evaluate MINN on three-class classification of potassium, calcium, and magnesium from 12-lead ECGs in MIMIC-IV-ECG, against twelve baselines spanning supervised and tabular methods, ECG foundation models, and manifold/graph approaches. MINN attains the highest K$^+$ Macro-F1 of 0.61 (best baseline 0.55), with consistent gains on Ca$^{2+}$ and Mg$^{2+}$ and a 31% relative improvement at 1% labeled data. Six targeted ablations show that the inhomogeneous Poisson formulation, not graph smoothing alone, drives the gain.
paper.tldr: 该研究表明，在低标注心电数据场景下，流形信息神经网络通过学习潜空间中的算子残差，比传统物理信息网络更能有效推断电解质水平。

paper.title: Learning Computational Structure for Sample-Efficient Prediction
paper.abstract: Statistical learning in high dimensions suffers from the curse of dimensionality. Fortunately, many functions of practical interest are compositionally sparse, meaning they admit a composition of local functions, each depending on only a few variables, allowing sample complexity to depend on local arity rather than ambient dimension. Yet realizing this benefit requires exploiting hidden compositional structure, which theory does not establish for practical gradient-based training. We study this gap with CSFRBench, a controlled benchmark that hides the target's compositional computation during training but retains it for diagnosis, and find that dense networks and sparsity-based baselines leave much of that benefit unrealized. Inspired by the spatial organization of biological neural circuits, we introduce Learned Wiring (LeWi): each neuron has a learned low-dimensional embedding, only nearby neurons connect, and embeddings and weights are trained jointly. LeWi improves sample efficiency on targets with hierarchical structure, intermediate reuse, or independent modules. Across 32 additional targets generated by independently sampled computation graphs, LeWi is the most sample-efficient method not given the target graph, with 27% lower mean learning-curve area than dense networks. Dense networks perform better on targets with a single high-arity function. LeWi's representations and connectivity align with the target computation. On 17 world-model prediction tasks spanning control, navigation, and manipulation, LeWi beats the dense baseline on 16 and wins 99/119 baseline comparisons. These results show that jointly learning connectivity and weights can exploit computational structure to improve sample efficiency.
paper.tldr: 该研究表明，基于梯度的训练可有效利用隐藏的组合稀疏结构，在高维预测中实现样本效率提升，但现有理论尚未充分解释其机制。

paper.title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
paper.abstract: Solution-phase synthesis of monolayer hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites is constrained by rapid out-of-plane crystal growth, uncontrolled nucleation, and strong interlayer aggregation, yielding flakes of only a few μm. We introduce a steric-engineering ternary-solvent growth strategy to synthesize monolayer and few-layer A2MX4 hybrid perovskites with exceptionally large surface areas. By combining alcohol cosolvents with an amine additive, out-of-plane stacking is suppressed. Using (PEA)2CuCl4 as a model system, monolayers with lateral areas exceeding 1000 μm2 are achieved, representing a massive dimensional increase over conventional methods. Molecular dynamics and quantum-chemical calculations show that longer-chain alcohols reorganize precursor solvation, while solvent volatility prolongs edge-mediated precursor transport during annealing. This strategy demonstrates universal applicability across diverse organic spacer cations (PEA+, F-PEA+, PentA+), metal centers (Cu2+, Mn2+, Pb2+), and halides (Cl-, Br-, I-). The large lateral dimensions enable direct, solvent-free electrical contact fabrication via physical shadow masking, bypassing chemical degradation from solvents used in conventional lithography. Planar devices fabricated from isolated ultrathin (PEA)2PbI4 channels exhibit ultra-low dark currents down to the 10^-15 - 10^-13 A range, enabling femtowatt-to-picowatt static power consumption, ~ 0.2 pW at 5 V, a 250-fold reduction relative to drop-cast films, while maintaining a high light-to-dark current ratio of 4.3 x 102. This work establishes precise steric and solvation control as a paradigm for scalable, compositionally diverse, low-static-power monolayer 2D perovskite optoelectronics.
paper.tldr: 该三元溶剂策略通过空间位阻工程合成超大面积单层杂化钙钛矿，尺寸提升逾百倍，为无光刻低功耗光电子器件提供新途径。

paper.title: Conditional Flow Models Convert Epistemic Uncertainty into Apparent Aleatoric Variance
paper.abstract: Conditional Flow Models (CFMs) are increasingly being used in place of deterministic predictors across machine learning, including for tasks that were classically formulated as regression. Given their success in such tasks, we ask the question: what useful information do the conditional distributions produced by CFMs carry beyond what a point predictor would provide? We identify a systematic phenomenon: in many natural regimes, CFM samples routinely have larger variance than the true conditional distribution, even in nearly deterministic regression problems. This effect is most pronounced where the model has not resolved the dependence on the conditioning variable, and thus the additional variance can be viewed as converting epistemic uncertainty in fitting the ground truth conditional distribution into apparent aleatoric variance in the generated samples. Through controlled synthetic and real-data experiments, and comparisons with explicit smoothing estimators, we show that the induced variance tracks model underfitting of complex or hard-to-fit targets, and decreases with additional training or data. We provide a theoretical account of the phenomenon in a simplified setting and demonstrate a consequent practical use-case of conditional flow-matching: designing high-coverage predictive sets that cover the ground-truth regression target.
paper.tldr: 条件流模型在自然场景中常将认知不确定性放大为表观随机方差，导致预测方差系统性地高于真实条件分布。

paper.title: Gene conversion is a key driver of diversity hotspots in Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens and virulence-associated loci
paper.abstract: Despite the long-held view of Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( Mtb ) as a genetically conserved pathogen, many genomic regions remain poorly resolved due to high sequence homology and repetitive content. Using complete genome assemblies generated from long-read sequencing of 151 globally representative clinical isolates, we comprehensively analyzed genome-wide patterns of genetic diversity and evolution across the Mtb genome. Our analysis uncovers pronounced diversity hotspots within paralogous regions (PRs) generated by recurrent gene conversion between homologous genes. In many cases, these hotspots exhibit more than an order of magnitude greater genetic diversity than the rest of the Mtb genome, which is otherwise characterized by remarkably low variation. Mutations within these regions display clustered substitution patterns, excess paralog-matching variants, and distinct mutational spectra consistent with ongoing gene conversion. Our analysis identifies over 300 individual gene conversion events (GCEs) distributed throughout the Mtb phylogeny. These GCEs occur predominantly within gene families associated with virulence and host–pathogen interactions, including the PE, PPE, and ESX families. Several of the most pronounced diversity hotspots occur in antigens encoded within PRs. Among these, the vaccine candidate PPE18 harbors mutations in validated epitope sequences and predicted alterations in HLA-II binding. Together, these findings demonstrate that gene conversion actively shapes antigenic and virulence-associated diversity in Mtb .
paper.tldr: 基因转换（gene conversion）在同源基因间反复发生，是结核分枝杆菌抗原及毒力相关位点多样性热点形成的关键驱动力。

paper.title: Influence of embedding depth on the pullout of a plate from a confined granular medium
paper.abstract: Understanding the behaviour of moving objects within confined granular media is important in many technical applications. In this work we study the vertical pullout of a plate-like intruder buried at different depths within a dense granular aggregate from the onset of motion to flow around the intruder in the steady state by means of a two-dimensional polygonal Discrete Element Method. We find that the peak and steady-state drag forces depend differently on their embedding depth for different friction coefficients. Depending on the strength of friction the plate may interact with the domain walls, which enhances the drag force until failure of the aggregate, but not in the steady-state as dilation around intruder directs the force chains emanating from the plate upwards and away from the walls. If the inter-particle friction is weak, it is possible for the overhead pressure to overcome frictional resistance beyond a certain embedding depth. This prevents the formation of dilated failure zones above the intruder and changes the failure mode of the aggregate, leading to a slower decay of the steady-state drag forces with pullout distance.
paper.tldr: 数值模拟显示，埋深对板状物体在受限颗粒介质中的拔出峰值力和稳态阻力影响显著，且这种影响受颗粒摩擦系数调控，高摩擦下板体可与边界相互作用增大阻力。

paper.title: Interfacial origin of magnetic compensation and topological-like Hall effect in crystalline lutetium iron garnet thin films.
paper.abstract: Ferrimagnetic oxides such as rare-earth iron garnets (REIG) have emerged as essential components of spin-based devices owing to their high Curie temperatures, low Gilbert damping, and excellent insulating properties. Recently, REIGs have attracted immense interest for hosting robust chiral spin textures that can be potential information carriers in next-generation spintronic devices. Here we investigate the structural, chemical, and magnetic behaviour of single-crystal Lu3Fe5O12 (LuIG) thin films for different film thicknesses on a Gd3(Mg,Zr)Ga5O12(111) or SGGG(111) substrate. Our results demonstrate the presence of a 3 nm-thick Gd-rich LuIG layer at the LuIG/SGGG interface, which gives rise to a magnetic compensation temperature around 50 K. We further probe the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in LuIG layers with an adjacent platinum ultrathin film. In addition to the magnetic compensation point, the AHE loops show pronounced nonmonotonic features, often attributed to the spin Hall topological-like Hall effect (SH-THE) and non-collinear spin textures arising from the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI). LuIG thickness-dependent AHE measurements reveal that the composition variation due to Gd diffusion breaks the inversion symmetry and could contribute to DMI. These findings shed light on fundamental understanding and engineering of the different interfaces of magnetic garnets for advanced spintronic device applications.

paper.title: The Uhlenbeck–Ford model in two dimensions: Reference system for fluid-phase free-energy calculations
paper.abstract: We investigate the Uhlenbeck–Ford (UF) model as a reference system for free-energy calculations in two-dimensional (2D) fluids. The 2D virial coefficients are computed exactly up to the tenth order and combined with molecular simulation data to construct highly accurate numerical representations of the equation of state and the excess Helmholtz free energy. We then determine the phase diagram of the model in order to establish the thermodynamic stability limits of the fluid phase and thereby identify the range of applicability of the UF model as a fluid reference system. In the course of this analysis, we identify the solid, hexatic, and fluid phases and show that the fluid remains the only thermodynamically stable phase, independent of density, for scaling parameters up to p ≲ 70. Finally, we demonstrate the practical applicability of the 2D UF model as a reference system through thermodynamic integration calculations of the free energy of a two-dimensional Lennard-Jones fluid.

paper.title: Electrochemical Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer Free Energy Surfaces from Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics
paper.abstract: Abstract Proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) is an elementary step in many electrocatalytic reactions, yet molecular-level descriptions of solvent reorganization energetics in these reactions remain limited. Herein, we describe a first-principles computational platform to calculate free energy surfaces and quantify reorganization energies for interfacial electrochemical PCET. Hydrogen electrosorption at Pt(111)/water interfaces is used as a model reaction to derive PCET free energy surfaces using ab initio molecular dynamics simulations in an explicit solvent. The reaction is described as a non-adiabatic transition between reactant and product states defined in terms of localization of electrons and the transferring quantized proton. Free energy surfaces are calculated from statistical fluctuations of the vertical energy gap. This computational approach directly incorporates explicit solvent dynamics into the calculated reorganization energies that are obtained from parabolic fits to the reactant and product free energy surfaces. The reorganization energies are quantitatively similar to the mean vertical energy gap near the free energy minima of the reactant and product state free energy surfaces. The calculated PCET reorganization energy of 3.19 eV compares favorably with previous semi-empirical estimates. This work establishes a robust computational platform to assess the role of interfacial solvent properties on intrinsic electrochemical kinetics.

paper.title: Comparing Nuclear Reaction Coordinates Driving Photoinduced Proton-Coupled Electron and Energy Transfer
paper.abstract: Abstract Proton transfer is coupled to electron transfer or electronic excitation energy transfer in proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) and proton-coupled energy transfer (PCEnT) reactions, respectively. Although photoinduced PCET and PCEnT have been studied extensively in anthracene–phenol–pyridine molecular triads, the nuclear reaction coordinates for these two pathways are still unknown. Herein, we identify the nuclear reaction coordinates for PCET and PCEnT in the triads by sampling the seam space between the relevant intersecting diabatic states. The reaction coordinate has contributions mainly from anthracene and phenol for PCET but involves the entire triad, including pyridine, for PCEnT. Both reaction coordinates involve motions related to contraction of the phenol C–O bond as well as motions within the anthracene rings that differ for PCET and PCEnT due to different charge distributions. The proton acceptor motion contributes more to the PCEnT than the PCET reaction coordinate. Both PCET and PCEnT reactions are concerted in that there is no stable intermediate, but they are both most likely asynchronous. Our analysis also suggests that PCET proceeds through a conical intersection in its minimum energy pathway, whereas PCEnT moves through an avoided crossing. The quantum mechanical treatment of the transferring proton within a vibronically nonadiabatic framework suggests that the kinetic isotope effect may be greater for PCEnT than for PCET, although more extensive calculations are required for confirmation. Understanding the fundamental similarities and differences between PCET and PCEnT mechanisms will help guide the design of proton-coupled systems that favor either charge transfer or energy transfer.

paper.title: ML/MM
paper.abstract: Electrostatic embedding allows a local machine-learning potential to respond to an extended molecular environment without including every environmental atom in its message-passing graph. We construct a fixed-charge machine-learning/molecular-mechanics (ML/MM) interface for the pretrained MACE-POLAR-1-M model. Analytic Gaussian monopole and dipole operators supply the environmental potential, the internal electrostatic features, and the interaction energy. Differentiation through both field-conditioned density updates gives forces on the model fragment and the environment, which are combined with a subtractive classical energy and exact link-atom force redistribution. A reciprocal-space extension treats three-dimensional periodicity at fixed cell. We assess the implementation using fixed-geometry numerical checks and 24 matched QM/MM reference calculations for a 2589-atom rhodopsin model, with 54 atoms in the neural-network graph. The analytic model gives a relative-energy root-mean-square error of 8.62 kJ mol−1 after one constant energy shift, and force-component errors of 0.07345 and 0.00797 eV Å−1 on the 53 real high-level atoms and 2536 environmental atoms, respectively. Analytic operators substantially reduce rotational errors while leaving the QM/MM accuracy essentially unchanged. A nearby water accounts for approximately 74% of the environmental squared force error. Matched charge-density and frozen-density force comparisons identify limitations of both the local multipole representation and its predicted coefficients. The results establish the numerical consistency of the embedding implementation and delimit the single-point accuracy of the transferred pretrained model.

paper.title: Combining Simulations and Spectroscopy to Design Protective Coatings on Sulfide Solid Electrolytes
paper.abstract: Sulfide solid electrolytes are attractive for all-solid-state batteries because of their high Li-ion conductivity and favorable processability, but their practical use is limited by electrochemical instability and moisture-induced degradation. Molecular surface coatings offer a scalable strategy to improve humidity tolerance and interfacial stability, yet there is limited understanding of the molecular-level factors governing surface interactions. By combining large-scale atomistic simulations enabled by a machine-learning potential with targeted experiments, we present a comprehensive framework for designing molecular coatings on Li$_6$PS$_5$Cl (LPSCl). Using a PET-MAD interatomic potential fine-tuned on an r$^2$SCAN reference dataset covering LPSCl surfaces, molecular adsorbates, and their interactions, we model surface adsorption of carboxylic (CA), sulfonic (SA), and phosphonic (PA) acids with alkyl chains of varying lengths and the interaction of these coated surfaces with water at finite temperature. The simulations show that lithiated head groups generally exhibit more favorable adsorption energies. Impedance spectroscopy shows that the lithiated coatings maintain 40--55\% of the initial ionic conductivity after powder processing. While adsorption strength is largely controlled by head-group chemistry and lithiation state, coating morphology depends primarily on alkyl-chain length and surface coverage. In particular, long-chain lithiated carboxylates form dense, brush-like hydrophobic layers that reduce water access to reactive Li surface sites, with protection setting in at a coating thickness of approximately 0.8 nm. Consistent with these predictions, longer carboxylate chains suppress H$_2$S evolution more effectively. Because thicker coatings also hinder Li-ion transport, intermediate chain lengths offer the best balance between moisture protection and ionic conductivity.

paper.title: Dataset merging strategy for efficient construction of a machine-learning force field: A case of CeO2 surfaces with an oxygen vacancy
paper.abstract: The accuracy and transferability of machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) critically depend on the quality of the training database. Here, we propose a dataset merging strategy for efficiently constructing a transferable MLFF for pristine and oxygen-defective CeO2 surfaces. The proposed strategy is based on three key elements: (1) initiating on-the-fly training from small, less stable slab models to accelerate early stage convergence by sampling diverse high-energy configurations; (2) sampling diverse local structures by gradually increasing the temperature during molecular dynamics simulations while avoiding excessively rapid atomic motions and unphysically short contacts; and (3) merging independently generated datasets from slab models with different thicknesses and defect conditions to improve transferability. The resulting MLFF is validated on larger slab models containing 144 atoms and applied to structural optimization of pristine and oxygen-defective surfaces as well as lattice oxygen diffusion pathways on defective surfaces. The predicted pathways and energy barriers are in good agreement with density functional theory results, particularly for pathways involving relatively large structural and energetic changes. Furthermore, the merged MLFF was applied to ideal CeO2(111) slabs containing up to 5183 atoms, yielding only weak size dependence of the predicted vacancy-migration barrier. These results highlight that systematic dataset merging across model sizes and configurations provides a practical route to constructing transferable MLFFs for complex oxide surfaces.

paper.title: Dual-Channel Solvation Forces at Polymer-Brush Interfaces
paper.abstract: Integrating statistical-mechanical pole theory with molecular dynamics simulations, we extend asymptotic correlation theory to polymer-brush-grafted soft interfaces, achieving quantitative, parameter-free predictions of oscillatory solvation free energies. We uncover a dual-channel physical mechanism governing inter-surface forces: interactions across disordered brushes are governed entirely by bulk-liquid correlations (the oscillatory channel), whereas dense, crystalline brushes induce capillary freezing of the confined solvent, opening a monotonic attraction channel of interfacial phase-transition origin.

paper.title: Low-variance force estimators for nuclear quantum mean forces
paper.abstract: Quantum equilibrium structure can be sampled using classical molecular dynamics with a learned effective potential for a single path-integral replica, but the primitive mean-force estimates obtained from path-integral molecular dynamics with that replica held fixed are noisy. We derive a scaled-gradient estimator with zero sampling variance for a one-dimensional harmonic oscillator and an estimated 4.7--57.5-fold reduction in constrained-sampling time for the molecular tests. The resulting potentials can be trained on these forces like standard machine-learning interatomic potentials and yield stable production simulations from which quantum expectation values of position-dependent observables are obtained as classical ensemble averages.

paper.title: Mechanism-Driven Optimization of Proton Transfer in Mn-Catalyzed Amine-Boranes Dehydrogenation: The Way to Turbo Mode
paper.abstract: Improving the efficiency of the individual steps in catalytic cycles is one of the main cornerstones of homogeneous catalysis. In particular, optimization of proton transfer processes by the incorporation of nitrogen donor moieties in the second coordination sphere of transition metal constitutes a privileged strategy to boost the rate and modulate the selectivity of electrocatalysts for small molecules activation. However, proton-relay strategies remain largely unexplored in homogeneous (de)hydrogenation, particularly through the use of exogenous nitrogen bases. We report herein that the rational choice of amine additive as proton transfer mediator can largely improve efficient Mn-based catalytic system for amine-borane dehydrogenation working through the cooperation between Mn + and MnH species. Addition of 1.0-5.0 mol% of simple tertiary amine such as Et 3 N led to 7-45-fold rate acceleration and the increase of TON values by 65-420% for all substrates. This upgrade is due to a combination of lower activation barrier for the rate-determining deprotonation of Mn-coordinated amine-boranes and a higher amount of catalytically active cationic metal species Mn+ present in solution under these conditions. In addition, meticulous mechanistic investigations revealed the crucial role of ammonium salt concentration in this catalytic process thus paving the way for further improvements. Accordingly, the use of a binary Et 3 N/Et 3 NH + mixture instead of pure Et 3 N again speeds up Mn-catalyzed Me 2 NHBH 3 dehydrogenation by a factor of ten to achieve unprecedented TOF of 125 s −1 and TON of 105 at 60°C. Beyond achieving the best performance reported to date for this substrate, our results highlight how the judicious optimization of a priori trivial elementary steps in the catalytic cycle, without altering the intrinsic reactivity of the metal center, can dramatically enhance the activity of an already highly efficient transition metal catalyst.

paper.title: Co-Titration of Phosphatidylserine Lipids and a Channel Protein Using Constant pH Molecular Dynamics
paper.abstract: The protonation state of anionic lipids plays a central role in regulating membrane electrostatics, structure, and interactions with membrane proteins. Lipid titration in membranes is inherently collective and strongly influenced by local composition and lateral organization. Experimentally, determining lipid p K ₐ values in heterogeneous and dynamically organized membranes is challenging, making it difficult to disentangle intrinsic lipid properties from collective membrane effects. Moreover, lipid and protein protonation states can be electrostatically coupled, such that changes in the ionization state of one component can influence the titration behavior of the other. Here, we use constant pH molecular dynamics (CpHMD) simulations to investigate the titration behavior of phosphatidylserine (PS) lipids in bilayers with varying PS content, ranging from dilute mixtures with phosphatidylcholine (PC) to fully anionic membranes, as well as the cotitration of proteins and lipids using the OmpF porin embedded in a titratable PS membrane. We show that the apparent pKa of the PS headgroup depends strongly on membrane composition, increasing systematically with PS surface density. We compare the CpHMD-derived pKa values of OmpF acidic residues in various lipid compositions, ranging from fixed-charge PS to mixed PS/PC and fully titratable PS membranes. The resulting pKa shifts demonstrate that the protonation state of the surrounding lipid environment can substantially modulate protein titration, demonstrating coupled lipid–protein ionization. Together, these results highlight the electrostatic coupling between membrane lipids and proteins and establish CpHMD as a framework for capturing composition-dependent protonation behavior in complex membrane environments.

paper.title: Machine Learning Accelerated Simulation of Charge Regulation Effects
paper.abstract: Many solvated materials, from nanoparticles to polyelectrolytes, acquire charge through the dissociation or association of surface groups, a phenomenon known as charge regulation (CR). Recent methods use hybrid charge regulation Monte Carlo (CR-MC)/molecular dynamics (MD) to evolve the system while dynamically adjusting charges on the surface groups. However, this approach is computationally expensive, as Monte Carlo sampling can be as costly as the accompanying MD. In this work, we introduce charge regulation machine learning (CR-ML), a graph attention network that predicts the ionization probability of every surface site from the instantaneous configuration, the dissociation constant of surface groups, and the solution conditions. We show that CR-ML reproduces the equilibrium conformations and degree of ionization obtained with CR-MC for a hydrophobic polyanion. We further test CR-ML on the more complex system of two nanoparticles mediated by a polyelectrolyte, where it accurately predicts the charge asymmetry that develops between the two particles. Across these systems, CR-ML updates charges an order of magnitude faster than CR-MC while accurately reproducing its equilibrium properties. This framework opens a path toward large-scale simulations of charge-regulating materials for understanding and designing their responsive behavior.

paper.title: Enhanced diffusion sampling: Efficient rare event sampling and free energy calculation with diffusion models
paper.abstract: The rare-event sampling problem has long been the central limiting factor in molecular dynamics, especially in biomolecular simulation. Recently, diffusion models such as BioEmu have emerged as powerful equilibrium samplers that generate independent samples from complex molecular distributions, eliminating the cost of sampling rare transition events. However, a sampling problem remains when computing observables that rely on states which are rare in equilibrium, for example, folding free energies. Here, we introduce enhanced diffusion sampling, enabling efficient exploration of rare-event regions while preserving unbiased thermodynamic estimators. The key idea is to perform quantitatively accurate steering protocols to generate biased ensembles and subsequently recover equilibrium statistics via exact reweighting. We instantiate our framework in three algorithms: UmbrellaDiff (umbrella sampling with diffusion models), MetaDiff (a batchwise analog for metadynamics), and ΔG-Diff (free-energy differences via tilted ensembles). We demonstrate the three methods on toy free-energy landscapes and apply ΔG-Diff to protein folding free-energy calculations with BioEmu. Our methods reduce the cost of rare-state estimation, enabling protein folding free-energy calculations in minutes to hours of graphics processing unit time per system.

paper.title: A Tutorial on Physics Constrained Machine Learning for Hybrid Modeling, Optimization, and Control
paper.abstract: Physics-constrained machine learning (PCML) integrates domain knowledge, first-principles, and physical constraints into AI/ML models. In this work, we present a step-by-step tutorial of a modular PCML framework, KKT-HardNet, and illustrate how it could be used for hybrid modeling, process simulation, optimization and model predictive control in a single platform. KKT-HardNet combines fast inference capabilities of neural networks with guaranteed satisfaction of algebraic constraints through differential projection. It can handle heterogeneous data and enforce both linear and nonlinear equality and inequality constraints. The modular design supports custom neural-network backbones and user-defined projection mechanisms for PCML. To enable efficient end-to-end training, KKT-HardNet exploits implicit function theorem to backpropagate through the projection layer. This avoids computationally expensive automatic differentiation. This work also introduces an exact reduced-order Fischer-Burmeister reformulation and a primal-dual interior-point method as an alternative projection solve strategy. We also provide a diverse set of benchmarking problems for PCML in engineering applications. KKT-HardNet achieves orders of magnitude better performance in terms of both constraint satisfaction and inference time. The KKT-HardNet code and the benchmark datasets are available at https://github.com/souls-tamu/kkt-hardnet .

paper.title: The unifying Role of the “Oxo Wall” concept in Oxygen Evolution Catalysis
paper.abstract: The rational design of catalytic active sites on the surface of solids enables efficient interfacial proton-electron transfer processes in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and is thus essential for high-performance water splitting on electrolyzer anodes. Popular examples of rational catalyst designs include the Sabatier principle associated with solid-state quantum-chemistry volcano-type reactivity predictions. The use of molecular unifying concepts to predict and rationalize the design of catalytic active OER sites on solid surfaces is rare. Here, we develop an a priori, chemically informed catalyst-design principle by transferring the oxo-wall concept of molecular coordination chemistry to bimetallic solid catalysts. The molecular “oxo wall” rule essentially states that tetragonal metal complexes with multi-bonded M=O ligands do not exist for metals to the right of group 8. We hypothesize that pairing metals located on opposite sides of the oxo wall creates complementary electronic functionality and leads to enhanced catalytic activity relative to combinations in which both metals lie on the same side. We show that this framework – although rooted in molecular ligand-field effects and developed and validated in coordination chemistry – is capable of predicting and rationalizing reactivity trends of solid-state mixed-metal layered double hydroxides OER catalysts. The very predictive character of the molecular “oxo wall” concept as to reactivity and stability of multiple-bond M-O cores makes it a unifying guiding principle for molecular and solid-state OER catalysis. We anticipate that the cross-disciplinary findings that bridge molecular chemistry and solid-state electrochemistry will help to better design of O 2 -based technologies with improved performance.

paper.title: When do machine-learning potentials need a configuration-dependent kernel? Learning long-range interactions with Fourier neural operators
paper.abstract: Long-range interactions in machine-learning interatomic potentials are commonly treated by coupling learned sources through either a prescribed electrostatic kernel or a learned but configurationindependent one. Whether such a kernel suffices depends on the underlying screened interaction. We address this question by using Fourier neural operators (FNOs) to learn how latent source fields, built from the descriptors of a local backbone (here MACE), interact across the simulation cell. For a synthetic ionic system with tunable screening, a prescribed Coulomb kernel underestimates the longwavelength charge fluctuations by 43% under strong screening, whereas the FNO reproduces them within 3% and recovers 95–99% of the variance of the residual left by the local backbone. A linear FNO, which learns a configuration-independent kernel, performs equally well in the homogeneous case. Under inhomogeneous screening, rearranging the remote medium modulates the coupling between distant ions, a dependence that no configuration-independent kernel can represent. Among the models tested, only the nonlinear FNO responds to this modulation, and its force errors are 27–41% lower than those of configuration-independent models. In first-principles benchmarks of liquid water, lithium lanthanum zirconate, and Au 2 /MgO(001), MACE–FNO is comparable to a prescribed-kernel model for the bulk systems and more accurate for the interface. It further captures the reversal of the Au 2 wetting preference induced by remote Al dopants, with deviations below 5meV per cell from density functional theory. These results indicate that a configuration-dependent kernel becomes necessary once the screening medium varies, even though the energy remains quadratic in the charges for a fixed medium. Nonlinear FNOs, which learn such a kernel from energies and forces alone, offer a flexible route to environment-dependent long-range interactions.

paper.title: PULSES: multi-agent AI for autonomous excited-state model building and dynamics
paper.abstract: Simulating molecular excited-state processes requires resolving electronic and nuclear dynamics, but the cost of direct quantum-chemical calculations limits accessible system sizes and timescales. Machine-learning models can extend these simulations, yet they often need to be tailored to specific molecular systems and scientific objectives. Building and deploying such models requires coordinated decisions across conformational sampling, quantum-chemical labelling, model training, validation and dynamics. Here we introduce Paired agents for Unified Learning and Simulation of Excited States (PULSES), a multi-agent system that automates this workflow within expert-approved boundaries. A human expert and planner define the scientific objective, methods and decision boundaries, while an orchestrator coordinates domain agents and artifact-specific scientific assurance during execution. We evaluate PULSES on 15 computational chemistry tasks and demonstrate end-to-end applications to perylene exciton Hamiltonians, solvent-dependent biphenyl relaxation, and excited-state proton transfer in 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline. These results demonstrate traceable, expert-bounded construction and deployment of specialized excited-state models, while retaining scientific validation as a requirement rather than assuming that successful execution establishes correctness.

paper.title: Single-molecule cold chemistry: Isotopic branching ratios of the $\mathrm{H_2O^+ + HD}$ reaction at cryogenic temperatures
paper.abstract: Isotopic branching in ion-molecule reactions influences interstellar deuterium fractionation, yet its dynamics remain poorly understood for many important systems at astrophysically relevant temperatures. Here, we investigate H- and D-atom transfer in the $\mathrm{H_2O^+ + HD}$ reaction using single sympathetically cooled water ions in a cryogenic radiofrequency trap. Nondestructive identification of the products from 441 individual reaction events at a mean collision energy of 7 K reveals an $\mathrm{H_3O^+/H_2DO^+}$ product branching ratio of $1.50 \pm 0.15$ demonstrating a preferential H-atom transfer. The experiments are rationalized using quasi-classical-trajectory calculations which indicate a transition from direct dynamics at higher energies to a complex-mediated reaction under the present experimental conditions and point to an important role of intramolecular vibrational redistribution affecting the isotopic branching in this regime. The present results extend measurements into an astrochemically relevant energy regime and establish cryogenic single-ion chemistry as a new platform for resolving competing reaction pathways.

paper.title: Methodological Optimization of ATR-IR Spectroelectrochemistry for Powdered and Poorly Conductive Electrocatalysts
paper.abstract: In-situ infrared spectroscopy combined with electrochemistry has become a key tool for studying the processes that govern the activity of electrocatalysts under operating conditions. However, its application has been limited almost exclusively to model electrodes, which are either electronically conductive or specifically designed to maximise the ATR optical signal, thereby limiting its use for a family of emerging heterogenous catalysts typically available in powder form and exhibiting poor electrical conductivity. Extending ATR-IR spectroelectrochemistry to this type of catalyst requires simultaneously reconciling optical, adhesion and electrochemical requirements which, until now, have rarely been addressed systematically. Rather than focusing on the elucidation of electrocatalyst mechanisms, this paper presents a structured and transferable methodology for optimising ATR-IR spectroelectrochemical measurements on emerging classes of electrocatalyst. Three groups of interrelated parameters that mostly affect the feasibility of the technique, namely spectroscopic, interfacial and electrochemical parameters, are discussed proposing a step-by-step workflow that enables their methodological standardization and balance. The proposed workflow is validated by applying this methodology to three different materials (Ni(OH) 2 , ZnO and Zn-Al LDH) showing distinct spectroscopic, electrochemical and interfacial properties. The results demonstrate that, following appropriate optimisation, ATR spectroelectrochemistry can be extended to more challenging powdered catalyst layers, providing a practical and generalisable guide for future robust mechanistic investigations of this broad family of materials and contributing to the rational understanding and development of new electrocatalysts for reactions of energy and chemical interest.

paper.title: Anisotropic Electrical Conductivity in Close-Packed Two-Dimensional Polyaramids
paper.abstract: Polyaramids such as Kevlar ® are renowned for their high mechanical strength and chemical resistance; however, their non-conjugated backbones render them electrically insulating. Orbital alignment can allow close-packed stacked molecules to exhibit long range conduction, opening the possibility that insulating nanomaterials may form conducting arrangements. Herein, we report two-dimensional (2D) polyaramids with tailored end-groups that promote tighter molecular packing as their size decreases. Terminal groups with the size of a single methyl result in aligned films that exhibit highly anisotropic electrical conductivity up to 1.39 × 10 –4 S m –1 , comparable to or exceeding many undoped conjugated polymers. Charge transport occurs orthogonally across aligned, stacked polymer platelets while the in-plane direction remains insulating. The anisotropy reverses the behavior typically observed in-plane conduction of stacked 2D nanomaterials. The resulting films are photoconductive under 405 nm illumination with an external quantum efficiency of 0.62%. The mechanical and chemical stability of such conductive 2D polyaramids enables the first single-component, acid-stable polymer electrodes based on non-conjugated frameworks, capable of operating in harsh environments while exhibiting perfectly invariant cyclic capacitance for over 10,000 cycles at pH 2. The stability is enabled in part by the impermeability of such films to moisture and oxygen, underscored by their ability to suppress perovskite degradation with a 150 nm coating. Together, these findings underscore a newly realized mode of electrical conduction in close-packed 2D polymers, enabling ultra-lightweight and chemically stable electrodes for energy storage and sustainability applications.

paper.title: A Water Bridge Rewires CO2 Binding to Maleic Anhydride
paper.abstract: Abstract The earliest stages of atmospheric particle formation involve the cooperative assembly of oxygenated organic molecules with abundant atmospheric species, yet how intermolecular binding preferences depend on the presence of an additional molecular component remains poorly understood. Here, high-resolution Fourier transform microwave spectroscopy, combined with quantum-chemical calculations, is used to determine the gas-phase structure of the maleic anhydride–CO2–H2O cluster. The observed cluster adopts a nearly coplanar geometry in which H2O bridges maleic anhydride and CO2 through an O–H···O hydrogen bond and a C···O tetrel bond. Compared with the binary complexes, the ternary complex exhibits a different CO2-centered interaction motif: CO2 interacts with the oxygen atom of H2O rather than with a carbonyl oxygen of maleic anhydride. Orbital-interaction analysis further reveals a corresponding difference in the dominant donor–acceptor interaction channel, while energy decomposition identifies electrostatics as the largest attractive contribution in the ternary complex. These findings show that binding preferences established in isolated binary complexes are not necessarily retained in a chemically heterogeneous three-component environment.

paper.title: Rationalizing charge transfer: a single-molecule case study across three distinct surfaces
paper.abstract: Organic molecules are versatile building blocks for the formation of complex low-dimensional nanostructures on surfaces. Recently, interest has grown in translating on-surface synthetic protocols from noble metal surfaces to insulating surfaces, which offer technological relevance, and to magnetic or superconducting surfaces, which offer new routes to correlated phases. It is important, therefore, to understand how these alternative surfaces may alter the properties of adsorbates through processes like charge transfer and screening. Evidence for charge transfer is often obtained experimentally via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS), and theoretically via density functional theory (DFT). In this work, we systematically compare the properties of isolated macrocyclic emeraldine (Me$_6$) molecules on three different surfaces: metallic Au(111), a semiconducting ferromagnetic monolayer of FeCl$_2$, and a cleaved superconducting surface of bulk 2H-NbSe$_2$. We show that STS and DFT alone are insufficient to quantify charge transfer for these cases. Instead, we complement these methods with Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measurements and model Hamiltonian calculations to demonstrate that on Au(111) and FeCl$_2$, Me$_6$ molecules donate a single electron to the substrate, whereas on NbSe$_2$ two electrons are transferred from molecule to substrate. Our work provides insight into the interplay of charge transfer, screening, and molecule-substrate coupling, and develops experimental and theoretical methods for comparing the properties of adsorbates across different surfaces for future studies.

paper.title: Origin of electride states and their responses under pressure
Controlled Fabrication of Uniform Columnar Porous GaN Architectures by Electrochemical Etching
paper.abstract: Electrochemical etching (ECE) of n-type c-plane GaN enables the formation of porous architectures capable of enhancing the performance of optoelectronic devices and broadening the range of possible GaN applications. Here, we demonstrate that the addition of NaOH to Na2C2O4 (and other non-acidic etchant solutions) directs ECE toward the formation of nanoscale, vertically aligned, highly uniform columnar pore morphologies with relatively limited surface roughening. By varying the NaOH concentration within mixed electrolyte systems, the columnar pore shape, diameter, spacing, and bulk and surface porosity can be readily tuned. In addition to manually mixing NaOH with another etchant, aqueous basic electrolytes such as Na2CO3 and Na3PO4, each inherently containing significant hydroxide concentration through hydrolysis, also produce similar columnar pore morphologies, indicating that hydroxide plays the key role in directing the vertical pore growth. Chronoamperometry and pore structure analysis reveals that the mixed hydroxide-containing electrolyte systems exhibit a distinct, new ECE mechanism rather than a simple superposition of the individual ECE behaviour of each anion present. This work provides significant insight into the ECE mechanism for porous GaN, which is proposed to contain multiple reaction steps where hydroxide anions are involved in the formation of a reactive intermediate. These findings establish a versatile and controllable route for engineering columnar porous GaN architectures, offering significant advancement in applications requiring high porosity, ordered, and bespoke structures.

paper.title: Geometries are forgiving, basins are not: a practical guide to optimizing chemical structures
paper.abstract: A calculated molecular or materials structure is the input to almost every later number in a computational study, yet the step that produces it is usually reported in one line. Two kinds of failure are distinguished here, and the heuristic that follows is offered with its range of validity. Within a basin of the potential energy surface, and for the stiff modes and well-behaved closed-shell systems covered by the benchmarks reviewed, geometries are forgiving in energy: for well-chosen methods, bond lengths converge to a few tenths of a picometer and rotational constants to a few megahertz, and the coordinate system and Hessian guess mainly change the cost of the optimization; they can also change convergence behavior and, in difficult cases, the stationary point reached. Between basins, the answer can change qualitatively, because a wrong conformer, cluster isomer or polymorph can shift energies and properties by more than a change of functional or basis set in the examples examined. The heuristic fails for properties that depend on the geometry to first order, for very soft modes and weak interactions, and for systems in which the level of theory changes the topology of the surface. Published benchmark data on coordinates and optimizers, local and global search, wave-function and density-functional levels, basis sets and composite methods are replotted in a common graphical style; this does not make them statistically commensurable, and directly comparable results are distinguished from illustrative comparisons across studies. The review covers molecular optimization, conformer and cluster search, transition-structure location and machine-learned potentials, with periodic relaxation treated briefly. Worked examples show where a wrong basin or an unbalanced level changed a conclusion. Universal machine-learned potentials are assessed as pre-optimizers, a reporting standard is proposed, and a decision scheme by system class is given. Where the literature contains no benchmark, this is stated explicitly.

paper.title: Kinetic Limitations of Single-Atom Catalysts in Hydrazine Oxidation
paper.abstract: Abstract Single-atom catalysts (SACs) have attracted considerable interest, displaying impressive performance for a wide plethora of electrocatalytic reactions. However, the important question whether isolated sites are always beneficial remains unresolved. Here, by using the hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR) as a model reaction, we examine how isolated single-atom metal sites restrict the adsorption mode of intermediates to the monodentate configuration, which leads to weak intermediate stabilization and poor reaction kinetics. This contrasts with bulk metal sites where availability of the bidentate adsorption configuration offers better intermediate stabilization and dehydrogenation kinetics. As a result, Ir, Pt, and Pd SACs were found to require high HzOR overpotentials of 0.90, 1.21, and 1.19 V at 3 mA cm–2, respectively. Comparatively, their Ir, Pt, Pd nanoparticle counterparts with similar metal loading exhibit considerably lower overpotentials of only 0.35, 0.83, and 0.64 V at 3 mA cm–2, respectively. Taken together, our work contributes towards a more complete understanding of SACs, emphasizing the importance of considering site structure and the mechanistic demands of the reaction.

paper.title: Site-Selective Fluorination for Decoupling Oxidative Stability and Ionic Transport of Oxychloride Solid Electrolytes
paper.abstract: Fluorination in solid electrolytes is widely used to enhance oxidative stability owing to fluorine's high electronegativity, yet strong Li–F interactions hinder Li-ion transport. Here we show that this anodic stability–ionic conductivity trade-off can be largely decoupled through lattice-level anion design in the highly Li-ion-conductive LiTaOCl4. By distinguishing oxygen's framework-linking role from chloride's transport-defining role, we targeted fluorination at framework-linking O-sites to minimize perturbation of the Li-ion conduction network. The fluorinated oxychlorides retain ~10 mS cm–1-class ionic conductivity while raising the oxidation onset from 4.08 to 4.27 V versus Li+/Li, improving capacity retention as catholytes cycled to 4.5 V. First-principles calculations reveal that fluorination stabilizes oxidation-prone O- and Cl-derived electronic states through an inductive effect, while transport-network topology and correlated lattice dynamics preserve fast Li-ion transport. These results establish site-selective anion occupation as a design principle for decoupling oxidative stabilization from fast ion transport in mixed-anion solid electrolytes.

paper.title: Hunting the Enhanced Interaction of Donors with Post-Transition and Transition Metal Dichalcogenides: Comparative Study of NO 2 , H 2 S, NH 3 , and Aniline Adsorption on MoS 2 , SnS 2 , and ZrS 2 Monolayers
paper.abstract: Two-dimensional transition and post-transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs and PTMDs) are promising materials for applications in roomtemperature, physisorption-based gas sensing and monitoring. In recent years, the mechanisms behind the adsorption of electron-accepting molecules have been well established, leading to the development of composition-engineering pathways that may be used to enhance the chemiresistive signal, as well as to design and fine-tune selective devices. However, similar trends have yet to be found for the electron-donating species. Consequently, the present study employs density functional theory (DFT) methods to systematically compare the adsorption of three electron donors, hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S), ammonia (NH 3 ), and aniline (C 6 H 5 NH 2 ), and one baseline acceptor, nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ), on semiconducting 1H-MoS 2 , 1T-SnS 2 , and 1T-ZrS 2 monolayers. The set was selected to provide direct comparison of different substrate symmetries, d-block versus p-block metal centers, and example acceptor-versus donor-molecule behavior under identical theoretical description. It was found that donor analytes can experience substrate-dependent enhancement in charge transfer only when their HOMO lies sufficiently high in energy. Accordingly, at the vdw-DF-cx level of theory, only aniline shows pronounced differences in adsorption, donating on average −0.049, −0.119, and −0.143 e to MoS 2 , SnS 2 , and ZrS 2 , respectively, whereas NH 3 and H 2 S exhibit no comparable trend. This particular substrate order was correlated with the favorable positions of the conduction band edges as well as the spatial availability of the low-lying acceptor states. These results provide a theoretical basis for the mechanisms governing adsorption of donating species on pristine TMDs and PTDMs, and may aid in selecting a suitable material for physisorption-based devices.

paper.title: Nonlocal electrostatic field theory from microscopic description
paper.abstract: The study of electric fields in soft materials converges either to the study of point-like particles (local) in nonlinear theories or to the use of particles with finite sizes in nonlocal linear theories. In this work, we start from the microscopic equations of motion and construct a unified mean-field Fokker–Planck equation that describes the non-equilibrium electrostatics of nonlocal nonlinear systems. We obtain a generalized Poisson–Boltzmann equation for such systems, as well as their electrostatic free energy expression. In the linear approximation, we obtain an anisotropic susceptibility in an isotropic fluid, which allows for local linear response inversion in electrostatics.
