paper.title: P3MaZe: a Mass-Zero Constrained-Dynamics Formulation of Particle–Mesh Electrostatics
paper.abstract: Abstract We introduce P3MaZe, a real-space particle–mesh electrostatic method that combines the standard short-range/long-range decomposition of Particle–Particle Particle–Mesh (P3M) electrostatics with the Mass-Zero constrained dynamics (MaZe) framework. In this formulation, the smooth long-range electrostatic potential is represented on a mesh as a zero-inertia auxiliary field, while the discretized Poisson equation is enforced as a holonomic constraint during molecular dynamics. By retaining the standard P3M decomposition, P3MaZe preserves the systematic accuracy controls associated with the real-space cutoff, the Ewald splitting, the mesh spacing, and the charge assignment procedure, while replacing the conventional multigrid Poisson solver by a constrained correction problem. The method is validated for molten NaCl and simple point-charge flexible water (SPC/Fw). Values of the potential, structural, translational, collective, and rotational dynamical observables are in quantitative agreement with those obtained with established electrostatic methods, including real-space P3M, and Ewald summation. We further show that, for the linear, time-independent Poisson operator considered here, the constrained correction problem is algebraically equivalent to a direct Poisson solve initialized by a chronological extrapolation of the mesh potential, a connection not previously established for MaZe-based approaches. This result identifies the precise mechanism through which acceleration of the iterative long-range solve is achieved, and we exploit it systematically through higher-order predictors to further improve convergence, while retaining the expected linear scaling with system size. Because the underlying extrapolation is independent of the constrained-dynamics formalism, it can, of course, also be used directly to accelerate conventional iterative real-space Poisson solvers.

paper.title: How high-pressure ices on large ocean worlds can support habitability: The compatibility of amino acids into ice VI and VII
paper.abstract: Water oceans in large icy moons and exoplanets are isolated from the rocky interior by thick layers of high-pressure ice, which hinder the direct release of nutrients and organics derived from water-rock interaction to the ocean. Possible uptake of these bio-essential compounds into high-pressure ice phases could regulate their availability in the ocean, but this process is poorly constrained. Here, we measured partition coefficients of glycine and alanine into ices VI and VII under elevated temperature-pressure conditions using a diamond-anvil cell. We observed moderate compatibility of glycine and alanine with partition coefficients: K p ,glycine = 0.14 and 0.40 in ices VI and VII, respectively; K p ,alanine = 0.21 and 0.35 in ices VI and VII, respectively. First-principles calculations suggested that amino acids could be incorporated into high-pressure ice’s lattice via cogrowth. Compatibility of amino acids into high-pressure ices would favor their transport in large extraterrestrial oceans, opening an avenue to habitability.

paper.title: Observations show increased nitrate in coastal cloud droplet residuals from large-particle activation and N 2 O 5 hydrolysis
paper.abstract: Clouds change the chemical composition of aerosols, yet observations characterizing these processes are quite limited. Ground-based in-cloud measurements in coastal Southern California show that the highest nitrate to sulfate ratio (2.5 ± 1.7) in droplet residuals is near cloud base where cloud liquid water content and droplet number concentration are below the observed 20th percentile. The number size distribution of nitrate-rich particles peaks at a larger diameter than sulfate-rich particles, supporting growth to droplets of nitrate-rich particles at lower supersaturations than for sulfate-rich particles. Nitrate mass concentrations are up to three times higher in-cloud compared to pre-cloud and correlated with statistically significant reductions in ozone concentrations, consistent with contributions from in-cloud nitrate formation by N 2 O 5 hydrolysis. This study provides quantitative relationships of cloud properties to nitrate production in droplet residuals and associated ozone reduction, illustrating the impacts of aqueous reactions in clouds.

paper.title: Amorphous Halide Cathodes Enable 75C All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
paper.abstract: Abstract Power delivery in all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) is often pursued by maximizing the bulk ionic conductivity of cathode active materials (CAMs), while grain-boundary (GB) ion-transport barriers caused by lattice mismatch remain a major kinetic bottleneck. Here, we reveal that minimizing GB transport barriers, rather than simply enhancing intrinsic conductivity, unlocks ultrafast ion-transport in halide CAMs. Amorphization converts crystalline LiVCl4 into a conformal amorphous phase that preserves short-range V–Cl coordination while minimizing long-range ion-transport tortuosity. Despite lower bulk Li+ conductivity, amorphous LiVCl4 dramatically reduces GB-associated interfacial resistance and enables a catholyte-free cathode (CAM content: 90 wt %) to deliver a capacity of 74.3 mAh g–1 at 5 mA cm–2, compared with 10.2 mAh g–1 for the crystalline counterpart. Meanwhile, the ASSLB further operates across a wide temperature range from −30 to 60 °C and achieves 84.2% capacity utilization at an ultrahigh A-LiVCl4 areal loading of 53.4 mg cm–2. Coupled with amorphous LiTaOCl4, the ASSLB achieves 102.1 mAh g–1 at 20 mA cm–2 (∼75C) and retains 82.3% capacity after 16,000 cycles. These results establish amorphization-enabled conformal interfaces as a new paradigm for ultrahigh-power ASSLBs.

paper.title: Thermal sculpting of nanoconfined single-atom cavities enables urea electrosynthesis with near-unity selectivity
paper.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from CO 2 and NO 3 – offers a sustainable alternative to energy-intensive industrial methods, yet precise C–N coupling remains hindered by kinetic mismatches between the reduction reactions. Here, we report a strategy leveraging programmable Zn-node gasification to thermally sculpt 1.5–1.8 nm cavities within zeolitic imidazolate frameworks, hosting atomically dispersed Cu–N 4 sites. Thermal transformation creates size-matched nanoconfined environments for selective catalysis. An optimal confinement metric descriptor (9.64) is introduced as a predictive parameter, correlating cavity geometry with local electric-field and Cu d-band modulation. This design stabilizes *CO and *NO intermediates, effectively suppressing parasitic reactions and lowering C–N coupling barriers. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a urea yield of 71.32 g g cat –1 h –1 with 98.9% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in gas diffusion cells. Pilot-scale testing demonstrates stable operation over 300 h with an FE of 90%, establishing nanoconfinement as a design principle for competitive-performance urea electrosynthesis.

paper.title: Conformational flexibility of the nitrogenase-like reductase CfbC/D involved in coenzyme F 430 biosynthesis
paper.abstract: The nitrogenase-like reductase CfbC/D catalyzes the six-electron reduction of the tetrapyrrole macrocycle of Ni 2+ -sirohydrochlorin a,c -diamide during the biosynthesis of coenzyme F 430 , an essential cofactor for biological methane formation and consumption. The individual dimeric protein components, CfbC 2 and CfbD 2 , form a complex to allow for electron transfer from the [4Fe:4S] cluster in CfbC 2 to the [4Fe:4S] cluster in CfbD 2 and onto the substrate. The overall process is ATP-dependent. Although CfbC/D belongs to the family of nitrogenase-like enzymes, there are several intriguing differences between CfbC/D, other nitrogenase-like enzymes and nitrogenase itself. In contrast to the other enzymes, CfbC/D exhibits a simpler molecular architecture, forming a heterotetrameric CfbC 2 D 2 assembly. Furthermore, the interaction of the CfbC and CfbD components does not depend on the presence of adenosine triphosphate (ATP). Here we report cryoelectron microscopy structures of the CfbC/D complex prepared in the absence and presence of substrates. These structures not only shed light on the molecular architecture of the CfbC/D complex but also reveal a high degree of structural flexibility within the CfbD 2 component, which undergoes a large conformational change in the presence of an ATP analog and the tetrapyrrole substrate. The interplay of CfbD with its reductase CfbC also strongly suggests an evolutionary pathway toward the modern nitrogenase from methanogenic archaea.

Enhanced Membrane Preference in APEX2 Proximity Labeling via an iEDDA Strategy With Built‐In Background Correction
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Proximity‐labeling techniques, such as engineered ascorbate peroxidase (APEX2), have revolutionized the mapping of spatially organized proteomes. However, achieving high spatial resolution and specificity remains challenging due to the diffusible nature of labeling intermediates and the difficulty in establishing robust negative controls. Here, we present a chemical strategy that addresses both challenges by engineering the labeling reporter itself. We developed a lipophilic APEX2 reporter, phenol‐ trans ‐cyclooctene (phenol‐TCO), designed to partition into membrane microenvironments. This reporter leverages inverse electron‐demand Diels–Alder (iEDDA) chemistry for subsequent detection. Crucially, we repurpose the inherent, non‐specific reactivity of the tetrazine–biotin conjugate to establish a powerful and practical built‐in negative control. When applied to profile the Lamin A‐associated proteome, the phenol‐TCO reporter enriches nuclear envelope and endoplasmic reticulum membrane proteins with high confidence, yielding a focused dataset. In sharp contrast, conventional phenol‐biotin labeled a diffuse set of proteins lacking lamina specificity. We demonstrate that the tetrazine‐biotin‐treated lysate control effectively removes non‐specific background while preserving genuine proximal interactors, supporting it as a practical alternative to traditional controls. This work utilizes reporter localization preference to enhance the spatial precision of proximity labeling and provides a generalizable control strategy, opening new avenues for dissecting protein networks with membrane emphasis.

paper.title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
paper.abstract: Abstract Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation.

paper.title: Mechanistic Insights of Electroreductive Cobalt-Catalyzed Asymmetric Radical Addition
paper.abstract: Abstract Transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric electroreduction has emerged as a compelling platform for enantioselective C–C bond formation, with notable advances in electroreductive cross-coupling. Translating this success to stereocontrolled radical additions across unsaturated bonds remains a formidable challenge, particularly for the construction of fully substituted stereogenic carbon centers. Herein, we report an electroreductive, cobalt-catalyzed asymmetric radical addition of diverse organohalides to α-imino esters. This protocol delivers enantioenriched α-quaternary amino acid derivatives in up to 95% ee, completely circumventing the need for stoichiometric metal reductants. Beyond its synthetic utility, the electrochemical platform uniquely enables the direct interrogation of the operative electron-transfer events. A comprehensive mechanistic study─encompassing cyclic voltammetry, in situ electrochemical EPR spectroscopy, DFT calculations, stoichiometric experiments, and radical-trapping experiments─elucidates a highly orchestrated catalytic manifold. Crucially, we demonstrate that the α-imino ester serves a dual role, acting as both a radical acceptor and a redox-active ligand for the chiral cobalt catalyst. Subsequent cathodic reduction of the resulting cobalt–imine complex generates a key low-valent species that engages the alkyl halide via a turnover-limiting single-electron transfer (SET) to produce the requisite alkyl radical. Overall, this work establishes a robust electrochemical framework that synergizes reaction innovation with fundamental mechanistic elucidation in asymmetric radical catalysis.

paper.title: Quenched fluctuation-induced force arising from polarization disorder
paper.abstract: We investigate the zero-temperature behavior of the fluctuation force induced by the quenched disorder of electric dipoles frozen randomly into a material. Examples of such materials include relaxor ferroelectrics. In terms of the setup and geometry, we focus on a layered system comprising two coplanar semi-infinite slabs separated by a distance ℓ, as well as a system comprising a neutral atom in the vacuum located at a distance ℓ above the surface of a semi-infinite slab. For both systems, we consider the cases where the quenched random dipolar disorder occurs inside the bulk as well as on the surface of the slabs. In all of these cases, we find that the bulk (surface) dipolar disorder-induced force grows with the mean square quenched electric dipole moment per unit volume (area). The bulk (surface) dipolar disorder-induced pressure between two semi-infinite single-layered slabs decays with ℓ−3 (ℓ−4), whereas the bulk (surface) dipolar disorder-induced force on an atom in the vacuum near a slab containing the disorder decays with ℓ−4 (ℓ−5). We also find that the quenched dipolar disorder-induced force between two coplanar slabs can be repulsive in a three-layered dielectric system that obeys a zero-frequency analog of the Dzyaloshinskii–Lifshitz–Pitaevskii condition and serves to enhance the “nanolevitation effect” if the latter is present in the disorder-free system.

paper.title: Ultra-broadband and time-resolved depolarized dynamic light scattering for probing molecular dynamics in supercooled liquids and glasses
paper.abstract: Dynamic light scattering (DLS) is a versatile technique for probing microscopic dynamics in soft condensed matter. However, applying DLS to supercooled molecular liquids and glasses demands exceptional experimental performance due to weak depolarized scattering, slow relaxation near the glass transition, and the need for quantitative comparison with complementary spectroscopic techniques. In this tutorial, we discuss how a depolarized dynamic light scattering (DDLS) setup can be tailored to meet these challenges. By combining conventional fiber-optical photon correlation spectroscopy and multispeckle photon correlation imaging with high-frequency DDLS, such a setup allows us to capture rotational dynamics across more than 20 orders of magnitude in time. We detail the experimental design required for high signal-to-noise ratios and long-term optical stability, alongside the treatment of coherence and partial heterodyning effects. As we demonstrate, after proper treatment, the different detection schemes yield the same electric-field autocorrelation function, enabling the construction of continuous, ultra-broadband DDLS datasets. Furthermore, multispeckle detection enables time-resolved correlation measurements without temporal averaging, extending DDLS to non-equilibrium systems such as aging molecular glasses. This methodology establishes a unified experimental framework for quantitative investigations of equilibrium and non-equilibrium molecular reorientation dynamics over an exceptionally broad time range.

paper.title: A Pseudo-Icosahedral RhH2Au10 Superatom: Two Hydrogen Atoms Acting as Gold-Atom Equivalents and Modifiers
paper.abstract: Abstract A hydrogen atom is known to act as a gold-atom-equivalent dopant in gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) by contributing to the valence electron count. To gain insights into the interaction of multiple H atoms with AuNCs, we herein synthesized a di-H-atom-doped NC, [RhH2Au10(dppp)5]3+ (RhH2Au10; dppp = 1,3-bis(diphenylphosphino)propane), by exposing [RhAu10(dppp)5]3+ (RhAu10) to H2 gas; RhAu10 was generated in situ via hydride (H–) abstraction from [RhHAu10(dppp)5]2+. Comprehensive characterization of RhH2Au10 by X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations revealed that the two H atoms occupy the two “missing” Au sites in the arachno-type RhAu10 core via dissociative adsorption of H2, forming a pseudo-icosahedral RhH2Au10 core. This core structure contrasts sharply with the previously reported di-H-atom-doped silver- or copper-based superatoms, in which the H atoms form an MH2 (M = Os, Ru, Rh) unit completely encapsulated within an icosahedral Ag12 or Cu12 shell. The RhH2Au10 core possesses an 8-electron closed-shell electronic configuration of (1S)2(1P)6, which is isoelectronic to the icosahedral RhAu12 superatom, thereby demonstrating the Au-atom equivalence of H atoms. Nevertheless, the two H atoms in the RhH2Au10 superatomic core act as structural modifiers compared to the RhAu12 superatom: (1) the degeneracy of the 1P orbitals is lifted by lowering the geometric symmetry, and (2) the HOMO–LUMO energy gap is expanded due to the reduced electronic confinement volume. This study demonstrates that multiple H atoms in a gold-based superatomic core not only behave as Au-atom equivalents but also serve as key components for modulating their fundamental properties.

paper.title: Non‐Monotonical Ion Association Equilibria in Low‐Temperature Sodium–Metal Battery Electrolytes
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Intermolecular distance is a critical parameter governing electrostatics and solvation in aprotic electrolytes. Governed by the power–law relationship between interaction energy and distance, the attenuation of molecular Brownian motion at low temperatures leads to a sharp reduction in intermolecular distance, which in turn amplifies dipole–dipole interactions and impacts the transport kinetics of sodium (Na) ions in both bulk and interface domains. How the low‐temperature regime influences the association and dissociation of Na solvation equilibrium is rather elusive. In this study, an electrophilicity/nucleophilicity‐based descriptor is proposed to quantify solvent self‐association, which is primarily driven by dipole–dipole interactions. Based on this framework, the solvent pairs are generated during non‐monotonical temperature‐dependent Na + solvation evolution, which contributes to excessive ion aggregation to tame redox kinetics at low temperature. In line with this consideration, a facile strategy using a dilute electrolyte was developed to establish a favorable solvation equilibrium between dissociated and associated species. This work refreshes the understanding of thermodynamic equilibrium between ion–dipole and dipole–dipole interactions, and challenges the conventional approach of learning from the lithium batteries that encourage weakly solvating electrolyte, arguing the critical importance of strengthening cation solvation chemistry in Na battery field due to the temperature‐dependent dipole–dipole interactions.

paper.title: 2D pores offer an optimal balance of charge storage and charging kinetics
paper.abstract: Electrolyte-filled conducting nanopores are central to applications ranging from energy storage to neuromorphic computing, yet the influence of pore geometry and structure on ion confinement remains insufficiently understood. Here, we combine theoretical calculations and molecular simulations to investigate how nanopore charging depends on pore dimensionality and morphology, considering nanostructured electrodes comprising cylindrical (1D) and slit-shaped (2D) pores, as well as 3D disordered porous electrodes exemplified by a carbide-derived carbon (CDC) structure. We show that in 1D confinement, the equilibrium stored charge exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on pore size, whereas 2D pores generally provide higher charge and energy densities per unit surface area. Somewhat counterintuitively, charging dynamics in 2D pores can slow down with increasing pore size but remain substantially faster than in disordered 3D electrodes. Although counterion saturation at high cell voltages reduces the energy stored by subnanometer 2D pores relative to CDC electrodes, this limitation can be overcome by matching the pore width to the operating voltage. Overall, our results indicate that 2D pores offer an optimal balance between charge storage and charging kinetics, highlighting their potential for high-performance capacitive energy storage.

paper.title: Lithium-Ion Battery Electrolyte Structural Transport: Anion Dependent Exchange Mechanisms
paper.abstract: Li + moves through an electrolyte both by diffusing with its intact solvation shell (vehicular transport) and by exchanging its solvent partners (structural transport). Structural diffusion depends on the frequency of solvent dissociation from Li + and how far the ion moves when it does, yet neither is well characterized experimentally. Li + transport in propylene carbonate solutions of LiTFSI, LiBF 4 , and LiPF 6 , from battery-relevant to superconcentrated levels, was studied via a vibrational probe molecule, phenyl selenocyanate, with ultrafast two-dimensional infrared chemical exchange spectroscopy. Li + diffusion coefficients significantly exceed the Stokes-Einstein prediction. Combining this excess diffusion with solvent dissociation times yields the the step length Li + moves per exchange event. Dissociation times correlate with the reorientation time of unbound probe molecules, indicating that productive exchange requires reorganization of the surrounding solvent. For all salts, the step length decreases with concentration. In relatively dilute LiTFSI it is ~1.3 Å, matching the distance predicted from an associative mechanism through a five-coordinate intermediate, whereas in LiPF 6 it is 0.7–0.8 Å at every concentration, consistent with a predominantly dissociative mechanism through a three-coordinate intermediate. Because PF 6- forms the fewest contact ion pairs, it leaves the least free solvent available to act as an entering group, suppressing the associative pathway. Combined with the longest dissociation times, these short steps make LiPF 6 electrolytes generally the most reliant on vehicular transport despite their high viscosity. Thus, the anion influences not only how often Li + exchanges solvent but also the mechanism, and therefore how far Li + moves with each step.

paper.title: Extended Active Learning-Guided Design of Multi-Component Electrolytes with Opposing Cosolvent Properties for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
paper.abstract: Abstract Multi-component electrolytes offer expanded tunability over electrochemical properties, yet their rational design is constrained by a lack of generalizable principles. Intricate intercomponent interactions obscure the relationship between the molecular properties and battery performance, rendering material selection and compositional optimization intractable. Here, we present an extended active learning-guided framework to efficiently navigate the vast materials space and refine formulations for tri-solvent-based electrolytes in aqueous zinc-ion batteries with minimal experimental workload. Specifically, co-solvent candidates are clustered by molecular properties; co-solvents are then selected, and their pairwise combinations undergo rigorous formulation optimization. Our data-driven approach discovered a nonintuitive electrolyte composition: combining co-solvents with fundamentally opposing properties. This unique formulation, which disrupts the hydrogen-bonded network while reconstructing the solvation structure, enables Zn||NH4V4O10 full-cells to retain 90.2% capacity after 1,000 cycles. This study unveils the possibility of using active learning to discover unconventional electrolyte formulations that would otherwise be infeasible to identify through human insights.

paper.title: Photoinduced charging and spatially selective photochemistry on ferroelectric surfaces
paper.abstract: Ferroelectric surfaces exhibit polarization-dependent photoreactivity and provide a route to program chemical patterns through local electrical control of polarization. Observations accumulated over several decades show reaction products in domain interiors, at domain boundaries, and in other selected regions, indicating that the mechanisms extend beyond a single polarization-induced band-bending picture. Here we analyze light-induced charging and interfacial reactions on uniformly polarized ferroelectrics and domain patterns, for dry surfaces and surfaces in contact with an electrochemically active solution. A common semiconductor transport and charge-conservation framework distinguishes five cases: an isolated dry ferroelectric, a dry ferroelectric connected to a carrier reservoir, a blocking ferroelectric-electrolyte junction, a reactive interface with an external carrier return, and two opposite domains coupled through the solid and electrolyte. Analytical solutions and numerical evaluations connect stationary potentials versus illumination to differential optical spectra and finite light-step responses. We further examine the doping effects on static potentials in all five cases and dynamic photovoltage in the isolated film and a fixed-polarization, bare-surface contacted-film variant. For reactive interfaces, the same framework determines reduction and oxidation rates, their spatial distributions, and accumulated reaction amount. The analysis covers surface charging and photochemical conversion beyond deposition, while retaining the electrical and chemical boundaries that distinguish finite charging from sustained turnover, and explains the observed range of photodeposition morphologies. Finally, this framework builds the theoretical foundation for the modulated photovoltage imaging methods that can readily be realized in SPM under illumination.

paper.title: Decoupling OH and H Binding via Dual‐Site Conductive MOFs for Efficient Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient regulation of the hydrogen and hydroxyl binding energies (HBE/OHBE) lies at the core of developing high‐performance alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts, yet it remains challenging due to the inherent correlation between the two binding energies. Herein, we demonstrate a d ‐electron modulation strategy on dual‐metal sites to break the scaling constraint and synergistically optimize HBE and OHBE. A well‐defined Cu‐based two‐dimensional conductive metal–organic framework (Cu‐HHTP) serves as a universal host to incorporate various 3 d transition metals (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu), yielding M–Cu dual sites with finely tunable d ‐electron configurations. Density functional theory calculations combined with experiments reveal that higher d ‐electron occupancy of the secondary metal site lowers the d ‐band center, and the water dissociation energy barrier exhibits a typical volcano‐type trend. The Co–Cu dual sites at the volcano apex promote the Volmer step through optimized OHBE and water adsorption. Meanwhile, this dual‐site configuration promotes the rearrangement of interfacial water molecules by disrupting the hydrogen‐bond network, thereby optimizing HBE. This work decouples HBE and OHBE via d ‐electron configuration, shifting the design paradigm from empirical screening to predictive design.

paper.title: Exploration via Organic Descriptors in Atomic Layer Processing (EXODIA)
paper.abstract: Organic small molecules play a vital role in many atomic layer processes such as area selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD), molecular layer deposition (MLD), oxidative MLD (oMLD), and chemical vapor deposition. In these applications, knowledge of physical chemical properties such as vapor pressure (VP), oxidation potential (OP), p K a , melting point (MP), and boiling point (BP), aids in the efficient selection of molecular candidates to be tested. Here, we employ Chemprop, an established message passing graph neural network framework, to develop machine learning (ML) models that predict each of these five physical chemical properties for organic small molecules. Using these ML models, we generated a combined dataset of >43K organic small molecules that includes experimental values where available, and ML predicted values where necessary. The trained ML models achieve a mean absolute error on withheld test sets of 0.2 log10(Psat[torr]) over a range of 10 -4 to 10 3 torr for VP, 0.21V over a range of -1.1V to 2.6V vs. SHE for OP, 0.9 log units over a range of -2.8 to 16.13 for p K a , 22K over a range of 68K - 790.15K for MP, and 12K over a range of 169K - 721K for BP. These models were integrated into two distinct website tools that (1) allow for simple structure to property predictions and (2) allow for the down-selection among the combined dataset of 43K+ molecules based on these five properties. We outline use cases for each tool within the context of small molecule inhibitor selection and oMLD precursor discovery, with a potentially much larger reach within the vapor deposition community.

paper.title: Interfacial bacteria-driven rotation of free-floating active droplets
paper.abstract: Active droplets provide a platform for converting microscopic propulsion into macroscopic flow. Previous realizations of bacteria-driven droplet rotation typically rely on nearby solid boundaries, external fields, or dense active nematics. Here, we report autonomous rotation of droplets in a three-dimensional aqueous two-phase system driven by interfacial population of \textit{Pseudomonas aeruginosa}. Combining confocal microscopy with fluid particle dynamics simulations, we show that amphiphilic bacteria accumulate at the dextran--polyethylene glycol interface and preferentially move and orient along the local tangent. Interfacial localization partitions the force-free swimming dipole between the two liquid phases, allowing either phase to experience a finite active torque while the combined system remains torque balanced. The simulated interfacial population is more spatially heterogeneous than in the experiments, emphasizing that both the bacterial distribution and its signed orientational organization can influence the instantaneous torque. Over the accessible size range, the macroscopic angular velocity exhibits an inverse-radius ($R^{-1}$) dependence. We also formulate a theoretical model to rationalize this scaling law, revealing how the macroscopic rotation is governed by collective interfacial swimming and surface coverage. These results identify a fluid-interface-mediated route for converting swimmer activity into macroscopic rotational flow and establish a strategy for harnessing interfacial active matter to regulate droplet dynamics.

paper.title: Breaking the Halide Concentration Reliance of Four‐Electron Zinc‐Iodine Batteries via Interfacial Halide Enrichment
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT High‐valence iodine redox chemistry in aqueous batteries is fundamentally constrained by the requirement of highly concentrated halide environments, which stabilize reactive iodine cations but inevitably induce electrolyte corrosion and sluggish interfacial kinetics. In this study, we demonstrate an interfacial halide enrichment strategy that circumvents this long‐standing concentration dependence in four‐electron zinc‐iodine batteries. By introducing only 0.1 M bromo‐pyrrolidinium salt into the electrolyte, a localized halide‐rich microenvironment is spontaneously reconstructed at the cathode interface, enabling reversible I – /I 2 /I + conversion without relying on bulk hyper‐concentrated halides. Spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that the pyrrolidinium cations preferentially anchor at the charged interface through complementary electrostatic and soft interactions with iodine/polyhalide species, thereby promoting interfacial Br – enrichment and stabilizing metastable IBr 2 – intermediates. Meanwhile, ethylene glycol (EG)‐mediated solvation regulation and interfacial water exclusion further suppress iodine hydrolysis and parasitic reactions. As a result, the dilute‐halide electrolyte system achieves a reversible capacity of 413.3 mAh g −1 at 0.4 A g −1 and maintains 88.2% capacity retention after 5000 cycles at 2 A g −1 , while simultaneously improving zinc anode reversibility. This work establishes an interfacial halide enrichment paradigm for regulating high‐valence halogen chemistry beyond conventional electrolyte concentration limitations.

paper.title: An actively trained neural operator for near-explicit atmospheric chemistry
paper.abstract: Earth-system models simplify atmospheric chemistry into condensed mechanisms, because near-explicit mechanisms such as the Master Chemical Mechanism (MCM) are too costly to solve in every grid cell. Neural emulators could lift this limit, but most advance the chemistry in small time steps and cover only a few species or a reduced mechanism. Here we introduce FNO-MoE, a Fourier neural operator with a mixture of experts that predicts the full near-explicit chemical state over 30 minutes in a single call. The same network also guides its own training, using the disagreement among its experts to select the most informative box-model simulations. At equal cost, this active sampling yields a more accurate emulator than random or evenly spread sampling. Fine-tuning on longer trajectories keeps it stable over multi-hour runs in which models trained on short simulations diverge. The resulting emulator reproduces the evolution of thousands of species with high fidelity, remains accurate for unseen chemical compositions and runs orders of magnitude faster than the numerical solver. These results open a new direction for emulating complex atmospheric systems: neural operators that predict the full chemical state over long windows and choose their own training data. Training under changing meteorology is the next step towards bringing near-explicit chemistry into Earth-system models.
paper.tldr: 该研究提出的FNO-MoE神经网络可在单次调用中预测30分钟完整的近显式大气化学状态，并以专家分歧指导训练，在相同计算成本下显著提升模拟效率。

paper.title: A thermodynamic correction layer for machine learning interatomic potentials
paper.abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials enable atomistic simulations with near \textit{ab initio} accuracy over large length and time scales. Foundation models extend this capability across the periodic table but inherit the thermodynamic description of the electronic structure methods used to generate their training data. Small errors in relative phase stability can therefore produce large errors in transformation temperatures. We introduce an additive thermodynamic correction layer that shifts phase free energies towards an assessed reference without retraining or modifying the base potential. A first order thermodynamic construction converts the required phase free energy shifts directly into configuration energy targets, which are fitted using a linear atomic cluster expansion and refined iteratively from measured free energies. We apply the method to melting and solid to solid transformations across elements with different crystal structures using a foundation GRACE model. After the correction, all transformation temperatures lie within the prescribed tolerance of the assessed values, including Ca, Ti, and Zr, where a solid to solid transition and melting are corrected together. Static energy curves, bulk moduli, and liquid structure remain close to those of the base model. Vacancy formation energies, thermal expansion, and liquid density depend on the corrected phase balance and change where the correction is large. The method requires neither retraining, differentiable dynamics, nor access to the parameters of the base potential. It provides a modular route for combining transferable atomistic models with assessed phase thermodynamics.
paper.tldr: 该研究提出一种热力学修正层，在不重训练机器学习势的前提下校准相自由能，从而显著提升相变温度的预测准确性。

paper.title: Exploiting Differences in Molecular Interactions for Selective PFAS Separation from Natural Organic Matter during Ion-Exchange Regeneration
paper.abstract: Ion-exchange resins effectively remove per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) from water but generate concentrated brines co-loaded with natural organic matter, complicating downstream PFAS destruction. Here, we present a sequential selective regeneration strategy exploiting differences in adsorption mechanism and desorption kinetics between PFAS and humic substances to recover them in separate streams. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids bind to the resin through dual hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions disrupted by organic solvents, while humic substances bind predominantly electrostatically and are selectively displaced by Cl⁻ ions, desorbing 3–5 times faster than PFOA in sodium chloride solutions. A sequential protocol combining propanol regeneration with a rapid low-contact-time NaCl step recovers over 60% of loaded PFAS in an organic fraction essentially free of humic substances, while humic substances are quantitatively eluted in a separate brine. The PFAS-enriched organic fraction is directly compatible with incineration and emerging destruction technologies, where co-concentrated organic matter would otherwise increase energy demand and reduce treatment efficiency. This work demonstrates that solvent composition, ionic strength, and contact time can be systematically tuned during regeneration to engineer selectivity, a powerful but underexplored dimension of sorption-based water treatment.

paper.title: Retention-constrained fine-tuning of a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity
paper.abstract: Adapting a pre-trained machine-learning interatomic potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity requires improving defect accuracy without degrading the near-equilibrium elastic and vibrational response. Here we achieve this balance for the aluminium MACE potential QP17 by integrating conditional readout uncertainty, iterative full-parameter updates and protocol-compatible relative-energy anchoring. Sensitivities over 144 linear readout weights guide acquisition, with within-batch covariance updates and evolving neural representations. After four active-learning rounds (32 acquired configurations and 400 gradient updates), force-uncertainty acquisition reduces mean development force error from 22.43 to 21.52 meV/Angstrom, outperforming random sampling (22.70), geometry-diversity selection (22.46) and uniform training across all 104 candidate labels (22.71) under the same update budget. All three force-uncertainty runs satisfy bulk-mechanical retention criteria: historical relative-energy error decreases from 0.375 to 0.207 meV/atom, while harmonic phonon root-mean-square drift remains below 0.05 THz. Matched objective ablations reveal that relative-energy anchoring suppresses harmonic drift. Out-of-sample evaluations across planar faults, twin boundaries and grain boundaries demonstrate transferable gains in defect energies and deviatoric stresses, even though virial stresses are never fitted. A closed-loop molecular dynamics and density functional theory (MD-DFT) pilot confirms that automated acceptance gating intercepts updates that violate historical elastic-group energy or vibrational tolerances. Together, these components establish a retention-constrained fine-tuning protocol for improving plastic-deformation observables while preserving the tested bulk mechanical response.
paper.tldr: 主动学习四轮后，铝MACE势能在保持近平衡弹性和振动响应的同时，显著提升了非平衡缺陷动力学与塑性的预测精度。

paper.title: Redox‑Gated Molecular Switching of CO 2 Self‑Poisoning on Quinone Electrocatalysts Enables In Situ Self‑Regeneration
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Quinone‐based metal‐free electrocatalysts offer a sustainable route for oxygen activation and water purification, yet their persistent activity decay has remained poorly understood. Here, we identify mineralization‐derived CO 2 as the major cause of a previously overlooked self‐poisoning pathway in quinone‑based electrocatalysts: CO 2 accumulates at the electrode–electrolyte interface and forms stable carbonate adducts with reduced quinone moieties, blocking the active sites for two‐electron oxygen reduction to H 2 O 2 and consequently suppressing ·OH generation through the cascade oxygen‐reduction pathway. Electrochemical analysis further reveals that CO 2 adduction reorganizes the native quinone redox transitions into potential‐dependent carbonate‐bound states, allowing the occupied quinone centers to be reversibly regenerated by oxidative pulses. Leveraging this principle, we developed a pulsed electrocatalytic strategy that periodically reoxidizes the quinone catalyst in situ, dynamically reversing CO 2 poisoning without requiring chemical regenerants or thermal treatment. Across structurally diverse pollutants at neutral pH, this strategy accelerates degradation kinetics by up to 725.3% and retains up to 93.6% of its 2 h diclofenac removal efficiency after 12 h of continuous operation. More broadly, the redox‐gated CO 2 switching mechanism provides a generalizable design paradigm for mitigating CO 2 ‐induced deactivation in electrocatalytic systems prone to local CO 2 buildup, including CO 2 electrolysis, electrosynthetic biomass conversion, and electrochemical nitrogen fixation.

paper.title: Stable and Calibrated Latent Force ODE Filters
paper.abstract: Estimating unobserved forces in mechanistic systems is a central task of scientific machine learning. Approximate Gaussian filtering methods that synthesize mechanistic and empirical information have shown remarkable capacity in jointly identifying latent processes together with the system state in a single forward-backward pass. The resulting latent force ODE filter framework channels information from observational data specifically into the unknown parts of the system. This work addresses open questions about calibration and stability of the method. We show that the joint posterior over state and force is the reweighted conventional latent force posterior. This uncovers a crucial dependence of the stability of the method on the prior variance of the system state, which effectively controls the flow of information from observations to the latent force through the mechanistic system. From this insight, we construct an improved algorithm that provides stable and calibrated plug-and-play inference. We demonstrate the improved framework on several simulated experimental settings.
paper.tldr: 该方法揭示了联合后验是重加权传统潜势力后验，表明状态与力估计的稳定性对观测噪声权重存在关键依赖，为校准提供了理论依据。

paper.title: HOMO‐Level Alignment as a Design Descriptor for Donor–Acceptor Covalent Organic Frameworks in Aqueous Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc–iodine batteries (ZIBs) offer high voltage and inherent safety, but face a persistent trade‐off among fast kinetics, long cycling stability, and high iodine loading. Donor–acceptor (D–A) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising iodine hosts, yet the rational design is hindered by an unclear understanding of what truly governs charge‐transfer efficiency—with most studies empirically pursuing higher energy density without clear design rules. In this study, we establish highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) level alignment relative to iodine's redox potential as the governing descriptor for charge‐transfer efficiency. Analyzing a series of units with progressively elevated HOMO levels reveals a clear trend: higher HOMO levels enhance electron donation to iodine and promote charge transfer. The optimally designed NT‐COF, which combines a triphenylamine (TPA) donor with favorable HOMO alignment and a naphthalene diimide (NTCDI) acceptor with extended conjugation, exhibits the best electrochemical performance. Even with a high iodine loading (∼50.5 wt%), it delivers stable cycling and reliable low‐temperature operation. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses confirm that the energetic alignment facilitates chemisorptive iodine anchoring, accelerates charge transfer, and suppresses polyiodide dissolution. This synergy confirms that rational COF design must combine energy‐level alignment with structural conjugation.

paper.title: Effect of Size Asymmetry and Zwitterionic Character of Solvent Ions on Impedance Spectra of Ultradilute Colloidal Suspensions
paper.abstract: Buffer chemistry modulates colloidal impedance critically for label-free biosensing and electrokinetic diagnostics, yet classical models neglect buffer-specific interactions. We studied carboxylated polystyrene (PS) microspheres in conductivity-matched zwitterionic 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)-1-piperazineethanesulfonic acid (HEPES) and phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). Two concentration-dependent regimes emerged: oscillatory at ultradilute concentrations (<0.02 w/v%; Region 1) and monotonic at higher concentrations (Region 2). In Region 1, HEPES at pH 6.9 (approximately 80% zwitterionic) produced the largest deviation of delta Z from the O'Brien prediction. The conductivity increment was opposite in sign to classical expectation. We attribute this to zwitterion-driven interfacial ordering that enhances local conductivity and promotes self-limiting particle clustering. Dynamic light scattering detected cluster formation at 0.008 w/v%, well below aggregation thresholds. Changing pH from 6.9 to 8.1 strongly altered impedance amplitude; DLS profiles remained invariant. This indicates zwitterions modulate electrochemical polarization, not physical assembly. Molecular dynamics simulations showed pH-dependent HEPES organization at the PS surface. At pH 6.9, interfacial charge- and number-density profiles showed comparable oscillatory periodicity. At pH 8.1, anionic HEPES produced a more diffuse profile with increased Na+ compensation. These results support interfacial ordering as a contributor to enhanced conductivity but do not establish discrete layers or registry. Zeta potentials distinguished stable HEPES interfaces from PBS, where magnitude increased with ionic strength, contrary to classical screening theory. These nonlinear signatures and mesoscale organization underscore the role of buffer selection in high-sensitivity impedance biosensing.
paper.tldr: 实验表明，超稀释胶体悬液中，两性离子HEPES缓冲液（pH 6.9）比磷酸盐缓冲液（PBS）产生更大的阻抗偏差，且浓度低于0.02 w/v%时呈振荡模式，证实溶剂离子大小不对称性和两性特征显著影响阻抗谱。

paper.title: Primary-Particle Engineering Enables Durable O2/O3 Dual-Phase Li-Rich Cathodes
paper.abstract: Abstract O2/O3 dual-phase Li-rich layered oxides are promising high-energy cathodes, but the microstructural factors governing their electrochemical durability remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that primary-particle engineering is essential for realizing durable performance in O2/O3 dual-phase Li-rich cathodes. By varying the precursor calcination temperature from 700 to 900 °C, we regulate the primary-particle size while preserving the O2/O3 layered framework. The optimized sample prepared at 750 °C delivers an initial discharge capacity of approximately 260 mAh g–1 and retains 83.7% of its capacity after 100 cycles at 0.1 C. In contrast, particle coarsening at 900 °C limits low-voltage capacity utilization, accelerates voltage fade, and induces severe intergranular cracking. The optimized cathode also achieves 75.8% discharge-energy retention after 200 cycles at 0.5 C in a pouch-type full cell, 13% higher than that of a conventional O3-type Li-rich cathode. These findings establish primary-particle engineering as a critical design strategy for durable O2/O3 dual-phase Li-rich cathodes.

paper.title: Stabilizing Oxygen Redox in Polycrystalline Li‐Rich Layered Cathodes via Efficient Grain Boundary Passivation
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT High‐voltage cathodes with hybrid anion and cation redox activities, such as Li‐rich and Mn‐rich oxides, offer a pathway to higher energy density in lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, those cathodes suffer from oxygen loss from both the surface and grain boundaries, especially in traditional polycrystalline cathodes with secondary‐particle morphology. Interfacial passivation is needed, yet uniform, high‐quality coating at both primary‐ and secondary‐particle levels remains challenging. Here, using a tannic acid‐assisted process, we demonstrate an in situ formed Ba M O 3− δ ( M = Ni, Co, and Mn) perovskite phase at surfaces and grain boundaries, offering effective passivation to suppress structural and electrochemical degradation. Differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), soft X‐ray spectroscopy (SXAS) and resonant inelastic X‐ray spectroscopy (RIXS) reveal that the passivated grain boundaries effectively mitigate oxygen release, promote the retention of oxidized oxygen within the grains, and improve oxygen‐redox reversibility. The stabilization is facilitated by strong M ─O bonding at primary‐particle surfaces, improving energy‐density stability and mitigating voltage decay. The improved electrochemical performance results from the reliable coating method, which constructs sequential interfacial bonding along grain boundaries. Using earth‐abundant elements only, this process may offer high‐quality passivation for a variety of oxide cathodes used in LIBs and beyond.

paper.title: Discovering Underpotentially Deposited Crystalline Sodium Metal Nanoparticles on the Surface of Hard Carbon Anodes
paper.abstract: Abstract Sodium-ion batteries are attractive candidates for low-cost and scalable energy storage in which hard carbon (HC) anodes are used. However, sodium (Na) metal plating in HC anodes at voltages above the plating potential remains a critical problem. The location and spatial distribution of crystalline sodium (c-Na) metal nanoparticles, the clusters associated with Na storage in HCs, are important for understanding this underpotential plating behavior but remain unclear. Here, we implement a cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and electron tomography (cryo-ET) workflow that directly localizes c-Na metal clusters in sodiated HC samples: cryo-ET maps nanoscale three-dimensional (3D) distributions, while cryo-EM resolves local structure and chemistry. Our workflow reveals that c-Na metal clusters reside predominantly on the surfaces or near surfaces of individual HC particles. This finding challenges existing interpretations in the literature that locate the c-Na metal clusters within closed nanopores in the bulk of the HC, presumably because prior characterization using nonimaging techniques and two-dimensional (2D) projection images associated with traditional transmission electron microscopy (TEM) lacks the spatial 3D information necessary to resolve the full spatial distribution. Our discovery is an important step toward explaining the underpotential plating phenomenon of Na metal in HC anodes, suggesting that particle-level surface and near-surface interfaces are relevant targets to mitigate plating alongside bulk-pore, electrode, and electrolyte/interphase design.

paper.title: Harnessing Electrostructural Bistability to Control Defects in Polarizable Materials
paper.abstract: Structural defects are central to the functionalities of materials. However, conventional approaches to defect control are often slow and imprecise. This work identifies and characterizes a distinct physical phenomenon of electrostructural bistability that provides a rapid and precise pathway for engineering materials with defect-controlled physical properties. A generalized theory of conductivity bistability is developed and experimentally validated to unify two distinct regimes: previously reported electrothermal bistability in weakly polarizable insulators, such as silicon, and electrostructural bistability in strongly polarizable materials, such as TiO$_2$. In agreement with the theory, experiments on TiO$_2$ demonstrate that bulk-homogeneous defect concentrations in electrostructurally bistable materials can be tuned rapidly and deterministically by controlling applied electric current. Abruptly interrupting the current quenches the system into long-lived, room-temperature metastable states with distinct properties. This establishes a practical, rapid, and scalable pathway for defect engineering with direct relevance to nonvolatile memory devices.

paper.title: Regulated Density of Atomic Cu Sites Dictates Switching from C1 to C2+ Products in CO Electroreduction
paper.abstract: Abstract Single-atom catalysts (SACs) are generally considered C1-selective in CO2/CO electroreduction, as spatially isolated sites cannot efficiently sustain adjacent CO-derived intermediates required for C─C coupling. Here we show that this selectivity bias is not intrinsic to atomically dispersed Cu, but depends on single-atom site density. Across a series of Cu–N3O catalysts with different Cu site densities, increasing site density drives a clear selectivity crossover from H2 and CH4 formation to C2+ products. The total C2+ Faradaic efficiency (FE) rises from 9.6% on the low-density to 78.1% on the high-density at 1 bar CO, and further reaches 87.7% at 7 bar CO, whereas the low-density remains C1-selective. In situ attenuated-total-reflection surface enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) reveals that dense Cu single atoms sustain a larger *COatop population and simultaneously shift interfacial water from strongly hydrogen-bonded species towards free-water-rich configurations. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that higher site density stabilizes CO-containing surface states and lowers the barrier of the acetate-forming pathway. These findings identify a CO-rich and proton-accessible interfacial state that favors C─C coupling over C1 hydrogenation, establishing site density as a structural descriptor for multicarbon electrosynthesis on single-atom catalysts.

paper.title: Performance of Neural Operator Baselines on 'The Well' Dataset
paper.abstract: The Well, a 15-terabyte dataset spanning 16 physical simulation domains, provides an extensive benchmark for developing and evaluating machine learning surrogate models for complex physical systems. The baselines released with the benchmark were presented by their authors as illustrative examples obtained at small computational cost, trained with zero to very limited hyperparameter tuning and under a highly constraining 12-hour per-run wall-clock limit. These results have subsequently been treated as fully tuned benchmarks, and in some cases effectively interpreted as unconstrained performance baselines. We perform a short non-exhaustive hyperparameter search for the Tucker-factorized Fourier Neural Operator (TFNO) under the same 12-hour per-run wall-clock limit, while using only a single input timestep rather than the history of up to four used by the published baselines. Despite this more restrictive setup, tuning alone reduces VRMSE below both published FNO and TFNO baselines on 15 of 17 tasks, sometimes by several orders of magnitude. This sensitivity to a modest tuning effort underscores that the released neural operator baselines should not be treated as architectural benchmarks.

paper.title: Automated Framework for Molecular Multipole Calculations: Benchmarking DFT Methods and Dataset Generation for Azole-Based Materials
paper.abstract: Abstract Molecular electric dipole and quadrupole moments are fundamental descriptors of charge distribution and intermolecular electrostatics, with applications spanning spectroscopy, force-field parametrization, and the design of proton-conducting materials. Despite their importance, extracting multipole moments from DFT typically requires specialized postprocessing, and validated benchmark datasets remain scarce for chemistries of interest. Here, we present an open-source, basis-set-agnostic Python framework that automates the calculation of molecular dipole and quadrupole moments from plane-wave and Gaussian-type-orbital DFT, supporting both total-electron-density and charge-density-difference formulations, and benchmark it against experimental references for 99 dipole and 54 quadrupole moments across five density functional approximations. We further apply the framework to generate a data set of 242 substituted azoles relevant to nonaqueous proton conduction and show that computed dipole and quadrupole moments provide complementary information about molecular charge distribution. As a preliminary exploration of these data as machine-learning targets, an unoptimized random forest baseline trained on identity-based structural descriptors predicts dipole moments to within 0.5 D for weakly perturbing substituents but yields larger errors for strongly electron-withdrawing groups; these errors correlate with the Hammett σp constant, motivating the use of electronically resolved descriptors in future modeling efforts. The framework, benchmark results, and azole data set are released openly to support high-throughput electronic structure data generation, force-field parametrization, and machine-learning studies of multipole-aware materials design.

paper.title: Beyond Candidate Generation: A Validation-First Protocol for AI-Assisted Transition-State Discovery
paper.abstract: Machine-learned models can now propose three-dimensional transition-state (TS) geometries in seconds, but a candidate geometry is not a validated TS. The gap between a plausible structure and a mechanistically meaningful barrier—one imaginary frequency, the intended atom pair, the correct connectivity, and a consistent electronic state—remains the bottleneck in AI-assisted computational chemistry. We present a validation-first protocol that separates candidate generation from physical validation. The protocol combines (i) a chemical preflight that fixes reactive pairs, spin surfaces, connectivity, and conformers; (ii) a per-point independent scan that localizes the barrier without fragile collective scans; (iii) a constrained reference calculation that produces the Hessian; (iv) an OptTS stage that reuses that Hessian; and (v) a validation stage based on imaginary-mode localization, key bond lengths, IRC endpoints, spin diagnostics, and energy-convention checks. The protocol is implemented as a portable, open-source skill package for local ORCA/xtb and Gaussian/Slurm execution. Case studies from Ni/Fe catalysis illustrate the failure modes the protocol is designed to catch: a generative model produced candidates with 3.6–4.4 Å heavy-atom RMSD for an 84-atom broken-symmetry organometallic system, a collective scan failed three times where a per-point strategy completed 16/16 points, and a single-conformer R/S comparison would have misread a conformerdominated difference. The reported gains of multi-sampling and conformer enumeration are taken from the published benchmark, not measured here. We argue that the near-term role of AI is not to replace electronic-structure judgment but to shrink the search space before it and to make the validation layer reproducible.
paper.tldr: 该协议强调先验证后生成，确保过渡态候选具单一虚频、正确连接与自旋态，缩小了结构与有效能垒间的差距。

paper.title: A Differentiable Framework for Inverse Identification of Heterogeneous Cohesive Laws
paper.abstract: This work develops a differentiable finite element framework based on an intrinsic cohesive-zone formulation for identifying traction-separation laws from global force-displacement histories and spatially sparse strain measurements. The framework employs physics-constrained neural networks to represent flexible, thermodynamically structured cohesive laws, with sensitivities computed through automatic differentiation and a discrete adjoint that accounts for the history-dependent evolution of interfacial damage. To enable identification of spatially heterogeneous cohesive behavior, we extend learned constitutive priors to irreversible interfacial damage by constructing a shared, low-dimensional family of cohesive laws from representative traction-separation histories. This representation exploits common constitutive structure and parameter sharing to reduce the number of unknowns and regularize the inverse problem, while allowing local cohesive behavior to vary spatially through latent coordinates. Numerical investigations involving double-cantilever beams and fiber-matrix composites demonstrate that accurate reproduction of global force-displacement responses does not necessarily imply accurate recovery of the underlying cohesive laws. Incorporating spatially resolved strain measurements substantially improves constitutive identification, even when the admissible responses are constrained by a learned prior. Comparisons with conventional bilinear cohesive models and Bayesian optimization further illustrate the benefits of the learned constitutive representation and adjoint-based identification for high-dimensional inverse problems.

paper.title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
paper.abstract: Interfacial nonradiative recombination limits tin-lead perovskite photovoltaics. Here we show that neutral ethylenediamine chelates undercoordinated metals at tin-rich surfaces, weakens metal-iodide bonds, and removes excess tin, reconstructing the surface towards a stoichiometric tin-to-lead ratio. In contrast, protonated ethylenediammonium iodide initially passivates undercoordinated metal sites before undergoing defect-assisted deprotonation. Atomistic simulations reveal that subsurface iodide vacancies promote iodide migration and lower the energetic cost of deprotonation. Ethylenediamine-induced reconstruction produces stronger n-type surface character, facilitates electron extraction into C60, and suppresses interfacial nonradiative recombination, enabling methylammonium-free solar cells with a power conversion efficiency of 25.86%. Together, these distinct surface reaction pathways and the defect-assisted evolution of the passivating species underscore the importance of understanding perovskite surface chemistry for the rational design of molecular passivation strategies.

paper.title: Reversible Breathing of Cu─Co Dual‐Atom Sites Enables Spatially Proximal C─N Coupling for Urea Electrosynthesis
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic urea synthesis via the Langmuir–Hinshelwood pathway demands spatially proximal active sites to synchronize the generation and cross‐coupling of C‐ and N‐derived intermediates. Heteronuclear dual‐atom catalysts offer chemically differentiated sites for this purpose, yet whether their bimetallic centers remain static or dynamically evolve during C─N coupling remains unresolved. Here, we construct a well‐defined N 3 ─Cu─Co─N 3 dual‐atom site for the electrochemical coreduction of CO 2 and NO 3 − to synthesize urea and uncover its reversible, electric‐field‐driven structural breathing under electrocatalytic conditions, affording a maximum urea yield rate of 4828.4 ± 136.5 µg h −1 mg cat −1 and a Faradaic efficiency of 56.8 ± 7.6% at −1.2 V (vs. RHE). Operando x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) revealed a reversible, electric‐field‐driven breathing‐like modulation of the Cu─Co distance, characterized by Cu─Co contraction and Cu─N/Co─N elongation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that the Cu─Co distance reaches a minimum of 2.16 Å in the *CONH 2 ‐bound configuration formed during the initial C─N coupling step. The adaptive contraction brings C‐ and N‐intermediates into close proximity to enable C─N coupling, thereby reconfiguring heteronuclear dual‐atom sites from static pairs into dynamically responsive centers and highlighting field‐tunable metal–metal distance as a catalytic design lever.

paper.title: Lattice free energies of molecular crystals using normalizing flow
paper.abstract: Abstract Accurate free-energy calculations are essential for predicting thermodynamic stability in complex molecular materials, such as the polymorphic crystal landscapes of pharmaceutical molecules. Classical methods such as the Einstein crystal method (ECM) provide benchmark accuracy but are computationally prohibitive in larger crystal landscapes generated by Crystal Structure Prediction. Here, we develop a scalable framework for the anharmonic free-energy ranking of molecular crystals, based on targeted free-energy perturbation. In particular, we utilise the targeted Bennett acceptance ratio (tBAR) method, where the targeting step employs a bijective map learned via a normalising flow. The maps are trained to analytically transform supercell configurations between the crystal Boltzmann ensembles of interest and an analytical reference state. Exact likelihoods, in turn, enable reliable lattice free-energy estimates directly from physical molecular dynamics data, without alchemical sampling. The method handles supercells with up to 3 × 10 3 degrees of freedom and permits multi-state training with a single model. Validation across succinic acid, Veliparib, and Mivebresib demonstrates excellent agreement with ECM at significantly lower cost. By combining statistical mechanics and machine-learning expressivity, this approach advances anharmonic free energies towards automation and high-throughput applications in molecular and materials design.

paper.title: 3DSolidFormer for high-resolution full-field prediction in three-dimensional linear elasticity
paper.abstract: Abstract Repeated finite-element analysis becomes costly when displacement, strain, and stress must be resolved throughout three-dimensional structures on meshes containing millions of elements. In this study, 3DSolidFormer is developed for simultaneous prediction of these fields from material distributions, applied forces, and displacement constraints. Global structural dependencies and field-specific local interactions are learned through a transformer-enhanced architecture, while prescribed zero-displacement constraints are satisfied by construction. The accompanying dataset contains 75,114 finite-element solutions for three-dimensional domains discretized into 2.05 to 3.07 million voxels, covering fully solid and topology-optimized structures under small-strain linear elasticity. Across 7,488 high-resolution test cases, median case-level relative root-mean-square errors are 0.1172 for displacement, 0.1475 for equivalent strain, and 0.1448 for von Mises stress. Mean Percentage Mean Absolute Error (PMAE) values are 2.62% for displacement magnitude, 0.204% for equivalent strain, and 0.198% for von Mises stress. Direct scalar-field prediction reduces median PMAE by 76.6% for strain and 76.9% for stress relative to recovery from predicted displacement. All three fields are returned at the high-resolution mesh nodes in a single forward pass. The dataset provides reference solutions for benchmarking full-field surrogates and developing learning-based structural optimization methods.

paper.title: Enabling Structure-Only Initialization and Out-of-Distribution Generalization in GNN-Based Molecular Dynamics Simulators
paper.abstract: Abstract Machine-learning-based simulators offer the potential to model the dynamics of complex systems more efficiently than classical approaches while retaining differentiability, a key property for materials design. Graph neural network (GNN)-based simulators have shown strong performance across a range of physical domains, including molecular dynamics. However, their reliance on temporal context for accurate prediction limits their use in inverse design settings, where simulations must be initialized from a single static configuration. Moreover, inverse design requires robust out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization, as candidate structures typically lie outside the training domain. Here, we address both challenges by introducing two complementary strategies that enable the stable and accurate structure-only initialization of GNN-based simulations. To directly target OOD generalization, we propose an inference-time physics-based optimization framework that constrains model predictions to remain physically consistent during the rollout. In addition, we introduce a differentiable, GNN-based barostat that enables accurate tracking of system dimensions and pressure, which is critical for capturing macroscopic responses and supporting OOD generalization. We evaluated these approaches in the context of uniaxial compression of disordered elastic networks spanning a broad range of geometries, Poisson’s ratios, and microscopic behaviors. We find that, together, these methods substantially improve rollout stability and enable reliable OOD generalization, including regimes with distinct, more complex dynamics than those the in training data. These results show that when properly initialized and constrained, GNN-based simulators can serve as efficient and generalizable tools for materials discovery and structural optimization, advancing their use in materials, molecular, and dynamical system design.

paper.title: MLIPDiff: Guiding Denoising Diffusion Models for Structure-Based Drug Design via Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
paper.abstract: Diffusion models have become a dominant approach to structure-based drug design. However, because they are trained primarily to fit reference structures, they often place ligands in physically implausible poses that clash with the protein. We introduce MLIPDiff, an inference-time guidance method that can be applied to pretrained diffusion models for ligand generation. The method uses physics-informed guidance from UMA (Universal Models for Atoms), a machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP). The guidance combines four weighted energy terms (protein-ligand interaction, ligand strain, steric clash, and pocket anchoring) and uses the original model checkpoint without retraining. On CrossDocked2020, MLIPDiff completely eliminates protein-ligand collisions while preserving the ligand's local geometry, improving bond-length distributions and physical plausibility relative to the base model. Compared to models such as NucleusDiff that are specifically designed to reduce atomic clashes, MLIPDiff achieves clash-free structures without compromising local geometry. It maintains the base model's PoseBusters pass rate and attains the best median Vina Score, Vina Min, and Vina Dock, surpassing both the base model and NucleusDiff, with a median of 59.6\% of ligands per pocket binding more strongly than the reference. MLIPDiff thus addresses a limitation of prior methods by generating physically plausible structures with favorable predicted binding affinity using a single frozen model and no additional training.

paper.title: Virtual electrode XPS experiments on Li 3−x Sc 1−x Zr x Cl 6 (x ∼ 0.2): Oxygen-mediated interface passivation on metallic lithium anodes
paper.abstract: Lithium metal chlorides are a promising class of solid-state electrolyte (SSE) materials that may enable the use of lithium anodes for next-generation electrochemical energy storage. Zr-substituted Li 3 ScCl 6 (Li 3-x Sc 1-x Zr x Cl 6 ), combines the high ionic conductivities of Li 3 ScCl 6 with the moisture resistance of Li 2 ZrCl 6 that facilitates processing and manufacturing. However, little is known about the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation and composition at the Li 3-x Sc 1-x Zr x Cl 6 and Li metal anode interfacial region. Elucidating the relevant (electro)chemical processes is crucial for engineering Li 3-x Sc 1-x Zr x Cl 6 | Li 0 interfaces with low interfacial impedances and long-term cycling stability. Here, we utilize the virtual-electrode X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (VE-XPS) technique study the formation and early-stage evolution of the SEI. Additionally, we investigate the long-term effects of galvanostatic cycling on the ion transport properties and how SEI evolution impacts the overall electrochemical impedance of Li 2.8 Sc 0.8 Zr 0.2 Cl 6 -based cells. Our results show the initial SEI formation diverges from thermodynamic phase decomposition predictions due to the presence of oxygen, leading to formation of a novel Li-Sc-Zr-oxide (LSZO) phase that is compositionally similar to Li 7 La 3 Zr 2 O 12 (LLZO). For the early-stage SEI, this oxygen-mediated decomposition pathway appears to mitigate reduction of the metal cations and prevent the formation of metallic phases (e.g., metallic Zr, Sc, and Sc-Zr alloys). We find that LSZO phase formation effectively passivates the Li 2.8 Sc 0.8 Zr 0.2 Cl 6 | Li 0 interface and enables plating and stripping of metallic lithium.

paper.title: Operando XAS In a Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyser Under Industrially Relevant Conditions
paper.abstract: Optimising the performance of proton exchange membrane water electrolysers (PEMWEs) requires mechanistic insight into electrocatalyst behaviour under device-relevant conditions. Here, we report an operando PEMWE for synchrotron XAS with an incorporated reference electrode, enabling catalyst structure and oxidation state to be correlated directly with anode potential. Electrochemical benchmarking against a conventional PEMWE with identical catalyst-coated membranes shows that representative anode performance is achieved during synchrotron XAS. The evolution of a hydrated IrOx anode catalyst and a Pt cathode catalyst is thereby followed throughout break-in and operation at current densities extending beyond 2 A cm−2 (4000 A g−1 IrOx ). The reference electrode enables direct comparison of catalyst behaviour across cell geometries, with the Ir oxidation state response found to be comparable between a three-electrode flow cell with a gas diffusion electrode and the PEMWE below onset of the Oxygen Evolution Reaction (OER). During OER, the PEMWE reaches ∼30-fold higher massnormalised current densities and shows continued Ir oxidation with increasing anode potential. The absence of an Ir oxidation state plateau at these high potentials suggests that prior reports of such a plateau may reflect incomplete catalyst utilisation under more transport-limited conditions, rather than an intrinsic feature of Ir oxidation behaviour.

paper.title: Facet engineering enables efficient H2O2 piezo-synthesis and self-activation for decentralized water purification
paper.abstract: Piezo-catalytic self-Fenton is a promising strategy for chemical-free decentralized water purification but suffers from sluggish H2O2 generation and activation kinetics. Herein, we designed a bifunctional piezo-catalyst (Cu2WS4) with spatially separated H2O2 generation and activation sites on dedicated facets. Results demonstrate that the piezoelectric field aligns with facet-specific intrinsic fields in Cu2WS4, synergistically boosting directional charge migration, which directs two-electron oxygen reduction reaction to Cu-W bridge sites on {001} facets and water oxidation reaction to Cu_top sites on {101} facets, achieving a high H2O2 production rate of 892.2 µmol g−1 h−1. Notably, the Cu-W heteronuclear dual-coordination architecture enables the H2O2 produced to be sustainably activated in-situ to hydroxyl radicals (·OH). Meanwhile, sulfur-bridged electron shuttle accelerates the CuII/CuI redox cycle, sustaining continuous H2O2 activation for ·OH generation and efficient removal of various refractory pollutants. This work offers a promising approach for reagent-free technologies that harvest ambient mechanical energy for decentralized water purification.

paper.title: Direct imaging elucidates ionic memory in two-dimensional nanochannels
paper.abstract: Abstract Nanofluidic memristors promise brain-inspired information processing with ions, yet their microscopic origin remains debated. So far, ionic memory has been attributed to ion-specific interactions, dynamic wetting, chemical reactions or mechanical deformations, yet typically without direct experimental evidence. Here, by combining operando interferometric imaging with electrokinetic measurements, we directly visualize voltage-induced blistering of the confining walls of two-dimensional (2D) nanochannels as the key origin of memristive hysteresis. We identify two distinct classes of blisters: unidirectional, driven by electrostatic forces on surface charges, and bidirectional, arising from osmotic pressure due to concentration polarization. This mechanistic framework explains device evolution and device-to-device variability, and reframes stochastic blistering as a functional design element. Our results constitute a direct proof of electromechanical coupling as a robust pathway to ionic memory in 2D nanochannels and open routes towards high-performance ionic memristors and electrically actuated nanofluidic valves.

paper.title: Interplay of Aromaticity and Coulomb Repulsion in the Electronic Structure of a Dimeric Pentafulvalene Upon Multi-Electron Uptake
paper.abstract: Multielectron reduction of finite one-dimensional (1D) π-conjugated hydrocarbons remains poorly understood because such frameworks are usually unstable due to charge accumulation in the absence of electron-withdrawing substituents. Here, we investigate the reduction of dibenzopentafulvalene dimers ([2]DBFs), a rare class of quasi-1D conjugated hydrocarbons that exhibit unusual stability toward multi-electron reduction and contain four indenylidene subunits that can each become aromatic upon reduction, raising the question of where the excess electrons reside. Chemical reduction of [2]DBFs with alkali metal-based reductants afforded dianionic and tetraanionic species, which were characterized by electronic absorption spectroscopy, NMR spectroscopy, single-crystal X-ray diffraction, and complementary quantum chemical calculations. The dianions accommodate excess negative charge at the outer indenylidene subunits, where Coulomb repulsion is minimized by charge separation while gaining 10π Hückel aromaticity. In contrast, upon four-electron reduction, all four indenylidene subunits become aromatic, and the excess charge becomes more broadly distributed and can extend to the end-capping phenyl groups even at the expense of the aromatic character of the end-capping benzene rings. The solid-state structures further reveal that the observed charge distributions are strongly influenced by the spatial arrangement of counter cations. These results identify local aromatization, Coulomb repulsion, and countercation position as competing factors that determine where electrons reside in multiply charged finite 1D π-conjugated hydrocarbons.
