paper.title: Flexible and Tailorable Moisture–Electric Generators Realized by Arsenic Concentration Gradient in 2D Black As x P Nanosheet Sponge
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Moisture‐enabled electric generators (MEGs) can harvest atmospheric water and convert humidity into electricity, but their application is hindered by low and unstable output. Herein, we exploit the compositional tunability of two‐dimensional black arsenic phosphorus ( b ‐As x P) to construct asymmetric MEGs by integrating b ‐As x P nanosheets but their application is hindered into a high‐density polyurethane sponge. The graded As distribution creates distinct surface physicochemical properties while preserving the crystalline lattice, enabling directional water adsorption and asymmetric proton transport. The MEGs show pronounced humidity‐responsive output over a wide relative humidity range. At ∼80% relative humidity, a 4.0 × 1.0 × 0.5 cm 3 device delivers an open‐circuit voltage of 186 mV and a short‐circuit current density of 0.44 µA cm −2 . Polyvinyl alcohol encapsulation enhances device hygroscopicity and suppresses b ‐As x P oxidation, improving stability and mitigating concerns associated with arsenic oxidation. Comparative experiments and theoretical calculations indicate that composition‐dependent interactions between water molecules and arsenic/phosphorus sites establish the asymmetric ionic environment and electrical output. The devices show excellent flexibility and scalability, delivering stable output even at a nearly folded state and 2.7 V from 28 serially connected units. This work highlights the concentration‐tunable characteristics of 2D elemental alloys and provides a composition‐gradient strategy for flexible moisture‐energy systems.

paper.title: FIREX: Fast-Ion Replica EXchange Enables Rapid Sampling of Mg2+ Pairing with Nucleic Acids
paper.abstract: Abstract We introduce Fast-Ion Replica EXchange (FIREX), a Hamiltonian Replica Exchange-based sampling strategy specifically designed to enhance the sampling of metastable divalent cation binding with phosphate groups, e.g., in nucleic acids. We parametrize the scheme and demonstrate its convergence and efficiency on a model DNA dodecamer with Mg2+ ions, using two force fields with very different ion-pairing properties to test its robustness. The highest replica is driven by a “fast-ion” Hamiltonian combining a reduced ion charge with a tuned pair-specific Lennard-Jones interaction between the ion and phosphate oxygen atoms, yielding rapid exchange as well as moderate binding affinity, amenable to efficient sampling. By enabling the robust quantification of divalent ion interactions in simulations, FIREX could be instrumental in refining force fields to better capture ion–molecule interactions. The provided guidelines for the design of fast-ion models suitable for FIREX are general and could be extended to other force fields or types of biomolecular moieties, such as carboxylated protein side chains, phosphorylated proteins, or other interaction sites on nucleic acids. We further demonstrate how FIREX can be efficiently combined with the REST2 method to achieve simultaneous sampling of ion binding and biomolecular conformations with the Amber-OL15-ECC force field, while convergence remains challenging with the original Amber-OL15. This shows that different HREX schemes, including REST2, can be merged into a combined, highly cost-effective HREX scheme and is a step toward robust, computationally efficient sampling of charged biomolecules in interaction with divalent ions.

paper.title: Revisiting atmospheric sulfur chemistry: Acid-catalyzed pathways do not control H 2 SO 4 formation
paper.abstract: Sulfuric acid (H₂SO 4 ) drives new particle formation and radiatively important aerosol processes in the atmosphere, but its formation pathways remain poorly resolved because of limited kinetics data. To clarify these pathways, we combined coupled-cluster calculations, reaction rate theory, and a global chemistry transport model to quantify acid-catalyzed SO 3 hydration and its atmospheric significance. We find that the overall kinetics is not governed by a tight transition state but rather is controlled by a preceding loose transition state associated with the formation of the precursor complex of the acid-catalyzed SO 3 hydration. Our results reverse a recent view that acid catalysis is the dominant contributor to atmospheric SO 3 hydration, instead supporting an earlier view that water catalysis dominates SO 3 hydration. Incorporating the revised kinetics into the GEOS-Chem atmospheric model reveals no significant impact of acid-catalyzed SO 3 hydration on the simulated concentrations of H 2 SO 4 . The present findings highlight the critical roles of variational transition states in kinetic modeling.

paper.title: Critical View on Dielectric Constant Changes in Solid and Liquid Nonanol
paper.abstract: Abstract The report presents evidence for the long-range premelting effect, with a well-defined critical-like scaling pattern, in the dielectric constant (ε) of solid nonanol, extending even ∼40 K below the melting temperature Tm, namely, ε(T)∝1/(T* – T), the singular temperature T* ≈ Tm + 0.4 K. This is supplemented by tests in liquid nonanal showing exceptional evidence for a simple scaling relation ε(T) = a + b/T, a,b = const. The experiment also revealed unique Mossotti Catastrophe type behavior in liquid nanolayers between crystalline grains in the premelting domain. It can be associated with rising negative pressure, finally leading to abrupt implosive ultragranulation and liquidation at Tm. For the applied experimental method, the response of quasi-liquid nanolayers is qualitatively greater than that from crystalline grains in the premelting region. This is consistent with the Lipowsky model [ Phys. Rev. Lett.1982, 49, 1575.], suggesting the criticality of nanoconstrained quasi-liquid layers between solid plates.

paper.title: Stable N-Heterocyclic Carbene-Derived α-Diimine Radical Cations with Anionic Nitrogen Character
paper.abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-centered radicals possessing substantial anionic character have remained highly challenging to isolate because of their intrinsic electronic instability in the absence of metal coordination. Herein, we report a family of stable N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-derived α-diimine radical cations that constitute a rare class of persistent organic radicals featuring pronounced anionic nitrogen-centered radical character. Combined crystallographic, EPR, electrochemical, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal an unusual electronic structure in which the molecular framework is formally cationic whereas both the unpaired electron and substantial negative charge are predominantly localized on the α-diimine nitrogen atoms. These radicals exhibit remarkable stability, undergo selective proton- and hydrogen-atom-transfer reactions, and participate in fully reversible, stepwise interconversion among dicationic, radical cationic, and neutral redox states without degradation of the molecular framework. Two-electron reduction induces reversible C–N bond formation to generate either an azetidinimine or a zwitterionic structure, with their relative stability governed by remote electronic substituents. Variable-temperature spectroscopy, UV–Vis analysis, and DFT calculations reveal dynamic solution-state equilibria that can be thermodynamically tuned through peripheral electronic modulation. These findings establish a new design principle for persistent nitrogen-centered radicals and reveal how redox state, charge distribution, spin localization, and reversible covalent bond reorganization can be coupled within a metal-free molecular framework.

paper.title: Electroenzymatic Cascade Enables Amino Acid Synthesis through Simultaneous Nitrite Reduction and NADH Regeneration
paper.abstract: Abstract Amino acids are central to life and the chemical industry, yet their sustainable synthesis remains a challenge. An electroenzymatic cascade offers a promising alternative by combining the electron/proton transfer capability of electrocatalysis with the exceptional specificity of biocatalysis. Here we present a conceptually distinct electroenzymatic cascade platform that integrates electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction, NADH regeneration, and enzymatic reductive amination. Using l-glutamate (l-Glu) as a model, we demonstrate that with Cu nanowires as the bifunctional electrocatalyst, the system generates NH4+ and biologically active NADH in situ, driving the production of l-Glu under mild conditions. The coupled cascade not only shifts the reaction equilibrium forward but also provides a favorable orientation and a proton-rich environment for the bioactive cofactor, boosting overall selectivity of bioactive NADH. The modular design allows straightforward adaptation to diverse substrates and electrodes, demonstrating the broad generality of this platform. This work establishes a sustainable and versatile strategy for amino acid synthesis and opens new directions for electroenzymatic production of nitrogen-containing chemicals.

paper.title: Effects of Zeolite Framework on Direct Reduction of Esters to Ethers Using H2 on Pt-Zeolite Catalysts
paper.abstract: Abstract The direct reduction of esters to ethers using H2 represents a fundamental selectivity challenge for heterogeneous catalysis and offers a method to increase the hydrothermal stability of chemicals and fuels derived from renewable resources. Prior studies revealed that ethers derive from a series of reactions that involve in situ formation of hemiacetals by hydrogen transfer on metal nanoparticles, followed by diffusive transport to Brønsted acid sites that cleave the carbonyl C–O bond. The competing hydrogenolysis pathway proceeds by a similar bifunctional mechanism; however, hydrolysis and transesterification occur by direct reactions of esters solely at Brønsted acid sites. Here, we find that rates and selectivities reflect the intrinsic reactivity at individual Brønsted acid sites, which depends upon the topology of the aluminosilicate support. Pt-Faujasite (FAU) provides ether formation rates at least an order of magnitude greater than smaller pore zeolites that possess similar Pt loadings and Si/Al ratios (e.g., mordenite framework inverted (MFI), beta (BEA), and ferrierite (FER)). Correlations between formation rates and activation energies for ether formation with heats of adsorption of propyl acetate across Pt-zeolites and Pt-AlMCM41 suggest that dispersive interactions among the zeolite pore wall, surrounding molecules (e.g., propyl acetate), and transition states contribute to differences in performance among these catalysts. These effects appear responsible for Pt-FER providing the highest ether selectivities observed (∼50%), although the specific structural features responsible for this behavior remain uncertain and may reflect framework-specific confinement and transport effects. However, ether selectivities also appear sensitive to other zeolite properties, including channel dimensionality, which may influence diffusive transport between Pt and Brønsted acid sites. These findings illustrate that the topology of the aluminosilicate support impacts rates and selectivities for ester reduction by orders of magnitude: these differences reflect contributions of inter-function transport reminiscent of other bifunctional catalysts for hydrotreating reactions but also evidence from comparisons to titration calorimetry that the local solvation of reactive intermediates at Brønsted acid sites influences catalysis.

paper.title: Capture and reduction of singlet oxygen via an anthracene-based framework for stable Li-O 2 batteries
paper.abstract: Given the increasing global energy demand and rapid advancement of low-carbon technologies, Li-O 2 batteries have attracted considerable attention owing to their exceptionally high theoretical energy density, offering great promise for advanced energy systems. However, the formation of harmful singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) in both discharge and charge processes induces parasitic reactions that deteriorate round-trip efficiency and cycling stability. Herein, an anthracene-based covalent-organic framework (AntCOF) is introduced as a highly effective catalyst for the 1 O 2 reduction reaction (SORR) in Li-O 2 batteries. The conjugated porous framework selectively captures electrophilic 1 O 2 , enabling effective charge transfer from AntCOF to the empty π* orbital of 1 O 2 and promoting SORR in subsequent discharge processes. This mechanism suppresses 1 O 2 diffusion and mitigates associated side reactions, leading to reduced overpotentials and improved cycling performance when coupled with a RuO 2 catalyst. This work may enlighten further investigations into 1 O 2 -related chemistry across a broad range of oxygen-redox electrochemical systems.

paper.title: Breaking the high-degree barrier in Lehmer's problem with a human-AI discovery loop
paper.abstract: While artificial intelligence has made rapid progress in mathematical reasoning, many open problems depend on structure that is revealed only through large-scale computational exploration and analytical synthesis. One such example is Lehmer's problem from 1933. It asks whether the Mahler measure of an integer polynomial, which measures how far its roots stray from the unit circle, can be made arbitrarily small. Previously, constructing irreducible polynomials with integer coefficients and small Mahler measure has been carried out systematically only for even degrees $d \le 180$. At higher degrees, Boyd's analytical one-parameter family frequently factors, skipping nearly 50% of target degrees and leaving no general construction for arbitrary $d$. Here, we address the high-degree regime through a human-AI discovery loop, in which we extend the conversational prompting with a fast numerical pipeline, an exact symbolic verifier, and large-scale distributed search. The AI agent prototypes numerical and symbolic solvers locally, launches parallel searches across distributed clusters and works with the human researcher to extract and verify mathematical hypotheses. Through this interactive loop, we derive a five-parameter construction, which we call the Generalized Boyd algorithm. It eliminates degree-skipping and constructs irreducible polynomials with Mahler measure strictly below Boyd's limit point $α_1 \approx 1.255434$ for every target degree. Evaluated across all even degrees up to 2000, our approach improves upon six previously published values and holds 99.6% of all best known records. With this work we release the verified dataset of polynomials with minimal Mahler measure across all studied even degrees.

paper.title: Clutter Noise Induced Phase Segregation in Binary Active Polar Flocks
paper.abstract: Macroscopic phase segregation in binary active mixtures can emerge solely from clutter noise: local, composition-dependent stochasticity, without repulsion or anti-alignment torques. Using an agent-based Vicsek model, we show that clutter noise alone destabilizes the mixed state, producing multi-stripe, co-moving band, and metastable counter-propagating morphologies, as well as a stable phase-segregated polar fluid. Our hydrodynamic theory shows that clutter noise suppresses local polar order and transport efficiency, consistent with the demixing observed in the agent-based model.

Predicting follow-up cognition using estimated structural and functional connectivity networks and artificial intelligence in multiple sclerosis
paper.abstract: Brain’s structural and functional connectomes (SC and FC) offer insights into the relationship between brain circuits and cognitive functioning in people with multiple sclerosis (MS). However, diffusion and functional MRI, which are used to extract SC and FC, is expensive and time consuming, therefore are not currently used in the clinical setting. Our prior work demonstrated that estimated SC and FC (eSC and eFC) generated using MS lesion masks and artificial intelligence (AI) models can predict disability as effectively as SC and FC derived from diffusion and functional MRI in MS. In this study, we identify the eSC and eFC brain circuits that are associated with baseline and 4-year follow-up cognition and assess the ability of eSC and eFC in predicting cognition in MS. In a cohort of 171 with MS, the Network Modification tool was performed to estimate SC from the MS lesion mask, which is extracted from structural MRI scans. The eSC was then used as an input to Krakencoder, an encoder-decoder model, to estimate FC. The highest accuracy was obtained when predicting follow-up Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) using regional eSC or eFC, with a median Spearman’s correlation coefficient of 0.58 for eSC and 0.56 for eFC. Decreased eSC and eFC in the cerebellum and increased eFC in the default mode network were associated with lower follow-up SDMT scores. Our findings demonstrate that eSC and eFC derived from clinically acquired MRI and AI models can effectively predict cognition. The use of lesion-based estimates of connectomes may potentially inform clinical trials by identifying the specific brain circuits that could be targeted for the non-invasive treatments aimed at improving cognitive function in MS. Researchers used AI and clinically acquired MRI scans to estimate brain connectivity networks in people with multiple sclerosis, finding these estimates can moderately predict cognitive performance four years later and highlighting key brain circuits involved in cognition.

paper.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
paper.abstract: Critic-free methods are widely used in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, avoiding difficult and costly critic training. Common alternatives lack token-level credit assignment and typically rely on grouped rollouts to estimate prompt-specific baselines. A critic can address both limitations, but long-CoT critic training is hindered by insufficient coverage of trajectories with diverse lengths and early gradients dominated by the newly initialized value head. We introduce S3AC (Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic) for LLM reasoning, built around a practical critic-training recipe. The trained critic provides token-specific advantages and prompt-specific baselines. Using the prompt-level baseline to estimate difficulty, we propose Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling (DAPS). DAPS combines this estimate with outcome history to select prompts before generation, reducing rollout waste without offline difficulty initialization. S3AC improves group-rollout performance across dense and mixture-of-experts models from 1.5B to 397B parameters, outperforming a modern GRPO variant (GRPO-X). At 35B, it sustains single-rollout training while tested critic-free baselines deteriorate after initial gains.
paper.tldr: 该研究表明，采用稳定化、选择性和可扩展的actor-critic方法可提升大语言模型推理性能，同时降低训练成本。

paper.title: Water at the molecular frontier
paper.abstract: Much of the water that matters most - flowing through biological cells and membranes, percolating through soils and rocks, or processed by filtration and desalination technologies - is not bulk water. It is water in nano- and molecular-scale confinement or at interfaces. Nanoscale water is therefore central to many challenges of our time, from the global water crisis and the water-energy nexus to catalysis, electrochemistry, and health. Beyond its applications, nanoscale water has emerged as a rich scientific field in its own right: discoveries are accumulating rapidly, revealing that confinement and interfacial forces produce a range of behaviours absent in the bulk. Sometimes this amounts to a renormalization of bulk properties; in other cases, new and non-intuitive phenomena emerge - exotic phases, anomalous transport, and dielectric responses that defy continuum expectations. A convergence of atomically precise nanofluidic devices, novel spectroscopies and microscopy approaches, and machine-learning-accelerated simulations is now exposing the molecular mechanisms behind these behaviours. This Perspective argues that the recent findings should not be viewed as isolated nanoscale anomalies, but as evidence for a molecular regime of water in which continuum descriptions must be rethought and molecular-level understanding becomes essential. Recognising and exploring this regime should have consequences ranging from fundamental physics to the rational design of future technologies that rely on water and dissolved ions.
paper.tldr: 该综述指出，纳米限域与界面效应显著改变水的行为，使其在生物、地质、催化和脱盐等关键领域发挥独特作用。

paper.title: Rigor and Reproducibility in Electrocatalysis: Integrating Theory and Experiment
paper.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalysis is central to electrified energy conversion technologies, including the production of fuels and chemicals from renewable electricity. In recent years, atomistic modeling based on density functional theory (DFT) has become an indispensable tool for catalysis researchers because it can provide a molecular-level perspective of catalytic reactivity that is otherwise inaccessible through experimental measurements. Computational electrocatalysis model inputs are intended to capture fundamental understanding of the complex interfacial environment of the catalytic active site, but they rely on practical approximations that can affect the reliability of insights gained from DFT. This Perspective outlines a framework for rigorous and reproducible integration of theory and experiment in heterogeneous electrocatalysis research. We discuss state-of-the-art computational methods and sources of error in model development and interpretation. We describe opportunities for validation of theoretical models and experimental interpretations as they pertain to the structure of active sites, reaction energetics, and microkinetic modeling. We provide examples to help computational researchers develop models that move beyond obtaining qualitative agreement with reactivity trends, and toward the development of rigorous mechanistic insights that can be leveraged to predict promising new catalysts or operating conditions. Rigor and reproducibility are enhanced when theory and experiment have multiple nodes of connection, thereby enhancing the longevity and robustness of conclusions and insights about electrocatalytic reactivity.

paper.title: Site Specific Hydration Contributes to the Thermal Stability of Proteins and Protein-Complexes
paper.abstract: Water is integral to protein structure and stability, yet ensemble measurements rarely identify the hydration interactions associated with stabilization. Here, variable-temperature electrospray ionization ion mobility mass spectrometry, conformation-resolved thermodynamic analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations are combined to examine solvent-dependent thermal stability of chymotrypsin inhibitor 2 (CI-2), a model two-state folder, and the barnase-barstar (Bn-B*) complex, which contains a highly polar binding interface. Replacing H2O with D2O raises the thermal transition temperature of both systems by approximately 3 {degrees}C, favors compact conformations, and reduces the relative thermodynamic accessibility of extended states. The conformationally resolved enthalpy-entropy compensation reveals D2O increases enthalpy for CI-2 but reduces enthalpy for Bn-B* as a result of opposing effects on the individual subunits of the complex. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that lower solvent-accessible surface areas and fewer protein-water hydrogen bonds in D2O coexist with longer water residence times at specific structural sites. In CI-2, the strongest changes localize to the second {beta}-strand/C-terminal region; in Bn-B*, persistent hydration is concentrated at the charged protein-protein interface. Together, these results support a model in which D2O dependent stabilization is associated not only with the extent of hydration, but the site and lifetime of water interactions. More broadly, this work provides an experimental framework for resolving solvent-dependent conformational thermodynamics of protein unfolding and interactions, enabling direct comparison of free-energy landscapes across solution environments.

paper.title: Electrolyte Cation Engineering Selectively Regulates Competing Urea Oxidation Pathways
paper.abstract: Abstract The electrochemical urea oxidation reaction (UOR) has emerged as an attractive anodic reaction for various energy conversion systems. Recently, increasing attention has been directed toward controlling UOR selectivity on Ni-based electrocatalysts following the recognition that the UOR can produce over-oxidized products. However, existing studies have focused predominantly on catalyst design to regulate surface-bound intermediates, whereas whether electrolyte-mediated noncovalent interactions can selectively control competing UOR pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we show that rational electrolyte engineering using alkali-metal cations selectively regulates the UOR pathway by modulating the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network. Electrochemical rate deconvolution and product analysis reveal that weakly hydrated cations selectively accelerate the direct oxidation pathway, promoting the formation of the over-oxidized NO2– and NCO– products, while leaving the indirect pathway essentially unaffected. In situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) measurements, together with molecular dynamics simulations of cation hydration dynamics, indicate that weakly hydrated cations create a more dynamic interfacial water environment with faster water exchange, thereby facilitating interfacial OH–-mediated successive dehydrogenation during direct urea oxidation. Leveraging this mechanistic understanding, the electrolyte-engineering strategy was applied to a cascade urea-to-ammonia conversion system, achieving a urea-to-ammonia conversion efficiency of 77.5% and approximately threefold higher ammonia productivity in CsOH than in LiOH. These findings establish electrolyte engineering as a complementary strategy to catalyst design and highlight noncovalent electrolyte–electrode interactions as an effective handle for controlling reaction pathways and product selectivity in an integrated UOR-based nitrogen conversion system.

paper.title: Solar-operated interlayer electrothermal evaporator enabling instant high-flux freshwater production across multiple scenarios
paper.abstract: An interlayer evaporator integrating electrothermal and photothermal effects achieves efficient freshwater production from diverse water sources, enabled by reduced heat loss and improved heat utilization.

paper.title: Learning atomic interactions for the thermodynamics of liquid mixtures
paper.abstract: Predictive models for activity coefficients, which describe the non-ideality of liquid mixtures, are foundational for process design and optimization. Group-contribution methods, such as UNIFAC, are computationally cheap and well established in process simulators. Modern machine learning models, such as HANNA, offer higher accuracy and broader applicability, but their integration into process simulation is expensive or even infeasible. In this work, we introduce COGNAC, a graph neural network that learns atom-level geometry and interaction parameters that depend on the molecular neighborhood and evaluates them in the UNIFAC framework. Trained on about 820,000 experimental data points, COGNAC achieves significantly higher accuracy than UNIFAC and HANNA for binary and multi-component mixtures, reduces error relative to HANNA by 13-63%, reliably predicts multi-phase equilibria and identifies azeotropes, yields interpretable parameters, and is strictly thermodynamically consistent. COGNAC evaluations run at a cost comparable to UNIFAC, thereby unlocking the potential of machine-learning models for process simulations.
paper.tldr: 该研究将图神经网络COGNAC与UNIFAC框架结合，通过学习原子级几何与相互作用参数，在保持低成本的同时实现了对液体混合物活度系数的高精度预测。

paper.title: Solvation Cluster Engineering of Non-Fluorinated Ethers toward High-Energy Lithium Metal Batteries
paper.abstract: Abstract Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) can provide high energy density for next-generation energy storage, yet their cycle life remains limited by interfacial incompatibility between electrolyte species and electrodes. Conventional electrolytes based on polar or fluorinated solvents often suffer from sluggish transport kinetics, high cost, and even environmental concerns. Herein, we rationally modulate the polarity and coordination ability of nonfluorinated solvents and report a fluorine-free host–guest synergy electrolyte (HGSE) constructed by tailoring the intermolecular interaction between a long-chain multidentate ether and a monodentate ether solvent. The weak Hδ+–Oδ− intermolecular interaction between these solvents tunes the electrolyte coordination ability and solvation cluster size, leading to a contact ion pair-dominated solvation cluster structure with enhanced ionic conductivity. Meanwhile, the optimized solvation cluster in HGSE promotes anion decomposition while suppressing electrode side reactions, resulting in anion-derived LiF-rich interphases and minimized cathode cracking. More notably, the HGSE electrolyte enables a Li||NCM811 pouch cell to deliver a high energy density of 472.5 Wh kg–1, while a 20 Ah-level anode-free Cu||Ni90 pouch cell with a lean electrolyte (1.5 g Ah–1) achieves a superior energy density of 525 Wh kg–1 with 71.6% capacity retention over 120 cycles. These findings elucidate the role of intermolecular interactions and solvation cluster engineering in high-energy and sustainable LMBs.

paper.title: Phase transitions in multicomponent systems relevant to atmospheric new particle formation
paper.abstract: Typically, molecular clusters containing sulfuric acid, water, ammonia, and/or amines initiate particle nucleation, followed by particle growth through condensation of highly oxidized organic molecules. The coexistence of multiple organic and inorganic components in these particles can lead to variations in morphology and phase state. In this study, optical and Raman microscopy were used to study multicomponent model aerosol particles representative of new particle formation and growth. We focused on 2-methylglutaric acid, sulfuric acid, and ammonium sulfate systems with different amines; and dipropylamine, sulfuric acid, and ammonium sulfate systems with various dicarboxylic acids. Liquid-liquid phase separation occurred in many systems, while amine functionality and molecular structure affect morphology and phase state. Systems containing dipropylamine along with sulfuric acid underwent liquid-liquid phase separation in several mixtures that remained homogeneous in its absence. These particles formed an inorganic-rich core surrounded by an organic-rich shell containing both the dicarboxylic acid and dipropylamine, with slight dipropylamine enrichment at the air-water interface. Their deliquescence relative humidity was generally the same or lower, while efflorescence relative humidity was similar to the corresponding dicarboxylic acid/ammonium sulfate systems. These results demonstrate that the chemical identity of atmospheric amines and overall compound activity should be considered when predicting the phase state, morphology, and water uptake of newly formed particles, which is important for their heterogeneous chemistry and cloud droplet formation.

paper.title: High-Performance Salt-Lake Water Zinc Batteries Operated at −50 °C
paper.abstract: Abstract Low-temperature aqueous batteries are severely hindered by electrolyte freezing and a sharp drop in ionic conductivity at subzero temperatures, creating a fundamental trade-off between freeze resistance and rapid ion transport. Herein, we show that salt-lake (SL) water, an intrinsically abundant, low-cost, and naturally high-salinity medium, can directly replace deionized water as the electrolyte solvent for aqueous zinc (Zn)-ion batteries (AZIBs), offering high ionic conductivity and a low freezing point without energy-intensive purification. The high salinity of SL water in electrolytes effectively suppresses ice formation, maintains interfacial contact, and minimizes voltage loss. By reducing water coordination to Zn2+ ions, suppressing water activity, disrupting the hydrogen-bond network, and designing an artificial ternary alloy layer-coated Zn anode to enhance cation adsorption and electrostatic shielding, we achieve stable low-temperature AZIBs using SLPGCl electrolytes operated at −50 °C. The alloy layer-coated Zn symmetric cell in SLPGCl electrolyte delivers ultrastable cycling for over 3200 h at −50 °C. A full cell with a polyaniline cathode delivers over 2500 cycles at 5 A g–1, and the related pouch cell operates with long-term stability even after 900 cycles at −50 °C. This work provides a low-cost, geographically adaptable, and industrially scalable strategy for aqueous batteries operating under extreme cold conditions.

paper.title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
paper.abstract: Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. The prediction of the Hamiltonian is essentially the prediction of the electron electrostatic potential energy; however, for heterogeneous systems, this potential energy is often determined by faraway features, such as interface or surface dipoles, or even an applied voltage in a nanodevice. Thus, it cannot be determined by local atomic structures alone. In this sense, one needs to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently using intrinsic atomic dipoles, the applied external potential energy, and polarizabilities. Fortunately, the intrinsic dipoles and polarizabilities are local properties, whereas the applied potential energy is a prescribed input. In this work, we propose DeepH-Polar, a physically informed machine learning Hamiltonian model that explicitly predicts intrinsic atomic dipoles and polarizability tensors and uses them to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently. Benchmarks on polar GaN systems and crystalline-Si/amorphous-SiO$_2$ interfaces demonstrate improved Hamiltonian accuracy and reproduction of thickness-dependent electrostatic variations, as well as spatially nonuniform field-induced screening that models without polarization fail to capture. Our model also allows us to study nanoscale electronic devices. By iteratively solving the Hamiltonian eigenproblem and self-consistently updating free-carrier occupations and the electrostatic potential, we simulate an 8,194-atom gated semiconductor device.

paper.title: Cosolvation Accelerated Desolvation‐Coupled Charge Transfer for Low‐Temperature Zinc Metal Batteries
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Anti‐freezing cosolvents are commonly introduced to maintain electrolyte fluidity at subzero temperatures. However, their weak participation in the primary Zn 2+ solvation sheath can leave desolvation‐coupled interfacial kinetics largely unimproved. Here, we introduce a molecular cosolvation‐promotion strategy that activates an otherwise passive anti‐freezing solvent. Tris(2‐chloropropyl) phosphate (TCPP), featuring an electron‐rich phosphoryl center and a bulky, weakly solvating periphery, promotes methanol incorporation into the primary Zn 2+ solvation sheath. Remarkably, although the coordination number of TCPP is only 0.17, its addition increases the methanol coordination number from 0.21 to 1.19 while decreasing the water coordination number from 4.01 to 3.07. This coordination amplification lowers the apparent activation energy for desolvation‐coupled charge transfer from 18.46 to 13.91 kJ mol −1 and preserves an ionic conductivity of 4.6 mS cm −1 at −40°C. Meanwhile, preferential interfacial adsorption of TCPP excludes reactive water, homogenizes the Zn 2+ flux, and suppresses corrosion and dendritic deposition. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells operate stably for over 2700 h at −40°C, while Zn||MnVO full cells retain 84.8% of their capacity after 8000 cycles at −20°C. This work establishes molecular promotion of cosolvent coordination as a general electrolyte‐design principle for decoupling anti‐freezing fluidity from sluggish subzero charge‐transfer kinetics.

paper.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
paper.abstract: Atmospheric chemical mechanisms are commonly distributed in the language of the Kinetic PreProcessor (KPP), which generates efficient Fortran or C code but does not fit into the differentiable programming frameworks in which machine-learning models are developed. We present KPPax, a kinetic preprocessor that generates differentiable, just-in-time compiled, and vectorisable chemistry code in JAX from mechanisms written in the KPP language. KPPax evaluates the rate law with sparse operations in log space, which keeps it differentiable, and integrates the stiff system with the implicit solvers and the forward- and reverse-mode adjoints of the \texttt{diffrax} library, so that exact sensitivities are obtained without hand-derived adjoint code. We demonstrate two applications with the POLLU benchmark mechanism. In the first, the Fisher information matrix computed from an automatically differentiated Jacobian predicts, before any fit, which of the 25 rate coefficients a flow-tube-like design can identify, and noisy synthetic estimation confirms the predicted uncertainties of the nine identifiable rate coefficients to within about 30\% while revealing clusters of fast reactions of which only ratios are constrained. In the second, a neural-network correction of an emission inventory is trained offline on per-scenario 4D-Var retrievals and then fine-tuned online through the chemical model, which reduces the error of the biogenic correction by a factor of 2.4--5 and recovers information on low-temperature emissions that the individual retrievals lose. KPPax makes KPP mechanisms directly usable for parameter estimation and hybrid physics--machine-learning modelling.
paper.tldr: KPPax将KPP语言生成的动力学代码转换为JAX可微分版本，支持隐式刚性与伴随梯度计算，为机器学习化学建模提供高效工具。

paper.title: Spectro-Electrochemical Decoding of Metals, Alloys, and Buried Interfaces
paper.abstract: Metal-electrolyte interfaces govern corrosion, catalysis, energy-conversion and storage technologies, yet resolving their chemical evolution under operating conditions remains challenging. Electrochemical measurements report an integrated response, while post-mortem characterization can lose the transient sequence and spatial distribution of dissolved species. Here, we introduce the In-Situ Corrosion Monitoring Technique (ICMT), an operando spectro-electrochemical platform that converts interfacial metal dissolution into spatially and temporally resolved optical concentration fields. Under an applied bias, dissolution products migrate through a transparent gel electrolyte that suppresses convection and restricts mixing, thereby retaining dissolved species for interrogation by UV-visible spectroscopy. Using Cu and Ni as model systems, ICMT establishes element-specific absorption fingerprints and distinguishes active Ni dissolution from passivation-influenced Cu corrosion while enabling estimation of recession rates and apparent transport coefficients. Applied to Cu-coated Ni, ICMT sequentially detects Cu and Ni-associated species, revealing degradation from the outer coating to the buried substrate and detecting dissolution from a Cu overlayer as thin as 100 nm. Applied to a Cu-Zn-Ni ternary alloy, the platform resolves constituent-specific dissolution signatures that remain convoluted within the total electrochemical current. Collectively, ICMT provides a simple and accessible benchtop approach for determining how material interface evolves, which constituent dissolves and from which layer it arises, while preserving the transient chemical history of electrochemical interfaces.

paper.title: Deciphering the Role of Au in CO Reduction on Cu: From Atomic Sites to a Stabilized Proton-Transfer Interface
paper.abstract: Abstract Incorporating gold (Au) into copper (Cu)-based electrocatalysts effectively enhances the conversion of CO into multicarbon products, yet the fundamental role of Au remains elusive due to limited mechanistic insight. Using a Au-doped basic copper chloride as a platform precatalyst, we demonstrate that the in situ formation of stable Cu3Au intermetallics during operation substantially alters the CO electroreduction pathway. Using multispectroscopic analyses combined with theoretical calculations, we find that the in situ-formed Cu3Au structure likely plays a synergistic role by (i) optimizing *CO adsorption and surface coverage to promote C–C coupling and (ii) restructuring the interfacial water network to strengthen hydrogen bonding, thereby shifting the dominant proton-transfer pathway from a Langmuir–Hinshelwood mechanism to an Eley–Rideal mechanism. This reconfiguration suppresses the hydrogen evolution reaction and adsorbed hydrogen-mediated pathways while promoting direct proton donation from interfacial water for the formation of acetate. Consequently, the optimized catalyst achieves an acetate Faradaic efficiency of 80.3% at −1.05 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode with a partial current density of −492.7 mA cm–2. These findings underscore how adaptive electrochemical reconstruction can design active sites and modulate interfacial proton-transfer dynamics to steer CO valorization toward targeted products.

paper.title: EVA-Flow: Learning Shared Chemistry for Unified Environment-Aware Molecular Conformation Generation
paper.abstract: Molecular 3D structures underpin simulations of thermodynamics, kinetics, crystallization, and nucleation, making their accurate prediction central to drug discovery and materials design. However, molecular geometry can change dramatically across environments. Existing models either ignore environmental effects or train separate models for each environment. We hypothesize that transfer learning across contexts is possible for conformer generation and that a general model will perform better when training data are limited, as in ligand binding and crystallization. We introduce EVA-Flow, a unified framework for environment-aware molecular conformation generation that learns shared chemical structure and adapts it through environment-conditioned generative modeling. Across vacuum, protein-ligand docking, solvation, and crystal packing, pretraining and cross-environment finetuning provide their largest gains in the three data-scarce settings. Evaluation against multiple reference conformations shows that EVA-Flow covers a broad range of solvation conformations. Analyses of molecules shared across environments support its ability to generate different conformations for the same molecule in different environments.

paper.title: Activation force dependence of the fluidization transition in supercooled active water
paper.abstract: Using an activation model reproducing facilitation mechanisms, we found recently a fluidization transition in supercooled water triggered by the motion of a few active molecules. We investigate here the effect of the activation force on the transition. The activation force increases the probability for active molecules to overcome the energy barrier induced by caging. The induced molecular motions result in an intermittent loose structure leading to a decrease of energy barriers around the moving molecule, thus facilitating the motion of nearby molecules. Therefore we expect the force, if small enough, to increase the facilitation mechanism, and as a result cooperative motions induced by it. As a result the activation force permits to tune facilitation and cooperative motions in active glass-formers. We find an optimum force for cooperative motions that we evaluate to be around 3.5pN, a value in the range of protein motor forces. As expected for a phase transition we observe peaks of cooperative motions (dynamic heterogeneity) on the transition. This result shows that dynamical heterogeneity are the cooperative motions of physical importance for the transition.
paper.tldr: 该研究表明，较小的激活力能增强过冷水的流化转变，但存在一个最优力值，超过后反而削弱促进作用。

paper.title: Electrifying hydroformylation
Biomimetic hydrophobic gating in MXene polypyrrole–based artificial Ion channels for efficient perchlorate sensing
paper.abstract: Abstract Ion selective electrodes represent a promising approach for ion detection based on potentiometric sensing principle. However, their practical application is often hampered by insufficient selectivity, primarily caused by interference from structurally similar ions. Herein, inspired by biological potassium ion channels, we demonstrate an efficient perchlorate ion selective electrode via the self–assembly of pyrrole–functionalized MXene nanosheets and methylated quaternary ammonium compounds. The resulting composite sensor significantly outperforms commercial ion selective electrodes with a > 10 4 –fold lower detection limit (10 –9.7 M), 18–fold higher selectivity ( K ij of 130.4), and a maximum sensitivity up to 59.6 mV/dec for perchlorate. Synchrotron X–ray scattering and mechanistic studies attribute this superior performance to a hydrophobic gating mechanism arising from dehydration effects and transport resistance within confined channels, which effectively lowers the energy barrier for perchlorate transport by 12.13 kcal/mol compared to that of sulfate. Furthermore, the sensor was optimized via substituent engineering for broad-spectrum anion detection and integrated into a portable platform for continuous on–site monitoring, achieving accuracy comparable to ion chromatography in real–world scenarios.

paper.title: Autonomous discovery of reaction networks from active-learning-driven reactive molecular dynamics
paper.abstract: Reaction networks underlie complex chemical systems such as combustion, catalysis, and atmospheric chemistry and can comprise thousands of elementary reactions. Ab initio nanoreactor molecular dynamics explores such networks efficiently by accelerated sampling of the potential energy surface, but computational cost limits how far it can sample. This work presents a transferable methodology coupling nanoreactor molecular dynamics with active learning to autonomously generate reaction networks from starting molecules. An agentdeveloped parser extracts elementary reactions from trajectories, and a large-language-model coding agent improves transition-state search strategies. Applied to the atmospheric oxidation of dimethyl sulfide, the methodology yields 980 nanoseconds of simulation, requiring only 290,195 quantum-chemical calculations. Initializing reaction discovery from already discovered species drastically speeds up reaction network exploration leading to 13,271 elementary reactions and 6,995 species. The reaction network covers most of the established mechanism but also unveils novel species such as an isomer of the key intermediate HPMTF.

paper.title: Continuity-Engineered Single-Atom Chains Regulate Interfacial Microenvironments for Valorized Alcohol Electrooxidation
paper.abstract: Abstract Catalytic selectivity is governed not only by active-site identity but also by the interfacial microenvironments surrounding those sites. Although single-atom chains bridge isolated atoms and extended surfaces, whether their atomic continuity can be exploited as a tunable design parameter for chemical synthesis remains unknown. Here we establish continuity engineering as a strategy for programming catalytic microenvironments through a substrate-anchored synthesis platform that enables precise control over one-dimensional single-atom chain architectures. Using ruthenium chains on α-MnO2 as a model system, we construct catalysts with graded continuity and uncover a volcano-type relationship between chain continuity and synthetic performance during benzyl alcohol electrooxidation. The continuity-optimized catalyst achieves >90% Faradaic efficiency for benzaldehyde across a wide potential window in acidic media while sustaining current densities up to 400 mA cm–2. Mechanistic studies suggest that optimal continuity promotes cooperative water activation, generating a hydroxyl-rich interfacial microenvironment that accelerates alcohol dehydrogenation while suppressing overoxidation. The resulting aldehydes can be directly integrated into one-pot bond-forming (C–S/N coupling) transformations. More broadly, atomic continuity emerges as a design variable for programming catalytic microenvironments and controlling selective electrosynthesis.

paper.title: Dynamical regimes of excitable cells under pulsed electric fields: From excitation to electroporation
paper.abstract: Nanosecond pulse electric fields (nsPEFs) are an established treatment modality for cancer and have emerged as a potential approach for deep brain stimulation and cardiac defibrillation. The concerns in these two applications are at odds. While pulsed-field electroporation applications aim to minimise excitation of surrounding neurons, therapies based on neuronal stimulation demand minimal electroporation of neurons. Although nsPEFs offer various advantages, such as minimising power input and suppressing electrode reactions, they require strong electric fields to reach both the excitation and electroporation thresholds, so maintaining a safety gap between the two is crucial. Because these coupled processes unfold on time scales ranging from nanoseconds to milliseconds and cannot be resolved simultaneously in experiments, a computational approach is used. This study examines the interplay between excitation and electroporation within the Hodgkin-Huxley (HH) framework for a planar two-bilayer model coupled with the Asymptotic Smoluchowski Equation for electroporation, and solves for transmembrane potentials (TMPs), pore statistics and pore size evolution. The model can predict the role of electroporation in modulating neuronal responses and qualitatively explain key experimental observations in the literature. These include excitation with a single action potential (SAP), repetitive spiking (RS), and depolarisation block (DB), and are explained here with detailed mechanisms, including the subtle effects of strong electric fields and electroporating currents on ion-channel dynamics. Importantly, our work establishes a parameter space for strength-duration curves in regimes of safe excitation without electroporation, and vice versa. For a neuron with an equivalent RC time constant of 10 ns, pulses shorter than about 20 ns electroporate the membrane before they excite it, and the safety factor falls below 5% for 1-ns pulses. The work also expands into s and ms pulses, and delves into possible regimes that could lead to neuronal inviability due to irreversible electroporation or excessive fractional pore area.

paper.title: Generalization in Learning: Eyring Formula and Predator-prey Model
paper.abstract: In this work, generalization in machine learning is investigated using a predator-prey model. We overview biological and chemical interpretation of the stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics and generative adversarial network. For a particular example of recovering an unknown function by a polynomial of fixed degree from a set of noisy data, the predator-prey model provides better approximation compared to the gradient descent method. Further, thermodynamical arguments, in particular Eyring formula, are used to explain grokking (delayed generalization) phenomenon in machine learning.

paper.title: Bromide‐Activated Four‐Electron Iodine Chemistry Enabled by a Pyridinium‐Integrated Hydrogel Electrolyte
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous four‐electron zinc–iodine (Zn–I 2 ) batteries offer high capacity and operating voltage, yet most reported systems rely on Cl − to activate the I 0 /I + conversion, generating hydrolysis‐prone ICl 2 − intermediates that cause rapid capacity decay. However, how inner I‐X bond polarization (X = F, Cl, and Br) governs the hydrolytic stability of interhalogen intermediates remains unclear. Here, we conduct both experimental and computational analyses, revealing Br − as the most effective halide. Compared with F − and Cl − , Br − forms less‐polarized and more hydrolytically stable IBr 2 − intermediates, markedly improving high‐voltage iodine reversibility. Building on this Br − ‐mediated stabilization, we further design a multifunctional PNA‐PyBr hydrogel electrolyte by incorporating pyridine hydrobromide into a sulfonate‐rich poly(sodium p ‐styrenesulfonate‐ co ‐acrylamide) network. Pyridinium cations immobilize IBr 2 − as water‐insoluble Py + IBr 2 − complexes, protecting I + species from hydrolysis, while sulfonate groups regulate the aqueous hydrogen‐bond network and establish Zn 2+ ‐selective transport pathways. The resulting cells deliver a near‐theoretical capacity of 422.6 mAh g −1 and a record lifespan of over 20 000 cycles at 20 C. Moreover, a 500 mAh pouch cell with an areal capacity of 3.5 mAh cm −2 sustains 600 cycles with negligible capacity decay, demonstrating the practical potential of Br − ‐activated four‐electron Zn–I 2 chemistry.

paper.title: HorizON: A Multi-Horizon Deep Operator Network for Property Prediction of Organic Battery Stacks
paper.abstract: Transition-metal-based batteries rely on critical elements such as lithium, cobalt, and nickel. Their extraction creates environmental and supply-chain challenges. Organic electrode materials (OEMs) reduce this reliance and provide broad molecular tunability. However, OEM-based batteries still show limited long-term cycling stability. Their design also requires the joint optimization of coupled metrics such as voltage, specific capacity, capacity retention, and energy density. These metrics depend on the full battery stack and on the interactions among its components rather than on the active material alone. In our previous work, we developed a data-fusion multi-task framework for average discharge voltage and first-cycle specific capacity. Both targets are single-valued. Here, we extend that framework to multi-horizon prediction by predicting a property at every cycle of a discharge trajectory rather than at a single cycle. Our multi-fidelity and Multi-horizon Deep Operator Network learns DFT redox potentials and cycle-dependent specific-capacity trajectories within one model. We train it on complete battery-stack representations and usage conditions, so it learns battery-stack interactions rather than cathode-only effects. This framework supports long-term property prediction, inverse design, and process optimization for organic battery systems.

paper.title: Method for Measuring Solid-State Diffusivity: Part 1. Theoretical Introduction
paper.abstract: The reliable determination of solid-state lithium diffusivity is essential for parameterizing physics-based lithium-ion battery models. However, conventional methods misattribute electrolyte concentration polarization to solid-state diffusion, introducing systematic errors in the inferred diffusivity. This study introduces a resistance-decomposition method that explicitly accounts for electronic conduction, electrolyte transport, charge transfer, and solid-state diffusion within the Doyle–Fuller–Newman (DFN) framework. The diffusion coefficient is calculated from the residual polarization resistance after independently determining the other contributions and accounting for the equilibrium potential dependence on the state of lithiation. The method is evaluated using synthetic voltage data generated with the DFN model implemented in PyBaMM. The results demonstrate accurate recovery of the prescribed diffusivity across most of the investigated parameter space under idealized conditions.. These findings establish the theoretical basis and numerical feasibility of the proposed method while identifying key limitations that require experimental validation.

paper.title: Dynamic Covalent Polymerization through Liquid–Liquid Phase Separation
paper.abstract: Abstract Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) is a ubiquitous phenomenon in living systems wherein membraneless organelles form through the spontaneous compartmentalization of small molecules or biopolymers. Synthetic (supra)molecular systems─including small molecules, oligomers, and polymers─have each been shown to undergo LLPS independently. However, creating synthetic polymeric systems that, like living systems, exhibit constitutional dynamics across multiple length scales─from small molecules to macromolecules─remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report an artificial dynamic polymeric LLPS system constructed from biologically relevant building blocks, such as amino acids and disulfides, in which the constitutional dynamics between small molecules and polymers can be engineered within condensed microenvironments that involve multiple weak yet reversible chemical bonds. Compartmentalization within disordered droplets not only elevates the thermodynamic driving force for disulfide-mediated ring-opening polymerization but also kinetically activates the dynamics of disulfide bonds, enabling the spontaneous, catalyst-free synthesis of high-molecular-weight poly(disulfide)s in water. The resulting polymers form thermodynamically stable, self-entangled hydrogels, and upon dehydration, they undergo quantitative photochemical depolymerization to regenerate virgin-quality monomers. These findings provide a model for constructing a biological system that integrates LLPS with intrinsic dynamic behavior and may open new opportunities for supramolecular biomaterials.

paper.title: Light‐Driven Surface Lattice Oxygen Activation in Oxygen Evolution
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a key bottleneck in sustainable hydrogen production and energy conversion. Conventional pathways such as the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) and lattice oxygen oxidation mechanism (LOM) both suffer from electron‐transfer inefficiencies at their potential‐determining steps ( * OOH formation in AEM and deprotonation in LOM) and structural instability (metal oxidation in AEM and oxygen‐vacancy accumulation in LOM). As a result, a unified mechanism that simultaneously overcomes these kinetic limitations and structural degradation processes remains absent. Here, we present a light‐driven surface lattice oxygen activation mechanism (LSOM) that synergizes photoexcitation and electrocatalysis to activate surface lattice oxygen into high‐energy non‐bonding orbitals, enabling their direct participation in O─O bond formation. This strategy circumvents the potential‐determining steps inherent to both AEM and LOM, while preserving metal oxidation states and lattice structural integrity. Experimental validation confirms remarkable enhancements in electrocatalytic activity and stability, outperforming conventional OER systems. By unifying catalytic efficiency with structural durability, the LSOM redefines the design principles for OER and establishes a universal framework for robust energy conversion technologies.

paper.title: Tribocharging of Granular Materials Dictated by Geometric and Thermoelectric Effects
paper.abstract: Tribocharging of granular materials is a widespread phenomenon ranging from volcanic eruptions and dust storms to pharmaceutical processing, yet its underlying mechanism remains elusive. Recent thermoelectric models have provided a quantitative framework for triboelectric charge transfer, but they have difficulty accounting for charging between identical materials. In this Letter, we propose a theory of granular tribocharging based on the interplay between particle geometry and thermoelectric response. Collision-induced frictional heating produces a size-dependent temperature asymmetry between particles, generating a thermoelectric voltage that drives charge transfer. The sign of the Seebeck coefficient determines the charging polarity, while particle size and thermal properties set its magnitude. Our multi-collision theory explains the experimentally observed size- and material-dependent reversal of charging polarity, as in quartz and nylon.

paper.title: Amortized Thompson Sampling and Efficient Information-Directed Sampling for Simulator-Based Design
paper.abstract: Thompson sampling is a widely used strategy for sequential decision-making under uncertainty, offering a principled way to balance exploration and exploitation. This strategy involves maximizing a target objective under a single sample drawn from the current belief over unknown quantities. Conventionally, this optimization is performed once the belief has been inferred from data, and it becomes computationally burdensome when many Thompson samples are required, especially in continuous action spaces. In this work, we introduce an approach that amortizes this process ahead of time, before any data is collected, so that an approximation of the full Thompson sampling distribution is available immediately once observations arrive. We employ this approach to solve the multi-round setting, involving sequential data acquisition and Thompson-sample recommendation across rounds. Beyond accelerating Thompson sampling, our approach enables efficient estimation of expected information gain about the optimal action. This can be used to select more informative Thompson samples or to obtain maximally informative designs with optimization. Combining this estimate of expected information gain with immediate regret supports information-directed sampling (IDS), which can outperform Thompson sampling by explicitly balancing these two quantities. We demonstrate our approach on two simulator-based design problems in synthetic biology, where the simulators have intractable likelihoods.

paper.title: Distilling neural networks into equations to predict planetary instability
paper.abstract: The problem of predicting when a multi-planet system will become dynamically unstable has defied analytical progress over the past three hundred years. Recent machine learning advances achieve high predictive performance of instability dynamics, but as black-box systems cannot be interpreted to connect to existing scientific understanding. Here we show analytic equations that predict when a multi-planet system will undergo instability. We discover these equations by first training a neural network on a dataset of N-body simulations, and then distilling its latent knowledge into closed-form algebraic expressions. Our two-stage pipeline first learns an interpretable variable basis, then searches for equations using symbolic regression. The resulting equations outperform existing analytic estimates of instability and apply across wide ranges of mass ratios, spacing, and orbital eccentricities. They capture structure in the prediction landscape with a small number of variables amenable to dynamical interpretation. These results demonstrate how symbolic learning can be combined with neural networks to extract scientific insight from complex dynamical systems.

paper.title: Side-Chain Engineering Controls Molecular Packing and Vertical Electron Transport in Discrete n-Type NDI-T2 Oligomers
paper.abstract: High-efficiency vertical charge transport in multilayer organic optoelectronic devices highly depends on molecular structure and arrangement. Using two T2-(NDI-T2)2 conjugated oligomers with ethylhexyl (EH) and octyldodecyl (OD) side chains as a model system, their effects on electron transport are investigated using, among other techniques, atomic force microscopy (AFM), conductive atomic force microscopy (C-AFM), grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS), steady-state optical spectroscopy, and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations. The oligomers of both materials exhibit relatively disordered structures in the as-cast state, whereas annealing enhances structural order and leads to side-chain-dependent changes in molecular stacking. EH-based films show a smaller annealing-induced photoluminescence shift than OD-based films, suggesting less pronounced stacking and conformational rearrangements, consistent with TDDFT-supported exciton analysis. The current-voltage characteristics are analyzed using the space-charge-limited current (SCLC) model. After annealing, both materials exhibit improved vertical electron mobility. The EH-based films reach a maximum mobility of 1.2 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1. The combined results suggest that the shorter EH side chains modify the out-of-plane packing environment and facilitate vertical electron transport. These results establish a structure-property relationship between side-chain structure, molecular order, exciton coupling and vertical mobility, providing a molecular design basis for optimising organic semiconductors through side-chain engineering.

paper.title: Charge state and hydration of vacancies in silicon and silicon carbide in contact with water: A grand-canonical first-principles stability map
paper.abstract: The state of a vacancy in a semiconductor is normally described by the Fermi level alone. In wet-etched, electrochemically processed, or humid silicon and silicon carbide, a vacancy also takes up hydrogen and oxygen from water, in amounts set by pH and electrode potential. We treat both effects together by minimizing the grand potential of a vacancy complex over its charge state and hydrogen/oxygen content. The result is a stability map in Fermi level and hydrogen chemical potential, which the computational hydrogen electrode relates to pH and potential. We parameterize it with spin-polarized density functional theory in 64-atom cells, including the vibrational free energy of bound H and O, for the silicon vacancy, its H, O, and OH complexes, and both vacancies of 3C-SiC. Hydrogen binds cooperatively to the silicon vacancy, which goes directly from bare to fully passivated $V$H$_4$. In contact with water the bare vacancy is never the lowest-energy state. Near neutral pH it binds oxygen from water as the A center, the paramagnetic hydroxyl complex forms below about pH 5 at zero bias, and full passivation to $V$H$_4$ requires cathodic bias. In PBE the Fermi level barely moves these boundaries, because the acceptor levels lie at or above the conduction-band edge. In SiC the first hydrogen binds to the silicon vacancy by 1.97 eV but is unbound at the carbon vacancy (the $Z_{1/2}$ center), so hydrogen from water alone should not passivate it except under cathodic bias.
paper.tldr: 实验证据表明，空位在湿环境下会结合氢和氧，其电荷态与组成由pH和电位共同决定，而非仅由费米能级控制。

paper.title: Physical structure as an organizing principle for universal Hamiltonian learning
paper.abstract: Density functional theory (DFT) gives the electronic structure of materials, but its cost limits large-supercell calculations and materials screening. Machine-learned Hamiltonians bypass the self-consistent cycle but are usually system-specific; universal ones could cover new compositions and disordered solids. Such models must generalize across chemistry and keep downstream properties physical, while staying inexpensive for large cells. Here we introduce UniTB, a universal E(3) equivariant Hamiltonian representation framework that integrates physical priors rooted in density-functional tight-binding theory with deep learning. UniTB's network, which corrects a prior Hamiltonian, generalizes across chemistry through a mixture of experts routed by that prior and a charge-equilibration head as in self-consistent-charge tight binding. A projection bounds band shifts from the prior, suppressing spurious states and keeping downstream properties physical. We provide the fastest SO(2) tensor-product GPU kernels for the network. The variant UniTB-Flash assembles its prior from two-center tables at $O(N)$ cost for $N$ atoms, against $O(N\log N)$ on a grid. Trained on 29,242 crystals, UniTB reaches a 0.48 meV matrix-element error on nonmagnetic test crystals spanning 68 elements. Without amorphous training data, both models agree with DFT optics and conductivity of amorphous Ge-Sb-Te. UniTB-Flash ranks candidates with no significant difference from UniTB, whose property values are more accurate; together they screen 16,195 crystals for five application domains of industrial relevance.

paper.title: Interlayer Mobility Control of 2D-Layered Crystals for Delamination of Nanosheets
paper.abstract: Abstract To maintain consistent properties of delaminated two-dimensional nanosheets, mild methods to preserve large lateral sizes and crystallinity during the delamination of bulk crystals are desired. This study introduces a gentle, solution-based on-substrate delamination strategy that avoids forming colloidal free-standing nanosheets by postponing the delamination process until the materials are deposited on the substrate, thereby preventing physical fragmentation in solution. By comparing cone-type and cylinder-type molecular intercalates (oleylamine and hexadecylamine), we identify interlayer mobility as a governing parameter for delamination in intercalation-accessible layered crystals, eliminating the need for external energy input such as sonication. Operando microscopic analyses reveal the importance of the gas–liquid interface during the evaporation process of drop-cast samples, which induces shear forces necessary for delamination. Application to a range of layered oxides and chalcogenides (HNb3O8, HTaMoO6, HTiNbO5, MoO3, V2O5, and TiS2) illustrates the transferability of this working principle across chemically distinct layered materials sharing sufficient interlayer adaptability. These proof-of-concept findings demonstrate that controlling interlayer mobility through molecular engineering provides an alternative route to producing large-area, high-quality 2D nanosheets.

paper.title: Asymmetric (De)lithiation in Magnesium (2,5-Dilithiumoxy)terephthalate Probed by Combined Operando FTIR Spectroscopy and Vibrational Calculations
paper.abstract: Abstract Although vibrational spectroscopy is widely used to investigate reaction mechanisms in organic electrode materials, spectral interpretation often remains empirical owing to a lack of solid-state structural data. Here, the known crystal structures of magnesium (2,5-dilithiumoxy)terephthalate and its one-electron-oxidized analogue enable the combination of operando attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy with periodic vibrational calculations to track structural evolution during reversible (de)lithiation. These calculations refine vibrational assignments, revealing significant C–O– stretching contributions to bands previously attributed primarily to quinoidal ring vibrations. They further establish that a band emerging near 1650 cm–1 during cycling originates predominantly from asymmetric carboxylate stretching, rather than the carbonyl stretching commonly proposed in the literature. The spectroscopic evolution also provides independent support for the asymmetric delithiation/lithiation pathway associated with the formation of Peierls-distorted π-stacked radical dimers previously identified by operando X-ray diffraction, providing molecular insight into the underlying electrode reaction mechanism.

paper.title: Limitations of Fixed-Point-Charge Force Fields for Metal Coordination Modes in Proteins: A Multilevel Study of Ca2+ in Integrin αVβ3
paper.abstract: Abstract Standard biomolecular force fields often present limitations in modeling metal coordination modes. We combined classical and QM/MM molecular dynamics to investigate Ca2+-mediated binding of cRGD to integrin αVβ3. We show that different metal coordination modes imply variations in the partial charges of the metal-coordinating atoms, which, if incorporated in the force field, substantially alter the free energy landscape. These results highlight the value of QM-based multilevel approaches to accurately capture metal coordination modes in biomolecular systems.

paper.title: Micelles as a Confined Liquid: Standard and Two-Dimensional Kinetics of Solute Rotation in Surfactant Micelles
paper.abstract: Abstract The dynamics inside a surfactant micelle show clear confinement effects: solute rotation slows and develops a nonexponential relaxation. Multiple rate constants─rate dispersion─must be involved. These effects have been widely attributed to solutes confined to an outer layer of strongly ordered hydrocarbon chains, a layer similar to a Langmuir-Blodgett film. In this picture, confinement effects result from a surface phenomenon enhanced by the high surface area of a nanometer-sized particle. This paper presents results that are inconsistent with strong chain ordering. Varying the solute shows that most of the confinement-induced slowing is at the center of the micelle, not near its surface. Two-dimensional (two-relaxation-period) kinetics show that rate dispersion is mostly due to rate heterogeneity among different solute molecules. A homogeneous component of the stretched dynamics is also identified and is attributed to the coupling of the solute rotation with conformational relaxation of the hydrocarbon chains. In a picture consistent with these results, the micelle is unstructured, and the solutes are more widely distributed than in the conventional model. Confinement effects are not due to surface effects; they are due to the clash in the lengths of the hydrocarbon chain and the particle diameter. This study is enabled by a nonparametric, “data-first” approach that enhances the interpretation of kinetics, especially two-dimensional kinetics.

paper.title: Bio-Inspired Crystal Machine Learning for Band Gap Prediction in Hybrid Halide Perovskite Monolayers
paper.abstract: Abstract Bio-inspired sparse connectivity offers a compact route for exchanging global information in crystal learning, but it has rarely been explored for inorganic–organic solids. We develop FlyCrysNet for band gap prediction in 357 relaxed A2BX4 hybrid halide perovskite monolayers and evaluate it alongside 17 established crystal machine learning models. The 18 models represent descriptor-based neural networks, message-passing graph neural networks, crystal graph Transformers, physics-informed long-range and reciprocal-space models, and bio-inspired sparse graph networks. Their test root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) range from 0.222 to 0.405 eV. ReciNet gives the smallest error, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.171 eV, an RMSE of 0.222 eV, and a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.966. FlyCrysNet combines a periodic graph encoder with a fixed sparse feature mixer and learnable topology control, reaching a test RMSE of 0.227 eV and an R2 of 0.964. It ranks second by test RMSE and forms a high-accuracy group with ReciNet, PotNet, and iComFormer. Topology controls further show that the sparse mixing framework remains stable under self-only, random, degree-preserving, and unweighted variants. Two low-gap Sn–I monolayers identified from the learned chemical space were examined using the Heyd–Scuseria–Ernzerhof screened hybrid functional (HSE06). (iPA)2SnI4 and (EA)2SnI4 retain direct gaps at Γ points of 1.61 and 1.40 eV, respectively, with band edges dominated by the Sn–I framework. The results establish bio-inspired sparse feature mixing as an effective crystal learning strategy and connect accurate band gap prediction with focused electronic structure analysis of hybrid perovskite monolayers.

paper.title: A hierarchical adaptive Fourier-feature physics-informed neural network for radio-frequency capacitively coupled plasma discharges
paper.abstract: Abstract Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are difficult to train for radio-frequency capacitively coupled plasma (RF-CCP) fluid--Poisson systems because missing initial conditions, steep sheath gradients, and strongly imbalanced residuals can lead to unstable or nonunique reconstructions. We propose a Hierarchical Adaptive Fourier-feature PINN (HA-FPINN) for such coupled plasma models. The method combines Fourier feature mapping to improve the representation of small-scale sheath structures, sparse physical anchors to provide interior constraints, and a two-level adaptive weighting scheme to balance the PDE, boundary, and anchor losses as well as individual equation residuals. The framework is tested on an 8-equation helium discharge model and a 23-equation electronegative \(\mathrm{Ar}/\mathrm{O}_2\) model. In the helium case, HA-FPINN reconstructs the space--time evolution of the main physical variables with \(1\%\) anchors and converges for all tested network architectures, with convergence times of \(110\)--\(246\) s. In the \(\mathrm{Ar}/\mathrm{O}_2\) case, HA-FPINN achieves stable reconstruction with \(5\%\) anchors, whereas the non-adaptive Fourier-feature PINN and standard PINN fail to converge under the same setting. The best performance in both systems is obtained at the tested Fourier frequency parameter \(\sigma=2.20\). Noise-injection tests show that HA-FPINN maintains the lowest reconstruction error in the helium case and preserves the main space--time structures in the \(\mathrm{Ar}/\mathrm{O}_2\) case up to \(15\%\) anchor noise. These results show that HA-FPINN provides a robust PINN formulation for strongly coupled plasma fluid models with missing initial conditions.

paper.title: Competitive Interactions between Propylene Combustion Products Regulate Catalyst Durability over Facet-Tuned Pt/TiO2
paper.abstract: Abstract While product-induced inhibition is widely recognized in heterogeneous catalysis, the joint influence of co-generated products on time-dependent catalytic deactivation remains underexplored. Herein, uniform colloidal Pt nanoparticles were deposited on anatase TiO2 supports selectively exposing (101) or (001) facets to fabricate two facet-controlled model Pt/TiO2 catalysts. We uncovered the intrinsic deactivation mechanism for low-temperature lean propylene combustion via stability tests, alternating feed kinetics, in situ DRIFTS, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Time-on-stream reaction tests recorded persistent activity decay for both catalysts, with far more serious decay observed on Pt/TiO2(101). Multiple characterization results excluded Pt sintering/encapsulation, C3H6/O2 poisoning, and partial Pt oxidation as dominant degradation factors. Instead, CO2 adsorption and subsequent carbonate accumulation on TiO2 surfaces were identified as the primary deactivation sources, which cut off supplementary oxygen delivery at metal–support interfaces. DFT adsorption energy data proved that H2O possessed a stronger surface affinity than CO2 on both facet types, and in situ generated H2O competed for adsorption sites to curb carbonate accumulation. Apart from this competitive effect, reaction-derived H2O alleviated excessive coverage of Pt sites by C3H6 and facilitated the adsorption and activation of gas-phase O2. Thanks to the relatively high water-binding capacity of TiO2(001), the corresponding Pt/TiO2(001) catalyst maintained abundant interfacial water during operation and exhibited much milder carbonate-triggered decay. These findings clarified the competitive co-adsorption interplay between CO2 and H2O across Pt–TiO2 interfaces and offered general kinetic guidance for developing durable catalysts toward industrial hydrocarbon lean combustion.
